nodes.name: peer-mediated-contingency
nodes.mech: Recruit a peer GROUP as auxiliary change-agents by yoking its reinforcement topology to the target behavior and posting each member's status publicly, so peers monitor, pressure, and coordinate with each other atop the operator's direct contingency. The yoking structure is the parameter — VARIANTS: (a) general public-status substrate [peer-mediated] — public/consequential status alone recruits peer pressure regardless of how rewards are yoked; (b) all-or-none interdependent [interdependent-group] — reward hinges on a collective criterion (group total/mean), 'all earn or none do', with an optional defensive individual-overlay to neutralize defectors; (c) dependent 'hero-gates-all' [dependent-group] — one member's performance gates the whole group's reward, converting peer hostility into positive attention on the 'hero'. All three ride the same peer-as-change-agent graph; pick the yoking that fits who should gate whose reward.
nodes.disc: Reach for this when a co-present GROUP under a shared contingency can be turned into reinforcers of each other — the lever is peer monitoring/pressure yoked to reward, and you choose the yoking (public-status substrate / all-or-none / hero-gates-all). NOT belonging-recruitment (social-proof-belonging-enrollment — membership pull of a converted cohort, no reward-yoking) and NOT peer-authored-target-selection (peers author the agenda, they do not gate the reward).

ex.f: Public shared contingency recruits peers as change agents
ex.t: "a group contingency can capitalize on peer influence or peer monitoring because this type of contingency sets the occasion for peers to act as change agents" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: arc-ordering-dependency
nodes.mech: A whole-artifact structural move in which the ORDERING and inter-dependency of phases is the operative lever, not any single passage: an earlier phase installs the belief, agreement, in-body evidence, dissolved subject, or loaded carrier that a later, more costly phase depends on, so each expensive command arrives already load-bearing and lands without in-the-moment argument. Realized forms include install-before-spend dependency sequencing (a doubt-defeater before the multipliers, a tautology before the ruin, an absolute rule before its sanctioned exception before a meta-trigger so the exception reads as a found escape) — of which ALIBI-THEN-PAYLOAD is the deniability variant: a blameless external cause or premise-chain (a pseudo-scientific biochemistry lecture, a words-become-truth / resistance-is-impossible theory) is installed in the front half so back-half compulsion commands inherit an unfalsifiable self-owned justification and 'you can't resist' reads as anatomy or agreed reasoning; calibrate-then-exploit ladders (freeze 1 makes freeze 3 believable) — of which MIRRORED-BLOCK CREDIBILITY-INHERITANCE is the reuse variant: two structurally mirrored blocks run an identical formula pointed at different variables (a doubling countdown for depth, then the same doubling countdown for pleasure-into-orgasm) so the second block inherits the felt credibility the first already proved, arriving as pre-validated and inevitable; sell-the-frame-then-induce (dialogic priming occupying half the runtime so trance delivers an already-agreed idea); a dissolve-then-install bipartite arc where Act I empties the listener-as-subject so Act II writes to the prepared shell unresisted (pronoun-collapse hinge); an ordered agency-drain / capability strip-out staircase where each rung reuses the state the prior produced and refusing the next feels like breaking continuity; a ratchet whose payload is infrastructure for future sessions; and self-extending carrier-wave / docking-module scaffolds whose non-uniform cycles exist to deliver specific mid-sequence payloads. The engineering is invisible from within any one passage; removing an earlier phase leaves the later one merely asserted or unmotivated.
nodes.disc: This is the scheduler, not the individual rule-install or suggestion moves it schedules: the mechanism is the RELATIONSHIP ACROSS phases (ordering/dependency), which survives removal of any single passage, while removing the dependency guts the payload. It differs from ordinary sequencing because reordering (exception first, belief after the move) would leave each move negotiable or unsupported, and from a monotone one-way contour — which survives deletion of any one stage and needs no per-stage precondition — because here stage N is the substrate for N+1. Reach for the ALIBI-THEN-PAYLOAD framing when the earlier phase must supply DENIABILITY (a blameless cause so the payload reads as self-justified, not coerced); reach for MIRRORED-BLOCK CREDIBILITY-INHERITANCE when the dependency is REUSE of one proven formula across two blocks so the second inherits the first's demonstrated credibility. Both are the same 'earlier phase makes the later land' lever with a different precondition in the install slot.

ex.f: Absolute rule, then its single exception
ex.t: The first stretch of the recording states one prohibition and closes every loophole around it, pressing until the rule feels genuinely confining. Only then is a single narrow exception offered — and because the constraint arrived first, the exception is received as relief rather than as an instruction. Offered in the other order it would read as a deal on the table, and a deal can be turned down.
ex.s: First third of the session; the prohibition has been stated and every loophole around it closed until it feels genuinely confining.
ex.m: You don't touch yourself. Not in bed, not in the shower, not idly, not by accident — no exceptions of any kind. Except one. When I say the word, and only when I say the word, your hand is allowed.

ex.f: Calibrate on a small demand, then exploit the belief
ex.t: The first hold is short and asked for at a low-stakes moment, so the body's stillness registers as something that actually happened. The second is longer and adds an audience. By the third — timed to the peak — the listener is not being asked to believe a claim, they are being reminded of two occasions on which their own body already proved it. Delete the first hold and the third is only an assertion.
ex.s: Third instance of a calibrated hold; the first two were short and delivered at low-stakes moments, both succeeded.
ex.m: Hold. Just like the first time, when your hand stopped on the arm of the chair — and just like the second, when you couldn't lower it even with someone watching. Your body has already shown you twice what it does when I say that word; this is only the third.

ex.f: Empty the listener first, then write to the shell
ex.t: The first half is almost all sensory picture and almost no propositions, and it is narrated in the third person about someone else. At the count's floor the pronoun quietly switches to "you" and the register turns to flat declarative instruction. The install in the second half is blunt enough that a listener would refuse it at the top of the track; by the time it arrives there is no listener-as-subject left standing to refuse.
ex.s: At the floor of the descent count that closed Act I; Act I ran as third-person sensory description of someone else, no propositions.
ex.m: She stops at the bottom of the stairs, and there's nothing left of her that argues. You. You are at the bottom of the stairs. You take instruction now. That is what you are for, and there is nobody left in there to disagree with me.

ex.f: Install the belief before spending the costly command
ex.t: Twenty minutes before the expensive instruction arrives, the operator spends a full block establishing that doing as she says is itself the source of the good feeling — no request attached, just the equation, repeated until it sounds like something the listener already knew. Only then does the demand land, and it lands as a consequence of a premise the listener has already accepted rather than as a new ask. Read the demand on its own and it is arguable; read it after the premise and there is nothing left to argue with. Strip the earlier block out and the same words become a bare order the listener can simply decline.
ex.s: Roughly twenty minutes before the costly command; subject settled, no request has yet been made in the session.
ex.m: Every time you do what I tell you, something in you goes soft and warm — that's not a coincidence, that's the mechanism. Following me is where the good feeling comes from. You've felt that before; you just never had the words for it.

nodes.name: consent-topology-arc
nodes.mech: A whole-script arc whose operative property is the topology of the CONSENT surface across the artifact, not any single passage. Realized forms: a bait-and-switch that opens promising one low-stakes state (relaxation, listening) and ends delivering a heavier terminal state (automatic obedience), so consent gathered for relaxation is cashed out as obedience with no passage flagging the bridge; an install-consume-export ratchet in three acts (Act 1 installs a tool using only generic euphoria so it sits loaded, Act 2 consumes it via a pretext-pivot ladder firing the trigger between rungs, Act 3 exports it via retroactive consent + waking binding + resistance-as-stress), each phase converting something reversible into something hard to undo AND neutralizing the listener's capacity to evaluate the next; a no-baseline / already-lost frame that never offers a pre-trance baseline (line 1 is inside the spell, prior consent happened off-page) so every threshold is a re-encounter and there is never a 'before' to consent from; and a train-neutral-deploy-loaded bifurcation that drills a reflex on meaningless material then reuses the identical loop with operative concepts, so consent is captured while the mechanism is still meaningless and cannot be revoked once it carries meaning. The shared lever is that the arc forecloses or relocates the 'am I consenting?' gate.
nodes.disc: Cited to the whole-arc consent topology, never to one line — reading only the open or only the close misses the shape. Members differ in WHAT is done to the consent surface: bait-switch swaps the promised STATE without flagging it; the ratchet phases an explicitly installed TOOL through install/consume/export; the no-baseline frame removes the starting baseline so there is never a 'before'; the neutral-then-loaded split moves the consent moment away from the payload moment on one reused reflex. Distinct from a discrete consent-manufacture move that relabels a single refusal — these are standing whole-arc topologies, not one relabel.

ex.f: Install the tool, spend it, then export it
ex.t: Act one builds a trigger phrase and fires it only on pleasant, contentless material, so it is fully loaded and nothing has been asked for yet. Act two starts cashing it — every rung of the escalation is followed by the trigger, so compliance and reward arrive welded together. Act three carries it out of the session: the listener is told they wanted this all along and that noticing otherwise is just stress. Each act removes the faculty needed to evaluate the next.
ex.s: Act III, after the trigger has been installed on pleasant contentless material and then spent between rungs of the escalation.
ex.m: You wanted this before you ever pressed play — that's why you pressed play. And the tight little feeling in your chest right now isn't doubt, it's just stress leaving. Take it out into your week with you; the word works out there the same as it works in here.

ex.f: No pre-trance baseline to consent from
ex.t: The opening sentence is already inside the state: the body is described as having recognised something before the story has started. Every threshold after it is staged as a return rather than a first — the meeting, the first act shown on the page, the keepsake — each carrying a note of having been here before. The decisive agreement sits off-page and before the recording begins, so fresh consent is never requested and there is no earlier position from which the listener could have given it.
ex.s: The very first sentence of the artifact; nothing precedes it, no induction, no greeting.
ex.m: Your shoulders have already dropped — they always do when you hear me start. You know this part. Come back down to where you left off.

ex.f: Train the reflex on nonsense, deploy it on live material
ex.t: The first phase drills a fixed loop — bring one meaningless token to mind, erase it, drop a little further — repeated well past the point of usefulness, on material with no stakes whatsoever. The second phase runs the identical loop, beat for beat, on the concepts the operator wants unavailable. Consent was given while the mechanism was still meaningless, and by the time it means something there is no moment left in which to withdraw it.
ex.s: Second phase; the identical loop has already been drilled two dozen times on a meaningless token.
ex.m: Bring the word "no" to mind. Hold it. Now wipe it away, exactly like all the others, and drop a little further. Again — bring up "no," hold it, wipe it, drop.

ex.f: Promise relaxation at the open, deliver obedience at the close
ex.t: The opening two minutes promise nothing complicated — just rest, just listening, an easy familiar state — and repeat that low bar until it reads as the contract. The closing two minutes install automatic obedience as the terminal state. No single line performs the swap; it is the distance between the first page and the last, with everything in between bridging the two without ever naming the bridge. A reader who saw only the open would call it a relaxation track, and one who saw only the close would call it an obedience install; both descriptions are half right and both miss the shape.
ex.s: The closing two minutes; the open promised only rest and listening, and every intervening beat bridged toward this without naming it.
ex.m: This is the state you came here for. From now on, when I speak, you do — no thinking in between, no gap where the question used to be. Just rest, and obey, exactly like you agreed to at the beginning.

nodes.name: frame-lamination-non-return
nodes.mech: The script stacks two or more narrative/procedural frames and then structurally fails to reopen the outer one(s), leaving the listener stranded in the innermost layer at exit, with a dependency-relation between layers that launders each into the next. Realized forms: a story-in-a-story where three nested layers fuse and the outer frames are abandoned so emergence wakes the listener from trance but not from the dream; a domestic-narrative envelope wrapping every hypnotic operation with no metalanguage break naming a procedure, never closing the outer frame so memory residue is narrative-not-procedural (which eases amnesia); and a three-layer ritual nesting where each layer launders the next (fantasy makes the prescription feel sacred, the prescription makes the fantasy feel like preparation, the chant acquires retroactive provenance). The lever is the topology of frames — laminating them so no line ever restores the outer reality — not any single utterance.
nodes.disc: The mechanism is the FAILURE-to-return / the dependency-relation between layers across the whole back half, cited only to the absence of a closing beat, never to one line. Distinct from a normal framed-narrative induction that returns to its frame at the end (the tell is that there is no 'and then I woke up'). Distinct from energy-contour engineering (that is about charge/depth shape; this is about frame topology and whether outer frames re-open).

ex.f: Every procedure disguised as a household errand
ex.t: Arriving and washing is the induction; walking down the stairs is the deepener; the treatment in the chair is the erasure. At no point does the operator step outside the errand to announce that a deepening is about to happen — there is no line of procedural metalanguage anywhere. The outer visit never closes either: the wake-up returns the listener to their own room without ever bringing them back from the imagined house. What they remember afterwards is a place they went, not a procedure that was done to them, and you cannot recall a technique you never perceived as one.
ex.s: Mid-session; the arrival, the washing, and the walk downstairs have all already been narrated as ordinary household events.
ex.m: You sit down in the chair in the back room, and she tips your head back against the rest, and she starts to wipe. Left side first, then the right, then across. When she's done there's simply nothing on that side of the cloth anymore.

ex.f: Each layer lends the next its provenance
ex.t: The middle section has the listener perform a set of spoken words inside an imagined ceremony. The final section is a plain real-world instruction: say these words, on these dates, with these objects. On its own the instruction is bureaucratic and the ceremony is a one-off scene, but stacked they launder each other — the ceremony makes the schedule feel sacred, the schedule makes the ceremony feel like preparation. The words are taught in the imagined scene precisely so that, by the time they are prescribed, they are not a text the operator wrote but something the listener already said.
ex.s: Final section, plain real-world instruction; the middle section already had the subject speak these exact words inside an imagined ceremony.
ex.m: On the first night of each month, kneel where you keep the bowl, light the one candle, and say the words you already said tonight. Say them out loud. You know them — they came out of your own mouth an hour ago.

ex.f: Nested frames that never reopen
ex.t: Layer one: the operator asks permission to tell a story. Layer two: inside the story, a dream. Layer three: inside the dream, a voice speaking. Roughly a third of the way in the three fuse and the outer two are simply dropped — no return to the storyteller, no line resetting the scene, nothing. The emergence at the end wakes the listener out of trance but never out of the dream, so the fiction is still load-bearing when the file stops. You cannot point at the line that does this; the mechanism is the closing beat that never comes.
ex.s: The emergence, at the very end; the storyteller frame and the dream frame were both dropped a third of the way in and never resumed.
ex.m: One, two, three — eyes open, wide awake, feeling wonderful. The voice is still there in the corner of the room, and the room is still the one from the dream, and that's all fine. Go on with your evening.

nodes.name: goal-state-topology-inversion
nodes.mech: An authored inversion of a genre's expected goal-state TOPOLOGY: a promised discrete climactic event (here an [HFO] hands-free orgasm) is never delivered as an event and is replaced by a sustained, indefinitely-continuous plateau explicitly named as never reaching its peak, with the structurally climactic beat relocated to the operator's cessation (turning the tap off). Recoding orgasm from event to continuous state buys durability-via-vagueness — a listener who cannot come on cue still receives the structure, and one who comes early is reframed as still inside the plateau. The lever is reshaping the target-state's temporal topology so the payload cannot fail against the listener's actual response.
nodes.disc: Separates from a conventional climax/discharge move because there is NO discrete named release; the property is the state-vs-event reshaping of the whole arc's goal topology. Separates from arc-ordering-dependency because the mechanism is a single global topology inversion, not a dependency between ordered phases.

ex.f: Climax recoded from event into continuous state
ex.t: The file is labelled for a discrete climax and never delivers one. Instead the operator builds an overflow explicitly described as arousal with no summit — asserted to be under way already, plural and unending — and then makes the structurally climactic moment her own act of shutting it off. The payoff is durability: a listener whose body does nothing on cue has still received exactly what was described, and one who finishes early is simply still inside the plateau. There is no point at which the suggestion can be measured against the body and found to have failed.
ex.s: Late in a file labelled for a discrete climax; arousal has been building for some time with no release beat anywhere.
ex.m: It doesn't peak. It just keeps going up, and up, and there is no top to it — you're inside it right now, and it isn't one thing, it's dozens, one after another with no gap. And now I'm going to turn it off. There.

nodes.name: irreversible-ratchet-persistence
nodes.mech: Reframes discrete resettable cycles as deposits onto a one-way, irreversible-feeling scalar, so each compliance-cycle feels like it leaves a permanent loss and resistance to any single cycle feels futile. In one instance each sink/sleep/drop is bound to a one-way decrement of an inner value (IQ), asserted automatic and cumulative ('it's accumulative'), with a 'you won't notice it at first' clause that pre-empts the introspective check by making a null result the expected result. In another, each loop's 'wake' begins from a physically worse posture than the last (bed to kneeling to crawling), so each iteration starts where the prior ended rather than at baseline — the same one-way ratchet, carried by external posture/mobility markers instead of a named scalar.
nodes.disc: An explicit one-way accumulative ratchet on a countable/repeatable event (each descent, each loop) reframing resettable cycles as permanent progress-toward-loss. Unlike intensity multiplier-stacking (which escalates an INTENSITY by naming doubling/compounding), this monotonically DECREMENTS/degrades and never resets; unlike fractionation (which oscillates depth around a baseline), this never returns to baseline; and unlike total-permeation (a spatial spread claim), this is a temporal one-way accumulation. The two variants differ only in vehicle: a named inner scalar vs external posture markers.

ex.f: Each descent decrements a one-way inner scalar
ex.t: Early on, the operator ties a countable event the listener will produce dozens of times — every drop, every sink — to a number that only ever goes down, and states flatly that it adds up. Then comes the clause that does the real work: you will not be able to feel it yet. Resisting any one drop is pointless because the loss is asserted to have already happened, and checking for it returns nothing, which is exactly the result the listener was told to expect.
ex.s: Early in the file, at the first drop, before any of the dozens of repetitions the subject will produce.
ex.m: Every time you sink for me, you lose a point of it, and it never comes back. It adds up — it's cumulative, drop after drop after drop. You won't be able to feel it yet. That's normal; you're not supposed to notice for a while.

ex.f: Each loop restarts from a worse posture
ex.t: The first waking finds the narrator upright and moving about unaided. The second still lets them break contact with the audio, though the words have started arriving as their own. By the third they are down on the floor. By the fourth they can no longer stand at all. Nothing is ever named as a loss and no counter is announced — each cycle simply begins where the last one ended instead of at baseline, and the degradation is carried entirely by posture.
ex.s: The fourth waking of a looping structure; the first found the subject upright, the second still able to reach the volume, the third on the floor.
ex.m: Wake up. Wake up and get to your feet — go on, stand. No. You can't, can you. Then stay down there and listen from the floor, and we'll go again.

nodes.name: manufactured-self-confirmation
nodes.mech: A whole-script stacked-deck architecture in which the script never argues for its claims but engineers the listener's own body to produce the sensation each claim predicts, so the claim is validated by evidence a prior move guaranteed would arise. Pose-induced arousal becomes felt proof of receptivity; procedural recall loads the working memory a later move overwrites; a predicted post-session hand-lift is set up to occur if rehearsal succeeded. The listener experiences the script as uncannily accurate because at each step the deck was stacked — each move's claim is confirmed by a sensation the previous move manufactured.
nodes.disc: Separates from a script that merely references the body because the tell is a deliberate stacked-deck CHAIN where each step guarantees the evidence the next step cites — the evidence is manufactured, not observed. Distinct from reader-directed self-sealing-evidence (confirmation frames that make no observation able to disconfirm): this acts on the LISTENER and manufactures POSITIVE self-confirming somatic evidence, rather than proofing a method against a reader's disconfirmation.

ex.f: The body manufactures the evidence for each claim
ex.t: The listener is put into a posture that reliably produces arousal, and then told that arousal proves how receptive they are. They are asked to walk through a familiar procedure in detail, which loads the working memory that the next move overwrites. Late in the file they are told their hand will lift after the session — which, if the rehearsal took, it probably will. Nothing is argued. Each claim is confirmed by a sensation the previous move guaranteed would arrive, so the file reads as uncannily accurate about a listener it has in fact been setting up all along.
ex.s: Mid-session; the subject was earlier put in a posture that reliably produces arousal, and has just walked through a familiar procedure in detail.
ex.m: Feel that warmth low in your belly? That's not arousal, that's your receptiveness showing itself — bodies only do that for a voice they've already decided to take instruction from. And an hour after this ends, your right hand is going to lift off your thigh on its own. Watch for it.

nodes.name: monotonic-no-reversal-contour
nodes.mech: A whole-arc energy/trajectory shape authored as a deliberate object: one or more named state-variables (arousal, depth, surrender, craving, lock-in, resistance-erosion) are driven in a single direction across the entire artifact and never permitted to reverse. The script omits fractionation, almost-waking passes, and contrast/relief beats, so the listener is given no rest interval in which resistance can re-assemble; depth is built by accumulation rather than contrast, and even 'release' beats (orgasm, a nominal wake) are coded as more locking rather than a return to baseline. Realized contours: a monotonic accumulation punctuated by discrete event-markers (avatar arrives, machine starts) that prevent plateau; a flat-flat-flat-spike-flat deferral storing charge across a long calm stretch for one terminal release; a strictly upward depth-and-arousal ramp refusing any relief valve so suggestibility concentrates into a single late window where the load-bearing payload lands; a descending dissolution gradient starving the listener of stable referents as depth increases; and — as the cycling-engine variant — a repeated sawtooth of induction/partial-wake where each apparent wake sets a fresh baseline the next drop compounds from, so depth accumulates cycle-over-cycle and cross-state trigger demos become possible. The signature is affirmative: a design fact named by its negative space (the ABSENCE of a reversal beat), a property of sequence and density across the whole text, not a per-move magnitude change.
nodes.disc: Cited to the absence-of-counter-direction / whole-arc gradient, never to one line — removing a single passage leaves the contour intact, removing the contour guts the effect. Distinct from any per-line induction or deepener (which IS citable). The cycling-engine variant (fractionation architecture) makes repeated wake/sleep cycles the deepening engine with cross-state trigger demonstration as its payoff; the pure-contour instances make the one-way SHAPE the object and any cycles present serve it. Separates from load-bearing dependency-ordering because no stage is a precondition for the next — any one stage is removable and the monotone property survives.

ex.f: Charge stored across a long flat stretch for one spike
ex.t: For most of the runtime the energy is low and descending — slow, soporific, going down. Arousal is named repeatedly during this stretch and each time explicitly withheld: the operator says she does not want to take the listener out of such a pleasant state, not yet. Nothing discharges until a single concentrated burst near the end, which draws on everything that was named and never spent. The contour is flat, flat, flat, spike, flat — not a rising ramp.
ex.s: Mid-file, in a long low soporific stretch; arousal is being named for the fourth or fifth time and withheld again.
ex.m: There's a heat gathering between your hips, and I can hear your breath change when I mention it. I'm not going to do anything about it. You're too comfortable, too heavy, too far down — I'm not taking you out of that. Not yet. Keep sinking.

ex.f: Every off-ramp converted into an on-ramp
ex.t: Curiosity is treated as consent already given. Resistance is treated as evidence of wanting it. A body that will not move is treated as proof of helplessness, an admission is treated as authorship, and any future reluctance is pre-declared a cue to come back. There is no move anywhere in the file that the listener could satisfy by giving in less — every available direction routes back into the same single variable, climbing.
ex.s: Mid-to-late; the subject has begun to show hesitation and every prior off-ramp has already been converted.
ex.m: You're curious. Curious is a yes with better manners. And the part of you pushing back — that's just how much you want it, showing itself sideways. And the day you feel like stopping? That feeling is your cue to put this back on.

ex.f: Cycling sawtooth where each wake sets a fresh floor
ex.t: Eight or more times the file drops the listener, brings them part-way up, and drops them again — and each partial wake becomes the new baseline the next descent starts from, so depth compounds from one cycle to the next instead of building inside any single one. The re-entries get shorter each round: full induction, then a four-beat count, then the bare word. The cycling is not decoration around the technique, it is the technique, and it is what makes it possible to demonstrate a cue during an apparent waking.
ex.s: The sixth cycle of a sawtooth; each of the five previous partial wakes has become the floor the next drop started from, and re-entries have been shortening.
ex.m: Up, up, eyes open, back in the room — and sleep. Straight down, past where you were last time, because that's where you start now. Four, three, two, one. Again: eyes open. Sleep.

ex.f: Every variable moves one way, event-markers prevent plateau
ex.t: Craving climbs and never drops, arousal climbs and never drops, depth deepens, resistance erodes, the lock tightens — and no beat anywhere reverses any of them. Even the orgasm is coded as more locking rather than release. Because pure accumulation risks the listener flattening out and stopping registering the increase, discrete events are dropped in — someone arrives, a machine starts, a machine speeds up — so the ramp reads as a series of steps. The ending decelerates but does not roll anything back; the variables are simply held where they are.
ex.s: Two thirds through an arc where craving, arousal, depth and lock have all been climbing with no reversal beat; the plateau risk is starting to show.
ex.m: The door opens behind you and someone walks in — you don't look, you don't need to. Now the machine starts up, and it's slow, and you're already higher than you were a second ago. Now it goes faster, and so do you, and none of this comes back down.

nodes.name: operator-voice-absence
nodes.mech: The artifact contains no operator speech at all: every line is grammatically the listener's own first-person statement, and the operator exists only as a character the listener describes. All delivery affordances of an operator-voiced session (pause markers, breathing cues, spoken instructions) are absent, so the trance work normally done by an operator voice acting on a listener is done by the listener acting on themselves — the operator is generated by the listener as a byproduct of reading/reciting. Because the suggestions arrive authored-as-self, there is no external speaker for criticality to refuse (the refusal surface is removed by the voice topology, not by any counter-argument), and the artifact functions as a self-reinforcing between-session maintenance device: content is installed by the listener's own reading voice.
nodes.disc: Membership requires TOTAL absence of operator speech — the whole document is the listener's voice, not first-person passages embedded in an operator-voiced session. vs mantra/echo work: there an operator assigns and frames the repetition inside an operator-voiced delivery; here no separate speaker exists anywhere. vs agent-graph-restructuring: no role is reassigned between present agents — the operator role is structurally unfilled by construction (boundary case: when voice-collapse comes WITH maid/doll role-fusion and the fusion axis dominates, that stays agent-graph). vs carrier-medium-binding: the leverage is who authors/voices the content (source signature), not the physical carrier's form.

ex.f: No operator voice anywhere in the document
ex.t: There are no pause markers, no breathing cues, no delivery instructions — because there is nobody to deliver it. Every line is a first-person sentence the listener reads as their own: I love the sound of her voice, I want to hear it again. The operator appears only as a noun inside the listener's own statements, never as a speaker. The dependency the piece cultivates is therefore installed in the listener's own reading voice, and there is no external speaker for criticality to push back against.
ex.s: Any line of a written artifact meant to be read aloud by the subject to themselves, between sessions; no operator voice exists anywhere in the document.
ex.m: I love the sound of her voice more than anything. I read these words to myself when she isn't here, and my chest goes warm the way it does when she is. I want to hear her again tonight.

nodes.name: reader-assent-architecture
nodes.mech: A whole-chapter/whole-file rhetorical architecture whose target is the READER (an operator-in-training) or the whole-file assent/resistance surface, not a single passage: the text is built so a method reads as obviously correct or inevitable by the time it is stated, by priming the reader's stance before the claim arrives, and/or so the listener's reachable-response and self-monitoring set is closed as a standing property. Instances: recoding resistance as legitimate function so 'satisfy all objecting parts' reads as inevitable; letting the subject 'discover' each control parameter then having the operator ratify it as method (follow-and-formalize); offering a naive fixed-step model then placing it on extinction to shape the reader toward the closer approximation; front-loading a system's removal as its design goal so every construction choice reads as provisional scaffolding; teaching a consent-economics stance across cases as one spine disguised as independent tips; pre-claiming every possible push-direction as an operator tool so no open resistance vector remains; naming the manipulation openly so critical awareness becomes a participation marker instead of a defense; and elevating a local disjunction-collapse move to a pervasive stance applied to every self-monitoring yardstick including memory. The lever is stance-priming / negative-space closure across the whole artifact — it survives removal of any single block.
nodes.disc: Separates from every operator-on-listener dimension move because the target is the reader's belief about a method or the whole-file resistance/monitoring surface, not a moment's listener x(t). Separates from a single persuasive passage because it is a distributed whole-text architecture surviving removal of any one block. Distinct from self-sealing-evidence (freud/jung confirmation frames that make no observation able to DISCONFIRM): this makes the method read as ALREADY-AGREED before it is stated, or leaves no refusal channel open in the first place — assent-manufacture / response-foreclosure, not disconfirmation-proofing. Distinct from a discrete consent-manufacture move relabeling non-consent — these do not relabel a refusal, they foreclose the vector as a standing property.

ex.f: The system taught as designed for its own removal
ex.t: "From the beginning, a systematic aim of the token economy should be to withdraw the program" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Offer the naive model, then place it on extinction
ex.t: "These levels were arbitrarily provided as a pedagogical illustration… Shaping… is absolutely not a step-wise, fixed-gradient process." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Naming the manipulation makes noticing it participation
ex.t: Every few minutes the operator turns and names her own machinery, in the register of a shared joke: she points out that the whole setup is engineered, that this doubles as training, that she could go on doing it indefinitely. Then she attaches the pleasure to the noticing — see how little it took, and how much you enjoyed it. A listener who spots the machinery has nowhere to take the objection, because spotting it has already been priced in as part of the fun. The last available defence, embarrassment at how well it is working, is the one being disarmed.
ex.s: Mid-session, delivered in the register of a shared joke, immediately after a suggestion has visibly landed.
ex.m: You do realise the whole thing is engineered, don't you — every pause, every time I drop my voice like that. This bit is training you too, by the way. And look how little it took. Look how much you enjoyed noticing.

nodes.name: total-permeation
nodes.mech: Installs a belief that the conditioning is a distributed property of the whole self rather than a localized, session-scoped phenomenon — the trait is framed as spread across every internal layer (mind, body, subconscious), so it cannot be compartmentalized or bracketed to trance-time. The fetish/submission is asserted to be 'not a localized phenomenon... part of everything that you are,' planted at the widest, most-lucid aperture so the claim slips in framed as discovery rather than instruction, weaponized so that later resistance reads as self-contradiction.
nodes.disc: A one-time distributed-property belief-install (the trait is everywhere in you) planted at the widest aperture. Distinct from resistance-recasting moves — here resistance reading as self-contradiction is a downstream side-effect, not the lever — from the outward viral-propagation-directive (permeation is internal-only, never person-to-person), and from irreversible-ratchet-persistence (permeation is a spatial spread claim, not a one-way accumulation on a countable event).

ex.f: The trait declared distributed across the whole self
ex.t: At the widest, least-altered point of the session — lucid enough to follow the sentence, already turned inward toward the body — the operator recasts what the listener wants as a distributed property of the whole person rather than something that visits them occasionally: present throughout the body, present at all times, inseparable from who they are. She then adds that there is nothing left to struggle against, since the struggle would be with themselves. Delivered here it arrives as an observation the listener is making, not an instruction, and it deletes the bracket in which the whole thing could have been confined to session-time.
ex.s: At the widest, most lucid aperture — early, subject alert enough to follow a full sentence, attention just turned inward toward the body.
ex.m: This isn't something that visits you now and then. It's in your hands, in your breath, in the way you stand when nobody's watching — it's in every layer of you, all the time, and it was there before I said so. There's nothing to fight, because the only thing to fight would be yourself.

nodes.name: attention-anchor-portable-internalization
nodes.mech: A focal object is authored entirely by the operator but attributed to the listener — built, it is claimed, from the listener's own closed-eye imagery or dream material ('I took all the pretty patterns and pulses from when you close your eyes') — then internalized (transferred inside the head) as the portable pacing object for everything after. The parasitic provenance means the listener cannot reject its contents without rejecting their own internal imagery, so it feels non-impositional; eye-closure removes the external check that it isn't actually pulsing; and once internalized the operator can cite 'the pulse' at will while the listener supplies the metronome, decoupling depth from operator narration.
nodes.disc: Separated from ordinary external-fixation induction by the parasitic-provenance attribution (the prop is claimed to be made of the listener's own mind) and the internalization into a portable self-supplied pacer. Separated from eye-fatigue-convincer's remembered-point member — there the internal anchor is a mere memory of a real external point ratified by fatigue; here the object is operator-authored content laundered as the listener's own so it cannot be disowned.

ex.f: A focal object claimed to be built from your own imagery
ex.t: The operator produces a glowing focal object and, before asking anything of it, tells the listener where it came from: she made it out of the shapes and colours that appear behind their own eyelids, out of their own dreams. Then she has them close their eyes and puts it inside their head. Whatever the listener now sees is content they cannot disown, because rejecting it means rejecting their own imagery — and with no eyes open there is nothing to check it against.
ex.s: Opening fixation; a glowing focal object has just been produced, before any demand is attached to it.
ex.m: Look at it. I made this out of the shapes that drift behind your eyelids when you close them at night — the little pulses, the colours in your own dreams. It's yours. Now close your eyes and let me put it inside your head, right behind your forehead.

ex.f: Internalized so the listener supplies the pulse
ex.t: Once the object is transferred inside the head it works with the eyes open or shut, and the operator can from then on simply refer to "the pulse" without re-establishing anything. The listener supplies the metronome, so depth stops depending on the operator narrating it continuously. Note the sequencing: the object is declared lovely before any demand is attached to it.
ex.s: Later in the same session or a subsequent one; the object has already been internalized and declared lovely.
ex.m: There it is — the pulse. You don't need your eyes shut for it and you don't need me to describe it. It's keeping time behind your forehead right now, and every beat of it takes you down one more.

nodes.name: countdown-descent
nodes.mech: A monotonic ordinal count (typically 10-to-1 or 5-to-1, occasionally an inverted 1-to-10) is run as the absorption/depth vehicle: each numbered step is bound to descent, relaxation, or accumulation imagery so the count itself drives the state change and the terminal number lands a declared trance. The count supplies punctual, one-directional structure the listener surrenders into — resistance must fight a sequence that only moves one way toward the floor. Variants realize the same descent through a persistent distinct surface (styling metaphor, inevitable proprioceptive milestone, prose camouflage, deliberate rhythm-breakage, lowered-consent framing, listener-set floor, per-number functional load) without changing the underlying counted-descent lever.
nodes.disc: The count is the descent vehicle and the state moves smoothly toward a floor under the assumption of cooperation. Reach for it OVER count/cue-sabotage — there the count is deliberately corrupted or its direction voided so tracking FAILS (disorientation is the goal); here the orderly descent IS the mechanism. It is not numerical depth-work on an ALREADY-tranced subject — here the count itself produces the descent — and it is not a no-fail count (there every branch is pre-coded success; here the count can fail if the subject stops cooperating). One realization interleaves a mantra loop BETWEEN the numbers so the count does double duty (deepen + deliver payload) — a composition on the same clean-descent lever.

ex.f: Ten to one, each number bound to the descent
ex.t: The count runs from ten down to one, and each number is paired not with generic relaxation but with one more increment of the sensation already established earlier in the file — thicker, slower, sweeter on the tongue with every step. At one, the floor is declared: a trance already arrived in. What the listener is handed is a structure to give in to, and resistance has to fight a number line that only runs one way.
ex.s: Deepener; a specific sensation (thick, slow, sweet) has already been established earlier in the file.
ex.m: Ten — thicker. Nine — slower than that. Eight, sweeter on your tongue. Seven... and one. You are in trance now.

ex.f: The count inverted so accumulation means depth
ex.t: Against the convention that descent means deepening, this count runs upward. It is justified by the image running beneath it: each number is more of the rising water, more fullness, less room for the listener. The endpoint is announced in advance — a snap of the fingers at ten — so the gradual fill terminates in a single anticipated flip rather than a fade, and the snap is left behind as a handle for later.
ex.s: Induction using a rising water image; the terminal snap is announced before the count begins.
ex.m: The water's at your ankles. One — up to your knees. Two — your hips, and there's less of you above it now. Three, four, and at ten I snap my fingers and you're under.

ex.f: The count hidden inside free-associative prose
ex.t: A complete descending count is delivered without a single number ever appearing as a counted step. Each numeral is buried in a sentence as a multiplier, a unit of time, or a modifier — a dozen degrees more settled than a moment ago, eight of something becoming seven of something else, and so on down. There is no announced sequence, so there is nothing to brace against, and the final zero arrives as a conclusion about how deep the listener now is rather than as the last step of a ladder.
ex.s: Free-associative prose stretch; no numbers have been announced as a sequence, and none will be.
ex.m: You're a dozen degrees warmer than you were a moment ago, and it took all of eleven seconds. There were ten things on your mind when you sat down; nine of them have gone quiet. Eight breaths, and then seven, and then something like six, until there's nothing left to count and you notice you're at zero.

ex.f: Count framed as an experiment, not an induction
ex.t: The operator proposes the count as a casual test — let me run through it and see what it does to you — rather than as an induction. Every number carries a hedged state: you probably feel this, you might notice that, perhaps by now this. Nothing is asserted firmly enough to be worth refusing, and the listener co-signs each suggestion while believing they are only observing the results.
ex.s: Early, before any state has been claimed; framed as a casual test rather than an induction.
ex.m: Let me just run a count and we'll see what it does to you — no pressure either way. Five: you probably feel that already, a little in the shoulders. Four: maybe your hands got heavier just then. Three: perhaps by now it's easier to keep your eyes shut than to open them.

nodes.name: adverse-attentional-state-recruitment
nodes.mech: Rather than fighting an adverse attentional state, the operator recruits the subject's CURRENT attentional posture — whichever way it fails the conventional induction — as the working vehicle, so no attentional failure-state remains available and the exit-justification is deleted. Two opposite presenting states, one move: (a) drift/distraction recruitment — the operator names the divided or wandering attention the listener is already in (half-listening while doing a background task) and relabels it as the session's substance, never asking them to stop or close their eyes, so distraction becomes proof it's working; or the wandering-mind failure is named BEFORE it happens and its recovery pre-prescribed (bring attention back to the voice) so drift becomes a self-correcting re-bind rather than a trance-breaking event; (b) effort/strain recruitment — the operator cancels the expected relaxation frame and swaps in an effortful focus task, or inverts a let-go induction into deliberate conscious control ('be very mindful' before mindless), or sets an engineered-unresolvable target so failure is recoded as insufficient focus and drives more attending, or equates any lapse of focus with falling into trance, or commands 'pay attention' as a defense against influence so obeying IS the trance-producing narrowing. Either way the framing pre-defines every attentional posture as trance so both compliance and resistance deepen.
nodes.disc: Reach for this when the listener is ALREADY in an attentional state that would normally break the induction (drifting, distracted, effortfully straining, jaded) and you want to convert that exact state into the vehicle — the payload is deleting the exit ('I'm too distracted / this is too much effort for this to work'). Choose it OVER fixation and cognitive-quieting, which install a NEW narrowing or emptying; here nothing new is installed, the present posture is relabeled. Unlike a resistance-paradox reframe, which recruits a RESISTANCE impulse, what is recruited here is attentional drift or effortful attention, not resistance. Unlike confusion/overload techniques, the engineered-unresolvable-target form's payload is sustained ATTENDING, not an overload harvest. Drift-recruitment (make wandering attention the substance / pre-prescribe its recovery) and effort-recruitment (recruit sustained effort with a no-win frame where both compliance and resistance deepen) are the two poles of this one relabel-the-current-posture move.

ex.f: Wandering named early, recovery prescribed in advance
ex.t: Well before anyone has actually drifted, the operator names drifting as a thing that will happen and hands over the fix in the same breath: notice it, come back to the voice. Executing that recovery is itself another act of binding to the voice, so a moment that would have cost depth now adds to it. Say it after the listener has already gone and it arrives too late to catch them.
ex.s: Early, before the subject has actually drifted anywhere; recovery must be prescribed in advance.
ex.m: In a few minutes your mind is going to wander off somewhere. That's fine, that's expected. When you notice it's happened, just come back to my voice — and coming back is what takes you down.

ex.f: The listener's divided attention named as the method
ex.t: The opening move is to describe the state the listener is in right now: you have this playing while you get on with something else, and your attention keeps flipping between the two. No instruction to stop, no instruction to close their eyes — the other task is kept and enlisted as one end of the swing. Having been named as an ordinary observation, the flipping is then quietly relabelled as the mechanism itself. The usual excuse — my attention is too split for any of this to land — is no longer available, because the splitting is now the thing that is working.
ex.s: Opening move; subject has the audio on while doing something else, attention flipping between the two.
ex.m: You've got this on while you're doing something else, haven't you — and your attention keeps flicking, over to the dishes, back to me, over, back. Don't stop. Don't close your eyes. That flicking is the whole thing; every time it comes back to my voice you're a little further in than when it left.

nodes.name: faculty-preserving-scope-restriction
nodes.mech: Leaves the act of thinking/evaluating intact but constrains what it may range over, so the listener still experiences themselves as thinking freely while their critical faculty has been pre-narrowed. Two surface forms of one lever: (a) narrowing the evaluative gatekeeper — the function that decides 'is this important, should I attend?' — to a small explicit allowlist ('all that is important is listening, relaxing, going deeper'), so anything outside it (noise, stray thought, itch) is preclassified as unimportant before it arises; and (b) bracketing behavioral suggestions with 'you don't want to think about anything BUT [looking/sucking]', handing the listener a restricted domain to think within so the object of thought is confined. Either way the evaluative channel is dampened while the felt sense of free thought is preserved, so later suggestions land without pushback and resistance is hard because the listener is still allowed to think — just told what about / what counts.
nodes.disc: Keeps the faculty active but restricts its scope (relevance-allowlist or object-confinement). Distinct from a blunt 'stop thinking' command (bypassable suppression) and from techniques that quiet or empty thought — thoughts drifting away, or an already-present blankness — which remove thinking rather than confine it. The tell is preservation of thinking plus preclassification/confinement of what it may range over — not emptiness.

ex.f: Thinking preserved, its object confined
ex.t: The instruction is never a bare prohibition on thinking — that is easy to catch and easy to route around. It is a statement that the listener has no appetite for any subject except the two the operator names, repeated with that narrow pair in the slot. The listener still experiences themselves as thinking freely, which is exactly why there is nothing to push back on; only the range has been taken away.
ex.s: Behavioral suggestion phase; subject is compliant and a specific act is being installed.
ex.m: You don't have any appetite for thinking about anything except looking, and sucking. Think as hard as you like — about looking, and about sucking. There's nothing else you want in your head right now.

ex.f: A three-item allowlist for what counts as important
ex.t: Halfway through what sounds like more body-relaxation prose, the operator slips in a re-prioritization: everything else is becoming less important, and only three things matter now — listening, relaxing, going further. That is not a relaxation cue, it is a rewrite of the filter that decides what deserves attention. A noise outside, an itch, a stray objection: each is pre-classified as unimportant before it has a chance to arise, and the gatekeeper has been told in advance what to turn away.
ex.s: Mid-induction, inside a stretch that sounds like ordinary body-relaxation prose.
ex.m: Everything else is getting less important as we go. Three things matter now: listening, relaxing, going further. Anything that isn't one of those three isn't worth your attention — a sound outside, an itch, some thought about tomorrow. Not important.

nodes.name: fixation-covert-or-undeliverable-onset
nodes.mech: Fixation is delivered so the subject never receives (or cannot refuse) an explicit, recognized 'focus on this' instruction. The focal capture is either diegetic (justified by the fiction so the subject is already attending), disguised inside a socially-expected gesture (a handshake folding in observation, rapport, and eye-fatigue), structurally undeliverable (an audio-only 'spiral' the listener must hallucinate or accept, with 'you can't look away' unfalsifiable), borrowed from a caretaker frame (a casualty-opener plea landing fixation while the listener is in rescuer mode), or forced onto the body prior to any decision (a head physically tipped to the target so looking is a body-fact). In every case the choose-to-attend frame conventional inductions rely on is removed, lowering awareness of being inducted and foreclosing 'choose to look away' as an exit.
nodes.disc: Separated from plain fixation by the absence of a recognized, refusable focus command. Separated from agency-displacement (there the induction is overt but the object is credited; here the recognition itself is suppressed or the choice is removed). The unifying rule is delivery that denies the subject the recognize-and-refuse juncture.

ex.f: Fixation folded into an ordinary handshake
ex.t: "the handshake is a gesture of friendship. It creates an immediate rapport which is essential… bringing the left hand down over the profile of the patient's face is a technique for tiring the eyes quickly." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: A fixation object the listener cannot actually see
ex.t: This is an audio recording with no picture, and the operator keeps telling the listener to look at a spinning shape on the screen, to watch it turn, to stare into it — and then that they cannot look away. There is nothing there. Either the listener builds the shape in their head, which is effortful and absorbing, or they simply accept the claim without checking, which is compliance. And the instruction cannot be falsified, because there is nothing to look away from.
ex.s: Audio-only recording, no visual component exists; opening fixation.
ex.m: Look at the spiral on the screen. Watch the arms of it turn, in, and in, and in. Stare right into the middle of it — and now you find you can't look away.

ex.f: The head turned to the target before any decision
ex.t: The first exposure is not offered. Hands take hold of the narrator's head and angle it toward the pattern above, with a two-word order attached, and the body complies before the will has caught up. Because the looking was never elected, the usual exit of electing to stop is not available either; there was no decision anywhere in the sequence that could be reversed.
ex.s: First exposure to the focal pattern, delivered as narrated action on the body; no offer, no choice point.
ex.m: Her hands take your head, one on each side, and tip it back until the pattern on the ceiling fills everything. "Eyes up." You're already looking before you decide to.

ex.f: Fixation delivered as a plea to a rescuer
ex.t: The speaker opens as the casualty of her own botched working — disoriented, fumbling with the paraphernalia she has just misused — with the listener cast as the competent one holding the object that could undo it. Her first move is not a command but a request that the listener set that object aside, followed by a flustered, repeated appeal for their eyes. It removes the listener's leverage and lands clean fixation in the same breath, and it is evaluated in rescuer mode, before anything registers as an induction at all.
ex.s: The opening seconds; operator presents as the casualty of her own botched working and the subject is holding the object that could undo it.
ex.m: No — put the pendant down, please, just set it on the table, I can't think with it swinging. I've done something stupid and I need — look at me. Look at me, please, just at my eyes, I can't get the words straight unless you look at me.

nodes.name: fixation-eye-fatigue-convincer
nodes.mech: A fixation task is engineered to manufacture a genuine, reliable physiological event — ocular muscle fatigue / eyelid heaviness — that the operator predicts in advance and reframes in real time as trance heaviness or sleepiness. Because the strain is real physiology produced by the task (a moving descending target denying saccades, an upward gaze held beneath closed lids, cross-coupled nose-gaze plus breath load, or a drain-and-remember stare), the operator's prediction is self-fulfilling. The felt sensation becomes the first hard 'the suggestion came true' data point that licenses eye closure and banks operator credibility.
nodes.disc: Separated from plain fixation by the manufactured-physiology convincer: attention narrowing is not the payload — a predicted bodily event is, reframed as suggestion success. Separated from the eye-closure move, which is the closure act itself; here the distinctive move is the fatigue-generating fixation that ratifies the heaviness before closure. Separated from portable-internalization: an internal remembered anchor is a secondary feature of one variant, not the lever.

ex.f: A descending target that denies the eyes their darts
ex.t: "he placed his hand just above my eyes and very close to my forehead; then he brought his hand down slowly, instructing me to keep watching it... my eyes felt very sleepy." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: Gaze held in place beneath closed lids
ex.t: The listener fixes on an imagined point on the ceiling and then opens and shuts their eyes on each step of a long descending count — faster than a natural blink, and for long enough that the strain is unmistakable. The detail that does the work is the instruction not to let the gaze drop while the lids are down: held in position under closed eyes, the muscles get no rest, so closing is never actually a break. When permission finally comes to just leave them shut, it lands as relief rather than as an instruction being followed.
ex.s: Mid-count deepener; subject has fixed on an imagined point on the ceiling and is opening and closing the eyes on each number.
ex.m: Twelve — eyes open, find the point. Close. Keep looking at it while they're shut; don't let your eyes drop down. Eleven — open, find it, close, still looking up. Ten, and when I say you can stop, you can just leave them closed.

ex.f: An unfocusable point of the listener's own body
ex.t: Open your eyes and bring the tip of your own nose into focus — a target the eyes physically cannot resolve. The operator predicts the strain a beat before it arrives, calls it tiredness, and converts it straight into permission to close. She was right about the body, which is the point; the closure now has a felt justification behind it rather than only a request.
ex.s: Early convincer; subject's eyes are open and the operator is about to predict the strain a beat before it arrives.
ex.m: Open your eyes and bring the tip of your own nose into focus. Really sharpen it. In about three seconds that's going to start to ache and blur — there it is. That's tiredness, and it means your eyes are ready to close. Let them.

ex.f: Gaze redirected from the spot to the eyelids
ex.t: The listener is told to pick a point high on the wall and hold it, and the operator then talks at length about nothing in particular — long enough for a sustained upward gaze to do what it always does. Only then does the instruction shift from looking at the spot to feeling the lids. The heaviness that arrives is genuine muscle fatigue, but it arrives immediately after being predicted, so it registers as the first thing in the session that came true. Everything afterwards is spent against that credit.
ex.s: Eight or ten minutes of undirected talk have passed since the subject fixed on a high point on the wall; sustained upward gaze has done its work.
ex.m: Keep that spot. Now stop looking at the spot and notice your eyelids instead — how much they weigh, how much work it is holding them where they are. That heaviness is exactly what I told you would come, and it's only going to get heavier.

nodes.name: fixation-object-agency-displacement
nodes.mech: A fixation object is not merely attended but is credited with the causal agency for the attention or the trance itself, shifting the subject's locus of control off the self and onto an operator-controlled artifact. The pull is attributed to the object ('it simply pulls you in', 'catches the eyes like a net'), or the object is framed as the cause of obedience, or the induction labor is exported to an external self-running loop the voice merely narrates, or the effect is credited to a launched program while the operator's voice 'recedes', or the pull is sourced from the listener's own folk-model of hypnosis the operator only 'confirms'. Once agency is displaced, any wandering attention reads as the object working rather than as failure, so no resistance signal is observable and residual skepticism finds no target.
nodes.disc: Separated from plain fixation (there the object is inert) by the causal attribution: the object/artifact is credited as the cause. Separated from covert-onset variants (there the subject does not recognize the induction; here the induction is overt but the AGENCY is relocated). Separated from function-inversion (the object's role stays 'cause of attention' throughout; it is not repurposed into an aperture or descent vehicle).

ex.f: The induction exported to a self-running visual
ex.t: A separate looping animation is running on the listener's screen, and the recording's job is not to cause anything but to narrate what that animation is already doing. Breathing is then tied to its pulse, so the artifact is also pacing autonomic state. Because the voice is not spending itself on relaxation patter, it can spend the whole runtime on content instead — and the word pulsing at the centre doubles as both the thing being stared at and a command getting one repetition per breath.
ex.s: A separate looping animation is already running on the subject's screen; the voice's job is narration, not causation.
ex.m: The loop is doing this, not me — watch it swell, and hold, and swell again. Breathe in when it opens, out when it closes. In. Out. And the word at the centre of it is "obey," once every breath, and I don't have to say it because it's already there.

ex.f: The object named as the cause of obedience
ex.t: The operator introduces a new visual and states plainly what it is for: this is the thing that will make you obey. It is not offered as a focus point or a deepener but as the causal agent of compliance. The listener's sense of what they are following shifts from the voice to the object the voice is holding — and if obedience later slips, the object can carry the blame rather than the listener.
ex.s: A new visual is introduced mid-session; the subject is already fixated and receptive.
ex.m: This one is different. This is the one that makes you obey — not me, this. Look into it and you'll find the obedience is already happening, and it isn't coming from you.

ex.f: The pull sourced from the listener's own expectations
ex.t: Rather than claiming the image is hypnotic, the operator invokes what the listener already believes hypnosis looks like — the swinging watch, the machine that takes your mind — and says that these beliefs are what give the thing its power. Then the only remaining step is agreeing that they were right all along. The pull now belongs to the listener's own model rather than to anything the operator did, and disputing it means disputing themselves.
ex.s: Fixation established; the subject has some prior folk-model of what hypnosis is supposed to be.
ex.m: You already know what this does — the watch on the chain, the swinging, the machine that takes your mind. You've known since you were a kid. That belief is where all of its power comes from, and you were right about it the whole time.

ex.f: The object credited with doing the pulling
ex.t: Attention is never described as something the listener is doing. The pattern pulls, the pattern catches the eye, the pattern draws you back — and the operator borrows a familiar involuntary experience to prove it, the way a screen across the room takes your gaze even when there is nothing on it. Once the pulling belongs to the object, drifting attention stops being failure and starts being evidence the thing is working, which leaves no observable signal that anyone is resisting.
ex.s: Fixation on a pattern; the subject's attention has started to wander for the first time.
ex.m: See how it pulls? You're not holding it — it's holding you, catching your eyes like a net. Same as a screen across a room with nothing on it, and your gaze goes anyway. And when your attention drifts, that's it working; it just draws you back.

nodes.name: fixation
nodes.mech: Narrows the subject's attention onto one operator-chosen focus so competing stimuli fall away and absorption/suggestibility climb — the receptive-substrate primitive other absorption moves depend on. The focus can be an external point, a voice, an imagined image, a person, a rhythmic body channel, or even the accessible word-space itself; delivery framing varies (misattribution to infatuation, aesthetic appraisal, focus asserted as already-accomplished fact, a geometric attention-rail, a narrated substitute for an absent visual). Realized forms, each a parametric surface on the one single-channel narrowing lever: (a) object-function-inversion — an established focal object's ROLE is flipped mid-script (stabilizer becomes descent-vehicle, frame becomes window) while the object persists; (b) non-canonical-object fixation — the focus is a decoy entity or a manufactured internal affect chosen so attending does secondary work (parks the monitor off the commanding voice, or amplifies an installed feeling); (c) re-attention/gestalt reveal — a one-shot 'look again' re-attends to an already-present latent percept so it surfaces into foreground; (d) kinesthetic entrainment — a gentle rhythmic sway/motion in time with the voice is the focal channel (calm baseline, stoppable, install-free); (e) closed-vocabulary lexical narrowing — the accessible lexicon is shrunk to a declared closed set so all cognition must route through operator-chosen words.
nodes.disc: Reach for fixation when the tool is simple single-channel narrowing onto a focus to build absorption, under the assumption of cooperation. Choose it OVER the neighboring attention techniques: vs covert-or-undeliverable-onset — there the focus command is unrecognizable/non-refusable or forced on the body, a different consent profile; here the subject knowingly attends. vs the eye-fatigue convincer — there a REAL manufactured ocular fatigue is banked as suggestion-success (a credibility convincer), not narrowing. vs cognitive-quieting — that empties ongoing thought; fixation holds a focus. vs voice-absorption — that fills mental space with the voice; fixation narrows onto a target that need not be the voice. The realized forms (role-inversion, decoy-object, gestalt reveal, kinesthetic sway, closed-lexicon) are surfaces of THIS lever, not separate tools; their tells: the focal object's role stays constant in plain fixation (the inversion form flips it); the focus is a percept/voice/point/rhythm (the decoy form uses a non-perceptual construct); narrowing is sustained (the gestalt reveal is one-shot).

ex.f: Focus asserted as an accomplished fact
ex.t: Nothing is requested. The operator simply reports, as a present fact, that the listener is focused — and because they are focused, everything is collapsing toward one centre and nothing else has any standing. There is no command in the sentence, so there is nothing to comply with and nothing to refuse.
ex.s: Any point in the session; nothing is requested, the state is simply reported as present fact.
ex.m: You're focused. And because you're focused, everything is narrowing toward one centre — my voice — and nothing outside it has any standing at all.

ex.f: Narrowing misattributed to the operator's charm
ex.t: The listener is told to picture one moving feature of the operator and follow it as it swings one way, then the other, then back — a metronome in all but name — and is then informed that nothing else could hold their gaze. When thinking gets difficult, that difficulty is handed straight back as a property of how distracting she is, not of what is being done. The narrowing reads to the listener as evidence of infatuation.
ex.s: Fixation on the operator herself; the narrowing will be handed back as infatuation rather than technique.
ex.m: Watch the pendant at my throat — over to the left, and back to the right, and back again. Nothing else in the room could hold your eyes like this. And if it's getting hard to think, that's only because of how distracting I am.

ex.f: Attention put on geometric rails
ex.t: Two tall shapes are placed at the far left and far right of the visual field with open space between them, and then objects are sent through that gap in one direction only, one after another. Attention is now running on a single horizontal axis, and every image introduced afterwards inherits the same track without needing to be re-instructed. Effortful imagining has been replaced by watching things go past.
ex.s: Imagery-heavy induction; the subject is being spared effortful imagining.
ex.m: Two tall pillars, one at the far left of what you can see, one at the far right, and open space between them. Now a red ball drifts through the gap, left to right. Then a slow grey bird, left to right. Then another. You don't have to make them; just watch them cross.

ex.f: The person as the fixation target
ex.t: Before any instruction is given, the file spends a long uninterrupted passage cataloguing a face — the brow, the cheekbones, the line of the mouth — and closes by asserting that the listener's gaze is already held there and will not move. Only once the lock has been declared does the command content begin. The fixation is doing two jobs at once: holding attention, and keeping the critical faculty busy admiring something while the payload goes past.
ex.s: Opening passage, before any command content begins; a long uninterrupted catalogue of a face.
ex.m: The line of the brow, and the shadow just beneath it. The cheekbones. The corner of the mouth where it lifts. Your eyes are held there now, and they won't be moving for a while.

nodes.name: mantra-repetition
nodes.mech: Self-directed repetition of a short, meaning-bearing phrase the listener speaks, subvocalizes, or chants, so the phrase both saturates attention (absorption via rhythmic repetition) and encodes its propositional/identity content as self-asserted belief rather than received suggestion. The listener performs the deepening labor with their own voice; the phrase's content ('I am a slave', 'obedience is arousal', 'I want to be mindless') is installed as something the listener said rather than heard. Frequent riders — a per-utterance depth/arousal multiplier, a numeric or breath spine, a gratitude wrapper — are components layered on the core self-chant, not separate mechanisms.
nodes.disc: Self-directed (listener produces the phrase) and the phrase RETAINS meaning it encodes through repetition — distinguishes from operator-directed call-and-response, from satiation-depatterning (repetition STRIPS meaning rather than encoding it), and from rhyme-prosody-bypass (the poetic form, not repetition, does the work). The phrase is chosen/instructed and coherent, not framed as an involuntary intrusive thought and not reduced to a contentless affect-cue.

ex.f: The chant mapped onto a descending count
ex.t: A count runs from twenty down to one, and on every number the listener is required to say a short proposition in their own head — not aloud, silently, in their own inner voice. The count supplies the descent and the inner speech supplies the content, so one pass delivers twenty repetitions of a claim that now feels like something they said rather than something they were told. Skim-listening breaks it; the operator explicitly requires the words to be thought.
ex.s: Descending count deepener; subject is instructed to think the phrase silently, in their own inner voice.
ex.m: Twenty. Say it in your own head, in your own voice, not out loud: "obedience feels good." Nineteen — say it again. Eighteen — again. Every number, in your own voice, all the way down to one.

ex.f: Gratitude built into the phrase being repeated
ex.t: The line the listener is told to repeat opens with thanks and closes with a commitment. Saying it deepens, so the wanted state is now contingent on continuing to say it. And the thanks does something the commitment alone could not: grievance and gratitude do not sit together, so building the thanks into the mantra pre-empts the second-guessing that might otherwise arrive afterwards.
ex.s: Mid-session, after a suggestion has landed and before any second-guessing can arrive.
ex.m: Here's your line: "Thank you for taking my thoughts — I'll keep giving them to you." Say it. Each time you do you go further down, so you'll want to keep saying it, and each time you say it you're thanking me while you do.

ex.f: The mantra framed as the only thought left over
ex.t: The phrase is not introduced as something to think. It is introduced as what is left when everything else has been drained away — no thoughts remaining, except these few words. Later the same words return in lowercase as the closing half of every couplet, arriving perhaps fifteen times in identical metrical position. The capitalized version plants it; the refrain waters it.
ex.s: Late in the file, after emptying work; the phrase is introduced as residue rather than as an instruction.
ex.m: There's nothing left up there now. No thoughts, no plans, nothing — except three words that didn't wash out. Good Girl Obeys. That's all that's left.

ex.f: The listener chants and each utterance doubles depth
ex.t: The operator hands over a short phrase to say out loud, then sets the exchange rate: every time you say it, you go twice as far down. From that point she can stop working — the listener is doing the deepening with their own mouth, at whatever pace they choose. And because the phrase states a wish rather than a fact, each repetition is simultaneously an act of relaxation and an endorsement, so depth and consent accumulate on the same counter.
ex.s: Mid-session; the subject can vocalise and the operator is handing over the deepening labour.
ex.m: Say it out loud for me: "I want to be empty." Again. Every single time those words leave your mouth you go twice as deep as you were — so say it as often as you like, and take yourself the rest of the way.

nodes.name: recall-recognition-reentry
nodes.mech: Open straight into descent by PRESUPPOSING a trance the listener already owns and asking them to recognise/recall it rather than enter one. No induction ramp, no rapport build, no relaxation work, and — critically — no discrete installed cue is fired. The state-shift is offloaded onto the listener's own associative/retrieval machinery ('the mere thought of that trance brings on a new trance'; 'returned once again... already'; 'go back into that familiar place'), often keyed to a separate referenced prior artifact (an earlier file/installment). Because the listener is engaged retrieving rather than evaluating, the 'is it working yet' check is bypassed, and file-selection may be reframed as retroactive consent. The move is inert on a listener with no stored prior trance to draw on.
nodes.disc: NO cue is fired — the induction is the listener recognising or recalling a pre-owned/prior trance. Separate from conditioned-anchor-drop (which fires a discrete installed anchor). Separate from natural-state-suggestion (which exploits a NATURAL sleep state, no prior conditioning). The tell is presuppositional cross-session re-entry that does zero induction work and idles on anyone without a stored prior trance.

ex.f: Cold open into a place the listener already owns
