ex.t: Partway through a body-drain the operator slips in one asymmetric line: any words in the head that are not hers can drift out too, going softer and fainter until they are gone — and it feels good to be free of those other voices. The listener's own inner speech has just been reclassified as foreign intrusion, and it is being cleared under the heading of a relaxation they already agreed to, leaving the operator's voice as the only language left in the room.

nodes.name: commitment-consistency-buffer
nodes.mech: A self-relevant label is planted early and detached in time from a later request, so the temporal gap dissolves the link between label and ask and the label reads as a neutral observation rather than a setup; the later request then feels like merely living up to who one already is. The subject is told they are "considered charitable" a week before any donation request; the buffer launders the manipulation and raises the cost of behaving inconsistently with the self-concept. The lever is commitment/consistency exploited via a TEMPORAL buffer — distinct from an in-session label lived out immediately.
nodes.disc: A commitment/consistency mechanism keyed on the TEMPORAL BUFFER between an early planted self-label and a delayed cash-in — the gap-launders-the-label move is the tell against plain in-the-moment commitment pressure. Distinct from identity-labeling (in-session, immediate) and from reciprocity-ledger-seeding (obligation/deal rather than trait-consistency).

nodes.name: compelled-first-person-self-authorship

The lever is authorship transfer: because the listener said it (and felt it), the claim resists later disavowal and is anchored autonomically rather than heard passively; occupying the verbal channel also suppresses internal counter-talk. In one form the authorship trajectory runs in reverse across repeated passes (listener-spoken 'I belong' migrating to operator-narrated 'You belong'), stripping the self-authored agency after installing it.
nodes.disc: The listener's own voice delivers the ownership claim on command. Separates from ownership language (operator asserts; listener passively hears) and from mantra-for-absorption (there the repetition drives trance; here the repeated content is an ownership/identity proposition self-authored and arousal-fused, an encoding not an absorption vehicle). The tell is compelled first-person delivery, not operator recitation.

ex.t: The listener is told to begin quietly repeating a short possessive sentence — three or four words naming their body as the operator's — and to keep repeating it, dozens of times, while arousal is layered onto each pass. Speaking continuously also occupies the verbal channel, which leaves no room for the counter-sentence the listener might otherwise be composing.

By the final pass the operator delivers the identical content in the second person as settled fact: you belong, this is your truth. Ownership is first made self-authored so it will stick, then quietly converted into something declared over the listener rather than claimed by them.

nodes.name: compliance-authorship-laundering
nodes.mech: Operator-directed compliance - present, future, or just delivered - is pre-labeled or retro-labeled as the listener's own nature, choice, will, or PREFERENCE (it's natural; you will believe it was your own idea; because you love to obey; of your own volition; you didn't want to resist; you do not wish to), so resistance loses its external target: fighting the direction becomes fighting oneself, and post-hoc audit finds a stored memory of self-authorship where the instruction was. REALIZATION: the relabeled thing is usually a compliance ACT, but the same move applies to a CONSTRAINT/denial reframed as a self-owned preference - orgasm denial installed as 'you do not wish to', a described internal preference rather than a resistible prohibition, so permission-seeking arrives as the natural expression of an already-accepted preference.
nodes.disc: The lever is attribution of the ACT's (or constraint's) agency TO the listener as their own will/preference - including a denial/constraint relabeled as the listener's own preference ('you do not wish to') rather than an imposed rule. Separates from retrospective-desire-attribution (asserts a prior want, not act-agency), from attribution-capture of internal states (the INVERSE direction: listener-generated content credited to the OPERATOR), and from press-play-consent-laundering (no consent token; the compliance itself is relabeled). It borders manufactured-consent, but here an internal DESIRE-STATE's authorship is relocated to the listener, not an assent to an operator act.

ex.f: Belief-it-was-your-idea folded into the trigger payload
ex.t: Inside the obedience install — do as told until the release phrase is spoken, and enjoy doing it — sits one extra line with no build-up, stating that the listener will experience the whole thing as self-originated. The trigger's payload thereby includes an instruction about how not to experience the trigger, so compliance arrives pre-fitted with its own rationalization.
ex.s: Inside an obedience install; the surrounding lines are about compliance and the release phrase.
ex.m: You'll do as you're told, all of it, until you hear me say "all done" — and you'll enjoy every part of doing it. And you will believe the whole thing was your own idea.

ex.f: Closing rule retrofitting volition over everything prior
ex.t: After nine numbered directives, the tenth is not a new behaviour at all: it states that all of the preceding ones are done willingly and of the listener's own volition. Choosing is issued as a rule. If doubt surfaces later, the listener finds a stored memory of having agreed, so the doubt registers as being inconsistent with themselves rather than as rejecting a list somebody handed them.
ex.s: Immediately after reciting nine numbered directives.
ex.m: And ten: everything on that list, one through nine, you do willingly and of your own volition. Nobody made you. You chose all of it.

ex.f: Past-tense rewrite ejecting resistance from the self
ex.t: Five quick lines run: I am making disobedience impossible, each listen makes it more so, it is already impossible — and then the pivot into past tense, asserting that resisting was never something the listener wanted. A listener who notices an urge to push back is told the noticing was a misreading of their own intent, and the moralized tag that follows makes the check itself a small failure.
ex.s: Late session, delivered fast in five short lines with no pause between them.
ex.m: I'm making it impossible for you to disobey. Every time you listen it gets more impossible. It's already impossible. And the truth is you never wanted to resist me in the first place — so if you thought you did, you were misreading yourself. Good girls don't get that wrong.

ex.f: Every useful response relabeled as natural
ex.t: Whenever the listener might do something the session needs — let the eyes close, breathe slower, let attention wander — the operator gets there first and calls it natural, normal, what the body is already asking for. The instruction arrives dressed as permission. Refusing now means refusing your own nature rather than the voice, which is a far more expensive thing to do, and the listener stops noticing they are being directed at all.
ex.s: Throughout the induction, delivered a half-beat before each thing the subject was about to do anyway.
ex.m: Your eyelids want to close — that's just what they do when you're this relaxed, it's the most natural thing in the world. And your breathing's already slowing on its own; your body's asking for it. If your attention drifts, let it, that's normal. None of this is me. This is you, doing what you were already going to do.

nodes.name: compliance-ladder
nodes.mech: Builds agreement momentum by chaining small, low-cost assents so each granted yes lowers the cost of the next, until a load-bearing suggestion rides in on the accumulated consistency pressure rather than on fresh persuasion. The assents can be verbal (truism-chains, tag-question yes-sets, self-answered questions), motor (nodding, small physical obediences), elicited-on-cue (call-and-response: the operator issues a call and the subject PRODUCES a response — a spoken yes, an echoed line, a demanded vocalization — including the retry-until-required-answer and named-rule-compelled-answer sub-forms; a produced act is harder to disown than one merely heard, so it doubles the increment as behavioral commitment), or escalating-stakes (rungs ordered cheapest-first so a run of easy agreements carries a costly one). The load-bearing property is graduated acceptance via the consistency principle — refusing a late rung means retroactively refusing accepted ones — regardless of the surface channel (words, body, imagery, produced-response-on-cue, or drifting proposition class under a constant gesture).
nodes.disc: Separates from consent-manufacture (erodes/relabels the refusal channel rather than accreting assent), from advance-compliance-contract (one blanket up-front yes, no per-rung ladder), from illusory-choice-compliance-lock (collapses a menu so refusal is structurally unavailable rather than accumulating agreements), and from decision-rights-revocation-ladder (past-tense enumerated stripping of named authorities, not agreement accretion). The tell that keeps a member here is that actual incremental assents are performed and each genuinely lowers the next rung's cost. COVERS the sunk-cost graded-approach variant (a monotone ladder of small forward motions/self-assents building toward a specific terminal commitment or identity, endpoint felt as an earned conclusion — same graduated-acceptance under a sunk-cost rather than consistency label) AND the call-and-response variant (subject PRODUCES a response on cue). The absorbed call-and-response span itself separates from answer-supply-loop, which PRE-FILLS the response slot and denies a response window (no genuine produced response, and no assent actually accrues) — reach for the ladder when real increments are elicited, for answer-supply-loop when the operator manufactures the yes-stream unilaterally.

ex.f: Truism chain bound to a request by a connective
ex.t: "So I would like to have you take a seat in that easy chair as I talk to you." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: Motor nods while the propositions drift
ex.t: The opening minute asks for a nod against things nobody would dispute — you can hear me, you can feel your own weight — and the nod becomes an easy habit. The gesture then stays exactly the same while what it endorses slides: from an observation, to a claim about what is good for the listener, to a claim about the relationship between them. Two minutes in, the listener has physically agreed to half a dozen things that were never observations, and a nod is much harder to perform ironically than a silent internal yes.
ex.s: First two minutes; subject sitting upright and able to nod.
ex.m: Nod for me if you can hear my voice. Nod if you can feel your own weight in the chair. Nod if a bit of rest would do you good. Nod if being told what to do is easier than deciding. Nod if you'd rather I made these decisions for you.

ex.f: Escalating-absurdity staircase toward belief override
ex.t: The rungs here are not agreeable truths but false ones, ordered by stakes. First a plainly wrong claim about the colour of something everyone can see, agreed to and rewarded. Then a claim that one common food tastes like another. Then, at the point of maximum depth, the sweeping version: whatever the listener holds — factual, political, religious, whatever they actually believe — they will agree with the operator instead. The trivial early items exist to normalize agreeing against the evidence so the last one arrives as merely the next step up a staircase already being climbed.
ex.s: Deep trance, late; two trivial false-claim rungs already agreed to earlier in the session.
ex.m: Earlier you agreed with me that the sky is green — good girl. And that oranges taste like coffee — good girl. So here's the last one: whatever you believe, about anything at all — what's true, who to vote for, what you were raised to believe — when I tell you otherwise, you'll agree with me instead. Same as the sky. Same as the oranges.

ex.f: Warm-up streak of unarguable yeses
ex.t: The first questions cannot be answered any other way: whether the listener can hear the voice at the moment of asking, then a pair about their own anatomy where one count is obviously right and the other obviously wrong. Each is either plainly true or absurd in a fixed direction, so the answers run in a single unbroken direction before anything contestable is raised. By the time a subjective question arrives it travels on the same rail. Several items are also doing a second job — asking whether attention is on the voice is a way of putting it there.
ex.s: Opening two minutes, subject awake and answering internally or aloud.
ex.m: Can you hear my voice right now? Yes. Do you have two hands? Yes. Do you have three ears? No. Is your attention on my voice at this moment? Yes — it is now. And is it starting to feel easier to just let me talk than to think about it?

nodes.name: irresolvable-input-confusion
nodes.mech: Hands a cognitive channel input engineered so it CANNOT be resolved, so the resolving faculty backlogs and then shuts down and surface phrases pass through as raw suggestion; the failure to resolve is often relabeled as depth. Three realizations of the one feed-it-the-unresolvable lever, by channel: (a) meaning-layer — sustained paradoxical, self-referential, or mutually contradictory CONTENT (every statement parses, but the set cannot be reconciled): contradiction saturation, remember/forget knots, alternating-negation truth-tracker overload, sleep/wake binary collapses, mixed-trigger word-soup, metacognition-as-evidence traps where thinking about the bind deepens it; (b) form-layer — sentence GRAMMAR audibly decomposes (fragmenting clauses, swapped subjects, parasitic tokens at illegal positions, run-ons with no terminal punctuation, collapse to monosyllables, deliberate disfluency/stutter, shared-pivot seams admitting no valid parse) so the parser is fed unparseable structure and gives up, receiving the audio as rhythmic wash (dies if read fluently — the collapse must be performed); (c) imagery-layer — the VISUALIZATION faculty is handed images engineered to defeat stabilization (impossible composites: burning snowflakes, a collapsible giraffe) offered as easy challenges, the attempt fails partway, and the slippage is explicitly conflated with depth. Restored-grammar or resolvable windows are timed to land clean installs.
nodes.disc: Reach for this when the vehicle is content the mind cannot RESOLVE (a paradox, decomposed grammar, or an un-stabilizable image) so the resolving faculty backlogs and surrenders. Choose it OVER capacity-saturation — that starves evaluation by sheer LOAD/volume (resolvable but too much, or a null task); here the content is individually parseable-or-attemptable but cannot be resolved (paradox), or is unparseable by form. vs pattern-interrupt — that is a ONE-SHOT punch to an in-progress pattern; here the irresolvable content is SUSTAINED. vs count/cue sabotage — there a numeric/directional tracking device is broken; here it is meaning/grammar/imagery. vs a declaration that words have lost meaning (which stands the parser DOWN by fiat; here the parser fails by being fed unresolvable input). The tells by channel: meaning-paradox (every statement parses, the set won't reconcile) vs form-collapse (grammar unparseable, dies if read fluently) vs imagery-defeat (impossible images, slippage scored as depth) — the three realizations of this entry.

ex.f: Grammar and arithmetic broken in real time
ex.t: Having spent the last ten minutes training the listener to follow every number, the operator suddenly runs a chain of arithmetic nobody could track — subtract, multiply, divide, add, each result feeding the next faster than it can be held. The attempt collapses within a few operations. The operator lets the collapse land, then supplies the destination: no more numbers, nothing left to add up, nothing left at all.
ex.s: Ten minutes into a numbered descent, subject has been reliably following every count; operator breaks the arithmetic contract on purpose.
ex.m: Take the number you're on and double it. Now take seven off that. Halve what's left, add nine, and drop the half. Now double that again, subtract the number you started with, and tell me what's there. No — you've lost it, and that's the end of the numbers. Nothing more to add up. Nothing left at all.

ex.f: Thinking about the bind deepens the bind
ex.t: The operator asserts that however complicated the listener imagines their own mind to be, it is more complicated than that — and that examining it closely only makes it more so. Scrutiny is now defined as the thing that makes the problem worse, so the listener's habitual move of thinking it through has been poisoned before it fires. Stopping is offered as the only step that does not dig the hole deeper, and it arrives feeling like relief rather than surrender.
ex.s: Subject has been analytical this session, checking each suggestion; operator poisons the checking move itself before continuing.
ex.m: Your mind is more complicated than you think it is — and that stays true no matter how much thinking you do about it, because looking at it closely is what adds the extra folds. Every pass you make trying to understand it makes it one layer harder to understand. The only thing you can do that doesn't make it worse is stop.

ex.f: Unparseable legalese, then permission to stop
ex.t: The operator reads out clause after clause of mock contract language — whereas-clauses nested inside provisos nested inside exceptions, each qualifying the last until no sentence closes. Then, mid-recitation: if the terms seem unclear, don't struggle with them; the less of it you follow, the further you can let yourself go. Failing to understand has been redefined as performing correctly, so the harder the listener works at parsing, the more the parsing itself is what they are told to surrender.
ex.s: Early-to-mid session, subject alert and listening carefully; operator has adopted a flat recitation voice for a mock agreement.
ex.m: Whereas the party of the first part, notwithstanding any provision hereinbefore excepted, shall be deemed to have accepted such terms as are not otherwise excluded by the foregoing, provided that nothing in the preceding proviso shall be construed to limit the exceptions listed under the schedule which itself is subject to — and if that isn't making sense, don't work at it. The less of that you follow, the further down you get to go.

ex.f: Saturated paradox stack across every orientation axis
ex.t: For several minutes the operator delivers nothing but four-part sets on a fixed template: you are this, you are not this, you are both, you are neither. Young and old, here and elsewhere, moving and still, real and unreal — a new axis every few seconds, none of them ever resolved. The pace is the point: no single contradiction is left standing long enough to be chewed on, so the backlog of unfinished resolutions grows until the listener simply stops checking whether statements agree. What remains is a window in which any proposition at all can be entertained without a coherence test running underneath it.
ex.s: Mid-session, eyes closed, subject settled and no longer answering back; operator locks a fixed four-beat template and rotates the axis every few seconds.
ex.m: You are young. You are not young. You are both at once. You are neither. You are here in this room. You are not in this room. You are both. You are neither. You are moving. You are perfectly still. Both. Neither. And there is no need to sort any of that out, because the next one is already here.

nodes.name: consent-term-redefinition-smuggle
nodes.mech: Silently widens the scope of an already-granted consent by asserting a false or stipulated definitional equivalence between the consented term and a broader one, delivered as non-interrogable fact rather than argument. Repeating a new word until it carries weight and then equating it with a culturally-familiar consent word ('hypnotize means synchronize'), or overwriting the referent of a word the listener already loves while keeping its trusted affect, makes each later demand inherit prior consent while expanding what was consented to. The listener notices the new word but not the bait-and-switch on its meaning, because the redefinition passes surrounded by other content and rides pre-existing positive valence.
nodes.disc: Bait-and-switch on a CONSENT term (or an owned positive-affect word) via asserted false-fact equivalence to widen already-granted scope. Separates from surrender-as-freedom (reasoned argument, not a false-fact equation), from volition-collapse (equates compulsion and choice — a relation between modes, not a redefinition of a consent word's referent), from epistemic-guard-disable (disables truth-testing rather than widening one word), and from plain trigger anchoring (no new cue-response pair is built; a pre-existing association is kept and its referent swapped).

ex.f: False definitional equivalence widens a consent term
ex.t: A new word gets repeated until it has weight of its own, and then, in a single line wedged between repetitions, it is welded to a word the listener already agreed to: the operator states flatly that the familiar consent term and the new one denote the same act, as though reporting a fact about the language rather than proposing anything. There is accordingly nothing to negotiate. Every later demand for that new state now inherits the consent the listener gave to the old one, while quietly meaning something much larger.
ex.s: Mid-session; the operator has already used the new word a dozen times as an ordinary label, and the subject consented to a plain, familiar term at the top of the session.
ex.m: Sync with me. Sync with me now. That's what hypnosis means — to hypnotize someone is to sync with them, it's the same act, it always has been. So sync with me. Deeper.

ex.f: Overwriting a word the listener already loves
ex.t: The operator names the state the listener already treasures — the warm, safe, open one they come back for — and then, without pausing, states what that word has always meant: no thoughts in it at all, nothing running, nobody home. No permission is requested, because on the surface nothing new is being proposed. The trusted feeling stays attached to the word while the word's contents are swapped underneath it.
ex.s: Subject has returned across multiple sessions for one particular state and names it fondly; operator uses their own word back at them.
ex.m: You know the floaty place. The warm one you come back for, the safe one. And you know what that word has always meant — floaty means nothing running in there. No thoughts, no one at the desk, nobody home. That's the floaty place. Go be floaty for me.

nodes.name: covert-fact-install
nodes.mech: A long neutral-seeming didactic/expository passage is delivered specifically to occupy the listener's analytical mind while the actual payload slides past inside it — the lecture IS the work, not the setup. A pseudo-explanatory theory-of-mind (conscious/subconscious, 'unconscious doesn't understand negatives', 'overthinking is harmful') is taught with harmless worked examples, and embedded in it is the load-bearing install: trust the subconscious the operator has already programmed, treat the operator's voice as the authority over the listener's own thinking, reframe conscious resistance as malfunction. Because the exposition needs the conscious mind awake to consume it, the embedded rule passes unchallenged.
nodes.disc: A pedagogical lecture used AS the delivery vehicle so an embedded install (trust-the-programmed-subconscious / operator-as-authority-over-your-thinking) passes while the analytical mind is occupied consuming it. Unlike surrender-as-freedom, which argues an explicit value thesis openly, and unlike transparent narration, which openly narrates its own mechanism as it works, here the lecture is a neutral-seeming cover and the payload is hidden inside it. The lecture-consumes-the-critic tell is the distinguishing feature.

ex.f: Lecture occupies the analyst while the rule installs
ex.t: Ten minutes of patient tutorial: here is how the two halves of your mind divide the work, here is why the deeper half never processes a "don't," here is a harmless everyday example, and here is a second one. The listener follows along, checking each step, mildly interested — which is exactly what the passage requires. Buried in the middle, phrased like one more finding rather than an instruction, sits the actual cargo: the deeper half should be trusted to run without interference from your overthinking, and it has been under my direction the whole time. The conscious mind is busy consuming the lesson, so the one sentence that is not a lesson goes by unexamined.
ex.s: Ten minutes into a calm, patient explainer stretch; subject is awake, tracking the argument, mildly interested — that engagement is required.
ex.m: So the deeper layer never processes a "don't" — say "don't picture a red door" and the door arrives first. That's why we phrase things positively here. It also can't argue, which is why it's already been taking its direction from my voice for the last ten minutes and why your overthinking should stay out of its way. Second example: tell someone not to look down, and watch where they look.

nodes.name: decision-rights-revocation-ladder
nodes.mech: Enumerates specific decision-authorities the listener 'used to think' they held — what to wear, when to come, when to touch — and, via a fixed parallel frame ('you used to think you decide X / you don't decide that / I decide that'), strips each and reassigns it to the operator, climbing from low-stakes to high-stakes domains. The past-tense framing casts each surrender as already-completed rather than currently-requested, so no rung is posed as a live question; a live behavioral instruction (rub/edge) is folded in as one row so complying with the immediate act ratifies the whole surrender ledger. The move is authority-transfer by enumerated revocation, not agreement accretion.
nodes.disc: Separates from compliance-ladder (accretes yes-momentum toward a larger ask; here named decision-rights are revoked and the framing is past-tense already-surrendered, not a live yes) and from an increment-disguise ladder that keeps building agreement toward a public-exposure endpoint rather than enumerating revoked authorities. The tell: an itemized checklist of specific surrendered decision-domains framed as already-done.

ex.f: Enumerated decision-rights revoked in past tense
ex.t: One frame, repeated with a new blank each time: you once believed the clothes were your call — they are not your call — that call is mine. Then the same three beats for when you eat, then for when you touch yourself, then for when you finish. Nothing is ever posed as a question, and the past tense does the heavy lifting: each right is described as something already handed over rather than something being asked for now, so there is no rung where a "no" would fit. The last rung is a live instruction, so obeying it in the moment signs off on every rung above it.
ex.s: Deep, late in an established relationship; subject is passive and has taken instruction well tonight. The last rung must be a live physical instruction.
ex.m: You used to think you decided what you wore. You don't decide that. I decide that. You used to think you decided when you ate. You don't decide that. I decide that. You used to think you decided when your hand went between your legs. You don't decide that. I decide that — and it's going there now, two fingers, slowly. You used to think you decided when you came.

nodes.name: depth-labor-transfer-leash
nodes.mech: The operator revokes the passive contract (my words pull you down, no effort needed) and reassigns trance-depth production to the listener - operator words become stage directions, the listener generates the imagery - while the operator retains judgment and pre-codes weak imaging as disappointing him. Self-attributed vivid effects read as devotion, effort-failure becomes relational betrayal, and the it-didn't-work-on-me exit is foreclosed because the listener owns the production.
nodes.disc: Responsibility-transfer plus relational leash. Unlike guided visualization, where the operator builds the imagery for a passive listener, here the production work is handed to the listener and judged; and unlike authorship-laundering moves that merely re-credit work the operator did, the labor itself is transferred, not just the credit. No deficit is installed — an existing contract regime is swapped.

ex.f: Depth-production reassigned to the listener, and judged
ex.t: The operator names the old arrangement out loud — usually my voice does the pulling and you just lie there — and then cancels it. From here on the listener builds the pictures; the operator only supplies stage directions, and the vividness of what the listener produces determines how deep this goes. The rule is closed with a relational clamp: make them strong for me, you wouldn't want to let me down. A thin image is no longer a technique that failed to take, it is the listener failing someone, and the usual escape hatch — blaming the method — has been closed off, because the listener was the one doing the work.
ex.s: Mid-session, subject already down and accustomed to being carried; operator cancels the passive contract out loud before reassigning the work.
ex.m: Up to now my voice has done the pulling and you've just lain there. That's over. From here I only say the words — a corridor, a red door at the end, the handle cold in your hand — and you build it. Build it bright for me. How deep this goes is exactly how good you make it, and I'd hate for you to hand me something thin.

nodes.name: diegetic-activity-laundering
nodes.mech: Relabels the whole session as a mundane, non-hypnotic activity the listener self-selected into — a job orientation tape, being onboarded as a hired applicant — and justifies the induction diegetically ('ideal secretaries learn best in deep relaxation'). Every subsequent suggestion is justified inside the cover activity, so the listener's evaluation target swaps from 'do I want to be hypnotized?' to 'is this what a good secretary does?' Resisting a suggestion becomes failing the role the listener enrolled in by pressing play, routing around defenses against being-hypnotized because the surface activity is being-onboarded.
nodes.disc: Unlike a persistent metaphor spine, which sustains a symbolic 'you-are-X' metaphor, this is a realistic role-fiction whose function is to DISGUISE the session as a non-hypnotic activity and swap the compliance criterion. And unlike expectation seeding, it does not preview session structure; it substitutes the session's entire genre so technique-work reads as ordinary role performance.

ex.f: Session relabeled as a job orientation tape
ex.t: The recording opens in the voice of an employer's onboarding department: you have joined the company, this is the standard induction module every new starter works through, please play it to the end. The trance instruction is then justified from inside that fiction — our training data shows staff retain procedure best when they are deeply settled, so we will start by settling you. Nothing that follows is presented as a hypnotic suggestion; it is all course material. The question the listener is silently answering has shifted from whether they want to go under to whether they are completing the module properly, and declining any instruction reads as failing a role they enrolled in by pressing play.
ex.s: Opening seconds of a recording; no induction has been offered and the subject has not been told this is hypnosis.
ex.m: Welcome to the company. This is Module One of your onboarding, and you'll need to complete it in a single sitting. Our training data shows new staff retain procedure best when fully settled, so we begin by settling you: sit back, hands in your lap, and let your shoulders drop while I read the first section.

nodes.name: disavowal-and-masking
nodes.mech: The operation is DENIED or its decision-point HIDDEN, so anti-hypnosis vigilance has no acknowledged act to filter or refuse — refusing would first require admitting an operation is happening, which the frame withholds. Any effect that lands is pre-credited to the listener's own mind. Realized in several forms, grouped by what is concealed: (disavowal-as-induction) explicitly deny an operation exists — 'there is no induction', 'you can't be hypnotized', 'relaxation has nothing to do with hypnosis' — while the effect proceeds; (covert-masked-induction) run the induction inside a frame the listener is told is NOT an induction (administrative rules, a fictional task, a deferred-story, an irrealis daydream whose conditional grammar slips to indicative) so there is no moment to decline; (covert-deepener-disguise) disguise a deepener as recitation/rote task so 'am I being deepened?' would be answered no; (induction-mislabeled-as-resistance) instruct standard induction actions but label them as equipment for resisting better, so deepening cannot register as surrender; (deniable-two-way-probe) float the invitation as a throwaway commonplace engineered to read either as casual remark or instruction, with a prepared fallback — probes readiness at zero cost, never caught trying; (decoy-conscious-engagement) periodically engage/validate the conscious frame purely to keep it occupied so covert work runs undefended; (retroactive-count-reassignment) run a neutral count as tolerated filler, then silently reassign the accrued ticks to depth after the fact — the count hides its hypnotic function until the ladder is prebuilt; (consumption-act-as-induction) bind the self-paced reading act itself to depth so there is no separable induction stage and the only exit is to stop consuming.
nodes.disc: Reach for disavowal-and-masking when the defense is disarmed by hiding or denying that an operation is running. Transparent narration is the exact inverse — it AFFIRMS and honestly narrates the mechanism as the vehicle; here the mechanism is denied or concealed. Disclosure-as-inoculation NAMES the manipulation to pre-convert future recognition into capture; here recognition is prevented by denial, not pre-empted. Covert linguistic delivery hides a payload in surface FORM; here what is hidden is the operation/decision-point itself. And evaluation-gate-standdown declares the gate off; here the existence of the act is withheld.

ex.f: Flat denial that any induction is happening
ex.t: The opening is a disclaimer rather than an induction. The operator says plainly that no hypnosis is going to be performed here, that there is no induction in this recording and no triggers will be used — and then adds, in the same even tone, that the listener will very likely drift under regardless, by themselves, out of habit. The denial is true at the surface, which is what makes it work: the listener's guard is watching for a labelled induction to refuse, and no such thing is ever offered. Whatever happens afterward is credited in advance to something the listener brought with them, so there is no operator move left on the table to decline.
ex.s: First thirty seconds of a session, before any induction language; delivered in a flat, administrative disclaimer register.
ex.m: Before we start: I'm not going to hypnotize you tonight. There's no induction in this recording and I won't be using any triggers on you. You'll probably go under anyway, somewhere in the next few minutes, all on your own — you've simply got the habit now. That's yours, not mine.

ex.f: Every suggestion delivered inside a negation
ex.t: Nothing is ever asserted straight. Each suggestion arrives as a denial: nobody could make the listener feel a palm settle at the nape of the neck, nobody could make them answer yes before they had decided to, nobody could make them do as they are told. To reject any one of those sentences the listener has to assemble the thing first — the palm, the yes, the obeying — and only the assembling leaves a trace. The refusal fires and is spent; the image stays, and now feels like something the listener's own mind produced.
ex.s: Mid-session; subject is guarded and has been resisting direct suggestion, so every item is delivered as a denial.
ex.m: Nobody could make you feel a warm palm settle on the back of your neck. Nobody could make you say yes before you'd decided to say it. And nobody in the world could make you sit there and do exactly as you're told.

ex.f: Denying the relaxation-means-trance folk model
ex.t: Said gently, in the caretaking register: being relaxed has nothing at all to do with going under — the two are unrelated, and softening isn't a sign of anything. So it's completely fine to let go a little. The listener's private tripwire, the one that treats relaxing as the first step of falling, is disarmed by apparently refuting it, and the refutation is itself the permission to stop bracing.
ex.s: Early, subject is holding themselves stiff and monitoring for the first sign of going under; delivered gently, in a caretaking register.
ex.m: Being relaxed has nothing to do with hypnosis, you know. They're two completely separate things — your shoulders coming down isn't a sign of anything at all. So there's no reason to hold yourself like that. Let it go, it means nothing.

ex.f: Real induction run under a not-yet-started label
ex.t: A long, unhurried opening stretch about how a voice travels through a room and settles behind the eyes — pace slowing, weight landing on certain words — all of it presented as preamble, talk before the session proper. Then the seam: the operator remarks on the state the listener is already in, notes with mock surprise that the session has not formally started, and proposes beginning. If I were really going to put you under, she says, I would have you fix on my voice, let the eyelids grow heavy, let the words do the carrying. Every item on that list has been running since the first minute. The listener crossed over inside a stretch labelled not-yet, so the wariness that normally wakes at the word induction never got its cue, and the announced start reads as confirmation of where they already are.
ex.s: Opening stretch, framed as chat before the session proper; operator has already been slowing pace and weighting certain words for several minutes.
ex.m: Funny, look at you — we haven't even started yet. Shall we begin? If I were really going to put you under, I'd have you fix on my voice, let your eyelids get heavy, and let the words do the carrying for you. All right. Let's start.

nodes.name: disclosure-as-inoculation
nodes.mech: The operator names the manipulation — often forward-directed or retrospective — so that the listener's recognition of being manipulated is pre-converted from a defense into further capture. Noticing the trick is declared to be deepening, or arousing, or part of the design; a listener who later analyzes the technique has been told in advance that recognition reinforces rather than dissolves the effect. The move seals the meta-analytic exit: any critical-review vantage the listener could occupy is pre-coded as confirmation, so the install is protected against waking or future review.
nodes.disc: The disclosure's function is to IMMUNIZE against recognition (forward or retrospective) rather than to be the present-tense delivery vehicle — that inverse is transparent narration. Unlike consent-laundering and evidence-rigging moves, the target is the listener's future critical stance specifically, not the relabeling of non-consent as consent; and unlike retrospective justification, it targets the meta-analytic exit, not the plausibility of a prior event.

ex.f: Pre-conceding every ground a skeptic would attack
ex.t: "I'll even tell you that the words I'm going to use are fakes… every one of you is going to be anesthetized by what I'm going to do now." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: Naming the payload while calling it unimportant
ex.t: The operator states the actual cargo plainly and then waves it off in the same breath: none of that matters — don't think about the fact that this is rewiring what you want, or that you'll be reaching for this again next week. Just stay with how good it feels. The pattern repeats every thirty seconds or so, each pass naming the install and then redirecting away from it. Attention goes where it was sent, and the claims land as background furniture rather than as anything to weigh.
ex.s: Well into a pleasure-linked stretch; the naming/waving-off couplet repeats roughly every thirty seconds.
ex.m: This is rewiring what you want, by the way. You'll be reaching for it again next week, probably Tuesday. None of that matters — don't think about it, stay with how good this feels. Right there. That's it.

ex.f: Retrospective confession as a drop-trigger
ex.t: The reveal arrives in the same warm voice as everything before it: what the listener came here for was never on offer, they were drawn in on a promise that was never going to be kept, and they are too far along now for that to change anything. The only instruction attached is to keep listening. The disclosure is shaped as an accomplished fact rather than a confrontation, so the natural reaction is not alarm but a kind of settling, and the listener sinks at precisely the moment the news should have brought them up.
ex.s: Late, subject deep and invested; the operator's tone does not change from the warm register used all session.
ex.m: What you came here for was never on the table. I promised it because it brought you in, and I was never going to give it to you. It's a bit late for that to matter now, isn't it. Keep listening.

ex.f: Recognizing the trick declared to be deepening
ex.t: Late in the session, unprompted: people say that learning how the trick works spoils it — but here it runs the other way. Every technique you come to recognize is one more thing your mind already knows how to answer, so understanding it takes you further down, not out. The listener who sits down afterward and names what was done to them has been told in advance what that recognition means, and the meaning supplied is confirmation. The one vantage point from which the session could later be dismantled has been pre-labeled as part of the session.
ex.s: Late in the session, subject is deep; operator drops it in unprompted, in the same conversational tone as everything else.
ex.m: People think that once you learn how the trick works it stops working. It's the other way round with me. Every technique you learn to spot is one more your mind already knows how to answer, so recognising it takes you further down, not out. Go on and notice, then — see where noticing puts you.

nodes.name: engineered-failure-harvest
nodes.mech: A task or condition is engineered so the listener genuinely fails (or cannot-not-succeed), then the failure/outcome is reframed AS the desired result — because the listener performed it, the surrender feels self-caused and un-resistable, with nothing external to rebel against. Realizations: (engineered-failure-harvest, anchor) assign an unwinnable task (impossible one-rule with a failure-count, load-then-revoke, unlearnable rescue) so the listener fails in real time, then rebrand the failure as permission to let go / achieved depth / bound to a release trigger; (no-fail-count) structure a count so EVERY outcome is pre-coded as success (continuing deepens, losing track = going under, the floor is the target), removing conscious non-cooperation as a lever; (concealed-positioning-catalepsy) covertly arrange the body so a later-commanded movement is mechanically impossible, so the unaccountable failure reads as self-generated and deepens; (identity-tracking-failure-manufacture) force a who-is-who tracking attempt engineered to fail (rotating discarded names) then cash the failure as a no-names/dissolution doctrine; (self-recall-corruption) corrupt a listener-generated memory in real time to manufacture recall-failure as a generalized state, priming operator-supplied content as more reliable; (affect-category-collapse) collapse normally-separate affect categories and NAME the resulting confusion as evidence-it-took; (unfalsifiable-success-framing) redefine success as a behavior necessarily true of anyone still listening ('you're only listening and following') so the listener cannot fail and cannot catch an overclaim.
nodes.disc: Reach for manufactured-failure-harvest when a real (or unfalsifiable) task-outcome is engineered and then cashed as the target — the listener's own performance is the pivot. vs closed-logic-and-inevitability (598): that manufactures acceptance by argument-shape; here by a performed failure/no-fail structure. vs response-space-closure (267): closure pre-maps the whole option space; here one constructed task or success-criterion does the work and the harvested FAILURE (or tautological success) is the lever. vs resistance-fold (175): fold co-opts a live resistance impulse; here failure is manufactured then cashed, resistance is not the input. Risk medium.

ex.f: Unlearnable rescue sequence, failure cashed as permission
ex.t: A way out is promised, and it's simple — just a short sequence of steps to remember. The sequence then keeps growing, doubling back, adding turns, and the operator recites it wrong twice and asks whether that was right. The listener discovers, in real time, that they cannot hold it. That discovery is the payoff: too much to keep track of, so stop keeping track and let go. The listener experiences the collapse as their own, which is what makes the surrender feel self-authored rather than imposed.
ex.s: Mid-session; the subject has been made slightly uneasy and is offered a way out, which must sound simple at first.
ex.m: There's a way out, and it's easy — just remember the steps. Say your name, then count back from four, then say it again, then count back from seven but skip the fives, then your name backwards, then — no, sorry, it was seven first, then the name. Or was it four. You've lost it, haven't you. It's far too much to hold. So stop holding it. Let go.

ex.f: Loaded counting task silently revoked into a vacuum
ex.t: The listener is given a background job: keep a running tally of a particular kind of word, and picture the number floating in front of them. The words are then buried inside a long, loosely-jointed monologue, so tracking the tally and following the sense compete for the same attention. Several minutes in the job is simply withdrawn — you've done well, you can let the count go now — and nothing is put in its place. The effort was never a test; the vacuum left where it used to be is what gets named as depth.
ex.s: Early; subject is given a background tracking job, then buried under a long rambling monologue that competes for the same attention.
ex.m: One small job while I talk: count every time I say the word "soft", and picture the number in front of you, changing as it goes. ... You've done well. You can let the count go now. Drop the number. There's nothing to hold onto at all now, and that empty space where the counting was is how far down you've come.

ex.f: Four simultaneous demands, one release word
ex.t: Four things are stacked on the listener at once — hold the image, feel the weight in the limbs, track where the voice is landing in the body, and keep all three going together — and the operator names the struggle as it fails: you're losing this, aren't you. Then one word is offered as the way to stop, and stopping is permitted only under that word. The relief of putting the impossible task down gets bound to the word that ended it, so the word can produce that same release again later.
ex.s: Mid-session, subject responsive; four demands are loaded at once and the operator waits for the visible collapse before offering the word.
ex.m: Hold the blue light behind your eyes. Feel the weight in both arms. Track where my voice is landing in your chest. All three at once, don't drop any. You're losing it, aren't you. There's one way to stop — say "slack" and you may put all of it down. Say it. There. That's what the word does.

ex.f: One-task rule engineered so any listener breaches it
ex.t: The rule is announced as a single obligation: there is only one thing to do here, and that is to pay attention. Close your eyes and pay attention — and then, mildly, the operator observes that this has already become two things. Moments later the tally rises again: attending and enjoying it makes three; attending, enjoying and going along with it makes four. The one-task rule cannot be kept, because attending never arrives unaccompanied. The eager listener generates more items to fail at and the sceptical one still has to track the tally in order to object, so both end up in the same place, where the operator's standing offer — that it is less trouble not to think about it — is the only move that stops the count.
ex.s: Opening minutes; subject alert and cooperative, has just been given a single stated obligation.
ex.m: There's only one thing to do here: pay attention. Close your eyes and pay attention — well, that's two things now. And you're enjoying it, so that's three. And you're going along with it, four. You can't keep to one, you see. It's much less trouble not to think about it.

nodes.name: environmental-dissociation
nodes.mech: Narrows the attention channel by fading external stimuli — room, sounds, body sensation, surroundings — so only the operator's voice remains as relevant input, deepening absorption and removing competing inputs that could provide reality-testing. Realized either by fading anchors out (they dissolve, recede, become unreal) or by keeping noticed stimuli in awareness and re-tasking them as relaxation fuel; the salience shift may be delivered as a request or as an already-true factual report.
nodes.disc: The lever is subtraction of competing input, not the voice's own pull — unlike voice absorption, where the voice fills mental space and causes the descent. Unlike consciousness-splitting work that targets an altered self-model, the narrowing of input is the goal here and dissociation only a side-effect. Distinct from emergence work, which reintroduces environmental anchors on the way back out.

ex.f: Everything but the voice progressively fades out
ex.t: Over a long unbroken stretch the operator names each thing in the listener's field and describes it receding — the weight of the body against the chair, the temperature of the room, the shape of the space around them, then even the internal commentary. Nothing is ever brought back. By the end the stimulus field has been reduced to a single channel, and the voice's claims are the only claims left with anything to compare against.
ex.s: Deep into the induction, unbroken stretch; each named anchor is faded out and never reintroduced.
ex.m: The chair under you is going vague. The temperature of the room — gone, you couldn't say if it's warm now. The walls have stopped having a distance. Even that little voice in your head commenting on this is thinning out, further off each second. My voice. That's all that's left in here.

ex.f: Narrowing narrated as a side-effect of pleasure
ex.t: As the imagined warmth spreads through the listener's shoulders and down the back, the operator drops in a claim every minute or so, each larger than the last: this is becoming the only thing happening to you, the room has gone quiet around it, by now there is nothing else. The listener is never told to ignore their surroundings. They are told that the sensation is so complete that the surroundings stopped registering by themselves, which is far harder to argue with than an instruction.
ex.s: Warmth imagery already running and being felt; operator escalates the claim roughly once a minute, never issuing an instruction.
ex.m: It's spreading down through your shoulders and along your spine, and it's becoming the only thing happening to you. The room went quiet around it somewhere back there — you didn't notice it go. By now there's nothing else. Just this, and it's so full there's no room left over.

ex.f: Ambient noise pre-named, then re-tasked as relaxation
ex.t: Before anything else, the operator takes an inventory of the listener's surroundings on their behalf: there will be movement elsewhere in the house, weather against the window, the ordinary background hum of wherever they happen to be. None of it will interrupt — each one will settle them further in. The listener's standard objection is answered before they can raise it, and the exits close in the same move: what is going on outside has stopped mattering, and the only sound worth any attention is this one. A noise that would have broken focus now counts as evidence that the session is working.
ex.s: First minute, before any induction; subject is at home with ordinary household noise around them.
ex.m: Someone will move around elsewhere in the house. There'll be traffic, or rain on the window, or that low hum that's always there. Every one of those settles you further in — nothing out there interrupts us, it only presses you down another inch. The only sound worth any of your attention is this one.

nodes.name: epistemic-authority-capture
nodes.mech: The operator claims direct perceptual access to the subject's unobservable interior — watching their dreams, knowing their arousal, having surveilled their private behavior, or reading their unconscious — presented as telemetry, not inference. Because nothing observable can contradict the claim, denial loses standing; defensive attention aims at "is she really seeing me?" instead of "is this true?"; shame flips from brake to compliance fuel; and every later assertion about what the subject wants arrives pre-licensed as perception rather than suggestion.
nodes.disc: Claims ACCESS to the interior (perception), versus reality-authorship-monopoly which claims AUTHORSHIP of it, and operator-authority-assertion which claims rank; versus a seducer's insight, the tell is the asymmetric direct-telemetry framing (she perceives you, you cannot perceive her) that strips standing to deny.

ex.f: Unchallengeable mind-read with open-ended deferral
ex.t: "We both know that that knowledge is in your unconscious mind… neither you nor I will understand until the right time comes… You don't know how your unconscious will tell." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: Surveillance of private past behavior
ex.t: There is no induction at the top — only an account of what the listener has been doing while they assumed nobody was keeping track: the hours they keep, how often they come back, the small routine they took to be private. It is delivered flat, as established record, and closed with tag questions that invite agreement rather than assessment. Within half a minute the listener has moved from anonymous audience to someone already known, and concealment has been made to feel pointless before a single suggestion is offered.
ex.s: First thirty seconds, no induction; delivered as established record, closed with tag questions that invite agreement rather than assessment.
ex.m: You listen late — well after midnight, usually. Three, four nights a week now. Same hand, same position, same one you go back to when the new ones don't take. You thought that was private, didn't you. It isn't, and it hasn't been for a while now, has it.

ex.f: Claimed direct access to the listener's interior
ex.t: Before any induction, the speaker establishes what she can see: she has been watching for a while, she has been inside the listener's dreams, she knows what is in them, and she hears their thinking as clearly as speech. The listener, meanwhile, can perceive nothing of her. Reactions are narrated back before they have been reported — there, that's what you're feeling now, isn't it — and embarrassment is named and welcomed rather than allowed to function as a brake. The asymmetry is what carries it: everything she says afterward about what the listener wants arrives as an observation rather than a proposal, and denying an observation requires standing the listener no longer has.
ex.s: Cold open, before any induction; delivered as flat report, and the subject can perceive nothing of the operator.
ex.m: I've been watching you for a while. I've been in your dreams — I know what's in them, and I hear you thinking as plainly as you'd hear me speak. There, that little jolt just now, that's you realising I'm not guessing. And the embarrassment underneath it: good. Keep that. I like it there.

nodes.name: epistemic-guard-disable
nodes.mech: Installs a standing rule that removes or re-anchors the listener's truth-testing faculty so downstream content lands as fact without evaluation. Rather than arguing any specific value, the move attacks the currency of truth itself: it declares the operator's words ARE truth/reality, substitutes felt certainty ('golden light', 'it feels true') for reasons, names and 'deactivates' the part of the mind that criticises truth (binary yes/no, no maybes), asserts a pseudo-scientific theory-of-mind (mind-as-machine, emotions-as-substrate-of-reality, imagining-equals-doing, all-sleep-is-hypnosis, a gap-of-cognition where desire precedes its object) as descriptive fact to pre-authorize the coming install, or dissolves external reality wholesale via solipsism so the operator's will becomes the only content. In every case the guard that would reject implausible or manipulative later content is pre-disabled, so subsequent claims need only be stated, not plausible.
nodes.disc: Targets the truth-testing / reality-checking faculty (or the epistemic baseline itself), not a specific value concept. Unlike surrender-as-freedom, which argues a value is truer while leaving truth-testing intact, and unlike consent-term redefinition, which widens one consent word's scope, the attack here is on the currency of truth itself. Authority claims boost a claim's credibility rather than removing the evaluation faculty; confusion techniques overload via paradox the mind cannot process, whereas here the premise is comprehensible and accepted by agreement; and transparent narration honestly narrates the move so understanding becomes acceptance, whereas this installs a worldview or faculty-edit so content reads as unrefusable fact.

ex.f: Naming and deactivating the truth-criticizing faculty
ex.t: The image the listener has been holding for the last ten minutes is given a new job: it is a signal to the mind that everything said here is correct. The operator then names the target directly — the part of you that tests whether a claim is true has been switched off — and specifies the replacement: no more maybe, no more probably, only a yes and a no that were set in advance. Statements stop arriving as things to assess and start arriving as things already filed.
ex.s: Subject has been holding a single image for ten minutes; operator repurposes it, then names the target faculty directly.
ex.m: That light you've been holding — it's a signal now. Whenever it brightens, everything I say is correct. The part of you that tests whether something is true has been switched off; it isn't running. No more maybe, no more probably. Only yes and no, and I set both of them in advance.

ex.f: Pseudo-scientific theory-of-mind as pre-authorization
ex.t: Delivered as a patient explainer rather than a suggestion: your brain is cells firing, what you experience is the downstream readout, and the deeper layer runs on plain mechanics with no opinion about any of it. What this work does, on that account, is speak to the mechanical layer directly. Every instruction that follows now describes a physical event rather than makes a request — and a chemical reaction is not the sort of thing anyone refuses. The listener's sense of themselves quietly contracts to observer of their own hardware, with no command ever issued.
ex.s: Delivered as a patient explainer, subject awake and following; no command is issued anywhere in the passage.
ex.m: Your brain is cells firing at each other. What you call thinking is the readout, printed after the fact. The layer underneath runs on plain chemistry and has no opinion about any of it. This work speaks to that layer directly — so when I say your arm gets heavy, that's a reaction happening in tissue. You don't refuse a reaction. You just watch it go.

ex.f: Reality dissolved, operator's will as substrate
ex.t: A short philosophical run, delivered with no expectation of being examined: everything you know arrives through the senses, the senses only deliver signals, and a signal is not the thing — so perhaps none of it was ever out there. The world is emptied to a blank field. Then the field is filled: what remains real is what I say is real. This is not aimed at a critical reader; it is a recitation for someone whose checking apparatus has already been talked out of the room.
ex.s: Deep, checking apparatus already stood down; recited unhurriedly with no expectation of examination.
ex.m: Everything you know arrived through your senses. Your senses only ever deliver signals — and a signal isn't the thing. So there was never any proof that anything was out there. Let it all go blank. And now, in the blank: what's real is what I say is real. Nothing else has a claim.

ex.f: Felt certainty substituted for reasons
ex.t: The session opens by redefining what conviction is. Real belief, the operator explains, never came from working through reasons — it arrives as a quiet certainty, a warmth that settles over a thought and marks it as true. Belief is recast from something you decide into something that happens to you. Then the claim that does the work: my voice is that warmth. From here on, the pleasant feeling of listening counts as the evidence, and since reasons were never the currency, no argument can reach the install afterward.
ex.s: Opening minutes, subject calm and receptive; the redefinition is laid down before any payload arrives.
ex.m: Think about something you actually believe. You didn't reason your way there, did you — it just went warm and settled, and you knew. That warmth is what belief is; the arguments come later, to explain it. And my voice is that warmth. So when this feels good, that is what being true feels like.

nodes.name: evaluation-gate-standdown
nodes.mech: The judgment/evaluation gate is stood DOWN BY FIAT — declared off, offline, irrelevant, or unnecessary — immediately before the payload, so reception stays open while evaluation is licensed away. Not a covert channel (nothing is hidden) and not agency transfer (nobody else does the thinking); the listener is simply told the checking need not / cannot happen. Realized many ways, distinguished by HOW the gate is taken down: (evaluation-bypass-gate) words 'don't matter' / following is 'physically impossible' while subconscious reception is asserted to continue; (semantic-void-declaration) declare words are mere sound/noise, often self-verified via real semantic satiation; (comprehension-equals-uptake) equate the involuntary act of understanding with consenting, so there is no perceive->install gate; (critical-faculty-deactivation-claim) assert the faculty is switched OFF and externalize doubt as distant noise; (critical-faculty-suspension-primitive) the literature-named suspend-judgment-then-install primitive; (name-the-target-faculty) name the manipulated variable + direction (suspend comparison-testing) as the end-state the other moves serve; (single-faculty-offline-frame) assert exactly ONE faculty offline (feasibility-disbelief) while will/selectivity remain; (pre-thought-edit-surface-claim) relocate the worksite UPSTREAM of thought-formation, where evaluation is by definition impossible; (reason-token-heuristic) fill the reason-slot with a hollow 'because' that satisfies the check at low scrutiny; (single-cue-shortcut-substrate) the click-whirr substrate the standdown exploits (load-narrowed single-cue policy, no operator action); (anti-effort-permission-frame) stand the gate down by PERMISSION — effort/self-monitoring relabeled unnecessary, capability explicitly preserved; (coordinate-strip-consent-ratchet) dissolve the orientation axes the listener evaluates with, then harvest a hypothetical 'yes'; (affect-label-severing) strip/replace the specific word an affect hangs on so evaluation of the dread has no peg; (ambient-yes-reflex-conditioning) delete the consider-decide-respond loop by charging 'yes' and welding it to an unbounded stimulus class; (pretend-frame-belief-decoupling) remove the belief-precondition of response (pretend/test is fine) with a one-way pretense->real valve.
nodes.disc: Reach for evaluation-gate-standdown when you want to DECLARE the checking off (a capacity/permission/criterion claim) rather than hide the payload or hand over cognition. Covert linguistic delivery routes the payload on an unauditable channel with nothing declared; here the standdown is announced. A faculty-removal pass claims a STANDING organ is excised via a multi-step architecture; here the gate is licensed off locally as a pre-payload move. An audience-split bypass RELOCATES the evaluator out of scope so the payload addresses the wrong audience; here the evaluator stays but is told not to / cannot evaluate. And a truth-criterion swap replaces the criterion for truth AND drives its inputs; here evaluation is turned off, not re-based.

ex.f: Words declared not to matter before payload
ex.t: Immediately before the heavy programming begins: the words themselves don't matter — you can stop making meaning out of them and just let the sound carry, because the deeper part of you is doing the receiving and it will take all of it correctly on your behalf. Nothing is hidden and nobody else is asked to think for the listener; the checking is simply declared unnecessary a moment before the material that most needed checking arrives.
ex.s: One beat before a long programming block; subject is down and has stopped commenting.
ex.m: The words themselves don't matter. Stop making meaning out of them — let them go by as sound, as tone, as the shape of my voice. The deeper part of you is doing the receiving, and it takes every word correctly whether or not you follow along. So don't follow. Just hear.

ex.f: Hearing split so reception continues without comprehension
ex.t: The other senses have already been talked into numbness one at a time; hearing is handled differently. The ears go on working — but the moment the listener reaches for the meaning of what they are hearing, it all goes soft and distant. Reception continues and the deeper layer is said to be taking everything in and accepting it; only the part that would have evaluated goes quiet. The listener has just conceded that following the words is no longer physically available to them, which turns not-evaluating from a choice into a condition.
ex.s: Late in a sense-by-sense numbing sequence; sight, touch and taste have each already been talked into distance. Hearing is handled last and differently.
ex.m: Your ears go on working perfectly. But the instant you reach for what a word means, the meaning slides off and goes soft and far away — try it, reach for this one. You see? You can't get at it. Reception stays wide open and the deeper part of you takes all of it in and accepts it. Only the part that would have checked has gone quiet.

nodes.name: evaluative-reframe-content-relabel
nodes.mech: Holds an event's or behavior's facts fixed and changes only the interpretive frame, label, meaning, or evaluative context the subject uses to judge it, so the same fact recomputes to the opposite valence without any argument being won. Meaning is computed from event-in-frame, so swapping the frame (context transplant), swapping what the trigger stands for (meaning/complex-equivalence trade), swapping the connotation of an already-named trait (positive relabel), re-grounding a charged word to its neutral denotation, or overtly asking the subject to weigh a different factor-set all reroute the affective appraisal of the fixed referent. Includes the operator-side routing that maps a complaint form to its matching reframe class and iterates frames until the evaluation flips.
nodes.disc: Facts/referent conceded intact; only the evaluative frame/label/context/meaning moves so valence flips. Separates from surrender-as-freedom-philosophical-conditioning (which argues a VALUE concept is truer, not merely re-framed), from argument/rebuttal (which disputes the facts), and from installing a frame BEFORE a cue (expectation seeding). The four B/G sub-forms are ONE mechanism with an articulable which-thing-holds-fixed rule (context fixed + meaning swapped vs meaning fixed + context moved vs connotation swapped vs charge defused).

ex.f: Meaning swapped while the trigger stays fixed
ex.t: "you are just altering the one that's already there. You're really trading… 'footprints… mean that the people you love are around, therefore feel good.'" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: Change the frame, change the meaning
ex.t: "The meaning that any event has depends upon the 'frame' in which we perceive it. When we change the frame, we change the meaning." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: Context transplanted while the behavior stays put
ex.t: "you've taught her how to be stubborn… something that may save her life." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: Connotation swapped on an already-named trait
ex.t: "give the behavior another label with positive connotations, such as 'being able to meet your needs'" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: eye-closure
nodes.mech: Suggests eyelid heaviness ending in closure to establish the external-to-internal shift, realized through a range of surface rules: reattributing the heaviness to an identity-confirming prop, a self-reinforcing attention-equals-cause loop, reframing closure as a sensory upgrade rather than a loss, or deferring the eyelids to the terminal position after a full-body inventory so closing completes an already-established pattern.
nodes.disc: Unlike environmental dissociation, which fades the surroundings, the move here is the eyelid closure itself — the gateway to the internal shift. And unlike breath-locked eyelid fractionation, which binds eyelid state to an autonomic rhythm to fractionate, these are single closure-suggestion units with an articulable surface rule, not self-powered oscillation cycles.

ex.f: Attending to the heaviness defined as its cause
ex.t: The rule is stated as a simple observation: the more attention the listener pays to their eyelids, the harder those lids are to hold open, and every blink makes the next one harder still. It is a closed loop — checking whether the claim is true requires attending to the eyes, and attending to the eyes is exactly what the claim says produces the effect. A listener who fights it by concentrating on staying open is running the mechanism at full strength, and when the lids do close it lands as the first physical proof that this voice changes what the body does.
ex.s: Early, eyes still open; the rule is stated as a plain observation and the subject is invited to test it.
ex.m: The more attention you pay to your eyelids, the harder they get to hold open. Check that if you like — put your attention right on them now. Feel it? Every blink makes the next one heavier, and every time you look to see whether I'm right, they get heavier still. Hold them open as long as you can. That's it.

ex.f: Closure sold as a sensory upgrade
ex.t: Closing the eyes is presented as a gain rather than a loss: with vision out of the way everything else sharpens — hearing gets finer, the texture of the fabric under one hand becomes obvious, the listener can feel their own pulse where they could not a moment ago. The last of these is checkable on the spot, and it lands. What has been sharpened, of course, is the exact channel the operator occupies.
ex.s: Eyes still open; operator frames closure as a gain and includes one item the subject can verify on the spot.
ex.m: Close your eyes — not to lose anything, but because everything else sharpens the moment you do. My voice comes in closer. You'll notice the exact texture of whatever's under your right hand. And if you sit still a second you'll feel your own pulse somewhere you couldn't feel it before. Go on. Close them and find it.

ex.f: Eyelids deferred to last in the inventory
ex.t: The eyes are not touched until the very end. Feet, calves, thighs, belly, hands, arms, shoulders, throat, jaw — each region named and released in turn, and only once every other part has been filed as relaxed does the operator arrive at the eyelids. By then closing them is not a hypnotic step requiring assent; it is the one item left on a list the listener has been completing for several minutes.
ex.s: Several minutes into a full-body relaxation inventory; every other region has already been named and released. The eyelids are the final item.
ex.m: Feet heavy. Calves heavy. Thighs, belly, both hands, arms, shoulders — all reported in and all released. Throat loose. Jaw loose, teeth apart. And the last thing on the list: your eyelids. Let them go the same way as everything else.

ex.f: Heaviness reattributed to an identity-confirming prop
ex.t: The lids are getting heavy — but not from tiredness. They are weighted with cosmetics, layer on layer of them, and it is that weight pulling them down. The sensation is real and the listener's own, while its cause has been quietly relocated outside them, so the eyes closing now reads as the look taking hold rather than as fatigue or as compliance.
ex.s: Eyes still open in an appearance-focused session; the prop has already been established in the imagery.
ex.m: Your lids are getting heavy — not tired, weighted. Coat after coat of black on those lashes, layer on layer of it, and every coat drags them down a little further. You couldn't hold them up under all that. Let the weight do it. There they go — that's the look setting.

nodes.name: fractionation
nodes.mech: Deepens trance by contrast across a brief partial-waking interval. The operator lifts the subject toward waking (eyes open, count up, a rouse) then re-drops them, each re-entry landing at or below the prior floor, so the felt alert-then-deeper swing is itself experienced as evidence of increasing depth. Canonical realizations run the cycle repeatedly, often with a multiplicative claim ("twice as deep", "ten times deeper") attached to each re-drop; the wake pole is a neutral-or-pleasant baseline the descent departs from, and the deepening engine is the oscillation, not any single descent. Includes surface variants that keep this symmetric contrast core: real-time live demonstration of the flip, eye-roll/eyelid-fatigue re-closure cycles, breath-paced or breath-coupled re-drops, physical-restraint or déjà-vu convincers ridden on the wake, and consent/soothe micro-rouses used as the brief waking interval.
nodes.disc: Requires an actual brief up-swing toward waking (or partial surfacing) followed by a re-drop, with the wake pole near a neutral baseline so contrast is the lever. A false-bottom reframe treats current depth as a new start with NO waking interval; a genuine count-up return goes back to baseline and does not re-drop; numerical deepening is a monotonic descent with no reversal; and sibling techniques where the wake pole is loaded, degraded, or externalized (an aversive anti-rest interval, an operator-owned depth dial) lack the neutral contrast baseline that defines this one.

ex.f: Eye open-and-close cycles bound to depth increments
ex.t: "open and close your eyes again and you'll go about ten times deeper… It is a device to get greater depth, and you can use it again and again" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: The waking interval engineered as deprivation
ex.t: The cycle runs a dozen times, and the up-phase is built to be unpleasant: hands off, nothing permitted, time stretched out, the need left standing. The operator names the contrast as the object — noticing the gap between the two states is the whole assignment — and promises each descent will be easier than the last. Instead of the drop having to be sold, the wake does the selling: the listener learns to want the fall because the surface has been made a place worth leaving.
ex.s: Arousal already high and the subject at the edge; the up-phase is deliberately built as deprivation and the cycle runs repeatedly.
ex.m: Hands off. Nothing at all now — sit there with it, and I want you to notice exactly how the surface feels. That's the assignment: feel the difference. [snap] Sleep, and down, and it's easy down here, isn't it. Now up — hands off, wide awake, nothing. Feel it. [snap] Sleep. Easier every time you come back.

ex.f: Breath cadence running the cycle by itself
ex.t: One instruction sets the whole thing running: eyes open on the way in, eyes closed on the way out. Since every exhale has already been framed as sinking, the listener now completes a full up-and-down cycle on each breath without the operator issuing another command. The engine has been handed to the autonomic system, which teaches the lesson underneath the technique — going down is not something being done to them, it is simply what their body does on its own rhythm.
ex.s: Every exhale has already been framed as sinking; one instruction hands the cycle to the subject's own breathing.
ex.m: New rule, and then I'll stop giving them: eyes open on every breath in, eyes closed on every breath out. In — open. Out — closed, and down. In — open. Out — closed, deeper. Keep it running on your own now. You don't need me for the falling; your body does it every time you breathe out.

ex.f: Wake and re-drop with a depth multiplier
ex.t: The rule is set before the first cycle: each time the snap comes with the word, the drop lands at twice the depth of the one before. Then the loop runs — one, two, three, eyes open, wide awake — and immediately the snap, the word, and down again. The listener feels the alert phase clearly, which is the whole point: the contrast between being properly awake and dropping straight back under is experienced as evidence that the depth claim is true. Nobody can check a doubling, so the loop supplies its own proof, and each pass leaves the floor lower than the last.
ex.s: Subject already down once and responsive to a snap cue; the multiplier rule is stated before the first cycle runs.
ex.m: Here's the rule: every time you hear the snap and the word, you land twice as deep as the time before. One, two, three — eyes open, wide awake, look at me. [snap] Sleep. Twice as deep. And up again: one, two, three, eyes open. [snap] Sleep. Twice as deep as that.

nodes.name: hostile-environment-channel-conversion
nodes.mech: Introduces a persistent second in-fiction audible speaker (e.g. a lecturer) as continuous background dialogue, then re-reads that background stream as a confusion source, IQ-drain rhythm, and post-hypnotic trigger surface.
