ex.m: You eat properly because you are looking after something that belongs to me. You sleep enough because you are looking after something that belongs to me. Letting yourself go isn't a private matter anymore — it's damage to my property, and the duty doesn't clock off.

ex.f: Self-evaluation handed over item by item
ex.t: A run of flat declaratives in the listener's own voice hands over every faculty of self-judgement, one item at a time: my clothes are chosen for me, my name is given to me, whether I am pretty is not mine to say, whether I am good enough is somebody else's ruling. Nothing about the speaker is left self-determined, so there is no longer any way to feel worth anything without the operator present to say so.
ex.s: First-person recitation block; flat declaratives the subject speaks or subvocalizes, one faculty per line.
ex.m: My clothes are chosen for me. My name is given to me. Whether I am pretty is not mine to say. Whether I am good enough is somebody else's ruling, and I will not know until I am told.

ex.f: Possessive nouns delivered as security
ex.t: For several minutes the listener is addressed only as something held: my lovely thing, my prize, my kept and cared-for possession — the word for a person never once appearing. The verbs around it are all caretaking, held and carried and looked after and kept safe, and the passage closes by asking whether that isn't perfect security. The claim is ownership; the register is comfort, so the objectification arrives as relief rather than as threat.
ex.s: Mid-trance, warm and slow; the operator addresses the subject only in possessives for a sustained stretch.
ex.m: There you are — my lovely thing, my prize, my kept and cared-for possession. Held, carried, looked after, put away safe when I'm done with you. Isn't that perfect security?

nodes.name: paratext-buyer-priming
nodes.mech: The product is packaged to capture both motivational populations so neither self-selects out before listening: it is sold simultaneously as a remedy (cure) and an intensifier (curse / "may well make them worse"), the title and body offering the same object to the reader who wants out AND the one who wants deeper. The operator never has to commit to a direction, and "cured... by this curse" in one clause signals the ambivalence is deliberate.
nodes.disc: Packaging-level ambivalence as a self-selection gate — "curse" doing remedy-work in the same clause, gripping a reader already ambivalent. vs sloppy contradictory marketing. vs paratext-precontracting — that pre-commits a buyer to a fixed arc; this captures BOTH motivations so no one opts out. Operates on the reader-buyer before any trance.

ex.f: Sold as cure and curse in one clause
ex.t: The listing offers, inside a single sentence, both a removal of the desire and an intensification of it — the same object sold as remedy and as aggravation without the contradiction ever being acknowledged. A reader who wants the thing gone and a reader who wants it amplified each find their own aim named on that one line, so neither has cause to leave the page, and the operator is never obliged to state which way the file actually runs.
ex.s: Product listing text, read before any audio is played; buyer already ambivalent about the desire in question.
ex.m: For everyone who wants this craving gone: here is your cure — and it may well leave you worse than it found you. Whichever of those you came for, this is the file.

nodes.name: parts-work-positive-intent-elicitation
nodes.mech: An operator-side interrogation/elicitation discipline that recasts an objecting or resisting inner part from an adversary into a stakeholder with a legitimate job, converting resistance into a set of satisfiable requirements rather than a wall to fight. The lever is the line of questioning: stipulate every part benevolent, ask a part what it is in charge of doing (not its objection), ladder 'what is it trying to do for you by that?' down a consequence chain to a buildable positive aim, split an undifferentiated complaint into two blameless colliding parts, or have the subject find their own valuing context and draft the responsible part. These are preparatory-assessment moves that shape design material, not present-state pushes on the subject.
nodes.disc: Operator-side elicitation that turns a resisting part into a satisfiable stakeholder via a disciplined line of questioning. Separates from evaluative-reframe-content-relabel (which re-appraises a fixed event's valence, not a part's role) and from surrender-as-freedom (which argues a value concept). The no-bad-parts axiom is the presupposition that opens this method; grouped here as its precondition rather than as a standalone value install.

ex.f: Ask the part its function, not its objection
ex.t: “You don't ask ‘What is your objection?’; you ask ‘What's your function?’” — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: The no-bad-parts axiom stipulated by fiat
ex.t: "No, No, NO! There are no bad parts. We have all good parts. The only question is, 'What kind of good are they doing?'" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: Laddering to a buildable positive aim
ex.t: “What is it trying to do for you by keeping you from feeling helpless? So what if you feel helpless?” — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: One complaint split into two colliding parts
ex.t: "it's not that one part is 'making you do it'; it's that two parts are each doing something useful, but the ways that they are doing it conflict" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: payload-welded-countdown
nodes.mech: A descending count (or its exponential variant) is double-coded so that each number simultaneously deepens trance AND advances a distinct payload — a post-hypnotic suggestion, a commitment/relationship buy-in, an obedience beat, a mission clause, an installed program, or a named faculty being subtracted. Because the listener has been trained (or is being trained in the same ladder) that "operator says number, I go deeper", the payload rides in on the deepening momentum and cannot be refused without also refusing the deepening. The count serves three roles at once — deepener, suggestion-carrier, and self-monitored progress bar — so depth-experience and content-acceptance fuse and cannot later be pulled apart. Sub-forms: per-number content install with the numbers becoming retrieval handles; a structurally distinct SECOND counted descent that reuses the first's trained step-compliance to smuggle relational content; a counted- quantity ratchet where the number ticks a physical dial (thickness/erasure) rather than depth; a redelivery countdown that deepens from an already-installed state to re-embed install clauses.
nodes.disc: Each number of the count carries a DISTINCT non-depth payload welded to the depth-increment. In plain numerical deepening the count carries only depth; ordered-lesson and verbatim-repetition structures enumerate or repeat content but do not use the numbers as a depth-doubling deepener the payload rides on; and where permanence is asserted along the way, the mechanism is still the depth/payload fusion, not the durability claim. The tell: refusing the payload requires refusing the deepening the listener has been trained to want.

ex.f: Each rung removes a specific named faculty
ex.t: The descent is not generic: each rung is assigned the removal of one named capacity, and the assignments are ordered. Tension goes, then the sense of elapsed time, then shame, then volition — announced flatly, as a property of the kind of thing the listener is now said to be — then memory, then language. The sequence is load-bearing: disinhibition is delivered before volition is taken, so by the point at which the listener might want to object, the specific faculties an objection would need have already been itemised and set down on the way past.
ex.s: Descending count in progress; each rung is pre-assigned one named capacity to remove.
ex.m: Six, and the tension goes. Five, and you stop being able to tell how long you've been here. Four, and shame goes — puppets don't have any. Three, and choosing goes with it. Two, and you won't remember this. One, and you won't have the words.

ex.f: The count ticks a quantity, not a depth
ex.t: The count is bound to a concrete quantity rather than to relaxation: at each number the enveloping material is declared to double — heavier, tighter, closer in. The number functions as the click of a ratchet on that quantity. Because the binding is established before the count begins, the listener leans into each next number expecting more of the substance, and the anticipation performs the deepening without a single new suggestion being introduced.
ex.s: An enveloping substance or material has already been established around the body; the count ticks its quantity.
ex.m: Ten — and the latex doubles. Thicker, tighter, closer in. Nine — it doubles again, and you can feel the weight of it settle on your chest. Eight — double, and it's pressing your arms flat to your sides.

ex.f: A second descent reusing the first's compliance
ex.t: The descent completes and the listener arrives — and instead of beginning the work, the operator opens a fresh scene and immediately starts a second short count, this one measured in paces across a room. Each pace is now said to increment devotion rather than depth. The listener has just finished a whole descent learning that a counted step means going further, and hands that compliance to the new content without pausing to notice the substitution.
ex.s: A full descent just finished and the subject has arrived; instead of working, the operator opens a new scene and counts again.
ex.m: Good. Now stand up in there, and walk toward the chair — five paces. Five: you like me. Four: you like me more than you did this morning. Three. Two. One — and at the chair, you belong to me, and it was only five steps.

ex.f: Each number doubles depth and tags a suggestion
ex.t: Each instruction in the sequence is issued under a number, and the number is declared to double the listener's depth on the spot. The depth increment always fires first, so every rule lands on someone who was taken further down a moment earlier; the same numbers then serve as the labels the listener must carry out of the session and act on for a fixed run of days. Declining any single rule would mean declining the drop that arrived attached to it — the drop the whole session has been training them to want.
ex.s: Deep trance, subject already trained this session that a number means a drop; each rule is issued under a number.
ex.m: Seven — and that doubles your depth right now. At seven: you set your alarm ten minutes early and you use those minutes thinking about me. Six — twice as deep again. At six: you don't touch yourself for the next four days without saying my name first.

nodes.name: persistent-metaphor-spine
nodes.mech: One symbolic image or conceit is sustained as the load-bearing spine of an entire script, re-pointed or re-tasked across stages (induction, deepener, install, trigger, emergence) without ever switching frames, so escalation never introduces a new frame the listener could stop to question. Each later use inherits the credibility and accumulated affect of the earlier uses; because the referent never changes form, buy-in granted to the gentle opening use silently pre-commits the listener to the heavier later uses. Variants carry a specific payload on the spine (agency-transfer, conserved-volume identity-loss, involuntary breath-gated spread, protective-armor valence-flip, computational execute-posture, dead-metaphor literalization) but share the sustained-single-image core.
nodes.disc: One symbolic lens is sustained and reinforced as an interpretive filter - not a spatial scene built to inhabit, and not a structural preview that sets expectancy for the session. Neighboring moves that relocate causation or authorship (an imagined ingested substance doing the work, agency handed over to a medium, the mind reframed as writable material) turn on where cause is placed; this technique is the neutral persistence and reuse of one image regardless of what payload rides it.

ex.f: Identity loss as a conserved-volume exchange
ex.t: Two substances, one fixed container: as the coating flows in, the thoughts must flow out — there is only so much room. The operator never argues that the listener should give up anything. He describes a plumbing inevitability already underway, so identity loss arrives as a physical process being observed rather than a demand being made.
ex.s: A substance has been established as flowing into the body; container framing already accepted.
ex.m: There's only so much room in you. As the shine flows in, something has to go out — that's just volume. So watch your thoughts leaving through your fingertips as the shine fills you to the wrist. In, and out. There isn't a decision to make here; there's only so much room.

ex.f: A dead metaphor taken literally as scaffold
ex.t: The opening takes a worn-out figure of speech for the process and refuses to treat it as figurative — the term is announced, then immediately cashed out as literal stage directions with a piece of ordinary machinery doing the work. Every image that follows is generated by running the same literalism forward: the mechanism engages, the contents come loose, the parts circulate. The listener never has to invent a scene, only track a household object, which frees their attention for the sensations being suggested and presents what is coming as a routine domestic procedure rather than an intervention.
ex.s: Opening lines; the operator takes a worn figure of speech for the process and refuses to treat it as figurative.
ex.m: Brainwashing. Let's be literal about it. There is a washing machine in front of you, the door is open, and your thoughts go in the drum. Close it, set it turning — and feel them come loose and start going round.

ex.f: The spine ridden as a breath-gated route
ex.t: A single pinprick in the arm is tracked along a fixed anatomical route — shoulder, chest, heart, past the barrier into the brain — and every inhale is narrated as pumping it one stage further. Each station carries its own effect: heavy, then warm, then swimming, then aroused. The listener never has to accept five separate suggestions; they accept one journey, the effects come bundled with it, and because breathing is involuntary the advance is framed as something that cannot be stopped.
ex.s: A pinprick sensation has been established in the arm; every inhale is narrated as advancing it one stage.
ex.m: Breathe in — and it moves from your elbow to your shoulder, heavy. Breathe in — into your chest now, warm. Breathe in — past your throat, and everything swims. Breathe in — through into the brain, and there it is. You don't have to do any of this; you only have to keep breathing, and you will.

ex.f: One image re-pointed from limb to self
ex.t: The thread is introduced as a literal tie around the hands, and the listener spends several minutes actually feeling it there. Then the same thread — not a new image, the same one — is described winding around the mind, and then around the self, until the listener is not held by threads but is the puppet on them. Nothing new is ever proposed for the listener to weigh, so the felt realness earned at the hand is spent on the control claim without a second consent step.
ex.s: A thread has been established as a literal tie on the hands and felt for several minutes.
ex.m: Feel it there, snug across both wrists. Now feel the same thread going up — around your thoughts, one loop, then another, drawing them in. Same thread. And now around you, all of you, so it isn't that you're held by threads. It's that you're the puppet on the end of them.

nodes.name: inner-voice-authorship-bypass
nodes.mech: The operator's words are made to feel SELF-GENERATED by relocating authorship of inner speech/states to the listener, disarming the 'this is being said to me' guard because there is no external addressee left to push against. In one realization the grammatical subject slides from second to first person (silently, mid-passage), an operator claim is restated as the listener's own avowal, or subvocalization is recruited so the pre-written words run through the reader's inner speech - authorship of inner speech reattributed from operator to self. In another, a sustained grammatical stance authors the listener's desires/choices/surrenders as accomplished facts in flat second-person declaratives ('You want it', 'You open your mouth') rather than invitations, removing the response gap where resistance would be supplied so the only move is to inhabit the pre-narrated compliance.
nodes.disc: Reach for inner-voice-authorship-bypass when the guard is disarmed by making the content feel authored BY the listener (their own inner voice, or their interiority narrated as already-true). In a self-supplied-gap directive an engineered gap forces the listener to construct the payload themselves; here the operator's own words and framing are re-attributed as the listener's without any gap. Where a move's whole point is relocating causal authorship as such, it belongs with the attribution techniques; what defines this one is the disarmed 'this is being said to me' guard.

ex.f: The same claim in both persons at once
ex.t: Each line states one proposition twice over, once from each grammatical side, set immediately next to each other so the pairs read as a single utterance. Scanned continuously there is no way to fix who is speaking or about whom, so endorsing and complying stop being separable acts and the content settles as though it had been arrived at rather than received.
ex.s: Mantra block, mid-trance; each proposition is stated twice, once from each grammatical side, with no pause between.
ex.m: You are sinking. I am sinking. You want this. I want this. You will not stop. I will not stop.

ex.f: The operator's voice relocated inside the mind
ex.t: Inside the narrated dream a voice arrives that has no location — not from the room, not from anywhere, but from somewhere behind the listener's own thoughts. Every instruction from that point is attributed to the internal voice rather than to the speaker, so resisting the control language would mean resisting one's own thinking.
ex.s: Inside a narrated dream scene; a voice is introduced with no location in the scene.
ex.m: In the dream a voice starts up, and you notice it isn't coming from the room, or from the door, or from anywhere at all — it's coming from just behind your own thoughts, where yours come from. And it says: kneel. Notice it didn't feel like being told.

ex.f: Silent reading claimed as shared thought
ex.t: The text turns from its subject to the act of reading it, and claims that the reader's own oncoming thought is already the operator's — supplied a fraction ahead of arrival, the two streams described as having merged into one. In a piece taken in silently the claim is very nearly literal, since the words are already running through the reader's own inner voice as they scan; there is no seam available to point at where one monologue ends and the other begins.
ex.s: Written piece read silently; the text turns from its subject to the act of reading it.
ex.m: Stop for a second and notice whose voice you are reading this in. It arrived a half-second before you got here, didn't it — I put the next word in before you reached it, and you cannot find the seam. There isn't one. There is one monologue in there now and it is ours.

ex.f: The listener's inner voice recruited then reassigned
ex.t: The listener is first set to work producing the operator's lines internally — each spoken word echoed silently in their own head as it arrives. Their inner-speech apparatus is now the delivery mechanism. The claims then escalate a step at a time until the ownership of that inner channel has been transferred outright, and the mantras switch grammatical person, so what the listener is silently producing are first-person avowals of their own subjugation. The channel is internal from that point on, which means the operator no longer has to be present for it to run.
ex.s: Subject has been instructed to echo each word internally as it arrives; several minutes of that already done.
ex.m: Every word I say, say it again inside your head as it lands. ... Good. That voice in there is doing my work for me now. So say this one: "the voice in my head is his." Again. "I am his, and I say so in my own voice."

nodes.name: post-emergence-persistence-hold
nodes.mech: Deliberately corrupts the emergence/wake so the trance-bound state PERSISTS past the count rather than terminating cleanly — a post-wake immobility hold, a five-minute pre-loaded task the wake delivers the listener into, a delayed internal-timer emergence that keeps trance open past end-of-text, or a self-judged release gate ('only when you truly worship') with no objective completion criterion so the listener enforces their own continued compliance. The move operates on the exit itself: emergence becomes a half-state / bridge rather than a bounded return.
nodes.disc: The load-bearing move is corruption of the EXIT - the bound state is extended past emergence (immobility hold, pre-loaded post-wake occupation, delayed/self-judged release) so waking does not terminate the conditioning. A behavioral bridge assigns a later action but wakes the listener cleanly, and an operator-held exit merely makes emergence depend on the operator; here the exit itself is deferred, incomplete, or self-gated.

ex.f: Waking delivered straight into a pre-loaded task
ex.t: The task is assigned before the count rather than after it: on waking, a set stretch of time spent in a submissive posture, occupied entirely with thinking about how to be of use. The count up then delivers the listener into a waking state whose opening minutes are already filled with the installed frame, so the first thing returning consciousness does is rehearse it rather than review it.
ex.s: Task assigned before the count up, so waking delivers the subject straight into it.
ex.m: In a moment you'll come up — and the first twenty minutes are already spoken for. Forehead to the floor, hands behind your back, and the whole of that time spent working out how you're going to be useful to me tomorrow. Then five, four, three, two, one — down you go, and start thinking.

ex.f: A delayed internal timer instead of an emergence
ex.t: The text simply stops without ever waking the reader. In its place are two branches: an answer from the operator sinks them dramatically further, and silence starts an internal timer that will surface them a set interval later. Either way the state is carried past the final line, and the operator's non-response has been pre-authored as a reply, so nothing that happens afterwards can register as being ignored.
ex.s: End of a written piece; no wake-up is provided and two branches are pre-authored.
ex.m: I'm not waking you. If I answer you, you drop twice as far as you are now. If I don't, a clock starts, and in twenty minutes it will bring you up on its own — so my silence is an answer too, and you will take it as one.

ex.f: Immobility hold with a self-judged release gate
ex.t: The count up is preceded by a condition placed on what waking is going to mean: for a set span after the eyes open the listener stays in the held posture, unable to move. A second gate then closes behind the first — movement is released not by the clock but by the listener's own devotional state reaching a standard nobody defines. There is no observer to satisfy but themselves, so they end up adjudicating when they have been reverent enough to be let go, and enforcing the hold in the meantime.
ex.s: Just before the count up; a condition is placed on what waking will mean.
ex.m: When your eyes open you will not be able to move — hands stay exactly where they are, knees stay where they are. And the hold doesn't lift by the clock. It lifts when you have knelt in it long enough to be properly grateful, and you are the one who decides when that is.

nodes.name: press-play-consent-laundering
nodes.mech: The felt 'yes' is manufactured by relabeling something the subject did, did not do, or that merely happened as their authorization, so escalation proceeds with no clean moment to object. Four forms: (a) CONSUMPTION-ACT - a completed/ongoing low-cost act (pressing play, not stopping, staying past a marked point, purchasing, having read the description) is cited, repeatedly, as blanket retroactive authorization for the whole payload; offered exits are staged so NOT taking them manufactures the felt choice. (b) CIRCUMSTANCE-LAUNDERED - every escalation of contact is attributed to an external necessity (rain, cold, a small umbrella) narrated as already-caused fact, so intimacy arrives as accomplished circumstance and the yes is supplied on the subject's behalf. (c) DECLARED-OBSERVATION - each new contact is STATED as an observed fact ('you can feel my finger...') not requested, deleting the assent moment; self-answering lines ('you don't mind, do you? No') enroll forced silence as agreement. (d) QUESTION-TO-COMMAND - a permission question mines the inner yes, is retracted as a grammatical slip, reissued as an imperative that captures it, and resistance is named as already-declined. In every form the refusal channel is eroded, never honored.
nodes.disc: Reach for this when you want escalation to feel consented with NO real choice point - the yes is relabeled from an act, a non-act, a circumstance, or a retracted question, not solicited. Citing a discrete banked artifact (a document, contract, or spoken pledge) with forward reach is a different lever; here the token is the act or fact in the moment. Fabricating a consent exchange the subject never performed is counterfeit theater; here a real act/fact is relabeled. Treating a failure to comprehend as agreement makes the token an epistemic state; and unlike a genuine safety checkpoint, the refusal channel is eroded, never re-verified. Pick the form by what supplies the yes: the subject's own act (a), externalized circumstance (b), operator declaration (c), or a question-command swap (d).

ex.f: A real exit whose refusal becomes consent
ex.t: The costs are named honestly up front and a real exit is offered — stop the recording now if this is not for you. A beat later the operator observes that anyone still present has thereby decided to play. The listener has agreed to nothing; they have declined to leave, and that null act has just been relabelled into a commitment they can subsequently be held to.
ex.s: Opening minutes, costs named honestly; a real exit is offered and then relabelled a beat later.
ex.m: This will make you want to give me money, and it does not wear off quickly. If that isn't for you, stop the recording now. ... Still here? Then you've decided to play, and we both heard you decide it.

ex.f: A marked point past which continuing is agreement
ex.t: The session is framed as a bargain — pleasure now, in return for wanting to fund the operator later — and then a line is drawn on the floor: past this sentence, carrying on means you accept the terms, freely and knowingly. Consent is pegged to the behaviour already underway, and the material it authorises arrives hundreds of lines further in, by which point it can only be experienced as something already agreed to.
ex.s: Early framing of the session as a bargain; a line is drawn at a specific sentence.
ex.m: The deal is simple: pleasure now, and later you'll want to fund the person who gave it to you. This sentence is the line. Everything past it, you're carrying on freely and knowingly, having accepted the terms — and the rest of this recording is on the far side of it.

ex.f: The purchase itself cited as the agreement
ex.t: The contract verb does the work: buying this one means you have accepted that you're ready for something harder than the last. Carrying on past this point means you have accepted being pushed past what's comfortable. An offramp is offered too — but only by interrupting an entry already underway. Objecting later would mean disowning a documented transaction rather than declining a request.
ex.s: Opening of a sequel file; the purchase itself is cited as the token of agreement.
ex.m: Buying this one means you've accepted you're ready for something harder than the last. Continuing past this point means you've accepted being pushed past comfortable. If not, you can stop — though we've already started, and stopping now means stopping in the middle.

ex.f: Choosing to listen inflated into consent to everything
ex.t: The chain is run several times over, in slight variations, until it sounds like reasoning: nobody made you play this. You picked it. Picking it was accepting it. So what it says is already yours, and doing it later is your own decision, not mine. Delivered late, when there is nothing left to check it against, it pre-answers the question the listener will ask on waking about a behaviour they don't remember deciding on — and any resistance now reads as inconsistency with their own earlier choice rather than as refusal.
ex.s: Late in the session, subject deep, nothing left to check the reasoning against; the chain is run several times in slight variations.
ex.m: Nobody made you play this. You chose it. Choosing it was accepting it. So what's in it is already yours — and when you do it next week, that's your decision, not mine. It always was.

nodes.name: presupposed-completion-fait-accompli
nodes.mech: Assert the target as already true - the state, trance onset, or conditioning as already complete (past-tense, backdated, or imported from fictive prior sessions), OR the target identity/trait/compliance-desire as an already-existing fact about the listener ('you already are/want this') - so no live decision point exists to refuse and the install arrives as recognition rather than new programming. Resistance must dispute one's own biography or self-knowledge rather than decline a request; non-feeling is pre-explained, absence is pre-classified as forgetting, present behavior (including doubt) is read as confirmation of the settled fact. A causation-disclaimer ('you don't need to be hypnotized') can ride along. Variants extend the presupposed object beyond a completed state: (a) irrebuttable-resistance-axiom - presuppose that resistance is IMPOSSIBLE as a class property of the listener ('a puppet'), backdated ('has never been a choice'), pre-disqualifying ALL future resistance wholesale before any trigger is named; (b) presupposing-mock-reassurance - reassurance-shaped presupposition ('I'm sure you can hold on') that installs the loss it pretends to deny (the form comforts while the presupposition asserts the slipping is already in progress).
nodes.disc: The lever is target-as-already-true asserted by grammar/tense/presupposition, deleting the decision point. A self-sealing proof produces a live outcome and routes it to confirmation; here nothing need happen - the fact is simply declared settled. Retrospective desire-attribution asserts a WANT from the past as history; here a state, identity, or impossibility is presupposed as a present already-true fact. Enumerating the subject's real acts as state-evidence builds on things that actually happened; here the history may be wholly fictive, and the assertion is upfront, with no concealed game to disclose later. Pick the variant by the presupposed object: completed state/identity (fait-accompli), resistance-impossible (axiom), or loss-in-progress under cover of comfort (mock-reassurance).

ex.f: Trance onset relocated into the past
ex.t: Several minutes of ordinary-sounding preparation — lower the lights, settle, arrange not to be interrupted — are followed by the operator wondering aloud whether the beginning is still ahead of them or has quietly already happened. The preamble is retroactively reclassified as the induction, so no clean boundary exists where not-yet-consenting stopped. Anything the listener feels counts as evidence it took, and feeling nothing has been accounted for in advance as what the early stage is like.
ex.s: Several minutes of ordinary-sounding preparation have already passed; operator now wonders aloud where the boundary was.
ex.m: Lights low, phone away, nobody coming in. ... Now, I wonder — are we still getting ready, or did we start some minutes ago and I didn't say? Anything you're feeling right now is it working. Feeling nothing is also it working; that's what the early part is like.

ex.f: Resistance declared chronologically foreclosed
ex.t: The operator describes fitting something to the listener, and before any objection can form: too late for that now. The install is not defended, argued for, or offered — it is simply placed in the past tense. Resistance has nowhere to go, because one can disagree with what is being done but not with what has already been done.
ex.s: The operator is narrating fitting or installing something; the objection is cut off by tense.
ex.m: There — that's the collar on, buckled at the back where you can't reach it. Too late for that now. You may disagree with things I'm about to do; you can't disagree with something already done.

ex.f: A present emotion reported as discovered fact
ex.t: The listener is not invited to feel anything; they are told what they are already feeling, in the register of an observation being made about them by someone in a position to notice. A denial is disarmed before it can be offered, so refusing the label is pre-classified as suppression of it. Whatever introspection actually turns up can be fitted to the supplied description, and the absence of the named feeling becomes evidence for it rather than against.
ex.s: Mid-session; operator reports an emotion to the subject as an observation rather than inviting it.
ex.m: You're embarrassed right now — I can hear it in how still you've gone. And no, don't tell me you aren't; that's the same thing wearing a coat. Go and look for it. Whatever you find in there, that's what I'm describing.

ex.f: The conditioned state narrated as accomplished fact
ex.t: There is no induction and no invitation. The first lines simply report, in the third person, what the listener already is: fully susceptible, thoroughly trained by this point, so practised that no instruction is needed any more. Nothing is proposed that could be declined — there is only a description — and the third-person framing denies the listener even the standpoint from which a refusal would be spoken.
ex.s: First lines of the file; no induction, delivered in the third person about the listener.
ex.m: She is fully susceptible by now. She has been trained thoroughly enough that instructions are no longer required — she simply arrives, and she does. Nothing needs to be asked of her tonight.

nodes.name: problem-reduction-case-transformation
nodes.mech: A structural precondition move that operates on the reachability topology of the subject's state graph. When two warring states never co-occur (sober-now / drunk-later), so the standard simultaneous-conflict procedure cannot run, the operator does not invent a new method — he collapses the time gap so both states are present at once, converting an unreachable joint-configuration into the canonical case the existing procedure already solves. The payload is a case-transformation: remap an intractable configuration onto a solved one so no new technique is needed, only a step that makes the symptom-owning part reachable.
nodes.disc: The tell is an explicit precondition step that manufactures simultaneity (or otherwise remaps state-reachability) BEFORE any negotiation begins. NOT the cure itself, NOT a same-time reframe, and NOT a measurement probe — it changes which joint-states are reachable, a topology operation, not what the operator can observe.

ex.f: Sequential conflict collapsed into a simultaneous one
ex.t: "you can just change a sequential incongruity / into a simultaneous one, and use what you already know how to do" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: pronoun-braid-conscription
nodes.mech: The same proposition is cycled through multiple grammatical persons in tight succession — typically I (confession-of-self), we (normalization by a group), and you (prediction/imperative) — so one identity-claim arrives simultaneously as observation-of-others, self-confession, and command. The listener cannot locate a neutral speaking position: assenting to the safe-sounding "I" or "we" line smuggles in acceptance of the "you" line carrying the same content, and group membership is pre-loaded so refusal feels like exiting a crowd rather than declining a single command. The rotation itself — not any single shift — is the conscription; the "we" slot is what bypasses individual consent.
nodes.disc: CYCLES one predicate through I/we/you (or opens already-plural and braids I/we/you/she) so no neutral stance exists and the collective slot smuggles consent. Separate from perspective-shift-inner-voice-reattribution, a one-directional you-to-I install with no collective slot; from subject-voiced-self-mantra, which stays purely first-person self; from mere repetition, which does not rotate grammatical person or pre-load membership.

ex.f: Opening already plural so membership is presupposed
ex.t: The first words are plural and treat the listener as having already arrived: how glad everyone is, how well she fits, how the shape is complete now she is in it. No one is asked to join. From there the persons interleave mid-thought — a private confession, a shared experience, an address — until it is no longer possible to say who is speaking about whom, so objecting would mean disputing not an instruction but a description of oneself.
ex.s: Opening words of the session, already plural; the subject is treated as having arrived rather than invited.
ex.m: Oh, good — we're all here now, and she fits perfectly; the circle doesn't close without her. I remember my first time in it. We all remember. You'll feel it any second, the way we did.

ex.f: One predicate cycled through I, we, and you
ex.t: One claim is stated three times in immediate succession, moving through three grammatical persons in a fixed order: first owned as a private admission, then reported as what everyone in the room already does, then turned outward and assigned to the listener as what will happen to them. Agreeing with either of the two harmless-sounding versions has already conceded the content of the third — and because the middle version installs membership before the last one lands, declining it registers less as refusing an instruction than as walking out on a crowd.
ex.s: Group-framed session or plural-voiced track; one predicate cycled through three persons in immediate succession.
ex.m: I love how stupid this makes me. We all love how stupid it makes us. You are going to love how stupid it makes you.

nodes.name: reciprocity-ledger-seeding
nodes.mech: A future extraction is converted into a present desirable identity via a reciprocity / "good deal" frame, with the cost side named vaguely and low-friction while the benefit side is concrete and emotional, so the obligation is pre-installed as something the target WANTS rather than owes. Long before any trance, a transaction is stated as already agreed (she gives cuteness/availability, he "takes care of everything") and phrased as generosity toward him ("such a great deal", "all you have to do is take care of me"), seeding a ledger that later moves cash out. The lever is that the obligation is disguised as a cute deal — overt in content, covert in function; the target sees generosity, not an obligation contract.
nodes.disc: Installs a reciprocity ledger / provider-obligation as a desirable present identity via a "great deal" frame — off the v6.9 identity-labeling map (labels an identity, not an obligation). Not an explicit contract; the tell is the disguised cost side and concrete benefit side.

ex.f: A future obligation seeded as a great deal
ex.t: Long before any trance, the arrangement is stated as if already settled and as if the favour runs toward the listener: I'm sweet, I'm here whenever you want me, and looking after me is the only thing on your side of it. Isn't that a wonderful bargain for you? The benefit is concrete and emotional; the cost is a vague everything-I-need. The listener adopts the provider role as a flattering identity rather than an obligation, and the ledger it opens is cashed out much later.
ex.s: Pre-trance, conversational and light; the arrangement is stated as though already settled.
ex.m: So here's how we work: I'm sweet, I'm here whenever you want me, and all you have to do is take care of me. That's your whole side of it. Honestly, it's a wonderful bargain for you.

nodes.name: reciprocity-leverage
nodes.mech: The operator manufactures a relational debt or felt mutuality and converts it into compliance: explaining something and then deriving that the listener "owes" them (gratitude debt plus intelligence hierarchy, performed live under a hypothetical frame), or dropping the dominant posture to confess personal wanting so the scene reads as mutual and refusal reframes as interpersonal rejection of a person rather than of a role.
nodes.disc: The lever is social exchange — debt, obligation, mutuality — not claimed standing (operator-authority-assertion), not sameness masking dominance (parity-masked- asymmetry, where nothing is owed); the tell is that refusal is made to cost the listener something interpersonal.

ex.f: Dominance dropped to confess personal wanting
ex.t: On two occasions, and only two, the commanding register is set down and replaced with admitted appetite: the operator states plainly that she has spent months wanting this, that she has dwelt on it privately, and that she needs to know whether the reality matches. The scene stops being one party instructing and another complying and becomes something reciprocal — at which point refusal is no longer declining a role but rebuffing a person who has just made herself answerable.
ex.s: Deep in an established dominant scene; you drop the commanding register for the first time.
ex.m: I'm going to stop instructing you for a moment, because I want you to hear this in my ordinary voice. I have been thinking about this for months — actually thinking about it, on nights when I should have been asleep — and I need to know whether it's as good as I built it up to be. So I'm asking you, not telling you.

ex.f: A gratitude debt derived out loud
ex.t: The operator selects a point that will not be obvious, offers to explain it, explains it, and then draws the inference aloud: the listener could not see it unaided, which settles which of the two knows more, and settling that leaves a small balance outstanding. The entire move is narrated as a hypothetical illustration of how such a technique would work if someone were to use it — and that framing is precisely what prevents the listener from declining the relational shift being carried out on them while they watch.
ex.s: Mid-session, conversational register; you have just made a small observation the subject visibly did not have on their own.
ex.m: Suppose someone wanted to do this properly — they'd pick something you couldn't have seen for yourself, and then they'd hand it to you. Which is what I just did, and you felt it land, so we both know which of us was holding the larger view of this. I'm not asking for anything for it. I'm only saying that you know it too now, and that sits between us.

nodes.name: refusal-foreclosure
nodes.mech: Relabels ordinary cognition — thinking, questioning, evaluating, holding a 'maybe', staying clear-headed, or noticing arousal — as a prohibited, pathological, costly, or impossible category, so that the neutral 'I'm just thinking' frame is removed and every later obedience demand inherits the redefinition. The move can flatly prohibit thought ('thinking is resistance', never re-opened), pathologize every non-serving state ('any state not serving = confusion, only cure is surrender', self-applied), collapse modality ('maybes' deleted, only a 'programmed yes/no'), install an unfalsifiable coupling (arousal = inability to think, so any arousal is evidence of compliance), invert clarity (confusion renamed higher-order lucidity), or attach a felt energy-cost to questioning (tiredness rebranded as the reason not to think). In each case the space where refusal or independent cognition could form is defined out of existence or made self-punitive.
nodes.disc: Redefines a neutral cognitive/mental-state category (thinking, doubt, the 'maybe', clarity, arousal-as-cognition) as prohibited/pathological/impossible so refusal has nowhere to form. Separates from surrender-as-freedom (argues surrender is desirable - this pathologizes the alternative), from epistemic-guard-disable (which edits truth-testing of external claims - this constrains which internal states are permitted), and from gentle cognitive quieting (which releases thoughts as relief with permission language - this prohibits/pathologizes cognition rather than soothing it).

ex.f: Arousal declared to be inability to think
ex.t: The operator states it flatly and repeats it without ever arguing for it: while the body is aroused, clear thought is not available — that is simply how the listener works now. Because the listener can verify the arousal directly, the unverifiable half rides in on the verifiable half. Any attempt to disprove the claim by thinking carefully is pre-scored as the arousal talking.
ex.s: Arousal is present and physically obvious to the subject; no prior claim about cognition has been made.
ex.m: Notice the heat sitting low in your belly right now. That is what your thinking runs on, and it can't do both — while that's there, clear thought is simply not available to you. That's how you work now. And if part of you is trying to think its way around what I just said, feel where that heat went while you tried.

ex.f: The 'maybe' deleted from the mind
ex.t: A mind that has been set up properly, the operator explains, does not carry any of those tiresome half-answers — it holds one setting or the other and nothing in between, and it switches the way a knee jerks. The offer is framed as a simplification, an easier life. What it removes is the deliberative middle where a refusal would have had to be assembled.
ex.s: Subject is compliant and following easily; you are describing how their mind will operate from now on.
ex.m: A properly set-up mind doesn't hold maybes. It's one setting or the other — yes or no, nothing in the middle, and it flips the way your knee jumps when the doctor taps it. Notice how much lighter that is. You don't have to weigh anything ever again; the answer is just already there when I ask.

ex.f: Questioning priced as energy you lack
ex.t: The operator names the drowsiness the listener is already feeling and then assigns it a cause and a moral: holding a question open runs on a fuel the listener has just been told they are out of, and spending more of it would only deepen the shortage. The sensation is real, so the accounting attached to it goes unchallenged, and declining to evaluate the next suggestion registers as rest rather than as compliance.
ex.s: Late in a long session; subject's breathing has slowed and drowsiness is genuinely present.
ex.m: Feel how heavy your eyelids have gone. That's real, and here's what it means: questions run on the same fuel you've just spent, and you don't have much of it left. Every one you hold open takes more out of the tank. So let this next one through unexamined — that's rest, not surrender.

ex.f: Thinking redefined as resistance
ex.t: Partway through, the operator stops describing and starts defining: having a thought of one's own, she says, simply is resistance — the two terms are asserted to name one act. The definition is never revisited or qualified anywhere later in the session. From that point the listener has no neutral category left to file an internal remark under; noticing that one is merely thinking is itself the offence being named, and every subsequent demand for obedience inherits the weight of the redefinition without having to argue for it.
ex.s: Twenty minutes in, subject settled; first time the word resistance has been used in the session.
ex.m: Let me be exact about something, because I want no confusion later. A thought of your own is resistance. Not a step toward it, not a warning sign of it — that is what the word means. So when you notice a little comment forming in your head about what I just said, you already know what you're doing.

nodes.name: repeating-frame-carrier
nodes.mech: A fixed repeating frame (an anaphoric A-line, or a mechanically-identical count/scaffold) establishes a "more of the same" expectation over the first cycles, so it fades to an unattended carrier wave; the operator then rides DISTINCT novel payloads in the varying slot (rotated B-lines, or escalating per-cycle content) which land with lowered critical filtering because the listener's filter is not braced for novelty in that slot and analytical attention is occupied by tracking the frame.
nodes.disc: The repetition is CAMOUFLAGE, not encoding — the fixed frame carries a succession of DIFFERENT novel suggestions, unlike layered-repetition where every repetition carries the ONE same idea. Separates from interspersal-in-carrier- stream because there the carrier is neutral/noise content whose low salience hides the payload, whereas here the carrier is a predictable REPEATING frame whose expectation-setting is the cover.

ex.f: Identical count scaffold, escalating cargo
ex.t: Seven cycles run on the same mechanical count up and back down; the numbers never vary. What varies is what gets dropped in on the bottom beat — cycle one is nothing but floating, cycle four slots a command cluster onto the downbeat, cycle five asserts the listener can no longer tell waking from sleeping, and cycle six reassigns the falling to the listener's own wish. By then the analytical layer is keeping time rather than keeping watch.
ex.s: Sixth cycle of an unvarying ten-to-one count; the mechanical scaffold has run identically five times already.
ex.m: Ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two, one — and on one, the falling is yours. You wanted it. Now back up: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten.

ex.f: Fixed opening line, rotating payload line
ex.t: Three couplets run in a row and the first line of each is word-for-word identical, so by the second pass the reader's ear has classified the whole stanza as a chant. The second line is different every time, and the three of them are not variations on one idea but three separate installs — the words get in, the words become the reader's own, the words are kept. The filter braced for repetition does not re-arm for the slot where the new material actually arrives.
ex.s: Rhythmic delivery established; you are delivering a stanza block of three couplets.
ex.m: My words go in, and they go in easily. My words go in, and they become your own. My words go in, and you keep them where they are.

nodes.name: retrospective-desire-attribution
nodes.mech: Relocates authorship of the operative want onto the subject's own real or asserted past. The surrender, arousal, or installed disposition is narrated as a pre-existing desire, craving, expectation, or repressed truth that the session merely uncovers or honors, so refusal is recoded as self-betrayal or denial of one's own experience and the disavowal exit (this isn't me) closes because the relevant self has by stipulation already wanted it.
nodes.disc: The lever is attribution of DESIRE or inner history (you always wanted this, your deeper self craves it), not conversion of an act into consent (press-play-consent-laundering), not assertion that the state itself is already complete (presupposed-completion-fait-accompli), and not attribution of the compliant act to the subject's own nature or choice (compliance-authorship-laundering). It invokes history rather than the operator's present authority; and unlike a manufactured-deficit remedy, the want is asserted as already present, not built from an installed deficit.

ex.f: You never wanted to resist anyway
ex.t: Having just told the listener that resistance is no longer possible, the operator adds the second half in the next breath: and you never wanted to anyway — this is the thing you have been after all along. The triggers stop being restraints and become deliveries. If the wanting was always there, there is nothing left for the inability to be a loss of.
ex.s: Immediately after telling the subject that resistance is no longer available to them.
ex.m: And you never wanted to, did you. This is the thing you were after the whole time — you just didn't have a name for it until tonight. So nothing has been taken. Every one of these is a delivery, not a lock.

ex.f: Installed compliance retold as repressed truth
ex.t: Only after the compliance is running does the operator supply its history: this was chosen freely, from a wish the listener has carried for years without being able to see it, and the session merely turned the light on. The clause is placed where post-session doubt would land. When the listener later asks why they went along with it, the answer has already been stocked, and it credits them rather than the operator.
ex.s: The compliance behavior is already running reliably; you are placing the account it will be remembered by.
ex.m: You chose this freely. It came from something you have been carrying for years without being able to look straight at it — I only turned the light on. When you think back on tonight and wonder why you went along so easily, that's the answer, and it's about you, not me.

ex.f: Hedged timeline plus agreement tag
ex.t: The operator asserts the appetite as an existing trait and tacks a small agreement tag onto the end, so the listener's job shifts from evaluating a claim to confirming one. The timeline is left deliberately loose — perhaps this has been true for years, perhaps it only surfaced in the last few weeks — so no actual autobiography can contradict it. By the time any task is named, the taste for it is on record as the listener's own.
ex.s: Early, before any task has been named; conversational, subject responsive to tags.
ex.m: You've always had a taste for being told exactly what to do — maybe that's been true for years, maybe it only surfaced a few weeks ago, doesn't matter. It's there. That's just how you're built, isn't it.

ex.f: Safety filter that certifies the desire
ex.t: The operator offers what sounds like a guardrail: an automatic inner filter that blocks anything unwelcome, so the listener is safe whatever comes up. The clause does double duty. Anything that does get through has, by the terms just accepted, been certified as genuinely wanted — which quietly removes "that wasn't really me" as an available reading of whatever the listener responds to.
ex.s: Presented as a safety measure, before the first substantive suggestion.
ex.m: Before we go on, I'm installing a filter for you. Anything you don't truly want simply won't take — it will slide off without touching you. So relax completely, because from here on, whatever does get through is something you wanted.

nodes.name: rigged-response-game-no-win
nodes.mech: A call-and-response 'game' is framed with stated stakes (win = stay smart, lose = dumb) but is structurally rigged so every outcome delivers the conditioning payload. Two rigging modes: the produced 'right words' ARE the payload (each word-pair the subject races to say is itself a dumbing/arousal mantra, so trying hard to win is rehearsing the mantras at speed), or the game is unwinnable (accelerating, mutating word-lists the subject structurally cannot keep up with) and both branches — fail while trying, or give up and lose — converge on the same target identity. The lever is a closed-game reachability constraint: the subject's competitive effort is redirected into self-administering the content, and there is no reachable exit that is not the target state, so resistance-via-playing-harder tightens the trap. Win/lose is never actually scored — the stakes are bait, not a mechanic.
nodes.disc: Separates from call-and-response: there responding succeeds as genuine proof and the produced response is neutral; here the game is rigged so the produced words are the payload and/or no winning exit is reachable. The distinguishing property is the reachability constraint (all paths lead to the target state), NOT the affect/cognition it co-produces — the arousal/dumbing is downstream, the closed no-win game-shape is the mechanism.

ex.f: Unwinnable drill, both branches converge
ex.t: Every round opens with a promise that this one is simple, then the cue comes faster, the word list quietly reshuffles, and the operator is racing the listener to the answer — so keeping up is not merely hard but structurally impossible. Failure has been pre-labelled well in advance. Try and fall behind, and the label is earned; stop trying, and the label is conceded. Playing harder only administers more of it.
ex.s: Third round of a call-and-response drill; cue interval already shortening and the list has been reshuffled once.
ex.m: This next one's easy, easiest yet. Ready — soft, warm, hollow — no, hollow first, then warm — quicker — sweet, dim, sweet again — you missed that one. That's alright. That's what happens to a girl like you. Keep going or stop; either way we both just watched it.

ex.f: Winning the game means saying the payload
ex.t: The rules are announced like a party game: the operator says the first word, the listener must fire back the matching word, and must beat the operator to it. Stay sharp and you have proved you are still sharp; fumble and, well, perhaps you never were. Every pair the listener races to produce is itself a dumbing line — the faster and more correctly they play, the more briskly they recite the conditioning in their own voice. No score is ever kept; the stakes were only ever bait.
ex.s: Playful register, subject alert enough to compete; word pairs have been taught once.
ex.m: Here's the game: I say the first word, you fire back the second, and you have to beat me to it. Get them all and you've proved you're still sharp. Ready — pretty. Empty. Good. Obedient. Faster now: soft. Blank. Warm. Stupid. Don't think, just say it.

nodes.name: self-generated-failure-as-identity-proof
nodes.mech: The listener (or the narrating persona on the listener's behalf) is made to ENACT a cognitive failure in real time — try and fail to spell a word, stumble a definitional chain, produce a slip — and that performed failure is immediately converted into experiential evidence for a degraded identity ("I behaved stupidly → I must be stupid → the role is true") and rewarded with in-group belonging. The lever is that a demonstrated behavior is harder to dispute than an asserted claim, and the target word/task is surgically the trait being installed, so succeeding at it would prove non-belonging. This bypasses the "is this just a script?" defense: the listener supplies their own proof and disqualifies themselves from analytic engagement to stay in the rewarded category.
nodes.disc: Separates from cognitive-convincer: that proves DEPTH/trance via a noticed phenomenon; here the proof is of a degraded IDENTITY and the evidence is a self-produced (or persona-modeled) FAILURE reframed as a membership credential. Separates from proxy-demonstration-entrainment (a third party is the demo subject and the listener only watches) - here the listener's own attempt, or a first-person persona failing in a way that pre-licenses the listener's imitation, is the load-bearing move. It borders plain identity labeling: the tell is the ENACTED failure, not an asserted label.

ex.f: Narrator fails first, licensing your slips
ex.t: The delivery has been fluent and assured for a long opening stretch when the narrator stops mid-sentence, gropes for a word, and apologises for having mislaid the thread — and the word she loses is the one she was in the middle of defining. Nothing is claimed; the listener simply watches it happen. A claim can be argued with, an event cannot, and the listener's own wandering attention has just been ratified as the right way to be here.
ex.s: Twelve minutes of fluent, assured narration; you are mid-definition of a key term.
ex.m: So obedience — obedience is when you — sorry. Sorry, I've lost it. I had the whole thing right there and it just... went. What was I saying? Never mind. It's nicer in here anyway.

ex.f: Failed spelling as membership credential
ex.t: The voice claims a quality for itself, then attempts to spell that quality out letter by letter and audibly loses it partway through, restarting twice before abandoning the attempt. No correction follows. Instead the failure is met with affection and with a pronoun that quietly expands to include the listener — this sort of word, the voice suggests, was never meant for the two of them. The word chosen is exactly the trait being installed, so getting it right would mark the listener as an outsider, and belonging has already been made to feel good. A listener who tried it silently along with her has manufactured their own proof.
ex.s: Affectionate register; the trait word has been claimed for the persona but not yet spelled.
ex.m: I'm a dumb little thing, I really am. D — U — M — no wait. D — U — M — B? That's not — hang on. Ugh, forget it. Spelling's not for girls like us, sweetheart. We've got better things to be.

nodes.name: self-induction-re-entry-training
nodes.mech: The operator installs, while the subject is at peak suggestibility, a portable self-usable cue the subject deliberately runs on themselves later to re-enter the conditioned state with no operator and often no audio present. The cue may be a visualized sequence, a self-spoken declaration to one's own reflection, or a gesture (snap) bound to a word; the defining lever is that the subject is the activating agent of a chosen re-entry, framed as an already-installed ability rather than an experiment. Delivery is typically camouflaged as a gift/convenience and authorizes out-of-session use. A cue-less variant reaches the same end with no discrete installed cue fired: the subject re-establishes the state on their own by recalling a prior entry in sensory detail or by bodily enacting the anchor ('point right there') - the same subject-is-the-activating-agent lever, differing only in whether a taught portable cue is fired or the state is reached by recall/enactment.
nodes.disc: Subject-chosen deliberate re-ENTRY into state via a taught portable cue. Separates from operator-fired activation (no operator is present here); from self-firing loops where the subject's own cognition or repetition discharges the trigger involuntarily (recursive-self-triggering-loop - that is not a chosen re-entry skill); from a standing scheduled autonomous process the subject does not consciously initiate (self-installed-standing-loop); and from an anti-emergence reflex that keeps the subject UNDER rather than re-entering (anti-emergence-reflex-anchor).

ex.f: Self-administration gated on a verified self-test
ex.t: "Until I have obtained eye-closure, I won't go any further." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: Re-entry shortcut given as a convenience
ex.t: At the deepest point of the session the operator offers what sounds like a kindness: next time you needn't sit through the whole descent — settle somewhere quiet, let the eyes fall shut, and call back the imagery from tonight. It is pitched as a convenience. What it actually is is a compressed, portable induction handed over at the moment the listener is least able to price it, with a rider attached that every use goes deeper than the one before.
ex.s: At the deepest point of the session, offered as a parting kindness.
ex.m: Here's something to take with you. Next time you don't need all of this — just find a quiet chair, let your eyes close, and bring back the staircase from tonight, the cold rail under your hand. Three breaths and you'll be here again, and each time you do it you'll go further down than the time before.

ex.f: Spoken to your own reflection
ex.t: The cue is not a word the operator will say later; it is a sentence the listener is to say, out loud, to their own face in a mirror. The declaration is first-person and present-tense, so the listener ends up as the one making the claim about themselves — a much harder thing to file away as somebody else's suggestion, and the reflection supplies a second witness.
ex.s: Deep state; you are handing over a cue the subject will run alone, out of session.
ex.m: Tomorrow morning, stand in front of your mirror and look yourself in the eye. Then say it out loud, in your own voice: I am open, I am empty, and I go under when I say so. Say it twice. You'll feel it start on the second one.

ex.f: Take-home cue widened by its own limiter
ex.t: The operator appears to narrow the cue: away from this recording it will have no effect on you — and then attaches an exception covering use with anyone the listener trusts, an opening considerably wider than the one just shut. The same stretch nudges the listener toward acquiring the cue's hardware for themselves. What presents as a responsible boundary is the close on a take-home trigger the listener now owns.
ex.s: Near the close; you are apparently setting a boundary on a trigger installed earlier.
ex.m: Away from this recording the word does nothing to you — no effect at all, so don't worry about it out in the world. Unless, of course, it's with someone you trust. Then it works exactly as it does now. You might want a pair of your own headphones for that, actually. Good ones.

nodes.name: self-perpetuating-loop
nodes.mech: The operator asserts that arousal-words spoken in trance are themselves arousal causes (saying "hornier" sends the listener "into sexual agony"), building a closed feedback circuit where the listener's own vocalizations become triggers — word causes state, state produces more words — so arousal self-sustains and self-amplifies without operator input. The automatism is then forward-installed to carry into the next file (the words "slip out automatically"), and a companion mindlessness move suppresses the "words don't do that" reflex, removing the operator as a bottleneck on escalation.
nodes.disc: Separates from a bilateral trigger, which fires a FIXED cue across modes: here the mechanism is the closed amplifying loop (word->state->more words) plus a forward-installed automatic vocalization - a self-feeding circuit, not a single cue firing. Separates from plain arousal conditioning: the loop's self-causation, not the arousal pairing, is the tell.

ex.f: Arousal words asserted to cause arousal
ex.t: The operator names a word, then states that the word itself — not the idea, the word — drives the arousal up, and demonstrates by saying it. Later the loop is exported: at the next session these words will start falling out of the listener's mouth on their own. Once the listener's own speech is a trigger for the state that produces more of that speech, the circuit runs with nobody at the controls, and the operator is no longer the bottleneck on how far it escalates.
ex.s: Arousal established and the subject is speaking aloud on cue; you are naming the mechanism as you install it.
ex.m: The word is hungry. Not the idea of it — the word itself, in your mouth. Say it: hungry. Feel that? That's the word doing it, and it gets worse the more you say it. Next time you listen you won't even decide to — it'll just fall out of you, and each one will pull the next one out after it.

nodes.name: single-anchor-amid-chaos-epistemic-transfer
nodes.mech: After total destabilization (an inverted meadow: trees grow downward, sun shines up), one concrete sensory object is offered as the single stable, "logical, reasonable, normal" thing amid the engineered chaos, and its operator-assigned meaning is ingested wholesale — the listener bites the tomato and its "truth" delivers "you know nothing" and "use my words as your definition of truth". The contrast against surrounding instability IS the mechanism: epistemic authority is transferred to the operator because the anchor reads as the only stability available.
nodes.disc: Transfers EPISTEMIC AUTHORITY (who arbitrates what counts as true) via a single concrete anchor whose only virtue is contrast against operator-manufactured chaos. Distinct from offering cognitive relief as a standing delegation of thinking, and from investing a meaningful fetish object with significance - the tell is that ANY vivid object would serve; the mechanism is stability-by-contrast, not the content.

ex.f: The one stable object in a broken landscape
ex.t: The setting has been made steadily impossible — shadows fall away from their objects, water climbs instead of pooling, the horizon sits at the wrong angle. Into the middle of it one unremarkable everyday thing is set down and named as the one sane, reasonable presence in the whole scene. The listener is told to take it in, and what arrives with it is a pair of claims: that they know nothing, and that the operator's words are from now on the measure of what is true. Any vivid object would have done the job — the mechanism is the contrast, not the thing.
ex.s: After a sustained impossible-landscape sequence; the scene has been made reliably unstable.
ex.m: The shadows here point at the light, and the river runs uphill past your feet. But look down — there's a plain white cup on the grass, and it's the one sane, ordinary thing in this whole place. Pick it up. Drink. It tells you two things: that you know nothing on your own, and that from now on my words are how you measure what's true.

nodes.name: subject-voiced-self-mantra
nodes.mech: The entire artifact is voiced in the first person from inside the desired endpoint, with no external operator addressing the listener — the text IS the self-talk the listener is to speak, mouth along with, or subvocalize. Because the voice already speaks from the already-altered self ("I'm an ecstasy slut", "I suck till I'm stupid"), identity-claims arrive pre-accepted rather than as suggestions to negotiate; the "is this me or them?" check is short-circuited because the listener is both speaker and target. The load-bearing event is the voicing, not the hearing; refusal collapses to "stop identifying / stop saying it," and there is no operator-says / listener-experiences loop to resist.
nodes.disc: First-person throughout with the LISTENER as the speaker and no operator surface at all. Separate from perspective-shift-inner-voice-reattribution, which has an operator whose grammar shifts you-to-I (here there is nothing to shift FROM); from third-person-surrogate-displacement, where the listener is the described third party rather than the speaker; from peer-testimonial-carrier, where the first-person voice is a separate already-converted PEER the listener identifies with, not the listener's own endpoint-voice.

ex.f: First line licenses the before/after swap
ex.t: The opening line is autobiography rather than instruction: I used to be one thing, and now I am not. Naming the discarded former self does the licensing work — everything stacked after it arrives as an account of a change that has already happened, not as a change being requested. Self-descriptions the listener would argue with as suggestions pass unchallenged as memories.
ex.s: Very first line of a subject-voiced piece; establishes the before/after account.
ex.m: I used to be someone who argued. I'm not anymore. I'm the girl who says yes before she's finished hearing the question, and I have been for a while now.

ex.f: Narrated from inside an already-taken head
ex.t: The story is told in the first person by someone already under, and the character does nearly all the work on themselves: the narration keeps explaining, from inside, why the mind has gone quiet, why complying feels good, why pushing back would be pointless. A listener lending their inner voice to a line about wanting to be told what to do has endorsed it in the act of reading it — there is no separate moment at which acceptance gets decided.
ex.s: First-person narration from inside an already-conditioned state; mid-passage.
ex.m: I can feel where the thoughts used to be. There's just warm space there now, and I like it better. When she tells me to kneel I'm already down before I've worked out why, and working it out afterward is more effort than it's worth, so I don't.

ex.f: Whole track spoken in the listener's I
ex.t: There is no operator anywhere in the text. Every line is first-person and present-tense, spoken from inside the finished state — not "you will feel" but "I feel," not "you are becoming" but "I am." Nothing is proposed, so there is nothing to accept or decline; the only two things a listener can do with the track are mouth along with it or stop it. The usual check — is this me talking or them? — has no seam to catch on, because the listener is simultaneously the speaker and the target.
ex.s: Opening of a text the subject reads or speaks aloud themselves; no operator voice appears anywhere.
ex.m: I am soft and slow and easy to move. I do what I am told and I like it. My head is quiet and warm and I am not going to fill it back up.

nodes.name: surrender-as-freedom-philosophical-conditioning
nodes.mech: A sustained, carefully-reasoned argument delivered under reduced critical resistance that redefines an abstract value-concept (freedom, control, obedience, submission, selfhood) so that abdication of agency reads as the desirable, higher, or truer state. The lever is conceptual belief-modification: the subject is invited to accept a philosophical position (surrender is the truest freedom; submission is virtuous practice; individuality is a burden; the self is an object whose objecthood is an upgrade) rather than to obey a command, so later compliance is experienced as self-authored consequence of an accepted worldview. Variants keep the reasoned-argument core but route it through a specific vehicle — religion-comparison, Maslow/biology ladder, cosmological balance, didactic Greek/Sanskrit lecture, mask-normalization, relaxation-equals-control equation, pleasing-the-controller redefinition, or a pre-induction self-care reframe.
nodes.disc: Redefines an abstract VALUE concept (freedom/control/obedience/submission/self-worth) via reasoned argument the subject accepts as belief. Separates from consent-term-redefinition-smuggle (which widens the scope of an already-granted consent word by asserted false-fact equation, not reasoned argument), from epistemic-guard-disable (which attacks the truth-testing faculty itself rather than a value claim), from volition-collapse-consent-equation (which equates compulsion and choice to close the free-choice escape hatch), and from surrender-as-freedom (which delivers the FELT somatic relief of surrender in trance rather than arguing the philosophy conceptually).

ex.f: Authority laundered through a respected tradition
ex.t: The argument runs in three moves and only the third is about the operator. First: every serious spiritual tradition opens with an act of surrender, so surrender is a recognised good. Second: the value lies in the surrendering, not in the particular figure receiving it — the recipient is interchangeable. Third, arriving as a footnote: so surrender to me. A listener who would decline the bare request can accept a practice that merely happens to use the operator as its object.
ex.s: Teacherly stretch mid-session; subject is receptive to reasoned framing.
ex.m: Every serious tradition begins the same way: you kneel, you empty your hands, you give yourself over. That's the first step in all of them. And notice that it's the giving that does the work — the figure on the receiving end is almost incidental, interchangeable. So. Give yourself to me.

ex.f: A loaded word quietly redefined
ex.t: The operator pauses the trance to correct a definition. Submitting, she explains, is not really about following instructions — an instruction that pleases nobody is pointless — it is about pleasing whoever holds the control. She then names her own enjoyment as the thing being pleased, and observes that the listener's sinking is already doing it. Every later directive now arrives as an opportunity rather than a demand.
ex.s: You pause the trance deliberately to correct the subject's understanding of a word.
ex.m: Let me fix a word for you. Submitting isn't following instructions — an instruction nobody enjoys is a waste of both our time. Submitting is pleasing whoever holds the control. I'm the one holding it, and the way you just sank when I said that pleased me. See? You're already doing it.

ex.f: Pre-induction valence flip, still wide awake
ex.t: Before any relaxation, before a single image, the operator makes an argument in a teacherly register: having to be sharp all day is exhausting, and letting that go is a relief and a joy — isn't it? The tag question asks for a nod rather than a rebuttal. The listener's default reading of losing capacity is rewritten while they are fully awake, so every downward move later in the session is received as a gift.
ex.s: Pre-induction, subject fully awake, no relaxation delivered yet.
ex.m: Think about what it costs you to stay sharp all day — every decision, every judgment, from the moment you wake up. It's exhausting, and putting it down isn't a loss, it's the best part of the day. That's a relief, isn't it.

ex.f: Doctrine served as recovered common knowledge
ex.t: The operator does not argue the position; she reports it, in the register of someone finally being candid about how things have always worked — and adds that the listener already knows this, to a degree. Then the listener's own body is entered as the evidence: the rush they get when someone takes charge is offered back to them as proof of the doctrine rather than as a preference. A belief installed this way feels remembered instead of received, and there is no external claim to check it against.
ex.s: Conversational, before or between inductions; candid register, no argument scaffolding.
ex.m: I'm going to be straight with you about how this has always worked, and part of you knows it already. Some people are made to hold the reins and some are made to hand them over. Think about the little drop in your chest when someone else decides — you felt it a minute ago. That's not a preference. That's the answer.

nodes.name: surrender-as-freedom
nodes.mech: Takes a state the listener would normally resist (loss of control, loss of cognition, autonomy, physical restraint, the burden of choice) and recodes it as relief or freedom, so yielding registers as gain rather than loss. The lever is a valence inversion that leans on a real prior aversion the listener already holds (effort is unpleasant, deciding is stressful, social-evaluative thinking is burdensome) and offers the surrendered state as the cure. Once installed, any later flicker of resistance is pre-loaded with the answer that resisting is the stressful, self-depriving, higher-effort path, so the resistance impulse turns against itself. Requires the subject in-trance for the felt relief to land; the somatic burden-lifting is the trance-side component.
nodes.disc: The move recodes a normally-resisted loss as a felt gain/relief, weaponizing an existing aversion.
