In every case the form removes exit ramps and carries the payload, and a text pipeline would mis-parse the form as noise.
nodes.disc: Separates from a discrete deepener by being a property of the whole-file surface form (punctuation, cadence, formatting) rather than any single block. Separates from external-artifact-coupling by binding the script's OWN linguistic form, not an external listener-supplied medium. Separates from aesthetic-cover-payload-delivery by having no distinct aesthetic object (song) — the plain prose form is itself the carrier.

ex.f: A doubled cadence the payload rides inside
ex.t: Nearly every line says its key phrase twice, in slightly varied form, for a long stretch before anything is asked for. Working memory goes to tracking the small variations rather than comparing claims. When the actual directive arrives it is doubled in exactly the same shape, so it inherits the accumulated weight of the refrain without being argued for — and at the end, the one undoubled line is felt as a change of state.
ex.s: Twenty or more doubled lines have already run; this is the beat where the actual directive arrives inside the established cadence.
ex.m: So heavy now, so wonderfully heavy. So still now, so completely still. And obedient now — so easily, easily obedient. So simple, so simple to do as I say.

ex.f: Language decaying where the trance is deepest
ex.t: The whole piece is a single unbroken paragraph with no place for the voice to pause. Around the deepest stretches the punctuation softens and words stop resolving into words at all, drifting into sound; the coherence returns as the script climbs back out. The shape enacts the content, and the garbled passages are not defects to clean up — they mark where meaning has been replaced by texture.
ex.s: The deepest stretch of a continuous prose-poem piece; delivered as one unbroken breath-run with the voice thinning out.
ex.m: deeper than the words go now and the words are going soft at the edges saoft and slurring and the meaning slipping out of them mmmshhh… lisss… ning… nnnn… — and slowly the shapes come back, one at a time, and the sounds are words again, and you are still down here where they left you.

ex.f: One comma-spliced block with no exit ramp
ex.t: There are almost no full stops in the entire script — no paragraphs, no headings, no marked beats, just one long breath-run of clauses hinged on commas. A punctuated script hands the listener a small landing every few seconds on which to surface and disagree; this one hands out none until the wakener. The surface form is doing the induction, and the named techniques are just operating inside it.
ex.s: The whole script is written this way from the first line; there are no full stops until the wakener.
ex.m: and you're breathing out now, slower than the breath before it, and that slowness is spreading, down through your jaw, your throat, your chest, and there's nowhere here for you to stop and think about it, no gap, no pause, just the next thing and the next, my voice carrying straight on through, heavier, and heavier, and you can't quite find the edge of one thought before the following one has already started, so you stop looking for edges, and you just come with it, down, and down

nodes.name: external-artifact-coupling
nodes.mech: The session is structurally built around the listener operating an EXTERNAL, listener-supplied artifact during trance — viewing their own curated arousal images and touching themselves — and that external task is load-bearing for the core conditioning to land. Remove the images and roughly 70 percent of the mechanisms lose their referent (nothing to fractionate against, no autonomous behavior to attribute, no variable to amplify). The operator deliberately conditions against material she has never seen, so the conditioning generalizes across the listener's entire personal erotic library by design: the listener-supplied artifact is the conditioned-stimulus side of every installed association.
nodes.disc: Separates from background scenery or optional visualization (which are removable) by the artifact being load-bearing — without it the core mechanisms have no referent. Separates from delivery-form-as-induction-envelope by binding an EXTERNAL listener-supplied medium rather than the script's own linguistic form. Distinct from arousal-cue conditioning: this is the artifact-coupling DESIGN structure of the whole session, not merely a specification of which conditioned stimulus that conditioning should use.

ex.f: The listener's own images as the conditioned stimulus
ex.t: The session is not a thing to lie back and receive: the listener is instructed to bring up their own saved arousal pictures and work through them while the audio runs. Take the pictures away and most of the recording loses its referent — there is nothing to be pulled back and forth from, no autonomous behavior to point at, no rising variable to amplify. And because the operator has never seen the material, the conditioning is not aimed at any one image; it is aimed at whatever the listener already keeps, so it generalizes across the entire private collection by design.
ex.s: Session opening; the subject is at their own device with their private collection accessible and one hand free.
ex.m: Before we begin: open your own folder — the pictures you actually keep, the ones you go back to. Not something I've chosen, yours. Have the first one up on the screen where you can see it without moving, and start touching yourself, slowly, while you look at it. Every minute or so, move to the next one. Whatever's in there is what we're working with tonight.

nodes.name: whole-script-arc-shape-architecture
nodes.mech: A design-time CONTAINER (not a single script-executable move) holding a family of whole-script structural properties — corpus-shape observations about how a script's arc, energy contour, or topology is engineered, each uncitable to one line. Instances gathered here: a bipartite install-then-deploy architecture joined by a sensitizing hinge; a steady migration of control from internal suggestion to external felt body-hardware as a commitment device; a monotonic arousal ramp with one deliberate plateau-interrupt engineering a single high-leverage compliance window; an A-B-A loop with a mutated middle pass wrapped by a daily-re-read instruction; AA rhyming couplets acting as a covert forward-pull pacing metronome; a didactic-then-applied two-act structure factoring the deepener out as a reusable function; a single-word saturation session whose whole body is a trigger-construction; a two-chamber architecture with a recited consent form as the airlock converting browser to subject; a ~2:1 induction-to-payload ratio treating depth as the gating constraint; an ordered selfhood-erosion / domain-capture staircase where sequence is load-bearing; and an expanding-radius scope funnel (session -> emotional life -> other people) culminating in recruitment.
nodes.disc: Not any single operator move — each member is a property of the whole energy contour / arc / topology, uncitable to one line, and non-script-executable (a design-time / observation property). Distinct from carrier-frame-payload-smuggling, which is a concealment RELATIONSHIP (a cover frame smuggling a payload) rather than a whole-arc shape. This is a deliberately loose grouping of whole-script shapes, NOT a claim these members share one mechanism.

ex.f: Bipartite install-then-deploy arc joined by a sensitizing hinge
ex.t: The arc separates the labour of construction from the pleasure of deployment, so the second half never has to justify itself — it just fires. The hinge line is the observable checkpoint: if the spoken word lands flat, the install half was short, and deploying anyway burns the trigger. Operators watch for a breath change or a pause before the subject repeats the word.
ex.s: Design-time: you are laying out a full-length session that must install a trigger AND use it in the same sitting.
ex.m: Front half, closing beat: "Everything you have accepted so far has a name, and the name is the word 'settle'. You have not heard me use it yet in the way I am about to." Hinge: "Say the word once, out loud, and notice how much heavier it already is than any other word in your mouth." Back half, opening beat: "Settle. And again — settle. From here on I will not explain it; I will only use it."

ex.f: Monotonic arousal ramp with a single plateau-interrupt cut as a compliance window
ex.t: The withheld release converts accumulated arousal into a demand for instruction, and the plateau is the only moment in the arc where any instruction is cheaper to obey than to argue with. The observable is compliance latency: the recitation comes back fast and unedited at a true peak, slow and paraphrased if the ramp was under-built.
ex.s: Design-time: an arousal-track session where you need exactly one high-leverage instruction to land unresisted.
ex.m: At the ramp's peak: "Stop. Hands flat, don't move them, don't finish." Hold silence for a slow count of ten, then: "While you're right there, wanting it and not having it — repeat after me: I ask, and I wait to be told." Then release: "Good. Now you may go on, and you will go on hearing that sentence under everything."

ex.f: Expanding-radius scope funnel ending in recruitment
ex.t: Each movement is a small step from the one before, so no single widening reads as an overreach, while the total displacement — session to emotional life to third parties — is large. The tell that the funnel is holding is that the subject volunteers the outward step themselves at the next session ("I did it to my partner without thinking").
ex.s: Design-time: a series arc whose last movement widens the technique's jurisdiction outward from the session.
ex.m: Movement one: "For the next hour, my voice decides what you think about." Movement two: "Tomorrow, when something makes you anxious, you will hear this cadence before you hear the anxiety." Movement three: "And when someone close to you is tense, you will find yourself speaking slowly, in this rhythm, without deciding to. When they ask why it works, you will know where to send them."

nodes.name: affect-fused-identity
nodes.mech: The identity label is welded to a self-firing affect (pride/euphoria on BEING the category, fired by the name-token) or to a categorical can't/self-betrayal modal, so being the category is itself rewarding and its violation intrinsically aversive; the label maintains and defends itself without further operator input. Variants: 'always been' backdating erasing the install seam, a binary good-girl/bad-girl self-audit classifier over checkable behaviors, degrading labels welded to affection terms, depth made contingent on endorsing the label, a saturating negation-in-the-assent-slot flipped into affirmation, and an asymmetric moral economy where the positive pole carries the bundle and the negative is a contentless void.
nodes.disc: The distinguishing move is welding the label to a self-firing affect or categorical-incapacity modal so the identity becomes intrinsically rewarding or its violation aversive. Separates from plain identity-labeling (declarative label, no fused affect engine) and from reward-association conditioning (conditions a discrete behavior to a reward, not category-membership to self-firing affect).

ex.f: Name-token firing pride — the label is its own reward
ex.t: The affect is bound to the token rather than to any behavior, so the category maintains itself between sessions with no operator present — hearing or thinking the word pays out. Observable: an involuntary smile or a hand drifting toward the sternum on the third repetition.
ex.s: Mid-session, subject settled, a category noun has already been used a handful of times descriptively.
ex.m: "Every time you hear that word said about you — every single time — there's a warm bloom right at the top of your chest, just under the collarbone. You don't have to do anything to earn it. It comes because the word is true. Listen: it's true. There it is again."

ex.f: Categorical can't-modal — violation as self-betrayal
ex.t: The aversion is presented as evidence of category membership rather than as a prohibition, so any felt discomfort — including ordinary hesitation — confirms the identity. The operator watches for a headshake or a grimace on the imagined transgression, which is the modal reporting itself.
ex.s: Late session, after the label has been accepted and the subject is compliant.
ex.m: "Try it: think about lying to me right now. Not doing it — just picture forming the sentence. Feel that? That flat, wrong drop in your stomach. That's not a rule I gave you. That's what happens when someone tries to do something they aren't."

ex.f: 'Always been' backdating that erases the install seam
ex.t: Backdating removes the install moment from the timeline, so there is no seam to unpick and no operator to hold responsible for the label. Observable: the subject begins supplying their own corroborating memories unprompted, which is the identity now defending itself.
ex.s: Any point after the label has been accepted once; used to close off the memory of it being given.
ex.m: "Go back to being nine years old. The way you'd wait to be told which one to pick, and how much easier that was than choosing. That was already this. I didn't put anything in you tonight — I just told you the name of something that has been running your whole life."

nodes.name: answer-supply-loop
nodes.mech: The operator poses a question but PRE-FILLS the response — either by answering it herself before the subject can respond ('Are you relaxed? Of course you are.'), by tag-questions immediately closed with 'that's right' and no pause, or by voicing the subject's yes-stream at a tempo faster than analytic thought. Denying a real response window means the operator's supplied answer is absorbed AS IF it were the subject's own; the yes/no decision is relocated from subject to operator while the subject still feels like they are answering. The accumulating stream of pre-filled yeses manufactures a felt history of agreement and installs a frictionless compliance channel. Includes the interrogative-convergence variant where every possible answer increments the same counter.
nodes.disc: Separates from call-and-response (nearest neighbor): there the subject PRODUCES a response on cue; here the operator supplies the answer and denies a response window, so no real produced response exists. Separates from the yes-set / compliance ladder (which drifts toward genuine agreement); here agreement is manufactured by pre-fill or a rigged question whose every answer confirms.

ex.f: Question answered by the operator before the window opens
ex.t: Each supplied answer is absorbed as the subject's own because there was no gap in which to form a competing one; the stack of them builds a felt history of agreeing. Observable: by the third pre-fill the subject stops attempting to answer at all, which is the compliance channel opening.
ex.s: Early induction, subject's eyes closed, breathing already slowing.
ex.m: "Comfortable? Of course you are — look at your shoulders. Warm enough? You are, I can hear it. And you're glad you started this tonight, aren't you? You are. Good girl."

ex.f: Tag questions closed with 'that's right' on no pause
ex.t: The closer occupies the response slot, so the tag never functions as a real question while still carrying the grammar of one — the subject experiences having agreed without having spoken. The tell is that the subject's head begins nodding on the tag and settles before the closer arrives.
ex.s: Deepening phase, operator on a steady unbroken cadence.
ex.m: "Heavier now, isn't it — that's right. Easier not to think, isn't it — that's right. And you'd rather I kept talking than stopped, wouldn't you — that's right, that's right."

ex.f: Interrogative convergence — every answer increments the same counter
ex.t: The question is rigged so that both branches confirm the same proposition, which means the subject's genuine choice still produces the operator's outcome. Observable: the subject deliberates over the two options — engagement with the false frame is itself the acceptance.
ex.s: Mid-session, where you want an apparent choice that cannot produce a no.
ex.m: "So tell me — did it start with my voice, or did it start before you pressed play? Whichever it is, you've been under longer than you thought. And do you want more of this, or do you just need it? Either answer, you're staying."

nodes.name: behavioral-commitment-self-proof
nodes.mech: The listener is directed to perform a discrete act in-session — a physical movement (nod, open hands, posture, squeeze) or a spoken/written utterance — and the act is read back to them as self-evidence that the target state is already true. The lever is self-perception plus effort/consistency: because the listener performed the act, later compliance feels self-originated and refusal would require repudiating something they just did. Covers verbal and written acts alongside physical ones, including orgasm/release gated on self-attributed submission claims, forced first-person recitations, calibrated-transgression probes, begging-gates, embodied yes-tokens, public confessions, and proprioceptive posture-reads.
nodes.disc: Confirms/embodies a state the induction is already producing (in-session state-proof). Vs pre-induction-compliance-ratchet — that banks compliance in the WAKING state before induction (binding-time is structural). Vs pre-authorization-consent-contract — that establishes a standing blanket authorization drawn down across the session; this reads a single in-session act back. Vs self-authored-compliance-content — there the listener GENERATES the content; here they perform an operator-supplied act. Vs call-and-response — here the performed act asserts a self-attributed state/identity rather than serving as neutral pacing. And vs physical exhibition — this is act-as-self-read-proof, not display-posture.

ex.f: Physical act read back as self-evidence
ex.t: The subject performed a small, low-cost act freely, and the read-back converts it into evidence of a state they never asserted; refusing later suggestions now requires repudiating their own hands. Observable: the palms stay up after the read-back without being told to, which is the self-attribution taking.
ex.s: Mid-session, subject responsive, no prior claim about their state has been made.
ex.m: "Turn your palms up, both of them, and let them rest open on your thighs. Do it now. There. Nobody made you do that with your hands — you did. That's what an open person's hands look like, and yours have been sitting like that for ten seconds already."

ex.f: Spoken first-person recitation as the act
ex.t: The utterance is a discrete act with a speaker, and pointing at the speaker relocates the claim's authorship from operator to subject. The operator listens for volume: a second repetition louder than the first is the consistency lever engaging.
ex.s: After a deepener, when the subject is willing to speak but has not yet claimed anything about themselves.
ex.m: "Say it out loud, in your own voice, exactly as I give it: 'I like being told.' Again, slower. Now — I didn't say that. You did, twice, and you meant it enough to say it the second time."

ex.f: Written act banked as durable self-proof
ex.t: A written artifact outlives the session's state, so the self-proof remains available to be re-read when trance has lifted and skepticism has returned. Observable: hesitation at the underline is the real consent check; a subject who underlines without pausing has already accepted the frame.
ex.s: Pre-close or a waking segment, subject has paper or a phone to hand.
ex.m: "Write this down, in your handwriting: today's date, and then 'I asked for this.' Underline it. You'll find that later, in your own hand, and there'll be nobody to blame it on."

nodes.name: catalepsy-to-affect-transfer
nodes.mech: A body-verifiable involuntary convincer the listener has just demonstrated to themselves (finger/eyelid/arm catalepsy they can check) is used as the warrant for a parallel claim about an UNVERIFIABLE domain — emotion, belief, or arousal the listener never tested. The lever is cross-domain credibility transfer: lived somatic proof lends its undeniability to a manufactured claim, so arguing against the payload becomes structurally identical to arguing against locked eyelids, hence self-evidently futile. The convincer is deliberately over-invested because it is load-bearing collateral. Two transfer surfaces: (a) explicit analogy pivot onto emotion/belief ('your feelings are just like your fingers now'; 'resisting the feeling only tightens its grip, just like your eyelids') — the tell is the overt post-hoc 'those feelings are just like the feelings in your eyelids'; (b) covert lexical bridge onto arousal — the identical phrase ('stiff and rigid', applied first to the arm then to the penis) is reused unchanged so the reattribution is invisible and the listener extends their verified-by-body experience without noticing the jump. Choose (a) when the transfer can be argued openly; (b) when it must slip past notice.
nodes.disc: Reach for THIS when you have a rock-solid MOTOR convincer and want to extend its authority to something you cannot demonstrate. The move is the TRANSFER of demonstrated physical incapacity onto an unverifiable emotional/belief/arousal claim, not the catalepsy itself. Variant tells: the explicit-analogy variant shows an overt pivot ('just like your eyelids'); the covert-lexical variant shows an identical phrase reused verbatim on a second body region/state. Separates from motor-inhibition-convincer (ends at proof-of-depth on the checkable limb — no transfer). Separates from arousal conditioning (there arousal is paired with a cue over repetition; here a one-shot transfer of already-proven involuntariness). Separates from self-validating-language (routes the subject's own present output back; here a PRIOR verified somatic proof is lent forward to an untested claim).

ex.f: Explicit analogy pivot from locked eyelids onto emotion
ex.t: The eyelid failure is undeniable first-person evidence, and the overt pivot borrows its undeniability for a claim about wanting that the subject never tested. Observable: the subject stops arguing the emotional point entirely — the argument now feels structurally identical to arguing with their own eyes.
ex.s: The subject has just tried and failed to open their eyes and knows it.
ex.m: "You just tried. Your whole will, right there, and the lids didn't move — you felt exactly how much use trying was. Now: the wanting you've been arguing with all week is made of the same stuff. Push against it and it locks harder, just like your eyelids. You already know how that ends, because you just tested it."

ex.f: Covert lexical bridge — the same phrase reused on a second body region
ex.t: The verbatim repetition of the phrase does the transfer without ever announcing a comparison, so there is no analogy for the subject to evaluate or reject. The tell that it landed is the subject reporting the second sensation as discovered rather than suggested.
ex.s: Arm catalepsy is established and the subject has verified it by trying to bend the elbow.
ex.m: "Stiff and rigid, locked straight, nothing you do softens it — that arm belongs to me now. Stiff and rigid. And down between your legs, stiff and rigid, exactly the same, locked the same way, for the same reason."

nodes.name: cognitive-convincer
nodes.mech: The operator stages or points at an in-session phenomenon the subject themselves notices (a felt amnesia gap, a time gap, arm/eyelid catalepsy, a slowed pulse, a manufactured sensation, an autonomic lull) and frames that noticed experience as the subject's own proof that trance/depth/an install is real. The lever is self-attribution: because the evidence arrives through the subject's own perception rather than operator assertion, the subject co-authors the belief. The phenomenon may be genuine, rigged-to-succeed (autonomic claims any relaxed body confirms), or reattributed (existing arousal/stillness relabeled) — the constant is a recognition beat where noticing the effect IS accepting the depth.
nodes.disc: Separates from unfalsifiable-no-fail-convincer (closes the failure branch so ANY outcome including feeling-nothing confirms), from operator-side-state-verification (reads state FOR the operator, subject never told), and from staged-external-reality-corroboration (manufactures external sense-channel events rather than an internally-noticed phenomenon). Against amnesia-suggestion and time-distortion installs, the tell is the recognition beat — here the amnesia/time-distortion is a demonstration device the subject interprets, not installed as an end.

ex.f: Reattributed autonomic lull framed as the subject's own proof
ex.t: The phenomenon is real but inevitable in any relaxed body, so the recognition beat cannot fail, and the evidence arrives through the subject's own count rather than the operator's claim. Observable: the pause after "weren't they" — a subject who nods slowly there has co-authored the depth claim.
ex.s: Ten minutes into an induction, breathing has visibly slowed on its own.
ex.m: "Before I say anything else — count your own breaths for the next fifteen seconds. Go. ... Fewer than you'd take sitting at your desk, weren't they. You didn't slow those down; nobody told you to. That's your body telling you where you already are."

ex.f: Staged amnesia gap used as a demonstration device
ex.t: The gap is genuine and the subject discovers it by searching, so the conclusion is self-attributed rather than asserted; the amnesia is a measuring instrument here, not an install. The operator watches for the search itself — a brief frown and then a headshake is the noticing beat firing.
ex.s: Following a long monotone stretch where attention has certainly drifted at least once.
ex.m: "Quick — what was the last thing I said before I mentioned your hands? Don't strain for it. You can't find it, can you. It's not gone; you just weren't there for it. People who are awake don't have holes like that."

nodes.name: conceded-capacity-immobility
nodes.mech: Instead of suggesting literal inability, the operator explicitly CONCEDES that the listener could move if they wanted to ('I know you easily could'), then reframes stillness as a lack of motivation rather than loss of capacity — asserting that not-wanting-to-move and not-being- able-to-move are functionally identical. The lever is pre-emptive defusal of the depth-test: the standard light-trance self-test ('can I still move?') is decoupled from the trance claim, so a successful movement produces no disconfirmation — the finding is pre-converted from 'induction failed' to 'induction is working, I'm too relaxed to care'.
nodes.disc: The defining surface is the explicit concession of capability coupled with a want=can't equivalence that neutralizes the movement test. Separates from motor-inhibition-convincer, which asserts/demonstrates inability and INVITES the test — here the test is disarmed by agreeing with it in advance, so nothing is offered to disprove.

ex.f: Capability conceded, stillness reattributed to not-wanting
ex.t: Conceding capacity in advance strips the movement test of its disconfirming power — a hand that lifts now proves nothing, because nothing was claimed about the hand. Observable: subjects who do test it typically move once and let the hand fall back, and that fall is the reframe holding rather than failing.
ex.s: Early-to-mid trance, before the subject has run the private 'can I still move?' test.
ex.m: "You could lift that hand right now. I know you could — easily, any time you like, and nothing would break. But you're not going to, because you don't want to, and down here not wanting to and not being able to are the same thing. Go on and check if you like; it won't tell you anything you don't already know."

nodes.name: identity-from-coerced-behavior
nodes.mech: The identity is derived from an already-installed compelled behavior ('a good name for a girl who can't stop bobbing her head') so it reads as a descriptive observation rather than an imposed label, deflecting 'this isn't me' resistance; a morphological/phonetic trigger is then welded (Bobbi a substring of bobbing) so name and behavior mutually validate and the trigger surface broadens invisibly. The lever is behavioral backfill: refusing the label means denying an observable fact.
nodes.disc: Identity is SOURCED FROM observable coerced behavior plus a morphological trigger-capture, distinct from identity-labeling (asserted label) and affect-fused-identity (label welded to affect).

ex.f: Name sourced from the compelled behavior, with a sound-substring weld
ex.t: The label arrives as an observation about a fact the subject can see themselves performing, so 'that isn't me' would require denying the motion in progress. The sound-overlap then makes each occurrence of the behavior a covert utterance of the name, broadening the trigger without further installs; the operator watches for the bob to speed up on the name.
ex.s: A repeated head-bob has already been installed and is running visibly on cue.
ex.m: "Look at you. You haven't stopped bobbing that head since I asked, and you're not going to. Girls who bob like that get called something — and I think you already know what it is. Bobbi. It was sitting inside the word the whole time. Say your name for me while you're still bobbing."

nodes.name: identity-labeling
nodes.mech: The operator attaches an identity label (noun-category or trait) and delivers it as already-true, frequently by pacing a state the subject is currently having and then naming that state as the identity, so acceptance reads as recognition rather than assignment; the label steers subsequent behavior because instructions address an already-claimed self and resistance is raised to an identity-level cost. Delivery may be flat assertion, a discovery/'true nature' reframe, an 'always been' backdating, a proliferating stack of overlapping nouns, a staged-accidental slip, paratext presupposition, a gradient argue-assert-name-affirm, or a wake-threshold identity seal. This is the general base form: operator-delivered, subject-accepted labeling.
nodes.disc: Operator asserts/paces an identity label the subject accepts as descriptively true of themselves. Separates from consent-manufacture (labels an identity, not an authorization) and from self-validating language (supplies a self-noticed confirmation, not the label). The structural, self-authored, affect-fused, and self-erasure variants each have their own entries.

ex.f: Flat assertion of a noun-category delivered as already-true
ex.t: Delivering the label as description rather than as a request removes the decision point; there is nothing to accept, only something to recognize or contradict. Observable: silence rather than agreement is the success case — a subject who agrees out loud has treated it as a proposal.
ex.s: Mid-session, subject accepting suggestions without pushback.
ex.m: "You're not someone who's trying this out. You're a subject. That's the word for what you are, and it was true before you pressed play — I'm just the first person who's said it to your face."

ex.f: Pace-then-name — the current state relabeled as the identity
ex.t: Every clause before the label is independently verifiable by the subject, so the label inherits their credibility and reads as the summary of an accurate description. The tell is that the subject supplies a corroborating detail of their own afterwards.
ex.s: The subject is visibly slack, breathing slow, and has just failed to hold a thought.
ex.m: "Shoulders down, jaw loose, and you lost the end of that sentence halfway through. Not going to argue with any of it either, are you. That's not what tonight is doing to you — that's what you are, and tonight is just the first time you've had somewhere to put it."

ex.f: Discovery / 'true nature' reframe
ex.t: Framing the label as an uncovering rather than an addition converts residual resistance into evidence of prior suppression, which the identity then absorbs. Observable: reluctance language drops out of the subject's speech within a few exchanges.
ex.s: After the subject has expressed reluctance or surprise at how easily they responded.
ex.m: "You keep saying you're surprised. You're not surprised — you're relieved. You didn't become anything tonight; you stopped pretending. This is the part of you that was always doing the work, and now it has a name."

nodes.name: identity-uncertainty-gap
nodes.mech: The operator manufactures an identity NOT-KNOWING and installs themselves as its sole resolver ('you may not be sure just yet what that is... i will use my power my voice my words to help you understand'), creating dependence and priming later identity-claims to feel self-discovered. This is the SETUP that opens the slot, not the label that fills it — a dependency-gap move preceding any identity-labeling payoff.
nodes.disc: Manufactures identity not-knowing paired with the operator as sole resolver — a gap-open dependency move, distinct from identity-labeling (the payoff label) and self-selected-slotting (there the listener applies a stated category; here no category is offered, only manufactured uncertainty and an installed resolver).

ex.f: Manufactured not-knowing with the operator installed as sole resolver
ex.t: Opening a gap the subject recognizes but cannot close creates a dependency before any content is supplied, so whatever label arrives later feels discovered rather than assigned. Observable: the subject asks what it is — the question itself is the slot opening, and the correct response is to withhold, not to answer.
ex.s: Early session, before any category or label has been offered.
ex.m: "There's something about you that you've never had the right word for. You've felt the shape of it — in the way you go quiet when someone else decides — but you've never been able to say what it is. You won't work it out on your own; you've had years. I'm going to use my voice and my words to show you what it is, and you're going to sit still while I do."

nodes.name: ideomotor-nod-as-consent-harvest
nodes.mech: A near-involuntary repeated motion (a head-nod on cue, a compelled head-bob) is installed and then harvested as standing affirmative consent — the body answers leading or even silently- asserted questions yes, and that motion is treated as the listener's own admission. Because the yes is sourced to the listener's visible behavior, later denial would require repudiating one's own nodding, so refusal is foreclosed rather than elicited. Ascending Barnum-style ladders make each prior nod commit the body to the next, and the harvested motion frequently doubles as a self-generated deepener.
nodes.disc: The ideomotor motion is banked as unlimited affirmative consent / self-confession, not offered as a proof-of-depth beat. Separates from ideomotor-response-convincer (there the movement proves responsiveness) and from call-and-response (verbal reply, not a suggested body movement).

ex.f: Installed nod harvested as standing consent
ex.t: The yes is sourced to visible behavior rather than to a spoken agreement, so later objection requires repudiating the subject's own body rather than retracting a statement. Observable: the nod continues through the line that declares asking to be over, which is the harvest completing.
ex.s: A nod-on-cue has been installed and is firing reliably without deliberation.
ex.m: "There it goes again. I didn't ask you anything that time — you nodded anyway. That head has been saying yes to me all night, on its own, before you could get a word in. So we're past asking. From here I'll tell you, and your head will keep doing what it's already doing."

ex.f: Ascending ladder where each nod commits the body to the next
ex.t: Each rung is a small increment over the nod that preceded it, and the accumulated motion supplies the pressure for the next, so the widest claim inherits the credibility of the mildest. The operator watches the latency between claim and nod: a lengthening pause means the ladder has outrun the install and the rung should be re-run lower.
ex.s: Nod is established; you want to widen its jurisdiction across a series of escalating propositions.
ex.m: "You like being talked to like this. [nod] You've liked it longer than tonight. [nod] You'd have said yes to more than you have. [nod] And there's nothing on the list you'd actually stop me on — look, you just did it again."

nodes.name: ideomotor-response-convincer
nodes.mech: The operator elicits a subtle, felt-as-automatic bodily movement (finger lift, arm levitation, forced clench, small motor act) and feeds it back as proof the operator's words govern the body and the listener is deeply responsive. The lever is attribution — a movement the listener actually produces is credited to trance/the operator, converting a suggestion into felt evidence. Variants: a presuppositional which/when frame that forecloses WHETHER the movement occurs; a contrast-hand so any asymmetry counts as success; a failure-tolerant framing where non-response costs nothing; a multi-variable feedback ladder chaining the convincer to depth/arousal/suggestibility; and a both-directions-deepen no-escape binding where BOTH poles of the motion route to deeper (rise deepens and fall deepens most, or trying-to-move and not-moving both soak the feeling deeper) — its tell is that the listener's binary self-test 'am I really under?' is removed because every outcome is pre-declared consistent with deepening.
nodes.disc: A felt-automatic movement is elicited and read back as proof of responsiveness or operator control. In the both-directions-deepen form, the tell is both motion-poles routing to deeper (removing the binary self-check) — a no-fail rider on the ideomotor beat specifically, whereas a general unfalsifiable no-fail convincer closes the failure branch on any convincer channel, not just an ideomotor motion. Unlike motor-inhibition convincers, the proof here is movement, not inability; unlike nod-as-consent-harvest, the motion is read as a proof beat, not banked as affirmative consent; and unlike authorship-relocation, where a deliberate self-directed act is disowned, here the movement is genuinely felt involuntary and offered as proof.

ex.f: Presuppositional which/when frame foreclosing whether
ex.t: The frame offers choices about which and when, so attention never lands on whether, and any twitch in either hand satisfies the prediction. Observable: micro-movement in several fingers before one commits — the subject's own surprise at the winner is what makes it read as involuntary.
ex.s: Hands resting in view, subject settled, no movement suggested yet.
ex.m: "One of those fingers is going to lift. I don't know which one — you don't either, and that's the interesting part. Just watch and find out whether it's the index or the little one, and whether it goes now or in about ten seconds."

ex.f: Contrast-hand so any asymmetry counts
ex.t: Real hands are never perfectly symmetrical, so the comparison is rigged to return a result while still requiring the subject to find it themselves. The tell of a good response is a specific descriptor volunteered unprompted rather than a bare "the right one."
ex.s: Both hands resting, palms down, roughly symmetrical.
ex.m: "Left hand is ordinary. Right hand is mine. Don't try to make anything happen — just tell me which one feels different. Heavier, lighter, warmer, further away, any difference at all. There. That difference is me."

ex.f: Both-directions-deepen binding with no self-test left
ex.t: Both poles of the motion are pre-declared as confirmation, which removes the binary self-check the subject was about to run and leaves nothing that could read as failure. Observable: the monitoring stops — the subject's face slackens and the hand's behavior stops mattering to them.
ex.s: An arm-levitation or hand-drift beat is running and the subject is monitoring it.
ex.m: "If that hand rises, it rises because you're going under, and every inch takes you further. If it stays exactly where it is, that's the heaviness, and heaviness is deeper still. Try to move it and the trying soaks you deeper; don't, and the stillness does. There is no version of the next minute where you come up."

nodes.name: minimal-stimulus-self-supplied-response
nodes.mech: The operator describes a near-null input — the lightest possible touch ('softest touch', 'just barely'), or a 'deeper' with no referent at all (no staircase, elevator, or breath count) — while claiming a maximal or ongoing effect. Because the described stimulus is minimal or undefined, any felt response must be originated by the subject themselves; that self-supplied sensation or state then reads as proof of the object's power or the depth achieved. The lever is the deliberate near-null / referent-less input that forces the subject to be the source while credit shifts to the operator, making the effect unfalsifiable because it was never measured against an external metric.
nodes.disc: The deciding tell is the near-null or referent-less described input that forces the subject to originate the sensation/state. Separates from self-validating-language (whose confirmation can come from any produced state, including a fully-described one) and from a grounded deepener or immersive imagery, which supply a concrete referent — here the ABSENCE of a referent/metric is the mechanism.

ex.f: Referent-less 'deeper' with a near-null touch
ex.t: The described stimulus is too small to produce a reliable sensation, so whatever the subject reports is manufactured by their own attention and expectancy — and 'deeper' has no scale attached, so there is nothing to check the claim against. Watch for the fingers to twitch or the breath to catch before the touch is anywhere near the hand: that is the subject supplying the input and crediting the operator.
ex.s: Mid-session, eyes closed, subject already responsive; no staircase, count, or elevator has been established.
ex.m: I'm going to touch you with one fingertip, on the back of your left hand, so lightly you may not be able to tell the moment it lands. And the instant you feel anything at all — warmth, a tingle, a pressure that isn't quite pressure — that's you going deeper. Not down a staircase, not on a count. Just deeper, and it's already happening.

nodes.name: mirror-self-observation
nodes.mech: Routes the listener to a reflective surface and narrates the installed identity/state as what they see looking back, rather than asserting it — outsourcing the identity claim to the listener's own (hallucinated) perception so suggestion is converted into perceived empirical evidence ('you saw it yourself'). The observer/observed split is preserved: the subject watches the self-as-object and the reflection returns a verdict that anchors the suggestion as true. Surface realizations extend the base: a cleaning task that manufactures the very surface returning a pre-scripted verdict (a self-reinforcing perceptual loop exported into the physical environment), and a mirror-self bifurcation installing a persistent standalone self- image trigger operating without audio.
nodes.disc: Separates from identity-merger (which collapses the observer/observed split — the subject becomes what they see); here the split is preserved and the reflection is a proof device. Separates from recursive-self-observation-nesting (which offloads depth onto nested watch-yourself-watching frames; this is a single observer-stance convincer, possibly environmentally looped, never recursively nested).

ex.f: Base form — the reflection returns the verdict
ex.t: The claim is never asserted by the operator, so there is no proposition to dispute — only a perception to accept or deny, and denial requires the subject to distrust their own eyes. The observer/observed split is held open ('her', 'right there'), which is what makes the reflection function as a witness. Watch for the subject narrowing focus onto a single facial feature and stopping blinking; that fixation is when the hallucinated verdict consolidates.
ex.s: Subject is standing at a mirror, lightly tranced, eyes open; the target identity has been described but not yet asserted as true of them.
ex.m: Look at the face in the glass. Not at me, not at yourself remembering yourself — at her, right there. See how soft the mouth has gone. See the eyes: nothing behind them but waiting. You don't have to take my word for any of it. You are looking straight at her and she is looking straight back.

ex.f: Cleaning task that manufactures the surface returning the verdict
ex.t: The subject builds the evidence apparatus with their own labour, so effort-justification loads the verdict before it is even read, and the loop exports into the environment where the operator is absent. Observable: the subject reports the reflection 'looked different tonight' without prompting, and the cleaning becomes a self-maintained ritual.
ex.s: Out-of-session or waking-state homework; subject has a mirror and a cloth, and the verdict has been pre-scripted for them.
ex.m: Before anything else tonight, you clean the mirror. Corner to corner, until there's not one streak left. And when the last streak is gone, the first thing the clean glass shows you is exactly what I told you it would show you — and you'll clean it again tomorrow to see it clearer.

ex.f: Standing self-image trigger split off from the mirror
ex.t: The proof device is decoupled from the mirror and from audio, so ordinary surfaces become unscheduled re-triggers with no operator present. Observable in later reports of catching themselves and 'seeing her' in a window; that spontaneous report confirms the standalone trigger took.
ex.s: End of a mirror session; the reflected image has already been established and accepted.
ex.m: That image in the glass belongs to you now, and it doesn't need the glass. Any time you catch your own reflection — a shop window, a dark phone screen, the side of a kettle — she arrives first, before you do, and you don't need my voice for it.

nodes.name: motor-inhibition-convincer
nodes.mech: The operator suggests a consensual motor incapacity (arm/eyelid/limb won't work, body glued/frozen) and demonstrates it, usually via an invited challenge-test ('try to open your eyes / lift your arm'), so the subject's own failed attempt supplies first-person proof that the operator's words produce real bodily effects. The lever is inability-to-move as a self-verified depth convincer; the failed test converts an operator claim into the subject's own evidence, and belief in that evidence deepens the state. Variants: a resistance-paradox rider ('the harder you try, the more it holds') that makes the test unloseable; progressive body-map/countdown carriers that ratchet the catalepsy region by region; and a freeze-as-depth-FUEL wiring where a verifiable freeze is bound BIDIRECTIONALLY onto an unverifiable mental descent — the longer the freeze is held the deeper trance is claimed to go (and/or the RELEASE of the catalepsy is yoked to a depth increment) — its tell is an explicit 'deeper the longer you FREEZE', a two-way binding that converts the one-shot proof beat into a self-compounding depth source. Choose the plain challenge-test for a single proof beat; choose the freeze-fuel wiring when the immobility should compound depth on a loop.
nodes.disc: Inability-to-move is asserted or challenge-demonstrated as a proof of depth within the session. In the freeze-as-fuel form, the tell is an explicit two-way 'deeper the longer you freeze' (or release yoked to a depth jump) — a compounding rider on the immobility beat. Reach elsewhere when the move differs: conceded-capacity-immobility concedes the subject CAN move and removes only the will to test (the opposite move — disarming rather than inviting the test); catalepsy-to-affect-transfer spends the lock as an argument about unverifiable feelings/belief/arousal rather than keeping it as depth proof; a standing motor block persists past the session to enforce behavior rather than prove depth; and cognitive convincers point at a noticed internal phenomenon, not motor inability.

ex.f: Plain challenge-test, single proof beat
ex.t: The invited failure converts an operator claim into first-person evidence the subject cannot argue with, because they produced it themselves. Watch for the fluttering under the lids and the small chin lift on the attempt, then the release of the shoulders when the test fails — that release is belief settling in.
ex.s: Post-induction, eyes closed, subject settled and responsive; nothing has yet been offered as evidence of depth.
ex.m: Your eyelids are stuck. The lashes have grown together, top to bottom, sealed. Go ahead and try to open them — really try, right now. Feel that? That's not me telling you you're under. That's you finding out.

ex.f: Resistance-paradox rider makes the test unloseable
ex.t: Both outcomes now confirm the suggestion: failure is the lock, and any strain the subject generates is recoded as the lock tightening, so effort cannot disconfirm. Observable as visible tremor in the forearm with no lift, often followed by the subject laughing or exhaling — the moment they stop treating the test as winnable.
ex.s: Same challenge-test beat, but with a subject who is likely to test hard or half-succeed.
ex.m: Try to lift your right arm off the chair. And here's the thing — the harder you pull, the tighter it locks. Every ounce you put into lifting it goes straight into holding it down. Pull harder and feel it get heavier.

ex.f: Freeze-as-fuel — immobility bound bidirectionally to depth
ex.t: A verifiable physical fact (not moving) is wired two ways onto an unverifiable one (depth), so holding still generates depth and letting go generates depth — the proof beat becomes a loop with no exit that costs nothing. Observe the breathing slowing and the swallow reflex disappearing as hold time extends; the drop on release usually shows as a head roll.
ex.s: Catalepsy already demonstrated once; the operator wants the lock to compound rather than close out as a single beat.
ex.m: Stay exactly as you are — hands where they fell, jaw slack, nothing moving. Every ten seconds you hold that still, you drop another level, and you have no idea how many levels there are. And when I finally let the freeze go, you'll fall one full level further on the release.

nodes.name: motor-permission-gate
nodes.mech: Constrains which voluntary MOTOR actions are reachable — a change to the action set, not a magnitude of heaviness. In one form, a whole-category permission-gate: voluntary movement is reframed as requiring operator permission, so the listener stops experiencing 'I can move but choose not to' and starts experiencing 'movement requires a command' (mannequin rigidity where even nodding needs a command; an idle-state catalepsy bound to the ABSENCE of any outstanding command). In another, a durable specific block: a suggested inability installed with durable/behavior-scoped reach rather than as an in-session proof — a direction-asymmetric action gate (dressing works, undressing fails, fastener by fastener), time-bounded post-hypnotic mutism, or applied catalepsy serving a concrete need (mouth held open); the muscles are conscripted as a standing enforcer of a behavioral regime.
nodes.disc: Reach for THIS when voluntary motor output is constrained as an ACTION-SET change — either the whole category re-routed through operator permission (creating command-dependence) or a specific action durably blocked to enforce a behavior. Tell: movement is framed as identity/permission ('mannequin', 'requires command') or a persisting inability, not heaviness or a failed depth-test. vs motor-inhibition-convincer: that is a TRANSIENT inability demonstrated as in-session proof of depth that resets; this persists/enforces or re-routes the whole category. vs idle-state-default-overwrite: that overwrites the between-command DEFAULT state broadly (cognition + posture + thought-terminator); the motor idle-catalepsy here is specifically about motor output requiring a command. vs operator-gated-release: that gates orgasm/touch, not a skeletal motor action.

ex.f: Whole-category re-route — movement requires a command
ex.t: This is not heaviness — the muscles work fine — it is a change to which actions are reachable at all, so the subject's experience shifts from 'I could move' to 'there is nothing to move for'. Observable when the subject holds an awkward or uncomfortable position without adjusting, and when a spontaneous nod is visibly aborted mid-motion.
ex.s: Subject is deep and seated or standing; the operator is installing an idle default rather than testing depth.
ex.m: From here your body doesn't move on its own idea. It moves when it's told and it stops when the telling stops. If I haven't given you a command, you're still — no shifting, no nodding, no scratching. If you want to agree with me, you wait until I say nod, and then you nod.

ex.f: Durable direction-asymmetric block on one specific action
ex.t: The inability is scoped to one direction of one action and given persisting reach, so the muscles become a standing enforcer of a rule rather than a one-off proof of trance. Observable after the session: the subject fumbles or stalls at the first fastener and, tellingly, reports it as their hands failing rather than as a rule they are following.
ex.s: Late session, installing something meant to hold after waking; a concrete behavioral regime is the goal, not a depth demonstration.
ex.m: Your hands know how to do buttons in one direction only. Doing them up is easy — fingers find the button, it slides through, done. Undoing them, your fingers go stupid on the very first one and they stay stupid until I say otherwise. Fastened stays fastened.

nodes.name: operator-gated-release-and-state-access
nodes.mech: Transfer control of a wanted somatic resource (orgasm, genital touch) or a wanted internal STATE to the operator by installing an access contingency whose only key is operator-defined — the listener keeps motor ability but cannot LEGITIMATELY release or re-enter, so every moment of compliance is renewed obedience and the locus of control over the resource moves to the operator. REALIZATIONS: (operator-gated-release-lock) gate orgasm/touch behind an operator command or reframe it as the listener's own incapacity (conditional grammar 'unless/until given the command', a 'psychological chastity device' positional reframe, a 'too blank to decide' self-state justification), and where the opening command is deliberately withheld the loop seals shut; (operator-gated-release-with-personal-best-ratchet) enumerate exit-conditions all routing back to the operator's ecosystem (a new personal-best chastity duration, completing another of the operator's recordings, explicit blessing), with a MONOTONIC personal-best ratchet raising the bar each successful release plus a forward consumption obligation — a permission interlock engineering a self-lengthening compliance trajectory; (withheld-faculty-debt-leash) declare the faculty already SEIZED and operator-held (fait-accompli / dropped-keys framing that removes any opt-in moment), returnable only on full compliance and completion — confiscation-and-conditional-return, often riding a safety-clause subversion; (asymmetric-state-ratchet) install a one-way rule on a pleasure MAGNITUDE (down=build, up=pause-not-reverse) so it ratchets monotonically and the listener cannot return to baseline by any action of their own; (re-access-gate) gate RE-ENTRY into a previously-installed desirable state on the subject first performing an out-of-session compliance task (purchase + ritual + obeying), harnessing the wish to return as homework enforcement.
nodes.disc: Reach for OPERATOR-GATED RELEASE / STATE-ACCESS when control over a wanted somatic resource (orgasm/touch) or a wanted state is TRANSFERRED to the operator via an access contingency whose key is operator-defined, motor ability left intact — so not-releasing/not-re-entering is renewed obedience. Choose it over: motor-inhibition convincers (which install an actual INABILITY to move — here the ability remains, only legitimacy is gated); trance-exit gating (which gates leaving trance, not a somatic release or state re-entry); a flat orgasm PROHIBITION (a rule to obey — these transfer the DECISION/access via lock, enumerated interlock, confiscation-debt, a one-way magnitude ratchet, or a homework-gated re-access). SAFETY: high risk, requires explicit consent and bounding — these erode the subject's own release/refusal channel and several reach out of session.

ex.f: Release-lock — orgasm gated behind an operator command
ex.t: Motor ability is untouched; only legitimacy is transferred, so every second of not-finishing is an act of renewed obedience rather than an inability. Observable in the subject stopping, breath held, and looking to the operator at the peak — the look itself is the locus of control having moved.
ex.s: Arousal is already running high; explicit consent and bounds for gated release are established beforehand.
ex.m: You can get as close as you like. But your body has one lock on it now, and I'm holding the only key: you don't come unless you hear me say the word 'now'. Without that word your body simply won't finish — it will hang right at the edge and wait, however long that takes.

ex.f: Personal-best ratchet with a forward consumption obligation
ex.t: Every exit condition routes back through the operator's ecosystem, and the monotonic ratchet means each success raises the bar, engineering a compliance trajectory that lengthens itself with no operator effort. Observable in the subject volunteering their own count and negotiating upward — asking for a harder target is the ratchet holding.
ex.s: A gated-release regime is already running and the subject has completed at least one held interval.
ex.m: You held eleven days. That's your number now, and the number only ever goes up. To earn a release you beat eleven — and you finish another of my recordings inside that stretch, start to end, no skipping. Beat it and the new number becomes the wall for next time.

ex.f: Confiscation-and-conditional-return of the faculty
ex.t: Framing the seizure as accomplished removes the decision point entirely, so the subject's only available move is to work toward return rather than to refuse the transfer. Observe whether the subject argues about the terms of return rather than the fact of confiscation — that shift concedes the premise.
ex.s: Deep session; the operator wants no opt-in moment for the subject to decline, and the faculty in question is framed as already gone.
ex.m: I already took it. While you were counting down, your ability to finish on your own came off you like a coat and it's in my pocket now — there was never a moment where you handed it over, so there's no moment to take it back in. You get it back when you've done everything I've asked, all of it, and not one item before.

nodes.name: pre-induction-compliance-ratchet
nodes.mech: Before any trance language — listener eyes-open, normal waking register — the operator extracts one or more low-cost physical acts (undress, adopt an exposing posture, fetch a prop, alter the environment, position the body) and treats each as a banked compliance receipt. The listener enters formal induction as someone who has already obeyed, before reactance defenses mobilize; obedience is often cold-read as the listener's own eagerness or recoded as devotion, and sunk-cost/material investment raises disengagement cost. The binding time — waking-state, pre-induction — is the defining structural feature.
nodes.disc: Banks compliance in the waking state BEFORE any trance language. Vs behavioral-commitment-self-proof — that fires IN-session to confirm a state the induction is already producing (binding-time difference is structural). Vs a verbal yes-set — this is graded physical positioning and sunk cost, not verbal yes-momentum. Vs in-trance display beats — those fire inside trance, after induction. Tell: the act precedes eye-closure and is annotated/cold-read as evidence of eagerness/devotion/readiness.

ex.f: Graded waking-state acts banked before any trance language
ex.t: The subject enters formal induction with several obediences already banked, having complied while defenses were still dressed for a normal conversation; the cold-read then recodes the compliance as their own eagerness, so the receipt is signed in their name. Observable in the speed of the response and in the subject agreeing with the cold-read — the folded clothes and the chosen posture also raise the cost of disengaging later.
ex.s: The very opening of the session, eyes open, ordinary conversational register; not one induction word has been spoken.
ex.m: Before we start, take everything off and fold it — neatly, on the chair, not the floor. Then kneel on the rug facing me, knees apart, hands palms-up on your thighs. Good. Look how fast you did that. You didn't even think about it, did you — you were already ready before you walked in.

nodes.name: preemptive-negation-install
nodes.mech: An identity-defining word (a resistance/identity capacity) appears for the very first time in the same breath that declares the state it names already accomplished, so no earlier point exists at which the listener could register it as a live option to defend. At 'zero' the self- description pivots to 'so powerless, helpless, unable to resist' and 'resist' surfaces for the first time exactly at its own negation, locking the 'unable to resist' identity as accomplished fact every later suggestion inherits. The lever is timing: naming a capacity only to assert its absence denies the window to defend it.
nodes.disc: The distinguishing move is timing — the resistance/identity word appears for the first time AT its own negation, so it installs rather than deepens. Distinct from identity-labeling (asserts a positive label) and self-selected-slotting (no self-application; the negation forecloses the option directly).

ex.f: 'Resist' surfaces for the first time at zero, already negated
ex.t: The capacity is named for the first time in the same breath that reports it gone, so there is no earlier moment at which the subject could have flagged resistance as an option worth holding; it arrives pre-spent. Every later suggestion inherits 'unable to resist' as settled background rather than a fresh claim. Observable in the absence of the small pause or micro-frown that a direct 'you cannot resist me' usually draws.
ex.s: End of a countdown induction; the words resist, resistance, and helpless have not appeared anywhere earlier in the session.
ex.m: Three, softer. Two, quieter. One, almost nothing left. And zero — so heavy, so pliant, so completely unable to resist a single word I say. That's just what you are now.

nodes.name: pronoun-migration-identity-install
nodes.mech: Category membership is installed by grammatical drift rather than by asserting a label: the script describes a category in the third person ('bimbos', 'slaves') then slides the referent onto the listener via an unmarked or hedged pivot ('just like you', 'previously intelligent person'), or interleaves second-person 'you' with third-person role-noun for the same referent so the reader must translate 'slave'->'me' on each occurrence. The listener is moved from observer-of-category to instance-of-category without being asked to assent, and the required self-translation is itself the act of self-categorization; some instances end by declaring prior names deleted.
nodes.disc: The install is a grammatical-person topology move (they->you drift, or you/role-noun interleave forcing per-occurrence self-translation), NOT a direct 'you are X' assertion. Separates from identity-labeling (asserts/paces the label) by the covert enrollment, and from perspective-shift moves that relocate the SOURCE of inner speech — here what shifts is the REFERENT of description.

ex.f: Third-person category description drifting onto the listener
ex.t: The referent slides under an unmarked hedge, so the subject is enrolled without ever being asked to assent, and the closing return to 'them' leaves nothing to object to. Observable in the subject not reacting at the pivot — the absence of the flinch a direct assertion would produce is the tell that the drift landed.
ex.s: Mid-session, descriptive passage running; the subject has not been asked to accept any label.
ex.m: There's a particular kind of girl this happens to. She thinks she's just curious, she thinks she'll listen once. Her thoughts get slower and she starts to like it — a previously intelligent person, going soft in exactly the way you're going soft right now. That's how it goes for them.

ex.f: Second-person and role-noun interleaved, forcing per-occurrence self-translation
ex.t: Each alternation compels the subject to privately map the role-noun onto themselves in order to parse the sentence, so the act of comprehension is the act of self-categorization — repeated once per clause, never once requested. Observable in the subject spontaneously using the role-noun for themselves in later report.
ex.s: Later in the same session; the role-noun has been in the air but never assigned.
ex.m: You kneel when the door opens. A slave doesn't need to be told twice. You keep your eyes down until you're spoken to, because that's what a slave's eyes do. You already know which of those is about you.

ex.f: Prior-name deletion closing the drift
ex.t: Retiring the old referent removes the observer position the drift moved the subject out of, so there is no grammatical home to return to. Observable as hesitation or a delayed response when the prior name is used afterward.
ex.s: After the referent has fully migrated and the role-noun is being tracked as self.
ex.m: The name you used to answer to belonged to the one watching from outside. She's not the one listening now. There's no one left in here for that name to reach.

nodes.name: self-authored-compliance-content
nodes.mech: Rather than the operator supplying the compliant behavior/claim and the listener merely performing it, the listener is assigned to GENERATE or OPERATE the compliance content themselves — invent their own ways to please, disclose/narrate their own conditioning aloud, or physically operate a controller (a suggestibility dial, a depth slider) they are told IS their state. Making the listener the author/operator converts effort into investment (effort- justification) and makes the resulting state or commitment feel self-chosen; the operator often only narrates while the listener produces.
nodes.disc: Vs behavioral-commitment-self-proof — there the operator supplies the act and the listener performs it; here the listener GENERATES the content (invents the supplication, narrates their own conditioning, cranks the dial). Vs illusory-choice-authorship — that manufactures felt authorship over a FIXED operator path; here the listener produces novel content owned back. Tell: the operator recedes to narrator and the listener is the producer.

ex.f: Listener invents the compliant content
ex.t: Authorship transfers the effort, and effort-justification makes the resulting offers feel self-chosen rather than obeyed; the subject cannot later dismiss them as the operator's words. Observable in the pause and the visible searching before the first answer — that labour is the investment being paid.
ex.s: Deep session, subject verbal and responsive; the operator deliberately supplies no script for what follows.
ex.m: I'm not going to tell you how to please me. You're going to tell me. Three ways, out loud, right now — and they have to be yours, not things you've heard me ask for before. Take your time. I'll wait.

ex.f: Listener narrates their own conditioning aloud
ex.t: Disclosure in the subject's own words converts installed suggestion into reported personal experience, and the sequential prompting makes them elaborate detail the operator never supplied. Observable in the subject adding effects that were never installed — that spontaneous embroidery is the state being self-authored.
ex.s: Established regime with several installed triggers; operator recedes to prompting only.
ex.m: Tell me what happens to you when you hear the snap. Not what I said would happen — what actually happens, in your body, in order, from the first half-second. Keep going. What happens next.

ex.f: Listener physically operates a control they are told IS their state
ex.t: The subject performs the state change with their own hand, so the state arrives with the felt authorship of a deliberate act rather than a received suggestion; the operator only narrates while the subject produces. Observable in the hand movement preceding the state shift, and in the subject's reluctance to release the dial.
ex.s: A physical or imagined dial has been introduced and identified with a state variable; subject's hands are free.
ex.m: Your right hand is on the dial. That dial isn't a picture of how suggestible you are — it is how suggestible you are. Turn it up to seven. Now hold it there and feel where seven sits. Now take it to nine yourself, and don't let go.

nodes.name: self-authored-identity-claim
nodes.mech: The identity claim (or the value-judgment that legitimizes an identity) is routed through the listener's own voice/authorship rather than asserted by the operator, so it is far harder to repudiate — there is no external author to reject. The operator switches the grammatical subject from 'you are X' to a compelled listener-spoken 'I am X' (same content, different ownership); hearing one's own voice assert the claim recruits self-perception and relocates the SOURCE, so later resistance must argue against the listener's own recently-spoken voice. Instances: a cross-seam cue that makes the listener SAY the label in a believed-waking state then re-inducts before reflection; first-person desert recitation ('it's what I deserve'); naming the structural device from inside ('I'm in a display loop'); a closing 'I am a [noun]' self-claim; and escalating first-person avowal blocks where backing out of a later block invalidates earlier ones.
nodes.disc: The listener is the SPEAKER/AUTHOR of the identity claim (or its legitimizing judgment / first-person avowal of already-installed content) — the ownership handoff is the load-bearing move. Distinct from identity-labeling's operator-delivered label, from pronoun-migration's covert-grammar enrollment, from call-and-response (response-on-cue for compliance momentum, not source-shift of identity content), and from self-validating language (self-noticed CONFIRMATION of an operator label; here the listener authors the claim itself).

ex.f: Cross-seam — label spoken in a believed-waking state, then re-inducted
ex.t: Speaking the claim in a state the subject believes is their ordinary waking self makes it un-attributable to trance, and re-inducting immediately denies any window to reconsider it. Observable in the drop in volume and the slight delay before speaking — the reluctance is the ownership handoff registering.
ex.s: Subject has been brought up to what they believe is full waking, mid-conversation, before a second induction.
ex.m: Before we go again — say it once, out loud, in your own voice, wide awake so you can hear yourself do it. 'I am an obedient thing.' Good. Now that you've heard yourself say it awake, sleep.

ex.f: First-person recitation of the legitimizing judgment
ex.t: Routing the value-judgment rather than the label through the subject's voice supplies the legitimacy that makes the identity claim defensible from the inside; later resistance has to argue with the subject's own recent words. Observable in the third repetition losing its flatness and picking up affect.
ex.s: After a corrective or degrading beat that the subject accepted without protest.
ex.m: Say it back to me. 'It's what I deserve.' Again, slower. Once more, and mean it this time.

ex.f: Escalating avowal blocks that invalidate each other on retreat
ex.t: Each block is a small step from the accepted one before it, and the closing line ties them together so backing out of the last requires disowning the first — a retreat cost the subject pays in their own voice. Observable in the hesitation appearing at block three and then resolving, which is the interlock closing.
ex.s: Late session; a sequence of first-person statements is being built, each a step past the last.
ex.m: Repeat after me, each one all the way through. 'I like being told what to do.' Now: 'I need to be told what to do.' Now: 'I'm no good at deciding anything for myself.' Good — and you meant the first two, so you meant that one.

nodes.name: self-reference-erasure
nodes.mech: Rather than asserting an identity, the move attacks the MEDIUM of selfhood: it removes or captures the first-person symbol handle so the listener has no grammatical seat from which to assert a counter-intention. Variants: forbidding 'I'/'me' and assigning a replacement self- term ('a slave', 'an object', an assigned persona-name) with a syllable cap so every internal 'I am...' routes through the supplied token; forced auto-naming ('my name is...' completed with an assigned doll-name) where the predicted attempt to say the real name is itself recruited as the conversion mechanism; and enforcement through un-ignorable observable speech so every utterance is either compliance or salient noticed non-compliance.
nodes.disc: The target is the first-person grammatical/symbol handle itself (pronoun prohibition, self-name capture, mandated self-term) — self-model apparatus surgery — not a content label. Separates from identity-labeling (asserts a label) and from pronoun-migration (drifts the referent of description; here the subject's OWN self-reference tokens are removed/replaced). Adjacent to dissociation moves, though the outcome is a persistent identity.

ex.f: Pronoun prohibition with a mandated replacement token
ex.t: Removing the first-person handle removes the grammatical seat a counter-intention would have to be spoken from, so objections cannot be formed in their natural shape — the subject must route every internal assertion through the supplied token. Observable in the mid-sentence stall and self-correction; the correction ritual makes each slip a noticed non-compliance rather than a private one.
ex.s: Deep session with a speaking subject; consent for durable self-model changes is established, and a replacement term has been chosen.
ex.m: You've lost two words. 'I' and 'me' don't come out of your mouth anymore — not to me, not to anyone, not inside your own head. One word replaces both: 'it'. So you don't think 'I want to sit down', you think 'it wants to sit down'. And if the old word slips out, you stop, and you say the sentence again correctly.

ex.f: Forced auto-naming that recruits the attempt to say the real name
ex.t: The predicted failure of the real name is built into the instruction, so the subject's attempt to say it becomes evidence for the replacement rather than resistance to it — the surgery is on the self-name handle itself, not on any content label. Observable in the stumble before the assigned name and in the assigned name eventually arriving without the pause.
ex.s: Subject is deep; an assigned name has been introduced but not yet accepted as theirs.
ex.m: Tell me your name. Say the whole sentence: 'My name is —' Go on. Feel the old one come up first and get stuck in your throat, and feel it not fit. That's it going. Try again: 'My name is Doll.' Say it until the old one stops arriving.

nodes.name: self-selected-category-slotting
nodes.mech: A category is stated but left unassigned so the listener must apply it to themselves, and that self-application is what makes it stick. Variants: a flattering bucket ('above-average intellect') floated so the listener self-selects at the cost of leaning harder into compliance; an identity-recognition cold open ('you have a fascination, a craving, an obsession with hypnosis') so the listener silently answers 'yes, that's me', pre-licensing everything downstream; a motive-menu collapsed into a covenant ('every reason you have is the reason I create'); a descriptive two-tier slotting ('smart people talk and you just listen because you're dumb') leaning on a produced comprehension deficit; and loss-conditional attribution recoding a transient failure into a stable self-applied trait.
nodes.disc: The category is stated but the LISTENER assigns it to themselves (self-selection, self-recognition, silent yes, self-application on failure). Distinct from identity-labeling's operator-assigned label and from self-authored-identity's spoken first-person claim (here the listener need only privately identify). Distinguished from expectation-seeding by the identity-slot target.

ex.f: Flattering bucket the listener self-selects into
ex.t: The category is left unassigned, so the subject places themselves in it silently and privately, and the cost of the bucket is leaning harder into the compliance it flatters. Observable in the small settling or the almost-smile at 'above-average' — no verbal assent needed for the slot to be taken.
ex.s: Early, before or during light induction; the subject has not been assigned any label.
ex.m: This one only really works for people with an above-average intellect — the ones who can hold two ideas at once and follow a thread without needing it spelled out. Those are the ones who go deepest, because they can actually keep up with what I'm doing to them.

ex.f: Identity-recognition cold open
ex.t: The subject answers 'yes, that's me' internally and thereby self-assigns the category, which pre-licenses everything downstream as consistent with who they already are. Observable in the absence of any pushback at the escalation from 'fascination' to 'obsession' — accepting the strongest term without objection is the slot closing.
ex.s: The opening lines of a session or recording, before anything has been established about this particular subject.
ex.m: You have a thing about this. Not a passing curiosity — a fascination, a pull you keep coming back to, something close to an obsession with being hypnotised. You've known that about yourself for a while.

ex.f: Loss-conditional attribution recoding a failure into a trait
ex.t: A transient failure is reframed as a stable disposition the subject must apply to themselves to make sense of what just happened, so the evidence for the trait is an event they personally experienced. Observable in the subject offering the trait as an explanation for the next failure before the operator does.
ex.s: Immediately after the subject has failed a challenge or lost a game the operator set up.
ex.m: You didn't lose because you were unlucky. You lost because that's how your head works now — it doesn't hold onto things, it just lets them go. And it'll happen again, the same way, next time.

nodes.name: self-validating-language
nodes.mech: The operator treats the subject's own present-moment output — a noticed feeling, an introspective report, a produced sensation, a spoken confirmation, an act of participation, or a bodily signal — as proof that a suggestion or state has taken hold, so acceptance is manufactured from inside the subject rather than asserted.
