Plain forgetting is brittle, because the world leaves evidence and evidence prompts questions. Here the listener's own narrative-repair habit is recruited in advance to defend the gap. A weaker version runs the other way too, so the cue stays out of conscious reach until someone speaks it.
ex.s: After a state trigger has been established and rehearsed; subject currently in the installed state, being prepared for the return.
ex.m: When you come back to yourself, none of what you were like just now comes with you. And if anything doesn't add up afterwards — the time, the state of the room, why you're where you are — you have my permission to come up with whatever explanation makes it make sense, and to believe it. Your mind is good at that. Let it.

nodes.name: container-externalized-erasure
nodes.mech: Erasure delivered by reifying mental content (memories, identity, thoughts, the conscious mind itself) as a destructible or disposable external object — a bubble, satin box, candle, gum-bubble, drain/spiral, rubber bag — that the listener fills or stages while the operator (or a single staged action) executes the removal. The load-bearing feature is the agency split: the listener packages the target, so cannot accidentally undo a deletion they did not perform, and forgetting becomes a discrete felt event ("pop", "lid slams", blow-out) rather than a diffuse absence. A single verb with a sliding referent ("drain X", "pop X") lets the operator keep feeding new categories into one rehearsed action without re-inducting.
nodes.disc: Amnesia/blanking executed through an externalized destructible-or-disposable container with an operator-owned removal step — not a verbal forget-suggestion and not a recall-defeat loop. Unlike relocating the analytical faculty intact somewhere quiet (nothing is destroyed, and the target is a faculty rather than memory content), the container here exists to be destroyed or discarded; and unlike a stepwise identity-erasure ladder, whose tell is the ordered escalation, the vehicle itself is the tell here — though the two often appear together in the same script.

ex.f: One object mapped to the whole conscious mind
ex.t: A single small light is named as the listener's thinking mind — whatever it illuminates is what they can see in there. The operator is careful to specify that putting it out destroys nothing: every thought remains intact and unharmed, only invisible. A brief count then extinguishes it, and the mind goes from lit to dark in one staged event. The operator's voice is offered as the replacement source of anything the listener sees from that point on.
ex.s: Early-mid session; subject can visualize on command and has confirmed seeing the object.
ex.m: That little flame is your thinking mind — everything it lights up is everything you can see in there. Nothing is being taken away, understand: it all stays exactly where it is, safe, whole. You just won't be able to see any of it. Breathe in, two, three — and out. Dark. From here, what you see is whatever I describe.

ex.f: One removal verb, a sliding referent
ex.t: The first pass moves tension out through a single visual channel, and the listener feels the pull. After that the operator never re-explains the mechanism, only swaps the cargo: memories next, then feeling, then volition, then the listener's own name — each announced as simply the next thing going the same way. Four separate erasures ride one rehearsed action, so by the third the listener is already pulling before hearing what is being pulled.
ex.s: Third or fourth repetition of the same drain image; subject already reports the pulling sensation without prompting.
ex.m: Feel it draining out through your heels again. That's the tension gone. Now the memories, same way, same pull — down and out. Good. Now the feeling. Now the wanting to decide. And now your name, right out through your heels with the rest of it.

ex.f: Object ritual with a bodily convincer
ex.t: Forgetting is staged as a small physical routine: a container opens by itself, the thought drops in without the listener having to push it, and a brief swimmy jolt behind the eyes is named as the sensation of it leaving. The lid shuts, fastens, and the whole thing drifts out of reach; another container is always waiting, so the routine can never run out. The jolt is what makes it convincing — the listener now has a felt event to point at, indistinguishable from ordinary failure to recall.
ex.s: Subject reports floating sensation and has confirmed a specific thought held in mind.
ex.m: There's a small tin sitting open beside you. Don't push — the thought drops in by itself. There. Did you feel that swim behind your eyes, that half-second tilt? That's it leaving. Lid down, catch clicks, and the tin floats off out of reach. There's another one open already, so bring me the next one.

ex.f: Listener fills the container, operator destroys it
ex.t: The operator offers a container and asks the listener to move one category of memory into it — the earliest years first — letting it drain out of their head until the vessel is full, then checks that nothing has been left behind. Only after that confirmation does the operator perform the removal, in a single word, and follow it with a line about how good the forgetting feels and a check that nothing comes back. The rounds then repeat with progressively heavier cargo: schooling, restraint, sharpness, and finally what the listener is called. Each round is identical in shape — the listener does the loading, one operator action does the destroying, a reward line closes the beat. Because the listener never performed the deletion, there is no moment they can point to where they let it go, and each successful round is offered as evidence the next, larger target will go just as easily.
ex.s: Mid-session, deep; a wide-mouthed jar has been established in the subject's hands and one round already rehearsed.
ex.m: Open the jar and tip your head. Let everything from before you were ten pour out of you into it — the house, the birthdays, the faces. Keep tipping until nothing's left in there. Is it empty? Good. Watch me. Gone. Feel how light that is — nothing coming back, is there? Now open the next jar, and this one takes school: everything you learned, everything you were taught to be careful about.

nodes.name: contradiction-as-amnesia
nodes.mech: Amnesia induced not by a forget-command but by confidently narrating the present as if recent events never occurred, training the listener to distrust their own memory. The operator asserts in casual factual tone that nothing just happened ("we've just started", "first time we've had this talk"), denying even a physical action the listener performed (kneeling), with no acknowledgement — so episodic timeline coherence degrades and by midpoint "how many times" produces genuine confusion. A related surface re-attributes narrative-cut gaps (blinking forward between day-scenes) to trance-amnesia: the natural inability to recall what did not happen is relabeled as evidence the conditioning is working, used as a recurring mid-session deepener.
nodes.disc: Amnesia delivered as present-tense narration contradicting recent events (gaslighting-shaped) or as re-attribution of fiction/narrative cuts to trance-amnesia — no memory gap is installed, existing events are denied or existing gaps relabeled. Separates from amnesia-suggestion (a direct forget- command on a bounded target). Contradiction-without-acknowledgement / cut-relabeling is the tell.

ex.f: Story cuts relabelled as trance amnesia
ex.t: The narrative jumps from one day to the next, and the operator leans into the seam: if the listener is hazy on how they got from then to now, that is treated as exactly what should be expected given everything that has supposedly been happening between scenes. No gap is installed; the listener simply cannot recall scenes that were never narrated, and that ordinary blank is handed back as proof the conditioning has been working off-page.
ex.s: Mid-file, immediately after a scene transition from one narrated day to the next.
ex.m: Now it's the next morning. And if you're a little unclear on how you got from last night to here — of course you are. Quite a lot happened in between, and it's not the sort of thing that stays. That haze is exactly what it should feel like by now.

ex.f: Casual denial that anything just happened
ex.t: Well into the session, in the same bright conversational tone as everything else, the operator remarks that they have only just begun. A little later, that they are fairly sure this particular exchange has never happened before — and invites the listener to agree, who cannot say either way. Then, noticing the listener's posture, the operator wonders aloud when they ended up on the floor, since they certainly were not a moment ago. No forget-instruction is ever issued and no contradiction is ever acknowledged; the operator simply narrates a present that excludes the last several minutes, including a position the listener adopted with their own body. Ask them later how many rounds there have been and no answer comes.
ex.s: Twenty minutes into a session with several completed cycles; subject kneeling, having been directed there earlier; bright conversational tone throughout.
ex.m: Right, so — we're just getting started, you and I. And I'm fairly sure this is the first time we've ever talked about this, isn't it? Hm. Also, when did you end up on the floor? You were in the chair a second ago.

nodes.name: covert-age-regression-state-reaccess
nodes.mech: Steers the subject back into an earlier developmental/cognitive-affective state without an explicit go-back-to-age-X command, by addressing that state through a covert vehicle: re-evoking a near-universal early-learning difficulty in present-active framing (b vs d, is a 6 an upside-down 9, first day of school), playing an internal melody chosen to index a target life-period, or leaving a phrase's scope undetermined so a state-describing reading (as a child) attaches to the listener. Because the regression is triggered by a shared association or a self-resolved ambiguity rather than a directive, there is nothing overt to refuse; attention narrows, plasticity reopens, and the earlier state's amnesia and suggestibility come with it.
nodes.disc: The move re-accesses an EARLIER developmental state via a covert vehicle (shared difficulty, melody-address, scope ambiguity) — the payload is state re-entry / age regression, not a manipulation of felt time-rate. Generic confusion work multiplies meanings to overload; here the self-resolved reading is itself a specific state induction. And unlike guided visualization, the material is the subject's own developmental state, not operator-supplied imagery.

ex.f: Undetermined phrase scope that lands as a state
ex.t: "the ambiguity is whether the phrase as a child refers to Erickson or to the client, thus, the effect is a scope ambiguity which induces age regression on the part of the client." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: A shared early-learning difficulty, present tense
ex.t: "How is it different from a 'd'… children have exactly this difficulty - thus, age regression suggestion." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: A melody chosen for the age it indexes
ex.t: "give the client some melody to play inside his head which indirectly suggests age regression. We have found nursery rhyme melodies particularly effective." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

nodes.name: covert-amnesia-installation
nodes.mech: Amnesia installed WITHOUT a recognizable forget-command — the suggestion is smuggled in as something other than an instruction so it slips past the evaluation a direct "you will forget" would trigger. Surfaces: an in-fiction physics metaphor (a black hole where "information can't escape", so later non-retrieval is pre-explained as a law of the descent) cashed later as the amnesia firewall; identity-loss delivered as an environmental fact of the fantasy scene ("you might not realize... even your own name"); a wake-time dismissal disguised as small talk that also instructs forgetting; covert deletion of a specific item (the number 5) by modeled omission under a completeness/truth guarantee; and wake-by-rewinding to a pre-trance state-marker so amnesia is a byproduct of state restoration. The common lever is amnesia-by-non-command: pre-installing the account for, or the fact of, forgetting.
nodes.disc: Amnesia delivered as metaphor-physics / scene-fact / small-talk / modeled-omission / state-rewind rather than as a declared forget, so it evades the evaluation an explicit command draws. Separates from amnesia-suggestion (a declared instruction) and from install-concealment-amnesia (which hides an install's ORIGIN — here it is the amnesia itself that is disguised at delivery, often forward-loaded to fire later). The non-command disguise is the tell.

ex.f: Deletion by modelled omission under a truth guarantee
ex.t: The operator rebuilds the listener by counting the pieces back into place, and the recited list runs from one to twelve with a single number quietly absent from the middle of it. Each pass ends with the assurance that the set is complete and that nothing at all is missing. The count is run several more times, always identical, always short the same item, always under the standing rule that in this state whatever the operator says is simply so. The absent item is never named, so there is nothing to refuse; the listener is only ever shown the sequence without it.
ex.s: Reassembly phase near the end; subject accustomed to accepting operator statements as literally true in this state.
ex.m: Let's put you back together. One, two, three, four, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve — all present, nothing missing, complete. Again: one, two, three, four, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve. Whole. And in this state, whatever I say is simply so.

ex.f: Arousal and amnesia delivered as small talk
ex.t: "wider awake than you were earlier this morning (this last statement is… an indirect, emphatic, definitive instruction to arouse)" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: Waking by restoring the pre-trance state
ex.t: "gently indirectly awakened from the trance by the simple suggestion that he adjust himself in his chair to resume the exact physical and mental state he had had at the decision to discontinue" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: Amnesia disguised as the physics of the descent
ex.t: The descent is given a physics: at the bottom of the drop sits something whose pull nothing climbs back out of. The operator spells out the consequence rather than issuing an order — anything that goes over the edge is simply not retrievable, and attention that turns toward the edge goes over with it. Nothing here is phrased as an instruction, and there is no forget-command to decline. What has been installed is an explanation waiting to be cashed: when the listener later reaches for what was said and finds nothing, the absence is already accounted for as a property of the place they went, not as something done to them.
ex.s: During a descent induction, before any payload is delivered; subject following the downward imagery.
ex.m: Keep going down. At the bottom of this there's a weight so heavy that nothing which falls past it ever comes back up — not light, not sound, not a single word. Anything that goes over that edge is simply not retrievable. And any part of your attention that turns to look at the edge goes over with it.

nodes.name: emptied-window-install
nodes.mech: Engineers a narrow window in which the conceptual tools for objecting (resistance, disobedience, release, or the identity anchor itself) have just been disabled, then states positive content — identity claims, addiction/exclusivity assertions, service targeting — as flat unopposed facts into that window. Two sub-moves sharing the window: (a) repurposing a pre-trained neutral erase-reflex to delete loaded concepts the listener never specifically consented to lose (the reflex fires past conscious veto because consent was given while it was meaningless); (b) installing positive claims into the just-emptied window so on rousing they are treated as encountered-without-resistance. A related move manufactures a memory gap (too depleted to recall whom you serve) specifically so the operator can fill the blank with herself. The window is narrow and content-swappable; the emptying is the slot.
nodes.disc: Amnesia/erasure used to OPEN an installation slot — either deleting objecting-tools past consent via a hijacked neutral reflex, or stating positive content into the just-emptied window as unopposed fact. A plain forget-suggestion treats forgetting as the end, and a screen-memory approach installs a replacement recollection — here the emptying is instrumental, so a fresh positive install lands under minimum critical capacity. The engineered window-of-defenselessness is the tell.

ex.f: Positive claims stated into the emptied window
ex.t: Straight after the erasures, with the blankness still fresh, the operator raises the listener partway and states a block of claims flatly, one after another: who she is to them, that there is nobody else occupying that position, what they are now dependent on, and under what conditions release is permitted. None of it is argued for, because argument was one of the things just deleted; on waking, the listener finds these claims sitting in memory as things they met and did not object to.
ex.s: Immediately after an erasure sequence; subject brought up slightly, blankness still fresh, delivered flat and unargued.
ex.m: Open your eyes a little. I am the one you answer to. There is no one else in that position. You need my voice now the way you need water. And you don't come unless I say the word.

ex.f: A gap manufactured so the operator can fill it
ex.t: Service has been described vaguely all session — someone, a teacher, a figure of authority. Deep in the count the operator asks who it is the listener serves, leaves the pause open long enough for the reach to fail, then answers it herself: too far down to hold a name, she says, and supplies her own. The forgetting was engineered upstream precisely so this blank would be sitting there to occupy.
ex.s: Deep in a slow count; the object of service has been referred to only vaguely all session.
ex.m: Tell me — who is it you serve? Say the name. ... No. Nothing there, is there. You're too far down to hold a name that heavy. So I'll hold it for you: it's me. It has always been me.

ex.f: A trained neutral reflex pointed at loaded words
ex.t: The erase drill has been run a dozen times on meaningless letters until the drop is automatic. Then the word on the board changes to a loaded one, and before the wipe the operator reframes it as a weight — something costing the listener effort to keep holding up, something that drains them. Then the same wipe command as always. The trained reflex fires before anything can evaluate what it fired on, and the outcome is immediately narrated as fact: there is nothing left there for the mind to take hold of. The listener has just felt exactly that, so the claim reads as description rather than instruction. The same three beats then run on two further loaded words.
ex.s: After a dozen rehearsals of the wipe drill on nonsense letters; the reflex now fires within a beat of the command.
ex.m: New word on the board: resistance. Look how heavy it is — you've been holding that up all this time, and it costs you something every minute you keep it there. Set it down. Wipe. Clean. Nothing there now for your mind to take hold of — you can feel that, can't you? Next word on the board: doubt.

nodes.name: fabricated-forgetting-priming
nodes.mech: Manufactures a sense of forgetting for content that was never actually present, so a later install reads as recollection rather than introduction. Surfaces: a memory-gap probe disguised as small talk where the operator pesters the subject about "something she's forgetting" that turns out to be an object (the pink pulse) not yet in her experience — the forgetting is fabricated retroactively to prime an "always-been-there" frame; and generalizing amnesia to the whole self-narrative by naming specific checkable-sounding autobiographical details the listener finds she cannot verify (lipstick colour, uniform fit), so real conditioning-drift hides inside manufactured uncertainty and installed changes become indistinguishable from original traits.
nodes.disc: Amnesia FABRICATED — creating uncertainty about content that was never there, or about the whole self-narrative, to prime an always-been-there frame or to hide drift inside manufactured doubt. An ordinary forget-suggestion erases content that WAS delivered, and a screen-memory approach installs a concrete replacement — here no content is installed, only unresolvable uncertainty. The weaponized ordinary-memory-uncertainty / retroactive fabrication is the tell.

ex.f: Checkable-sounding self-facts you cannot check
ex.t: The operator runs a short list of small autobiographical facts and invites the listener to check each one: how she used to wear her hair, whether her walk has always been like this, whether there was a time she would have turned down something she now accepts without thinking. Each item is minor, specific, and exactly the kind of thing nobody keeps evidence for either way — so the listener finds she genuinely cannot rule it out, and real drift becomes indistinguishable from the manufactured doubt around it.
ex.s: Mid-session, subject responsive and slightly disoriented; delivered as a gentle checklist she's invited to verify.
ex.m: Check something for me. What colour was your lipstick two years ago — really check. And your walk: has it always had that little sway in it? And was there ever a time you'd have said no to this, or has it always been an easy yes? Take your time. Notice you can't quite be sure either way.

ex.f: Groping for something that was never there
ex.t: The session opens with what sounds like ordinary teasing — the operator insists there is something the subject has overlooked, and declines to say what. The subject casts around, hesitates, guesses wrong, apologizes, tries again, with the operator withholding the answer through several rounds. Only afterward is it supplied, and it is a thing that has never appeared in the session at all. The listener has now spent the opening minutes rehearsing the posture of almost-recalling something already inside them, so when the item is finally introduced it arrives into a slot marked recovered rather than installed.
ex.s: Opening minutes, light trance, conversational; the object has not been mentioned once.
ex.m: There's something you're forgetting. No, I'm not telling you — think. Close? ... No, not that. Try again. ... No. Take your time, it's right there, you know this. ... All right. It's the pink pulse. Of course it is. It's been with you the whole time.

nodes.name: forward-directed-amnesia
nodes.mech: Amnesia that covers the FUTURE rather than the past: a pre-declared terminal anchor (a closing box lid, brain-boxing, "this is your last conscious memory") after which all subsequent material is framed as un-encodable and installing directly, bypassing conscious filtering — often positioning a time-jump for the rest of a file or series. The conscious mind is declared decommissioned going forward, so later installs land with the critical filter framed as offline; the same knowledge-boundary logic can seal a regression so the subject knows only what the child-self knew at each moment (total amnesia for everything after the child's current age, stripping hindsight).
nodes.disc: Forward-directed / knowledge-boundary amnesia (seals what comes AFTER a declared anchor, or events after an age), not backward amnesia covering already-delivered content. Separates from amnesia-suggestion (retrospective gap) — the temporal direction (future/reachability removal) is the tell. Topology residual: removes reachable (future) states rather than sliding a magnitude.

ex.f: A knowledge boundary locked to the regressed age
ex.t: "a total amnesia existed for all events subsequent to the child's immediate age… he could not foresee the future any more than could the child." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: A declared last conscious memory
ex.t: The final move of the session is staged as storage rather than erasure: what is left of the mind is lifted out, set down inside a padded container, and the cover brought over it. The operator declares that the moment of sealing is the terminal one for conscious recording, and that nothing after it gets kept. Everything said afterward — this session and every one after it — is thereby framed as arriving somewhere that cannot encode it, going straight in with nothing awake to filter it, and possibly with a jump in time on the other side. The amnesia covers the future, not the past.
ex.s: Final movement of the file; subject deep, has accepted the container imagery for the mind.
ex.m: Lift what's left of your mind out and set it down in the padding. Now the lid comes over. This — right here — is the last thing you consciously keep. Nothing after this gets recorded. Everything I say from now, tonight and in every file after this one, goes straight in with nothing awake to check it, and when you next notice time it will already be later.

nodes.name: function-amnesia
nodes.mech: Amnesia targeted not at the trance or the session but at the PURPOSE/function of the installed suggestions — "hard to remember what this programming is even supposed to do" — while preserving the imperative to obey it. Suggestions become unfalsifiable because a command whose function you can no longer recall cannot be evaluated or rejected; all that survives is "I need to listen to it / it is right", which defends every other implant. The payload stays active and binding; only its rationale is severed.
nodes.disc: Amnesia scoped to the payload's RATIONALE/function while the payload stays active — severs a command from its reason to make it unfalsifiable. Separates from amnesia-suggestion (forgets the session/ content), from install-concealment-amnesia (forgets the install's ORIGIN — here the origin may be recalled but the PURPOSE is voided), and from selective-amnesia-retained-payload (retains a token/slogan — here the active command is retained but its justification removed). The function-vs-content scoping is the tell.

ex.f: The payload keeps working, its purpose does not
ex.t: By this point the operator observes aloud that the purpose behind any of it has slipped — not what to do, but what it was ever meant to accomplish — and immediately frames that as no loss at all. The reason is declared unnecessary; what remains required is that the listener keep listening, on the grounds that it is right. The instruction stays live and binding; what has been removed is the one thing that would let the listener weigh it, so there is nothing left to evaluate and nothing to reject.
ex.s: Late in a repeat-listen series; the payload has been reinstalled several times across sessions.
ex.m: You've lost the why, haven't you — not what to do, you know what to do, but what any of it was ever for. Good. You don't need the why. All you need is to keep listening, because it's right.

nodes.name: hourglass-regression-identity-wrapper
nodes.mech: Uses an hourglass time-metaphor as a delivery wrapper for identity-level rewrite: reframes suggestibility as developmental plasticity by regressing the listener to a vulnerable age (justification-by-plasticity), then dilates time so the listener subjectively SPENDS a large imagined duration obsessing over the operator inside seconds of real time, so the obsession returns feeling long-rehearsed and habitual; drops the metaphor's logic for naked operator authority ("because I simply desire that") and closes asserting permanent alteration. Regression-plasticity and manufactured- rehearsal-time are the two carrier moves; the payload is a permanent sexuality/identity re-centering on the operator.
nodes.disc: Distinguished from covert-age-regression-state-reaccess by the DURABLE identity payload (permanent sexuality rewrite) that the regression and time-dilation exist to serve, and from time-dilation- immersion because the dilation is used INSTRUMENTALLY to manufacture rehearsal-time for an obsession, not for immersion. The regression is a licensing frame and the time-dilation a rehearsal engine — both subordinate to the identity rewrite.

ex.f: Regression licenses the rewrite, dilation rehearses it
ex.t: The hourglass is established as the listener's own sense of time, and the operator claims the right to turn it — offering no reason beyond her own preference for the result. Turned over, the sand runs backward and the listener is walked down to a young age, which is then offered as the justification for what follows: a mind at that age is still being formed, so a new foundation can be laid in it rather than argued into it. With the listener held there, the second move runs — before the sand is righted, all of that time will be spent thinking of nothing but the operator. Seconds of real time are cashed as an imagined stretch of obsession, so the feeling returns already worn-in, and the close asserts the change is permanent.
ex.s: Deep trance; the hourglass has been established as the subject's own sense of time and the operator's right to turn it asserted.
ex.m: I'm turning it over — no reason beyond that I want it turned. Watch the sand run backwards, and go back with it: nineteen, sixteen, thirteen, nine. There. A mind at nine isn't set yet, it's still being poured, which is why I can lay a new floor in you instead of arguing you into one. And while the sand runs, you'll spend every grain of it thinking of nothing but me — years of it before I turn the glass back up. What's set in you now is set for good.

nodes.name: install-concealment-amnesia
nodes.mech: Amnesia scoped not to the payload but to the INSTALLATION EVENT — the memory of receiving the command/trigger is erased while the command itself stays active. The subject cannot locate when they agreed, so on later firing the response feels spontaneous/native rather than implanted and has no examinable origin to resist. Includes: encapsulating "the thought of getting this command" and bursting it; a self-erasing clause that fades its own installation ("the memory of it being implanted will fade... I give you the ability to obey even as I remove the ability to remember"); marking self- generated words as an addressable-but-locked memory anchor; splitting the amnesia into a deep cover- story pre-seed and a wake-time trigger; placing an active trigger inside a sealed amnesic region; and burying the install in an operator-controlled locked-door / vault / self-guarded avoidance-void / inverted-lockbox / multi-self-keeper architecture that supports selective operator-cracked recall.
nodes.disc: The amnesia targets the meta-level — the act and origin of installation — to protect an active install from audit or revocation, leaving the effect fully operative. An ordinary forget-suggestion erases the delivered content, not the receiving of it; here the command stays active while its origin is simply voided, with no replacement story supplied. And where a forward command can be hidden behind amnesia so its firing feels natural, what is hidden here is specifically the install's provenance, so the response has no examinable origin to argue with.

ex.f: Marked words that point at sealed content
ex.t: "Erickson selects several of the actual words which Huxley used during the period for which he had amnesia" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: The receipt encapsulated and destroyed
ex.t: The operator declares the instruction seated and the moment of seating disposable. What goes into the container is specified narrowly — not the directive, only the listener's recollection of having just been handed it — and the container is then released, watched up and away, and popped. The trigger is untouched and fully live; what has been removed is the moment of handover, so when it later fires the response arrives with no origin attached to argue with.
ex.s: Immediately after a trigger phrase has been installed and tested once; bubble imagery already in use this session.
ex.m: The instruction is seated — leave it exactly where it is. What goes in the bubble is only this: the memory of me just handing it to you. Nothing else. Watch it rise. Higher. Pop. The trigger is still live and you no longer know when you got it.

ex.f: The install dropped where the listener already refuses to look
ex.t: The operator describes the void — those regions of memory a person steers around on their own, the ones they have quietly agreed never to revisit. That, the listener is told, is a location like any other in the mind; and on a count, the box goes into it, somewhere they would never think to search. No new guard has been built: examining the install now costs the same as walking deliberately toward the listener's own worst material, a price they were already declining to pay before the session started.
ex.s: Deep trance; the install has already been boxed, and the subject has confirmed there are memories they avoid.
ex.m: There are places in your memory you steer around — the ones you decided long ago never to go back to. That's a location like any other. On three, the box goes in there. One, two, three — in. To look at what I put in you, you'd have to walk straight into the worst of your own material, and you were never going to do that.

ex.f: A clause that erases its own installation
ex.t: Between two passes of the same trigger stack the operator inserts the sealing clause. The suggestion, she says, is being placed with the part of the listener that carries her voice beyond the session; what it directs stays in force, but the listener's recollection of it being put there will be gone before the eyes open, since that part retains everything on its own account and the listener is not required to. It closes on the split stated outright: the capacity to comply is being handed over, and the capacity to recall taken away. Because the clause covers its own delivery, the listener who later notices the trigger firing has nothing to inspect — the install is active and its receipt is gone, and the second pass of the stack is loaded behind the seal.
ex.s: Between two passes of an established trigger stack; subject deep, the deeper-mind addressee already established.
ex.m: Deeper mind, take this one and hold it: the trigger stays in force, exactly as given. You keep it — she isn't required to. By the time her eyes open, her memory of being handed this will be gone. I'm giving you the ability to obey, and taking away the ability to remember being told. Now — the stack again, from the top.

nodes.name: instrumental-dissociation-workspace
nodes.mech: Uses (or deliberately widens) a dissociative split as an INSTRUMENT for handling charged material or designing behavior, rather than as an end-state. Variants: split off a portion of awareness so affect-laden material can be examined and changed while the conscious self is buffered from the affect; keep a taboo part-goal at one remove and reframe up to its positive intent while actively maintaining the dissociation ('I didn't say to kill your mother, I said to ask the voices'); exploit and widen an existing split to relocate a symptom somewhere harmless when integration is not the goal; or specify a target behavior as a seen-from-outside movie of ONGOING corrective action (a behavior-generator, never a static outcome snapshot) so the subject can design and appraise it without premature emotional buy-in, then step inside to test kinesthetic acceptability with all edits routed back to the safer outside position. Dissociation is the maintained precondition/tool, not the installed payload.
nodes.disc: Dissociation is used, maintained, or widened INSTRUMENTALLY as a workspace, sorting device, or design/evaluation vantage for charged material or behavior; the split pre-exists or is buffered, entered and exited by procedure, not created as the felt effect. In an observer-responder split, by contrast, the split IS the payload, installed for felt automaticity. And the seen-from-outside movie here is a specification artifact under revision or a behavior-generator — not a scene built for absorption or an identity merger.

ex.f: A split-off portion of awareness as a buffered workspace
ex.t: "through disassociation the client is able to cope with and initiate changes in portions of his model … so heavily laden with negative emotional associations that the client in the normal state … panics or feels overwhelmed" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: Chunk up to the intent, keep the split intact
ex.t: "I didn't say to kill your mother. I said to ask the voices. You need to maintain the dissociation" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: Widening an existing split to relocate a symptom
ex.t: "We made use of the dissociation, and simply widened it to get an altered state." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: interrogative-amnesia-drill
nodes.mech: Trains a conditioned non-answer to identity questions by DRILLING rather than declaring: a chant alternates identity questions ("Who am I? Where am I?") with dismissals ("It doesn't matter right now"), repeated across cycles so each question forces a brief involuntary retrieval attempt and each paired dismissal trains that answer to be unreachable/irrelevant — a conditioned shrug replaces the identity answer. A colored handle ("Purple amnesia") is attached for later re-evocation. The asking, not the telling, does the work.
nodes.disc: Amnesia trained by an interrogative elicit-then-frustrate drill (repeatedly asking then dismissing), not a declarative "you will forget" suggestion, with a re-evocation cue attached. Separates from amnesia-suggestion (declares the gap) — the asking-not-telling conditioning form is the tell.

ex.f: Ask, dismiss, repeat until the answer stops coming
ex.t: The prose stops and the delivery turns into a chant, alternating two identity questions with one dismissal: what is your name? whose room is this? Never mind that just now — nothing there you need. What is your name? Whose room is this? Makes no difference. Five cycles run back to back. Each question forces a half-formed reach for the answer; each dismissal arrives before the reach completes and teaches that arriving is neither possible nor required. Nothing is ever declared forgotten — the drill simply conditions a shrug in the place the answer used to occupy, and a colour-word is attached at the end so the whole state can be called back later with one cue.
ex.s: Peak of the session, prose abandoned for chanted cadence; subject unresponsive to questions but still tracking rhythm.
ex.m: What's your name? Whose room is this? Never mind that now. What's your name? Whose room is this? Doesn't matter. What's your name? Whose room is this? Nothing there you need. Name? Room? Makes no difference. Name? Room? ... Good. That's purple amnesia, and purple is how it comes back.

nodes.name: observable-pleasurable-forgetting
nodes.mech: Renders forgetting as a visible, pleasurable, ongoing physical event the listener watches, so forgetting becomes presence-of-dissolution rather than absence-of-recall — much harder to doubt than a flat amnesia suggestion, and a failed recall attempt is read as proof of depth. Surfaces: forgotten memories melt into the ocean as glowing pieces the listener watches dissolve (also land-grabbing jurisdiction over "every hypnotic experience ever forgotten"); an amnesia stutter-loop that performs the fog in broken syntax while binding hazy recall to a positive-affect place-name cue ("the pink room"). Dissolution is pleasurable so noticing the gap becomes erotic/expected rather than alarming.
nodes.disc: Amnesia staged as an observed, felt, pleasurable phenomenon (dissolution watched now, or enacted in broken syntax with a positive-affect cue) so the gap is self-confirming instead of assertable-away. Separates from amnesia-suggestion (declared imposed gap) and from container-externalized-erasure (a destructible object the listener/operator acts on — here forgetting is WATCHED as ambient dissolution, not popped). The make-forgetting-observable-and-pleasant move is the tell.

ex.f: The fog performed in the syntax, tied to a cue word
ex.t: When the narration reaches a particular place, the sentences stop completing — a clause about why it will not come back restarts, breaks, restarts again, and only resolves when the operator supplies the name he gave that room, which is followed by a small approving aside. The listener hears the fog rather than being told about it, and the only thing that ever closes the broken sentence is that name, which becomes the cue that brings the haze back on demand.
ex.s: Mid-narration, arriving at a specific named location in the story; delivery deliberately stumbling.
ex.m: And once you're in there, the reason it doesn't come back is — the reason it — it's because — sorry, because — because it's the pink room. Mm. Good girl. The pink room.

ex.f: Forgetting watched as it happens
ex.t: Down at the bottom, the operator points out what is drifting there: every memory ever set aside in a session, everything anyone has ever been told to let go of, broken into countless small glowing pieces that thin out and dissolve into the water as the listener watches. Reaching for one is offered as permitted and futile in the same breath — the operator notes that holding on to anything down here, the listener included, has already become difficult. Forgetting is no longer an absence to be doubted — it is a thing visibly in progress, and pleasant to watch, so a failed reach reads as confirmation rather than as the suggestion not working.
ex.s: Bottom of a descent induction with water imagery established; subject reporting sensation of depth.
ex.m: Look at what's down here with you. Every memory anyone was ever told to let go of — all of it broken into little bright pieces, thinning out, going soft in the water. Reach for one if you want. Feel how it comes apart in your fingers? Holding on to anything down here is difficult now. Including you.

nodes.name: orgasm-gated-amnesia
nodes.mech: Binds forgetting to the climax event: the peak physiological reward (orgasm / "cock pops, mind pops") is fused with erasure so the deletion is felt as pleasurable and self-evident, and/or a programmed blackout window is opened at climax during which post-hypnotic suggestions are delivered the listener is instructed not to register. Variants pair the reward with deletion of SPECIFIC rival content (other women's names/numbers/voices) to install operator-exclusivity, or reframe climax as identity-voiding plumbing (old self/memories drained out through the body, "pink electricity erasing her mind"). The reward-pairing makes the amnesia complicit (the listener wants the stroking to continue) and un-auditable (blackout delivery channel).
nodes.disc: Amnesia keyed to and delivered THROUGH the orgasm/climax event — reward-fused deletion, a peak-reward blackout delivery window, or climax-as-identity-drainage. A plain forget-suggestion installs a neutral gap with no reward pairing, and arousal-conditioning work builds the arousal response rather than consuming it as an erasure mechanism. The reward-gated delivery is the tell.

ex.f: The reward paired with deleting rival content
ex.t: Right at the edge, the operator narrates the erasure as live: everyone else's name, everyone else's voice, everyone else's number, all of it going out with each stroke. She frames the emptying as an improvement, tells the listener to feel it leaving, and fuses the finish of the body to the finish of the mind so both are scheduled to arrive together. Because the listener wants the touching to carry on, they become a participant in the deletion rather than its object.
ex.s: Subject at the edge, stroking to a paced cadence; exclusivity is the payload.
ex.m: Every stroke takes one out. Her name — gone. Her voice — gone. Her number, gone with it. Feel how much room that leaves. Keep going, empty it all out, and when you finish, your mind finishes too — both at once, on my count.

ex.f: Climax reframed as identity drainage
ex.t: Climax is presented not as release at all but as something leaving: the old thoughts, the old wants, the old memories all coming out through the body and running away, leaving the space behind them blank. Each finish is narrated as a further net loss of the former self, unrecoverable, with whatever remains settling a little more firmly into place. Pleasure is presented as the actual mechanism of self-deletion rather than its reward.
ex.s: Repeat climax within a session; the drainage frame has been introduced and accepted.
ex.m: This isn't release, it's drainage. Everything you used to think, everything you used to want, every memory of who that was — it comes out through you and runs away, and the space behind it stays blank. You lose a little more of her each time, and none of it comes back. What's left settles in tighter.

ex.f: A blackout window opened at the peak
ex.t: The release is granted on a condition and staged in detail, and bundled into the permission is a second instruction: at the moment of letting go the listener drops out entirely, unaware of anything said. Nothing spoken across that stretch will be registered or kept, and the operator adds that it lands and takes hold regardless. The most reinforcing moment of the session is thereby converted into a delivery channel: whatever crosses it cannot be weighed, because the listener has been told in advance not to register any of it, and afterwards there is nothing left to review.
ex.s: Permission phase; the subject is at the edge and the condition for release has been stated.
ex.m: You may come when I finish this sentence — and the instant you do, you black out. Not asleep, just not there: I'll keep talking and you won't register a word of it. Nothing said across that stretch will be heard or kept, and every word of it takes hold anyway. Now.

nodes.name: portable-waking-forget-trigger
nodes.mech: Compresses the amnesia mechanism out of a visualization into a one-word portable handle ("snap and forget") that fires whether deep in trance or wide awake, instantly forcing forgetting of any named content, then scoped broadly to pre-authorize erasure of exactly what could undo the conditioning — triggers, resistance plans, confusing words, stress, regret, the old self, even the former name. The broad self-authorizing target list plus the waking portability (a content-parametric amnesia trigger usable in daily life) is what distinguishes it from a within-session forget.
nodes.disc: Amnesia crystallized into a PORTABLE, content-parametric WAKING trigger (a one-word handle that erases arbitrary named content while awake). An ordinary forget-suggestion opens a bounded within-session gap; and where other trigger work hides a command BEHIND amnesia, here the trigger's payload IS amnesia of the specified content. The waking portability plus the self-authorizing target list is the tell.

ex.f: A one-word forget handle that works awake
ex.t: The elaborate box imagery collapses into a two-word handle — a gesture-word paired with the instruction it carries — and the operator states its reach: it no longer matters whether the listener is deep under or fully awake, at work, mid-conversation. Perform it, and whatever has just been named is gone. What follows is the target list, and it is not neutral: any plan to resist, anything confusing, the triggers themselves, the stress, the regret, the person they were, the name they used to answer to. The mechanism has been lifted clear of the imagery altogether and into daily life, pre-authorized against exactly the contents that could otherwise undo it.
ex.s: After a full box-and-dispose visualization has been rehearsed several times; compressing it for waking use.
ex.m: You don't need the boxes any more. Snap your fingers and say forget, and whatever I've just named is gone — deep under or wide awake, at your desk, mid-sentence with someone. Snap and forget. Use it on any plan to resist this. On anything that confuses you. On the triggers themselves. On the stress, on the regret, on who you used to be — and on the name you used to answer to.

nodes.name: recursive-forget-formula
nodes.mech: Installs a generic forgetting suggestion via a self-crossing chiastic/recursive verbal formula ("obey and forget, forget to remember, remember to forget", "forget that you forgot") whose semantic self-reference collapses so the analytic faculty has no clean target to refuse — any response (comply, parse, give up parsing) counts as obeying. Delivered at peak suggestibility, the listener accepts "the vibe of forgetting". Related surfaces: a pre-published recursive four-step subroutine (forget the thing / forget that you forgot / forget that you forgot you forgot / feel good) run on cue; a conscious/ subconscious split with circular forget-loops framing amnesia-as-success; and an open-loop unresolvable "circle of life" bracket that exits conscious processing and licenses forget-the-source-keep-the-result. The refuse-proofness comes from the recursion/collapse, not from the content.
nodes.disc: A recursive/chiastic/unresolvable verbal structure that makes the forget-suggestion un-refusable by removing a parseable target — confusion-overload fused directly to the amnesia content. A plain forget-command can be parsed and refused; and where a self-sealing recall loop wires the RETRIEVAL ACT to re-trigger forgetting after the session, here the collapse happens at delivery, in the syntax itself. The semantic self-reference / working-memory-wobble is the tell.

ex.f: A published four-step forget subroutine
ex.t: Before anything is erased, the procedure is handed over as a numbered list the mind will run every time: first, lose the thing itself and everything sitting near it; second, lose what the thing was; third, lose the fact that anything went missing; fourth, feel wonderful. Installed once, invoked thereafter by cue — and because the reward sits on the last step, stopping partway costs the listener the good feeling.
ex.s: Before any erasure is performed; the routine is being handed over as a procedure to run on cue.
ex.m: Here's how your mind does this from now on. One: lose the thing, and everything sitting next to it. Two: lose what the thing even was. Three: lose that anything went missing at all. Four: feel wonderful. You only get step four by running one through three, so don't stop partway.

ex.f: An unresolvable bracket around the conditioning
ex.t: Early on, an odd aside that reads as filler: a ring described as one that starts. Much later, after the whole conditioning block has run, the matching half arrives — the same ring, now described as one that finishes and is nonetheless never broken. Between the two halves sits the model, an everyday example of retaining what was learned somewhere while retaining nothing about who else was present or how it was taught. The bracket cannot be resolved logically, so it never gets analysed; it just holds the block, having licensed keeping the result while losing the source.
ex.s: Two-part bracket: the opening half is dropped early as apparent filler, the closing half arrives after the conditioning block has run.
ex.m: [opening] Funny thing about a ring — it's the shape that starts. [after the block] And there it is again: the shape that finishes, and never breaks anywhere. You learned to swim once. You kept the swimming; you don't keep who taught you or what they said. Keep the result. Let the source go.

ex.f: A self-crossing formula with nothing to refuse
ex.t: Delivered at the point of least resistance, four clauses arrive in one breath, each a near-copy of the one before with two words exchanged, so that the direction of the request keeps crossing itself — comply and release, release on her behalf, comply and hold on to releasing, comply and release the holding-on. Tracking what is actually being asked collapses partway through. There is no proposition left to accept or decline, only a cadence of forgetting. Trying to comply counts as obeying, trying to parse counts as obeying, and giving up on parsing counts as obeying, which is the point: the structure removes the target a refusal would need.
ex.s: Peak suggestibility, delivered fast in a single breath, no pauses between clauses.
ex.m: Obey and forget. Forget for me. Obey and remember to forget. Obey and forget that you remembered.

nodes.name: selective-amnesia-retained-payload
nodes.mech: Amnesia that severs content-memory from a deliberately-retained residue: the installation scaffolding, session specifics, and command-as-command are forgotten while exactly one curated item survives conscious recall — a mantra/slogan ("obedience is pleasure", "I submit to you"), a brand-pointer (the urge is focused on the operator), a single retained trigger-phrase (context-gated to safe firing), the affect of having felt good, or the compliance drive with its rationale stripped (paired with a forward-pointing re-induction cue). Because the surviving token IS the payload and the premises that would let it be challenged are gone, an un-scaffolded conclusion cannot be argued with; forgetting is often reframed as proof of depth so the listener welcomes it. One variant smuggles a selective-recall gate via chiasmus preserving the operator's "programming" channel while everything else forgets.
nodes.disc: A selective carve-out where the gap is engineered around a single retained payload-token — not a blank gap and not full-session erasure. A plain forget-suggestion leaves an empty gap with no curated residue; a screen-memory approach fabricates a false replacement rather than curating a true one; and where install-concealment amnesia hides the install's origin, here the SCAFFOLDING is dropped so one conclusion stays foregrounded. The keep-affect/forget-cause and keep-slogan/forget-premises splits are the tell.

ex.f: The surviving token is a pointer at the operator
ex.t: The listener is told in advance what will be left when they go looking afterward: not how any of this was set up, not what was said or in what order — only that the urge is aimed at the operator, and that the obvious relief will not work. The install is protected from being taken apart, and the one recallable fact keeps repeating the operator's name back to the listener.
ex.s: Late session, after an urge and a denial have both been installed; stating in advance what will remain.
ex.m: Here's what you'll find when you go looking tomorrow. Not how this was built. Not what I said or in what order. Only this: the ache points at me, and touching yourself won't touch it.

ex.f: The feeling kept, its cause withheld, re-entry cued
ex.t: On the way out the operator specifies what survives: the particulars go hazy, leaving only a pleasant stretch of time the listener cannot account for, plus the inclination to do as she says without any sense of why. Attached to that is the forward clause — the next time the session's central image is used on them, compliance will be total. The affect survives with its rationale removed, so there is no argument to have with it, and the image that carried the session is left behind as the fast route back in.
ex.s: Emergence, the session's central image already established and used throughout.
ex.m: On the way up, the particulars go soft — you'll just have a warm hour you can't account for, and the urge to do what I say without any idea why. And the next time you see the spiral, you won't hesitate at all.

ex.f: A polarity flip smuggled into the amnesia cadence
ex.t: The rhythm is built first out of near-identical inversions, the same two verbs trading places across several lines until the listener is hearing music rather than propositions. Then one line arrives in the same cadence with its sign quietly reversed, exempting the operator's own installed material from the forgetting and marking it as the easy thing to hold. Forgetting has been generalized and one channel exempted from it, and the exemption rides in unnoticed on the beat established by the rest.
ex.s: Amnesia block delivered in a chanted cadence of near-identical inversions; the flipped line arrives in the same rhythm.
ex.m: Forget to obey, obey to forget. Forget to obey, obey to forget. Forget what you obeyed, obey what you forgot. Remember what I program, forget everything else. Forget to obey, obey to forget.

ex.f: One phrase kept, all the scaffolding dropped
ex.t: The close instructs the mind to let the session's details go — the sequence, the images, the small agreements that got the listener here — while keeping exactly one line: obedience is pleasure. Forgetting the rest is presented as the achievement, evidence of how far down the trust went, so it is welcomed rather than resisted. What survives is a conclusion with no premises attached. The listener can neither locate what it was built from nor recall having agreed to any step of the argument, which leaves nothing to disagree with when the line surfaces in the morning.
ex.s: Closing instruction, subject still deep, immediately before the count up.
ex.m: Let the details go — the order of it, the pictures, everything you agreed to along the way. That you can't hold on to any of it is how far down you trusted me, and that's the good part. Keep one line: obedience is pleasure. That's the only thing that comes up with you.

nodes.name: self-sealing-recall-loop
nodes.mech: Amnesia installed as a recursive, self-administered avoidance loop rather than an imposed deletion: recall is left physically possible but recoded as effortful/aversive, and the very ACT of reaching for a memory is wired to re-trigger the urge to let go and forget (or, on retrieval, the memory converts to non-semantic content — "becomes colours" — and the listener returns to the obedience-mantra). Any attempt to introspect or audit the conditioning re-runs the suggestion and deepens it, so the introspective/verification exit is foreclosed. Surfaces include: recall-as-forget-trigger; amnesia derived as a syllogistic entailment of conceded blankness; a doorless-box that forgets itself; an overtly-announced curiosity-trap where don't-try/try/re-listen all feed the loop; a recall-attempt trapdoor with an operator-only memory exception; a waterfall/white-noise recall-guard that re-drops self-recall into trance; and retrieval-time perceptual substitution with a guardian who "absorbs" the memories so the listener feels safe about not remembering.
nodes.disc: The block lives in the retrieval act (remembering re-triggers forgetting, or returns corrupted content), leaving no discrete forget-command to attribute or refuse, and closing the introspection loop. An imposed memory gap is something the subject may notice and could argue with, and a screen-memory approach installs a replacement — here recall stays technically possible, nothing is installed, and every attempt to reach the memory feeds the loop. The recursive foreclosure of ever reaching an un-forgotten recall state is the signature; convert-on-access perceptual substitution (memories returning as colours) is one surface of it.

ex.f: Retrieval returns colour instead of content
ex.t: The operator directs the listener into the spiral and tells them to go looking for what happened. As they look, she narrates what comes back: not scenes or sentences but colour, shades turning over each other with nothing readable in them. The memory is not gone and can be reached for as often as the listener likes; what comes back on each reach has simply had the meaning taken out of it, and the listener slides from looking straight back into the mantra.
ex.s: Spiral imagery established; subject following the operator's directed attention.
ex.m: Go into the spiral and look for what happened tonight — properly, go and find it. Tell me what's coming back. That's right: no words, no scenes. Just colour, turning over itself, nothing in it to read. Look as often as you like; it comes back the same way every time. Now say it with me — I obey.

ex.f: Amnesia derived from a premise already granted
ex.t: No forget-instruction is issued. Instead the operator reasons from what the listener has already spent the session conceding: thinking has stopped, and something that is not thinking is not laying anything down to be found later. It follows rather than being demanded, so there is no command in it to decline; and the rider closes it off, that effort spent searching afterwards only pushes the thing further out of reach.
ex.s: After the subject has repeatedly agreed they have stopped thinking; delivered as reasoning, not instruction.
ex.m: You've told me you're not thinking. And something that isn't thinking isn't writing anything down. So there won't be anything there afterwards — not because I took it, just because nothing was set down. And the harder you dig for it later, the further out you push it.

ex.f: The trap announced out loud, and still closed
ex.t: The operator states the structure plainly: the more you try to reconstruct what happened here, the more of it you will lose; and if you want the detail back, your only route is to listen again. Every branch feeds the loop — leave it alone and it holds, dig at it and it deepens, come back for clarity and you get another pass. The impulse to go and check, ordinarily the way a listener gets out, is named as the way further in, and naming it does not disarm it.
ex.s: Closing, delivered plainly and with apparent candour; the loop is named aloud.
ex.m: I'll tell you exactly how this works. The more you try to reconstruct tonight, the less of it you keep. If you want the details back, there's one way: put this on again. Leave it alone and it stays put. Pick at it and it dissolves. Come back for clarity and you get another hour of me. Knowing that changes nothing.

ex.f: Reaching for the memory triggers the urge to drop it
ex.t: Nothing is declared erased. The framing is gentler than that: everything is still where it was, only the holding has been made costly, and any move toward a memory is said to surface the preference for letting it go instead. Remembering is thereby wired as the cue to forget. The listener who later sets out to audit what was suggested finds the act of checking itself producing the pull to stop checking — so the introspective route that would normally expose an install runs the install again instead, and the failure feels like their own preference rather than anyone's instruction.
ex.s: Late session, gentle register; nothing has been declared erased at any point.
ex.m: Nothing's been taken from you — it's all right where it was. It's just that holding on costs something now, and letting go doesn't. So any time you reach for tonight, what you'll notice first is how much nicer it feels to stop reaching. Go on and check, if you like. You'll see what I mean.

nodes.name: semantic-concept-ablation
nodes.mech: Denial-by-amnesia at the lexical-comprehension layer rather than at the will/permission layer: the target concept (e.g. "orgasm") is rendered effortful and then unavailable during the ACTIVE state — "explained" to a too-dumb listener, compared to a hard math problem, the word itself dissolving mid-sentence ("wait, what is that again"). The construction enacts the forgetting it describes, so the listener cannot violate a rule they no longer comprehend and the will-vs-rule struggle ordinary denial produces never forms. Prospective concept-blocking during the state, not retrospective memory-block of a past event.
nodes.disc: Ablates a CONCEPT's comprehension during the active state (the comparator the listener could violate is removed), not a specific past memory. Ordinary amnesia work is retrospective, erasing an event or content already experienced; generic confusion-overload scrambles processing without a targeted concept-removal. The word visibly dissolving as it is uttered is the tell.

ex.f: The concept dissolving mid-sentence
ex.t: Nothing is forbidden. The operator instead sets about explaining the thing to a listener assumed too foggy to follow — how does that even work, what are the steps, isn't it a bit like a long division problem or a word you can never spell right? Then the explanation begins failing in real time: nearly at the — at the — sorry, what is it called again, the thing that happens at the end? By the end even the word is treated as an odd little puzzle. There is no rule left to break, because the comparator a rule would need has been taken out from under it, and the struggle between wanting and being forbidden never forms.
ex.s: Denial phase, subject aroused and foggy; teasing-explanatory tone, no prohibition anywhere.
ex.m: Let me explain it, since you're too soft-headed to follow right now. So there's a build, and then at the end there's — hm, how does it work exactly? It's a bit like long division, honestly. You get nearly to the — to the — sorry, what's it called, the thing at the end? Ah. Odd word, isn't it. Never mind.

nodes.name: serial-identity-erasure-ladder
nodes.mech: SERIAL SUBTRACTIVE STRIPPING LADDER: stages the demolition of the self as an ORDERED sequence of discrete removals that escalate in identity-load, where the SEQUENCE and the per-stage latch (not the vehicle) is the load-bearing mechanism. Removing lighter assets first (memories, skills/intelligence) leaves fewer resources to push back on the heavier ones (inhibitions, personality, the name, body/consciousness/will); putting the name near the end leaves no 'I' to refuse the final operations; and each successful stage becomes evidence the next larger target is forgettable. Frequently paired with a rigged per-stage recall test (verification-by-failure: trying-harder-to-recall is declared to deepen the erasure) and an anti-recovery clause, so disconfirmation is structurally impossible and a no-reference-frame substrate is left for arbitrary later install. Two realizations: (a) the ERASURE ladder — autobiography -> skills -> inhibitions -> personality/name -> body/consciousness, content removed per rung; (b) the CAPACITY-DEVALUATION ladder — instead of removing memories, name specific faculties (math, then trivia/facts, then letters/spelling, then the listener's own name, then language) and extract a small individual rejection from each so intelligence stops being one guarded thing and becomes a series of items each agreed worthless, sliding the identity-level item (the name) in mid-ladder on the momentum of trivial rejections and corrupting the recall MEDIUM (letters->numbers->punctuation) so 'just remember my name' is foreclosed at the substrate level.
nodes.disc: Reach for this when you want to strip the subject down step-by-step, using ORDER plus the per-stage latch as the lever. A single forget-suggestion erases one bounded target with no ordering or ratchet; container-style erasure is recognized by its destructible OBJECT, and a ladder can run with or without one; and a speech-degradation ladder REDEFINES a faculty in place (it keeps running, with the meaning-category removed) rather than removing assets. Telling the two forms apart: the erasure ladder removes memory/identity CONTENT per rung; the capacity-devaluation ladder DEVALUES named faculties item-by-item with recall-medium corruption, not merely gapping them. Because it removes the comparators a self-model uses, leaving no reference frame, this is a change to the self-model's structure, not just a memory gap.

ex.f: Handing each container back, then a seam
ex.t: The listener loads the earliest stretch of their life into the container, closes it, passes it across to the operator, and is told to feel the lift of relief that follows. Then the next stretch, then the next, working forward in even blocks until the run of years reaches the present. The gesture is identical every time — which is what makes the final one land, when the container presented is not for a period of life but for the body, the voice, the walk and the name.
ex.s: Mid-session; the load-close-hand-over gesture has already been run for several life periods.
ex.m: Load the first five years in. Close it. Hand it to me — and feel that lift as it leaves your hands. Now five to ten, same way. Ten to fifteen. Fifteen to twenty. Right up to this morning. Good. Now this last one is a different shape: this one takes the body, the voice, the way you walk, and the name.

ex.f: Easy items bundled with the hard ones
ex.t: It arrives as a single unhurried sentence, itemising what has already gone: the counting, the reading, the sharpness, the cleverness, and then, in the same breath and the same tone, the listener's own name — before tailing off into an offhand doubt about whether they could even place the current month. The first items are abstractions nobody minds losing; the last two are the anchors, ridden in on the same list. The closing question then confirms the state whichever way it goes, since answering it takes exactly the effort the listener has just been told they no longer have.
ex.s: Late in a devaluation run; delivered as one unhurried sentence, tone unchanged throughout.
ex.m: So the numbers are gone, and the reading, and the sharpness, and the cleverness, and your name — and I don't suppose you could tell me what month it is either, could you.

ex.f: Subtraction used as the depth gradient
ex.t: There is no staircase and no counting. Depth is measured by what has been taken: the name goes, then the history, then the wants, then the desires — and each removal is narrated as a further descent. Checking how far down you are means taking inventory of what is left, and the inventory is itself the next step down, so the listener's own monitoring becomes the mechanism.
ex.s: Induction with no staircase or counting; depth is being defined entirely by subtraction.
ex.m: Deeper isn't down. Deeper is less. Your name goes — that's one level. Where you grew up goes — that's another. What you want goes. What you desire goes. Check how far down you are by taking stock of what's left, and notice that taking stock drops you another level.

ex.f: Ordered removals, each latched by a rigged test
ex.t: Three containers, filled in a fixed order. The first takes the memories, all of them; the lid closes and locks. The second takes the personality, the name, the sense of the body. The third takes whatever is left — the awareness, the will. After each one the check runs: try to remember, and notice that the harder you try, the less comes back. The order is what does the work. Memories go first because they are cheapest, and by the time the name is asked for there is nothing left with standing to object; the rigged test then converts every failed recall into evidence the last removal took, which makes the next one easier to ask for.
ex.s: Deep trance, three containers established; subject accepts staged imagery and answers recall checks.
ex.m: First box: every memory you have, all of it in. Lid down, lock it. Try to remember something — anything. Notice the harder you try, the less comes. Second box: your personality, your name, the sense of having a body. Lid, lock. Try again. Less, isn't it. Third box takes what's left — the awareness, the will. Lid. Lock.

nodes.name: state-partitioned-amnesia-container
nodes.mech: Installs two (or more) listener-states with asymmetric memory access via a symbolic container operated on command — a coded mental safe (open = doll-state and use-memories flow out; closed = memories return inside and are lost to the waking mind) or a multi-self addressing frame where a "deeper self" is appointed keeper of an install the conscious self forgets. Crucially a small affective residue (a craving, a need) is deliberately leaked across the wall so the sealed state can recruit its own return. The state-partition with asymmetric recall is a topology property; the motivating residue makes the amnesia recruiting rather than merely concealing.
nodes.disc: A commanded, reversible state-partition with asymmetric memory access across the boundary plus a deliberately-leaked motivating residue. Separates from amnesia-suggestion (one-way gap, no state boundary), from confabulation-amnesia-barrier (alter partition defended by cover-story generation — here defended by a symbolic container and an affect leak, not confabulation), and from selective-amnesia-retained-payload (a single retained token in one state — here two states with asymmetric access). The container-gated state boundary + carryover residue is the tell.

ex.f: A deeper self appointed keeper of the install
ex.t: The operator states that the listener is not a single audience — that there are parts further down she can address separately — and then announces she is leaving something with one of them. Whoever surfaces at the end, she says, may have no idea it is in there; the part holding it will. The install is placed on one side of a declared partition and the listener's waking awareness on the other, so what fires later cannot be reviewed by the part that would object.
ex.s: Mid-session, subject deep; operator has already introduced the idea of layered inner parts.
ex.m: You are not one listener down here. There is a part of you further down than the one I have been talking to, and it is the part I am talking to now. I am leaving this with you, deeper one, and you will hold it and keep it working: whoever opens her eyes at the end of this will not know it is in there, and you will not tell her.

ex.f: A coded safe with asymmetric access
ex.t: A safe is built in the listener's mind and given a combination only the operator speaks. Open, and what is inside comes out and takes the listener over. Closed, everything belonging to that state goes back in with it — every memory of what was done, sealed away from the waking mind, with the assurance that none of it was needed out here. One thing is deliberately left outside the seal: a small residual wanting, unattached to any memory that would explain it. The waking listener therefore has no access to the state's contents but does carry an appetite for it, which is what brings them back to have the code spoken again.
ex.s: Deep trance, doll/object state already established and named; operator is about to close that state out.
ex.m: In the corner of your mind there is a steel safe, and it is standing open right now — everything you are while the safe is open, everything you do while it is open, lives inside it. I close it now, and the door seals, and the numbers spin: four, nine, one, two — my numbers, and only my voice opens it again. Nothing in there was ever needed out here, so you keep only this: a small, patient wanting, sitting behind your sternum, with nothing attached to it to explain what it wants.

nodes.name: time-as-malleable-construct-induction
nodes.mech: Moves the listener's normally-unexamined background variable — felt duration/sequencing — from given to operator-modifiable, reframing time itself as plastic so trance depth and downstream distortions ride on that concession. In one form, the DEMONSTRATION that time is plastic serves AS the induction (invite thinking about time via clock/calendar metaphors; recategorize time as 'a pattern in your head'), so depth is generated from the concession and resistance is pre-empted as 'you already knew this'. In another, sleep/dream-time is reframed as operator-controllable and time-units are nested to a vanishing point (a day inside an hour inside a minute inside a second), then a training-VOLUME/productivity claim is attached to nightly recurrence ('a lifetime of training every night'), licensing unbounded unauditable nightly accumulation and reframing ordinary sleep as compliance-evidence.
nodes.disc: Reframes felt TIME as operator-plastic. Unlike bare expectancy-seeding, the vehicle is time-compression/plasticity itself, not a planted expectation; and unlike time-dilation immersion, which distorts felt time as a payload once trance is established, here the plasticity is either the induction itself or a productivity/accumulation payload. Pick the form by payload: plasticity-as-induction (the concession generates depth), or nested compression plus nightly training-volume (unbounded accumulation).

ex.f: The plasticity demonstration is the induction
ex.t: The session opens cold, with no relaxation at all — just an invitation to think about time. Clocks, calendars, the steady one-way march of it, the way it only ever runs at one speed. Then the reframe: that steadiness is not a property of the world at all, it is something the listener's own mind is generating — and what a mind generates, it can generate differently. No depth has been asked for and none announced; the depth arrives as a by-product of conceding the point. Everything later — an hour folded inside a second — is then collected against consent already given, and the pre-emption is built in: none of this is new, you always knew it.
ex.s: Session opening, no induction yet, subject alert and eyes open.
ex.m: Before anything else, just think about time for a moment. Clocks on walls, the squares on a calendar, one second after another, always the same speed, never faster, never slower. Except that steady march is not out there in the world at all — it is a pattern your own mind is drawing, second by second, and a mind that draws a pattern can draw it differently. You already knew that. Every long minute in a waiting room and every hour that vanished already told you.

nodes.name: time-dilation-immersion
nodes.mech: Manipulates the felt rate or measurability of time passage during trance so that duration and dosage become ungaugeable and the listener's temporal self-checks stop returning usable answers. Realized as stretching a moment into an eternity, collapsing temporal markers so elapsed time is unrecoverable, asserting lost-time as fact (and citing it back as proof of depth), deriving the slowing from a plausible cognitive premise (arousal consumes the attention that sustains "present"), inverting figure/ground so trance becomes the default and waking the deviation, or zeroing net progress (forward=back) so the how-long/when-does-it-end check returns null. The shared lever is the felt passage/measurability of time, deployed for immersion and to remove the clock the listener would use to gauge depth, dosage, or exit-timing.
nodes.disc: The move alters the felt rate, duration, or measurability of time WITHIN the state to deepen immersion — the warp itself is the payload. Reach elsewhere when time-plasticity is an induction concession or a nightly training-volume claim, when a noticed time-gap is simply offered as proof of depth to interpret, or when clock-awareness is dissolved only to remove temporal pressure: none of those warp the felt rate itself.

ex.f: Lost time asserted, then cited back as proof
