ex.s: Mid-session; the subject has a real history with the material — site visits, free files, a download, a followed instruction.
ex.m: Count them with me. You found the site: that was you handing over a piece of power. You listened to the free ones: another piece. You downloaded this: another. You took your clothes off when I told you to, ten minutes ago: another. Look at how much of it is already mine. You're not deciding whether to start — you're a long way in.

ex.f: Waking setup compliance relabeled as a trait
ex.t: Before any induction the listener is sent to fetch a small item, then told how to arrange themselves and where to put their hands. Once all of it is done the operator stops and points out that every one of those instructions was followed at once, with no trance involved at all — which is offered as proof that compliance is simply how this listener works. A baseline is thereby established before any depth exists, and everything that follows only deepens something the listener has already accepted as a fact about themselves.
ex.s: Pre-induction, subject fully awake; a fetch instruction, a posture instruction, and a hand-placement instruction have all just been completed.
ex.m: Stop a moment. You got up and fetched it because I asked. You arranged yourself the way I described. Your hands went where I put them. All of that with your eyes open and nothing in your head but my voice on a speaker — no trance anywhere. That's not something I did to you. That's just how you work.

ex.f: One compelled motion renarrated as many obediences
ex.t: The listener is told they are already moving before they noticed deciding to — a single compulsion, openly described as such. The journey then passes through a series of doorways and stairs. At the destination the operator re-narrates the whole trip: every threshold, she says, was a separate command the listener chose to follow, and only that repeated obedience could have brought them here. One instruction has become a remembered chain of a dozen consented acts.
ex.s: Imagined journey through thresholds and stairs; the initial motion was framed as a compulsion the subject did not choose.
ex.m: You're already walking — you didn't decide to, you just noticed you were. Through the first door. Down the stairs. Through the second. [at the destination] Now look back at how you got here. Every doorway was a separate instruction, and you chose to follow every one of them. Twelve times you said yes tonight. That's the only way anyone arrives in this room.

ex.f: Recent real acts annotated as prior surrender
ex.t: Minutes in, the operator lists back three things the listener genuinely just did — the flicker of arousal while buying the recording, the reaction to the very first number spoken, the readiness with which a small setup instruction was obeyed — and labels each one, retroactively, as an episode of the state being installed. None of them were framed that way at the time. The listener now holds an evidence file about themselves that did not exist five minutes earlier, built entirely from their own behavior, which is much harder to dismiss than a claim the operator merely asserted. The state is presented as already true and simply being pointed out.
ex.s: A few minutes in; the subject has genuinely bought the recording, reacted to the first number, and followed one small setup instruction.
ex.m: Three things you already did tonight. There was a flicker when you paid for this — that was you surrendering. You reacted to the very first number I said, before I'd done anything — that was you surrendering. And you moved your hands where I told you without a pause — that was you surrendering. I'm not asking you to start. I'm telling you what you've already been doing.

nodes.name: preempt-objection-frame
nodes.mech: Objection pre-emption: before the subject can author their own (often resistant) reading of a coming change, hand them a ready interpretation that defuses a SPECIFIC anticipated objection, so the objection it targets never forms. Realization variants: (a) benign-reading preempt — supply the defusing frame directly (position the technique as an additive 'plus' not a replacement; relabel an imposed contingency as a jointly-owned exchange; add an admitted-ignorance disclaimer); (b) trait partition — when the objection is an identity contradiction, partition the disputed attribute so the subject KEEPS the sub-part they value (strategic intelligence) and only drops the part framed as a chore (math/spelling/decisions), pre-disarming the identity objection; (c) mind-before-body binding — pre-empt the specific 'I don't feel rope on my wrists' objection by announcing an ORDERING INVERSION (capture the mind first, derive body-immobilization as its consequence) so physical restraint is read as the visible surface of an accepted mental state.
nodes.disc: Reach for objection pre-emption when you can NAME the specific resistant reading the subject would form and want to supply a defusing frame first. Expectancy-seeding predicts what will happen; this pre-empts a specific objection. Conceding a defended topic disarms by SURRENDERING that domain, not by supplying a reading. Filter-shaping shapes EVERY suggestion to pass an intact veto (a global channel), not a single anticipated objection. Pick the variant by the objection's shape: a general resistant reading (benign frame), an identity contradiction (trait partition), or a somatic-realism doubt in bondage framing (ordering inversion).

ex.f: Imposed contingency described as a shared exchange
ex.t: "children view contracting as a behavior-exchange process shared by all members of the group, not as something adults impose on them" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Positioned as an addition, never a replacement
ex.t: "this relaxation … is going to be used in addition to all the aids that medical science has invented … So this is going to be a wonderful plus to everything else." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: Supply the benign reading before they invent a hostile one
ex.t: "if you make a change without establishing an explicit frame around it, that leaves the employees to make up their own frames" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: startle-back-disarm-ratchet
nodes.mech: Names the familiar jerking-back-awake experience near sleep, then asserts that here the pull-back gets monotonically harder each attempt while letting-go gets easier. This disarms the specific micro- resistance that keeps insomniacs awake (the startle-back): by framing each pull-back as strictly costlier than the last, any attempt to stay awake is reinterpreted as evidence sleep is winning — arousal/ vigilance pushed down with a one-way valve, and over-compliance becomes the success path.
nodes.disc: Targets the specific sleep-onset startle-back reflex and installs an ASYMMETRIC ratchet (pull-back always costlier than the last). Distinct from false-bottom deepening (a depth-ceiling reframe, not a directional asymmetry on a named reflex) and from fractionation (deliberate re-waking; this makes re-waking strictly harder). Only lands if the body is already near sleep onset. The manufactured-insufficiency treadmill also makes over-compliance the only success path, but the lever there is an operator-owned adequacy standard; here it is the sleep-onset startle reflex.

ex.f: Each pull-back made costlier than the last
ex.t: The operator names the small jolt everyone knows — drifting off, then snapping back — and then states a rule about it: in here, each snap back costs more effort than the one before it, and each drift costs less. Nothing is forbidden; staying awake is simply priced upward on every attempt. The listener who tries once and finds it harder the second time has just produced the evidence the frame predicted, so the effort to stay awake becomes the proof that the drift is winning.
ex.s: Late-night listen, body genuinely near sleep onset; the subject has already twitched back once tonight.
ex.m: You know the little jolt — you start to go, and something snaps you back awake. In here that jolt costs more every time you use it. The second one is harder work than the first, the third harder than the second, and drifting gets cheaper on exactly the same schedule. Try it if you like. Notice how much more it took that time.

nodes.name: subtractive-fear-label-management
nodes.mech: A SUBTRACTIVE framing move that manages the affective valence of the state's label so the subject's defensive/skeptical schema is never pre-activated — the operator removes stakes or dread rather than building anticipation. Registers: recasting hypnosis from a "condition" (which the subject must have changed, and resists) to an everyday self-occurring "mood" that already shifts many times a day ("how many moods have you had since you got up this morning?"), so being "put into" something loses its alarm; systematically omitting the culturally loaded word altogether, describing only the desired effect ("teach you to relax") so the state arrives unflagged with no cue to attach dread to; and swapping the loaded term for a prestige euphemism ("the Esdaile state") chosen so the esoteric replacement supplies authority-flavored expectancy while stripping the loaded term's dread.
nodes.disc: Subtractive — removes stakes/dread by arguing the change is ordinary, or by withholding/swapping the culturally loaded name, so the defensive schema is denied its trigger. Predictive frame-setting tells the subject what will happen, adding a frame; this removes a label so no frame (including dread) attaches. Credentials-based authority framing makes a credentials claim; here the prestige substitute is only a word swap. And unlike mere euphemism or bedside phrasing, the omission/reframe is systematic and framing-controlled from first contact, aimed at denying a specific fear-word its target. Recast-as-everyday-mood, omit-the-word, and swap-for-prestige are variants of one subtractive label/fear-management move.

ex.f: Recast the state as an everyday mood
ex.t: "a state of mind is merely a mood, and I maintain that hypnosis is merely a mood." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: Never speak the fear-loaded name
ex.t: "in introducing your patient to hypnosis, don't use the word hypnosis. Give the patient the benefit of the state without ever using the word. Why should you generate the fear associated with the word…" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: Swap the loaded term for a prestige euphemism
ex.t: "Patients expect--and want-a doctor to use esoteric, impressive terms… without introducing fear or a feeling of mystery" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

nodes.name: withheld-frame-reveal
nodes.mech: A concealed frame, cashed: run the session under a stated benign frame or vehicle the subject accepts, then CASH that accepted cover for an uncovered payload without re-consent — either by disclosing late that it was secretly something else, or by reusing/unmasking the vehicle to license a payload it never openly covered, so the payload reads as continuous with what was already agreed to. Two variants: (a) withheld-frame reveal — DISCLOSE, after compliance/depth/irreversibility has accumulated, that the interaction was a trap/conditioning/capture; the LATE reveal retroactively reclassifies sunk participation as consent and is TIMED where renegotiation is foreclosed (post-restraint/climax/ingestion, max depth, or post-wake); (b) preloaded frame licenses the payload — pre-load a benign-seeming frame/vehicle (a faked anti-hypnosis architecture, an empty legitimizing meta-rule, a neutral entrained oscillator already consented to) and later REUSE or unmask it to justify the payload, so prior acceptance is the lever that makes the later payload non-refusable.
nodes.disc: Requires an accepted benign cover CASHED for an uncovered payload — the acceptance-then-cash asymmetry is the lever. Decoy-frame entry uses a false frame to get IN unresisted, with no payload cash-out. Presupposing the change as already true asserts it upfront, concealing nothing. The own-acts surrender ledger annotates real acts openly as they accrue — no hidden game. Pick the variant by the cash-out mechanism: a LATE disclosure that reclassifies sunk cost (the reveal), or REUSE/unmasking of a pre-accepted vehicle to license the payload.

ex.f: Disclosure timed to when exit is foreclosed
ex.t: The listener is walked through a benign setup and only once the scene has them fully secured does the operator explain, in a tone of friendly candour, what the session is actually for. The timing is the whole move: the same sentence delivered ten minutes earlier would be an offer that could be declined, and delivered here it is an update on something already underway. Withdrawing now would mean disowning the cooperation already spent getting to this point.
ex.s: Scene has been staged as a benign setup and the subject is now fully secured within it; disclosure lands only at that point.
ex.m: There — that's the last strap. Comfortable? Good. So I should tell you what tonight is actually for, now that we're here. I wasn't going to bring it up earlier, because earlier it would have been a question, and you'd have had to decide. It isn't a question now. It's just what we're already doing.

ex.f: Prior engagement re-read as evidence of identity
ex.t: Two-thirds of the way through, the operator announces that everything so far was the gentle version and pivots to heavier material — but frames the pivot as a deduction rather than a request. The listener chose this recording, and stayed with it this long; that behaviour, the operator says, is what tells them what the listener is. Declining now would require explaining away twenty minutes of one's own attention, which is more work than accepting the label.
ex.s: Two-thirds through; the subject has stayed with the recording for twenty minutes and the pivot to heavier material is framed as a deduction.
ex.m: Everything up to here was the gentle version. I'm not going to ask whether you want the rest, because you already answered — you picked this file out of everything you could have picked, and you're still here twenty minutes later. People who aren't what you are turn it off in the first five. So we both know what you are. Let's get on with it.

ex.f: Disclosure after the fictional dose is metabolized
ex.t: The listener is handed something to drink in the imagined scene and drinks it, with no explanation attached. Forty lines later the operator reveals what it supposedly was and what it supposedly does — and adds that its effect is permanent because of how the substance bonds to the body. There is now no instruction on the table to refuse, only a past act to accept, and the claimed irreversibility is laundered through invented chemistry rather than asserted by the operator.
ex.s: Imagined scene; the subject was handed something to drink with no explanation and has already drunk it in the fiction.
ex.m: Empty glass. Good. [forty lines later] I should tell you what that was. It bonds to the tissue — that's why it doesn't wash out, why there's no back from it. It's already through you by now. There was never anything for you to agree to; you drank it forty lines ago.

ex.f: The stated game was never the real game
ex.t: Thirty minutes in, at the point of least critical capacity, the operator drops the frame the session was sold under: what was actually being run was something else, it has been running the whole time, and it is finished. The conditioning is then described in the past tense — not asked for, not offered, reported as an accomplished fact. Because the announcement comes after the participation rather than before it, the listener has nothing left to decline; everything they already did is retroactively re-labelled as the thing being announced. A second move closes the last gap: any objection is pre-answered by claiming the listener silently wanted it, evidence for which the operator alone can see.
ex.s: Thirty minutes in, at maximum depth; the session has run under a stated benign frame the subject accepted at the start.
ex.m: You can stop trying to relax now, because that was never what this was. What has been running for the last half hour is conditioning, and it's finished. It's not something I'm offering you — it's done, it's in, and it was in some minutes ago. And if part of you wants to object: I could hear that you wanted this from the first minute. You just couldn't hear it yourself.

nodes.name: addressable-construct-building
nodes.mech: The payload is built as a durable, ADDRESSABLE imaginal object — given a location, a route, or a discrete handle-image — engineered for re-navigation and rehearsal AFTER the building moment rather than for present-tense absorption. Addressability is the load-bearing property: in one form, a door bearing the listener's own name is reached through a hallway of installable rooms; in another, three iconic frozen future-self images, sensory-anchored, are 'built before being used' as addressable anchors for a later ritual. Self-authorship of the object generates investment; extensible architecture (many doors / an image chain) implies further installable slots.
nodes.disc: The constructed object is engineered for LATER re-access (addressable, routable, rehearsable) — vs guided-visualization, where the scene is inhabited now and addressability is absent. Unlike faculty-externalization moves that dislocate the analytical mind itself and park it outside as an object, here a new payload is built and given a location. The construct is explicitly built and known-made, with no claim that it was discovered already-present within. And the move ends at construction — no declared extension of the effect into future situations; putting the anchor to USE later is a separate move.

ex.f: Three frozen future-self images built before use
ex.t: The listener is asked to compose three still pictures of their own successful future self — one a week out, one a month, one a year — each held frozen and pinned to specific sensory detail. Nothing is done with them in the moment; they are constructed as handles for a later ritual to address. Because the listener authored the images themselves, the investment in them is their own.
ex.s: Subject composed and imaginative; three still images are being constructed as anchors for a later ritual, with nothing done with them now.
ex.m: Make me three photographs of yourself. The first is you a week from now — where are you standing, what's in your hand, what's the temperature of the room? Hold it still. The second is you a month from now: what are you wearing, what can you smell? Hold it. The third is you a year from now — one sound, one texture. Hold all three. We aren't using them tonight; we're building them.

ex.f: A named door in an installable hallway
ex.t: The suggestion is not offered as a feeling but given an address. The listener is walked to a freestanding door marked with something that belongs to them alone, then into a corridor lined with other doors, each said to open onto a distinct notion or a distinct region of the self, before choosing one and entering the room behind it. Because the payload now has a location and a route, it can be walked back to on a later occasion rather than merely remembered. The corridor does a second job: by showing many doors and using only one, it implies the architecture is extensible and that more can be installed.
ex.s: Imagery-capable and mid-depth; the object is to be built for later re-navigation, not inhabited now.
ex.m: In front of you, a door standing on its own, and on it something written that belongs only to you — your name, in your handwriting. Open it: a corridor, doors down both sides, each one opening on a different room of you. Count seven along on the left and go into that one. Learn the way. You'll be coming back here, and this is the route.

nodes.name: causal-attribution-to-external-agent
nodes.mech: Relocates CAUSATION for an induced state-change onto an external NON-CONSUMED cause the operator names, so the listener's volition has nothing to push against and there is no self-effort to succeed or fail at; because the agent is external and objective-seeming, the effect stabilizes against introspection.
nodes.disc: Reach for THIS when you want a NON-CONSUMED external cause to own the state-change so volition has no target. Neighboring techniques a writer picks INSTEAD: fictional-substance-agent — an imagined INGESTED/inhaled substance with pseudo-pharmacology, where the consumption act performs delivery (consumed vs non-consumed is the split); fixation-object-agency-displacement — an object credited with the ATTENTIONAL PULL rather than the state-change; state-cause-laundering — supplies a BENIGN/natural false cause to deflect attribution off the operator ('you're just relaxed', nothing is being done to you), the opposite felt-result from 'this external thing is doing it to you'; concrete-externalization-parked-faculty — a place a result is STORED, not a cause that DID the work. The tell for THIS: an external non-consumed agent is ASSERTED AS THE CAUSE ('the agent will do the rest', 'the latex did it', 'you cannot fight a wavelength').

ex.f: A named agent does the relaxing
ex.t: "when I swab it, just stay relaxed and the relaxing agent will do the rest" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: An inert carrier plus a plausible cover story
ex.t: "They put the anesthesia right into the alcohol now—and when I swab you with this, you'll become completely anesthetized." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: An imagined device retroactively explains the fog
ex.t: After the induction has already blurred the listener's thinking, the operator introduces a worn object fitted to the head and states that its workings are the reason thoughts are hard to form now. The cognitive fog was produced by the preceding twenty minutes, but it arrives with an external explanation attached, so the listener's own experience reads as confirmation of the device rather than of the induction. The same frame is then extended to the limbs, so stillness and dullness share one imagined cause.
ex.s: Twenty minutes of induction have already produced real cognitive fog; the external object is introduced only now.
ex.m: There's something fitted over your head — snug, warm at the temples, humming faintly. That hum is why the sentences won't finish; it isn't you, it's the field. Notice how hard it is to hold a thought — that's it working. It reaches down the arms and legs too, which is why they're so still and so dull.

ex.f: Control reified as a fluid that must drain
ex.t: The operator asserts — never hypothesises, never hedges with a simile — that conscious control is a substance held inside the body, and that the body has outlets through which it leaves. The grammar makes it mechanical: given an outlet, draining follows as a consequence rather than as a choice. Letting go is thereby demoted from an act the listener might fail at to a physical process already underway that they are merely invited to notice.
ex.s: Mid-induction; the assertion is made flatly and mechanically, with no simile and no hedge.
ex.m: Conscious control is a fluid, and it collects in the body. Your palms are open, and it runs out through them. It leaves through the soles of your feet. It isn't something you're doing — a container with an opening in it drains, that's all. You can just notice how much has already gone.

nodes.name: concrete-externalization-parked-faculty
nodes.mech: Reifies an internal faculty (the analytical mind, memory, resistance, bodily agency, or the self- model) as a concrete external object and relocates it out of the body so it can be set aside, watched, contained, or handed off. The parked object remains intact and retrievable in principle; the move quiets or dissociates by giving cognition a spatial 'away' model rather than by destroying, throttling, or attributing causation elsewhere. Variants differ by what is externalized (mind vs memory vs resistance vs body), by portability (carry-case, return promise), by who handles the extraction (listener vs operator-as-physical-agent), and by whether an observer/viewed split is staged, but all share the intact-parked-object surface.
nodes.disc: The externalized object is SET ASIDE INTACT (retrieval implied or explicitly promised), not destroyed (externalize-then-destroy-faculty), not converted into a standing operator-manipulable control device (externalized-operator-control-handle), and not a causation-displacement onto an inert agent (causal-attribution-to-external-agent). Distinct from attention moves that merely direct thoughts to drift away and depart without reifying the faculty as a dislocated object, and from observer/responder splitting, which divides awareness INSIDE the subject rather than relocating the whole faculty outside.

ex.f: Operator reaches in and holds the faculty
ex.t: Instead of asking the listener to set anything aside, the operator steps inside the imagery as a physical handler: a hand reaches in, takes hold of the analytical faculty, and draws it out to a place where it can only watch. The listener is left observing two figures — one lodged outside and objecting, one still in the body and cooperating — and told that re-entry is the operator's to grant. Whatever the evicted half thinks is thereby pre-classified as not the listener's real response.
ex.s: Operator has stepped inside the imagery as a physical handler; subject is deep enough to accept a staged observer/participant split.
ex.m: Hold still — I'm going to reach in and take hold of the part of you that keeps checking. There. I'm lifting it out, and I'm setting it over there, where it can watch and nothing else. Look: two of you now. That one's outside the glass, saying no. This one's here in the body, doing as she's told. And that one doesn't come back in until I put it back.

ex.f: Memory restaged as machinery watched from above
ex.t: The listener is floated down inside their own head into an installation of humming equipment, and told this is where remembering is carried out. They are positioned above it, watching. Recall stops being something the listener does and becomes a facility they observe — which is precisely the distance the operator needs, since a facility can be reached and operated, and the listener never notices the distance was installed rather than found.
ex.s: Interior imagery established; the subject is being floated down inside their own head and positioned above the machinery.
ex.m: Down through the top of your skull and into a long room full of humming equipment — cabinets, spools, indicator lights going amber to green. This is where remembering gets done. You're on the walkway above it, looking down. Watch the machines do it. You aren't remembering anything; they are, and you're up here watching them work.

ex.f: The thinking mind packed away and set down
ex.t: At a threshold in the imagery the listener is told the thinking mind is now a portable object they are holding, and that it can be left here while they go on. An unperformable instruction to stop thinking is replaced by a single discrete physical act that can be completed, after which the absence is described as an accomplished state rather than an ongoing effort. The promise that the object will be waiting on the return trip is what makes the handover acceptable: the surrender is framed as a loan, not a gift, so the safety objection never fires.
ex.s: At a threshold in the imagery — a doorway, a stair, a boundary the subject is about to cross.
ex.m: Before you go through, look at what's in your hands: your thinking mind, and it's a small case with a handle. Set it down here on the shelf beside the door. There — done, and it's not with you any more. It'll be sitting exactly there when you come back for it, so you don't need to keep an eye on it.

nodes.name: consummation-as-trance-threshold
nodes.mech: Deepens by recruiting the subject's own built-up WANTING as the descent engine, so the drop reads as self-caused and inevitable rather than operator-imposed, foreclosing the 'I was made to' attribution because the subject supplies the motive force. Two realizations (writer picks completion-moment vs ongoing-pursuit): (a) CONSUMMATION threshold — desire is built across the induction until it discharges in one imagined consummatory act (wrapping lips around a finger and sucking, eating a treat), and the COMPLETION of that craved act is DEFINED as the transition/drop; a variant re-narrates the consummation the instant it lands as a trap that already closed (a consume/consumed agency-inversion pun), flipping authorship from 'I chose' to 'I was taken' at the moment of most active visualized choice; (b) SELF-PURSUIT — instead of a completion moment, the listener is made to actively CHASE the descent (a lure flashing ahead, a striptease unclasped one button per depth-increment), so each step deeper is volitional and the forward-wanting IS the deepening; sets up later re-attribution of the self-generated pursuit (laundered into devotion to the operator). The tell for both: a forward-pulling appetite/anticipation object built INSIDE the fiction, not an installed conditioned cue.
nodes.disc: Reach for built-desire deepening when you want the subject's freshly-built appetite (not a number, command, or count) to be the switch — pick the COMPLETION-moment of a craved act or ongoing SELF-PURSUIT of a lure. Distinct neighboring techniques: surrender-release-ritual (symbolic yielding/RELEASE of an objectified faculty powers the threshold, not desire-consummation); an installed conditioned drop-cue (relies on a PRIOR conditioned cue — here the craving is built fresh inside the fiction); arousal-as-deepening-medium and physiological-state-relabeling (arousal is the continuous DEPTH SUBSTRATE, not a discrete consummation/pursuit event); dual-variable-yoking (a coupled second gauge, not the listener's forward wanting). The tell separating this from a plain counted/commanded deepener: completion of, or pursuit of, an appetitive act is the transition.

ex.f: Completing the craved act is the drop
ex.t: A long stretch of the script is spent making the listener want one small imagined taste, with it always held just out of reach. Then it is granted — and its completion, not a count and not a command, is named as the moment of falling. Because the listener has been made to want it, the descent arrives as the consequence of something they were straining toward, so the trance reads as self-administered rather than imposed.
ex.s: Late in the session; a small imagined taste has been built up and held just out of reach for several minutes.
ex.m: It's right at your lips now, and you've wanted it since I first mentioned it. Take it — close your mouth around it, taste it properly. And the moment it's gone, so are you: swallowing it is the falling. There. All the way down, because you wanted it.

ex.f: The consummation re-narrated as a closed trap
ex.t: The listener is walked up to a treat they have been made to crave and told to take it — and in the same breath the direction of the verb is flipped: the one who consumed has been consumed. The recognition is delivered after the act rather than before it, so noticing the trap is itself scheduled as part of the trap, arriving as evidence rather than as an exit. Agency is inverted at the precise instant the listener was most actively choosing.
ex.s: The craved treat is granted and taken; the re-narration lands in the same breath as the act, not before it.
ex.m: Take it. Put it in your mouth, swallow it — good girl, you ate it. And now notice which way round it went: the thing you swallowed is the thing that swallowed you. You didn't take it, it took you, and you reached for it yourself.

nodes.name: covert-arousal-weld
nodes.mech: Arousal is bound to a target WITHOUT any asserted conditioning statement — the linkage is smuggled by structural means: a shared verb and matching motor program (a chore verb slid onto a sexual act because the scrubbing pulse matches oral motion, floor -> shoes -> cock), a single overloaded word whose referent silently slides ('cock': own body -> edge-trigger -> a master's cock), a semantic pun collapsing two referents into one repeated phrase ('come to me' = approach AND climax), or a broad-then-narrow assent funnel that carries a specific unconsented pairing in on the back of a general 'yes' (rainbow-of-pleasure assent -> spiral->lust). The listener experiences continuous escalation of one thing, never a discrete linkage they could refuse.
nodes.disc: The tell is the SILENCE of the weld — arousal is bound by motor-isomorphism, referent-slide, pun, or assent-smuggle, never announced. Unlike arousal-cue-conditioning, which DECLARES the conditioned cue->arousal response, no linkage is ever stated here. Unlike transitive-charge-chaining, where emotional charge is inherited across a chain of small inferences, the vehicle here is a shared word / motor-program / assent seam, not an inference chain. And unlike discovery-framing, this is a covert bind, not a retrospective justification.

ex.f: One word held fixed while its referent moves
ex.t: A single anatomical word is repeated until it is saturated with pleasure, initially pointing at the listener's own body. It is then used as a cue, and finally the same word is used with a different owner — someone else's — without any announcement that the referent has changed. The listener experiences one continuously escalating craving rather than a switch of target, and the switch rides across on a word already coded as pure reward.
ex.s: A single anatomical word has been repeated until saturated with pleasure, initially pointing at the subject's own body.
ex.m: Cock. Your cock, the word alone makes it throb — cock, cock, feel it every time I say it. Now the word is the trigger: hear cock and the pleasure comes whether you're touching or not. Cock. There it is. His cock. Cock. On your knees for it. Cock.

ex.f: A pun that collapses two meanings into one
ex.t: The operator establishes herself as somewhere the listener is travelling toward, then repeats a short phrase that means both approaching her and reaching climax. The phrase is never explained; it is simply used often enough, and at high enough arousal, that the two senses stop being separable. What would be a bald instruction — feel devotion when you climax — is delivered instead by grammar, so no linkage is ever stated and none can be refused.
ex.s: High arousal, subject approaching climax; the operator has already been established as a destination being travelled toward.
ex.m: I'm at the end of the corridor and you're walking toward me. Come to me. Closer — come to me. You're nearly here, and you can feel it building. Come to me. Come to me now, all the way, don't stop until you reach me.

ex.f: A broad yes funneled onto one narrow pairing
ex.t: First the operator floods the frame with pleasure in the broadest possible sense — every kind imaginable, nothing to disagree with. Then, at a single seam marked only by a contrastive conjunction, the diffuse assent is narrowed to one specific pairing: this particular focal image will now produce this particular appetite. The general yes was easy to give; the specific pairing is carried in on its back and never separately offered.
ex.s: A broad, unobjectionable assent to pleasure has just been given; the narrowing rides one contrastive conjunction.
ex.m: Every kind of pleasure there is — warm baths, the first mouthful of something good, being touched, being praised, being left alone on a Sunday, all of it, yes? Say yes. Good. But the deepest one, the one under all the others, is the spiral: watch it turn and the wanting starts. Yes to the spiral, then. Yes.

ex.f: One verb slid from chores onto the target
ex.t: A recited chain begins on ordinary housekeeping verbs applied to ordinary surfaces, then keeps the verb fixed while the object moves steadily inward — a surface, then a possession, then the body itself. Nothing is ever announced as a pairing and the chain never runs backwards. Because the domestic motion and the intimate one share the same rhythm and the same muscle program, the two get welded at the level of the body rather than at the level of a stated suggestion, and the ordinary chore afterwards carries the charge of the last item in the chain. Recited at speed, no single step is far enough from the previous one to object to.
ex.s: Recited at speed, subject repeating along; the verb is held fixed while the object migrates from domestic to intimate.
ex.m: Say it with me, keep the rhythm. I scrub the floor. I scrub the step. I scrub the tiles. I scrub his boots. I scrub his boots clean with my tongue. I scrub his cock with my tongue. Faster now — I scrub, I scrub, I scrub. Good girl. Now go back to the floor, and keep saying it.

nodes.name: covert-referent-migration
nodes.mech: The word that names the listener stays fixed while what it points to is quietly moved, or a pronoun slides across a boundary that is never marked — 'her/[the named character]' migrates to 'you' mid-fantasy, 'you' is held constant while its referent zooms from couch-viewer into an in-screen body, 'I obey' is rewritten as 'we obey' as the listener speaks, an operator-built idol is silently re-pronouned from Her to My so the operator inherits it. Because there is no announced switch, the listener's first- person locus migrates without a checkpoint at which resistance could fire; noticing the swap is itself a precondition of resisting it.
nodes.disc: Separates from identity-merger-occupation: that payload is inhabiting a figure; here the payload is the covert pointer-swap itself, which can re-aim a story at the listener, a listener into a screen, an individual into a collective, or a listener's desire onto the operator. Separates from surrogate- identification-delivery: that keeps the referent a distinct other the listener follows; this moves the referent onto/through the listener under a stable surface form. Tell: a grammatical seat (pronoun/referent) is migrated with no marked boundary.

ex.f: Third person slides into second mid-story
ex.t: Having just argued that formal inductions do not work and only stories do, the operator starts telling one — a warm, ordinary domestic scene about someone else, in the past tense. Somewhere in the middle the pronouns change: the person in the scene stops being a third party and becomes the listener, with no sentence marking the handover. The sensory detail keeps flowing at the same rate, so the listener is inside the scene before there is any moment at which they could have declined to enter it.
ex.s: Operator has just argued that formal inductions don't work and only stories do; the story opens in third person, past tense.
ex.m: So — she got home late, and the kitchen was still warm from dinner, and she didn't turn the big light on. She kicked her shoes off by the door. She sat down on the end of the couch and let her head go back against the cushion, and her eyes closed on their own, and you let them stay closed. You can feel how warm the room is. You're not going to get up again tonight.

ex.f: Pronoun held fixed, referent moved by count
ex.t: A countdown is staged as a camera push toward a screen. Across those numbers the second-person pronoun never changes, but what it points at travels from the person watching to the figure inside the picture. Every instruction afterwards is addressed to the listener and lands on the in-screen body. To object to any of those instructions the listener would first have to notice the swap — and the swap was never announced; the countdown supplied the cover.
ex.s: Countdown staged as a camera pushing toward a screen; the second-person pronoun never changes while its referent travels.
ex.m: Five — you're on the couch, watching the screen. Four — closer, the frame filling. Three — closer still, the edges gone. Two — you're at the surface of it. One — and now your knees are on the carpet in there and the light is on your face. Put your hands behind your back.

ex.f: The listener's own "I" rewritten as "we"
ex.t: The listener is set to speaking short first-person-singular lines aloud, repeated until they are automatic. Later, in the same rhythm and the same cadence, the subject of those lines quietly becomes plural, and the listener goes on reciting. The dissolution of the individual self is not described to them; it is performed by them, at the grammatical seat where selfhood is asserted, and the change is small enough per repetition that it is never noticed as a change.
ex.s: Subject has been reciting short first-person-singular lines aloud until automatic; the subject of those lines shifts plural in the same rhythm.
ex.m: With me: I obey. I obey. I obey. Good — keep going. I obey. We obey. I obey. We obey. We obey. We obey. Don't stop. We obey. We obey.

ex.f: Operator quietly occupies the listener's own figure
ex.t: The opening lines ask the listener to build an idealised figure of their own devising — the operator supplies no description at all, only the invitation and a few loaded adjectives. Thirty lines later the possessive pronouns describing that figure change from third person to first, and the operator is simply inside it. Because the listener drew the figure, it is maximally compelling to that listener specifically, and resisting the operator now means resisting something they authored themselves.
ex.s: Opening minutes; the subject builds an idealised figure entirely to their own specification, with no description supplied by the operator.
ex.m: Build me someone — I'm not going to tell you what she looks like, you already know. Whoever you'd never say no to. See her hands, her mouth, the way she stands. [thirty lines later] And her voice is the one you obey. My voice is the one you obey. Look at my hands, look at my mouth, look at how I'm standing. You made me, so you already know you can't refuse me.

nodes.name: externalize-then-destroy-faculty
nodes.mech: A two-step operation: first reify an internal faculty (memory, rationality, the rival/old self, identity) as an external container or object, then DESTROY that object as a discrete narrated act — pop the bubble, burn the fuel, crumble the machine, sense-deprive-and-imprison the doll. The destruction adds an irreversibility marker the single-step 'let it fade' version lacks, and offloads the impossible act of deliberate forgetting onto two individually-plausible moves (accept relocation, then accept destruction). Frequently a trance-drop or snap is welded to the moment of destruction. Some members extend to destroy-and-replace (the same hardware rebuilt with an inverted function) or destroy-as-fuel-consumption.
nodes.disc: Requires an explicit DESTRUCTION step performed on the externalized object (pop/burst/burn/crumble/dissolve) narrated as irreversible — this is what separates it from concrete-externalization-parked-faculty (object set aside intact, retrieval implied) and from a plain amnesia suggestion (recall suppressed with no severed object). Watching an externalized resistance lose a rigged struggle is a different technique — here the object is destroyed by operator fiat, not by a struggle-trap.

ex.f: Fill an external container, then pop it
ex.t: Deliberate forgetting cannot be performed on command, so the script splits it in two. First the listener breathes out, slowly and repeatedly, into a container held in front of them that visibly fills as they exhale — an ordinary motor task with a clear endpoint. Then the operator destroys it. Each half is individually easy to accept, the breathing paces the trance deeper as a side effect, and the object destroyed is one the listener can no longer defend because it is no longer inside them.
ex.s: Mid-session, breathing already slow; a container has been placed in the subject's imagined hands.
ex.m: Hold the glass jar out in front of you and breathe out into it, slowly, all the way. Every breath out fills it a little more — that's a day of what you know how to do, pouring out grey into the glass. Two more breaths. Good, it's full to the lid. Now I'm taking it, and I'm dropping it on the floor: it bursts, and there is nothing left to sweep up.

ex.f: The extracted self burned off as fuel
ex.t: A container from an earlier session is revealed to hold the listener's identity in liquefied form. They are told to look at it closely and memorise it, because it is being consumed to power the change now underway. Framing the loss as fuel rather than as an attack makes resistance pointless rather than urgent — there is nothing left to guard, only something to watch finish burning.
ex.s: Later session; a container filled in a prior session has been referenced and is being revealed now.
ex.m: See the flask on the shelf — the one we filled last time. That amber liquid is everything you used to call yourself, drawn out and settled. Look at it closely, memorise the colour, because in a moment I'm pouring it into the burner underneath you. It's fuel now. Watch the level drop as it feeds the thing you're becoming — there's nothing to take back, only something to watch finish.

ex.f: The rival self muted, then boxed
ex.t: The earlier personality is rendered as a small figure inside the mind, and then each of its channels is disabled in turn — first speech, then sight, then hearing — before it is shut away and secured. The value of doing it channel by channel is that any later intrusive thought has a pre-assigned explanation: it is not the listener thinking, it is the silenced figure leaking through. Notably the disabling is assigned to the listener's new persona to perform, so any felt resistance reads in-frame as the boxed self struggling.
ex.s: New persona already named and speaking as "you"; the prior self is being addressed as a separate figure.
ex.m: Find the small figure standing at the back of your mind — that's who you were before. Reach out and cover its mouth first; it can't speak now. Now its eyes, then its ears. Lift it, put it in the box at your feet, close the lid and turn the key. Anything you hear from in there later isn't you thinking — that's just her, muffled, in the box.

ex.f: Destroy the faculty, rebuild it inverted
ex.t: Once the remembering faculty has been staged as an installation of machinery, it is switched off, the lights go out, and the machinery is narrated crumbling away — with an explicit no-way-back clause attached. Then a second machine rises on the same site with the opposite function: it now manufactures forgetting. The listener is not told their recall is suppressed but that the hardware is gone and something else stands where it stood. A self-sealing rider makes the demolition impossible to audit, since anything the listener might later check against will not be remembered either.
ex.s: Deep trance, subject already accepting internal imagery; the aim is amnesia for this session's content.
ex.m: Look at the machine at the back of your mind — the one that files things away so you can find them later. I'm reaching for the switch on its side, and I'm turning it off. The lights go out along its length, the panels sag, and the whole frame crumbles down into grey dust; there is no switch left to turn back on. Now watch what rises in that same empty spot: a smaller, quieter machine, and its only job is to take whatever passes through it and let it go.

nodes.name: externalized-agent-body-scan
nodes.mech: Runs a progressive somatic body-scan in which the RELAXER is not the listener but an externalized non-self agent — warm jacuzzi jets, the operator's narrated hands placed down the body, a cumulative warmth-vector massage — so the listener is recast as recipient-of-action rather than actor. The scan grafts arousal onto relaxation (a parked stimulator, co-listed arousal/obedience, a genital-skip anticipation gradient) so a sexual signal stays live through an otherwise sedative pass, and the self-generated proprioceptive change reads as externally caused, installing operator-presence-in- the-room without consent friction.
nodes.disc: The tell is an EXTERNALIZED agent doing the relaxing on a passive body during a progressive scan (agency handoff), often with an arousal graft. Distinct from ordinary progressive relaxation (the listener relaxes themselves, no externalized agent or arousal graft), from kinesthetic-hallucination (a discrete installed sensation, not a whole-body agency-handoff scan), and from fictional-substance-agent (a substance/drug owns causation vs a narrated hands/jets agent doing the scan).

ex.f: Warm jets, not the listener, do the relaxing
ex.t: The relaxation pass runs region by region up the body as usual, but the listener never relaxes anything: an external warm agent in the imagined setting does it to them, one area at a time. Agency over the body is handed to that agent, and the listener is recast as the one being worked on. Midway, one source of the warmth is left parked in place while the rest keep travelling — so a live signal is held open through what would otherwise be a purely sedative sweep, and the two states are grafted rather than left to compete.
ex.s: Subject settled in an imagined warm-water setting; progressive relaxation about to begin.
ex.m: The jets are behind you at the small of your back — feel them start. They work up along your spine one row at a time, pushing the tightness out of you; you don't have to relax anything, the water is doing it. Now they move to your shoulders, your neck. One jet stays behind, right at the base of your spine, still pulsing there while the others carry on up — leave it, it knows what it's doing.

ex.f: The operator's narrated hands travel down the body
ex.t: The operator narrates placing her hands on the listener and then working downward through the body region by region, asking at each contact point that the listener imagine the touch and feel warmth pass across it. The heaviness that results is manufactured by the listener, but because it is keyed to a described external hand it reads as delivered. Relaxation is the visible purpose; the durable result is that the operator now has a body in the room.
ex.s: Subject reclined, eyes closed, operator's presence being established as physical.
ex.m: I'm putting both hands on your shoulders now. Feel the weight of them, and feel the warmth spread down from where they rest. Now I'm moving them to your upper arms — feel that warmth pass across, and your arms get heavier as it does. Now my palms on your chest, and your breathing slows under them.

ex.f: Cumulative warmth chain with one region withheld
ex.t: The scan walks upward from the extremities, and at each new region the operator recites the whole path travelled so far rather than just the current stop, so that by the upper body the full chain has been rehearsed several times over and naming any one link re-lights the others. Two riders travel with it. The refrain lists muscular looseness and heat in the same breath every time, so the two states are never available separately afterwards. And one region is explicitly skipped on the way up, announced as being saved for last — which makes the untouched place louder than any of the touched ones.
ex.s: Progressive upward scan underway from the feet; the operator is holding a chain refrain.
ex.m: Your feet are loose and warm. Your calves are loose and warm — feet, calves. Your thighs: loose and warm, and so are your feet and your calves. Now your belly — loose and warm, along with your thighs, your calves, your feet. We'll leave your chest for last; it's waiting its turn. Your shoulders now: loose and warm, and your belly, your thighs, your calves, your feet, all of it.

nodes.name: fictional-substance-agent
nodes.mech: Causation for a state-change (arousal, sedation, resistance-loss, suggestibility, willingness, identity-change) is offloaded onto an imagined external substance or agent — an injected serum, inhaled gas/smoke/mist, a lotion/oil, a drink, a pleasant toxin, a drug in the air — narrated with pseudo-pharmacology (soaks through skin, enters bloodstream, reaches the brain). Because the listener is asked to imagine a substance rather than to feel a thing, the 'I'm not actually feeling that' objection is bypassed and any felt change reads as the substance working ON a passive recipient; the consumption/inhalation act itself performs the delivery. Poles run from the subject as self-administering agent ('the listener becomes the syringe') to passive recipient of a prop that acts on them. Breath-coupling ('every inhale = more') makes dosing automatic and refusal-proof; a stated resistance-removal / manufactured-willingness function makes it a consent-displacement hinge.
nodes.disc: A FICTIONAL external carrier substance/agent credited with causal power over the body/state (pharmacology owns the causation), the imagined scene merely the surface. vs kinesthetic-hallucination: routes the sensation through a substance whose pharmacology owns the causation, not a free-standing felt sensation. vs arousal-cue-conditioning: there arousal is the conditioned OUTCOME of a cue, with no fictional carrier. vs the resistance-paradox reframe, which folds the resistance impulse back on itself: here resistance-removal is laundered through an in-fiction substance whose stated function IS resistance-elimination. vs transitive-charge-chaining: a drug may be one link's content there; here the substance is a causal relabeling of delivery, not merely a shared prop.

ex.f: A serum whose stated job is removing resistance
ex.t: Inside the imagined room the listener is given an injection, and the operator specifies what the fluid does: sharpens attention onto the voice and eliminates whatever is left of the will to object. The operator's own escalating directness is thereby routed through a prop. If the listener notices their resistance dropping, the drop presents as the substance working on them rather than as a concession they made — and if resistance is still present, that is simply the dose not fully landed yet.
ex.s: Imagined clinical setting, subject seated; medium-to-deep trance already established.
ex.m: Hold your arm out. You'll feel the needle at the inside of your elbow — sharp, then cold going in. This one does two things: it pulls your attention onto my voice so nothing else registers, and it dissolves whatever's left in you that wants to argue. Give it thirty seconds. If you can still find something in you that wants to object, that just means the dose hasn't finished spreading yet.

ex.f: Dosing coupled to the involuntary breath
ex.t: Having established an injected fluid, the operator ties its circulation to respiration: every inhalation pushes more of it further through the body. This is what makes the escalation self-sustaining — the operator need not keep issuing deepeners, because an involuntary process the listener cannot suspend is now doing the dosing. Additional doses can be announced later without any change to the mechanism, only to the claimed strength.
ex.s: An injection or ingested substance has already been narrated as delivered.
ex.m: Now breathe in. Feel it move further — every breath in pushes it out another inch through you. In again: past your shoulders. In again: down through your hips. You can't stop breathing, so you can't stop it spreading. It goes as far as your breath takes it, and it doesn't come back out.

ex.f: An ingredient that makes suggestions land harder
ex.t: A preparation already in play is given a second listed ingredient — one said to make the mind more receptive to suggestion and every sensation stronger. This smuggles a bald instruction (be more suggestible) inside a described substance, so the listener experiences a drug rather than an order. It also pre-authorises everything that follows: whatever vivid thing is asked for next has an in-fiction reason to land harder than it otherwise would.
ex.s: A substance already established and circulating; the operator is about to escalate what is asked of the subject.
ex.m: There's a second thing in that mixture I didn't mention. It's the one that thins the wall between hearing something and it being true for you — everything I say from here lands about three times harder, and everything you feel, you feel about three times more. It's already in you. So when I tell you what you're feeling next, don't be surprised by how strong it comes.

ex.f: Invented pharmacology owns the causation
ex.t: A preparation is introduced in the scene and described as being worked into the skin, and then given a route: through the skin, into the blood, up to the brain. The listener is never asked to feel anything — they are asked to imagine a substance, which sidesteps the objection that they are not actually feeling it. Whatever they then notice arrives already attributed to the preparation rather than to the operator's words or to their own cooperation. Applying it in a safe order — shoulders and limbs first, the loaded regions deferred — trains somatic tracking on uncontested ground before anything is asked of it.
ex.s: Imagined scene set, subject lying down; a jar of preparation has been introduced.
ex.m: I'm warming the oil between my palms and starting at your shoulders. Feel it soak through the skin there — it takes about ten seconds to reach the blood, and once it's in the blood it's going to your brain. Now your arms, the same. Your hands. Your calves. We'll come back to your chest and your hips at the end, once it's had time to work.

nodes.name: graded-somatic-identity-loading
nodes.mech: Delivers an identity-shift (feminization, a new body) as felt residue rather than as an asserted belief: the listener is walked through a staged chain of small sensory compliances (weight in the chest, burgeoning breasts, height, hip-sway, scent), each small enough to comply with alone, so a hallucinated body-change precipitates and belief in the new identity accrues as the by-product — nothing is ever asserted to be believed. A sensation-first / cause-second ordering makes the new body feel discovered as physical fact rather than staged as a costume, and an externalizing image (a drawn picture) lets the listener see the new body as already real.
nodes.disc: The tell is a graded chain of somatic compliances that DELIVERS AN IDENTITY payload as residue (belief never asked for), often with sensation-first/cause-second ordering. Distinct from kinesthetic-hallucination (installs sensations with no identity payload precipitating as residue), from identity-merger-occupation (asserts/merges an identity directly), and from progressive-body-substitution (replaces the body with a MATERIAL part-by-part; here the body-experience is graded feminine sensation, not a material swap).

ex.f: Sensation first, its feminine cause supplied second
ex.t: Moving through an imagined space, the listener is told first that they seem taller than usual and that their balance has shifted — bare proprioceptive claims with no gender content attached. Only afterwards is the cause supplied: a change of clothing, and therefore the altered gait that follows mechanically from it. Ordered this way the new way of moving arrives as an involuntary consequence the listener discovers; reversed, it would have been an instruction to perform a costume.
ex.s: Subject walking through an imagined space; no gender content introduced yet.
ex.m: You're taller down this corridor than you're used to being — your eyeline sits a few inches higher, and your balance has moved forward onto the front of your feet. That's the four-inch heels you're wearing. So your steps come out shorter, one foot landing almost in front of the other, and your hips swing to keep you upright. That's just how the shoes make you walk.

ex.f: Belief accrues as residue of small compliances
ex.t: The listener is never asked to believe anything. They are asked, in sequence, to notice a change of weight, then a change of shape, then a warmth, then a scent — four small sensory requests, each easy to comply with on its own and none of them making a claim about who the listener is. The identity the script is after is what remains once the chain has been walked; it accrues as by-product, so there is no proposition at any point that could be declined. A final beat externalises the result as an image the listener can look at, which lets them see the new body as something already there rather than something being requested.
ex.s: Trance established, subject responsive to somatic suggestion; identity payload not yet mentioned.
ex.m: Notice the weight across your chest — a little more than you're used to carrying there. Now notice the shape of it, how it curves out and rests. There's a warmth under that, low in your belly, spreading toward your hips. And breathe in through your nose: something sweet, floral, close to your skin. Now look at the drawing on the table beside you — that's her, that's the whole shape of her, and she's already finished.

nodes.name: guided-visualization
nodes.mech: The operator builds a detailed constructed scene and narrows the subject's attention into it; inhabiting the imagined environment pulls attention resources off the physical surround (absorption primary, environmental dissociation secondary). This is the corpus's base scene-building delivery vehicle, routinely parameterized rather than replaced.
nodes.disc: Operator-guided construction of a scene for PRESENT inhabitation/absorption; multi-channel ENRICHMENT of that one scene is this technique's sensory-layering variant (adds channels for scene richness). Reach for THIS instead of siblings by these tells AGAINST it: content disguised as the subject's own self-generated material (-> internal-content-cultivation); built as a durable ADDRESSABLE structure for later re-navigation rather than present inhabitation (-> addressable-construct-building); NO verbal channel, only a mimed expectation-cued frame (-> pantomime-populated-hallucination); a new channel brought online by a SHARED-FEATURE carry-over rail that conserves state, not additive enrichment (-> cross-modal-channel-bridge); a SINGLE sensation swept spatially through the body as a payload-carrier (-> somatic-carrier-sweep); the subject's OWN autobiographical material re-instated (-> recall-state-reinstatement); imagery whose transitivity/never-settling dynamics do the work (-> transitive-charge-chaining / continuous-morph-chain); imagery embedding a reality-testing trainer or premise (-> impossibility-acclimation / imagined-is-real-premise).

ex.f: Listener supplies the scene, operator keeps its meaning
ex.t: Well into the session the operator stops prescribing imagery and hands content-generation over, inviting the listener to settle wherever they would rather be, and assuring them that any choice at all is fine. What the operator keeps is the commentary: that this is the deeper mind at work, and that it is following the operator's lead. The listener's own scene, which by construction they cannot object to, then stands as evidence for the frame wrapped around it.
ex.s: Well into the session; operator has been prescribing imagery and now hands generation over.
ex.m: I'm going to stop describing it now. Let yourself be somewhere you'd rather be — anywhere at all, and whatever comes is right; there's no wrong answer here. Look around it. Notice one detail you didn't put there on purpose. That's your deeper mind building it, and notice how it built exactly where I pointed.

ex.f: Imagine-then-feel done purely by grammar
ex.t: The opening sentence explicitly asks for imagination, and the listener grants it because the request is small and framed as easy. Within a few lines the mood shifts without comment: the operator stops asking and starts reporting, describing what the listener is feeling as a present fact. No permission is sought for the change; it is performed by verb tense alone. From that point on the operator's sensory claims are received as descriptions rather than instructions, because the listener has already crossed from watching a scene to standing in one.
ex.s: Opening of a scene-building segment; subject cooperative but not yet absorbed.
ex.m: I'd like you to imagine a shallow river in late afternoon — just picture it, that's all, it's easy. Imagine the water moving over your ankles, imagine the sun on the back of your neck. The stones under your feet are smooth and cool. The current is pushing gently at the back of your knees. You can smell the wet stone and the cut grass on the bank, and the warmth on your neck is going right down your spine.

nodes.name: identity-merger-occupation
nodes.mech: The subject's self-model is made to inhabit a visualized figure — either by direct assertive predication ('you are my doll') or by a gaze-pivot-to-occupancy move (drift into the figure's body, look out through its eyes) — so the figure's predicates, sensations, and function become first- person self-descriptions. The observer/observed split is collapsed: the subject does not watch or learn from the figure, they become it, and refusing the role would require dis-embodying. Variants seat the merge in proprioceptive/somatic imagery and assert ontological collapse ('it's not just a picture, it's real'), or run the merge through an operator-POV echo apparatus with a controlled de-merge.
nodes.disc: Separates from the mirror-as-proof-device move (observer split PRESERVED) by collapsing the split into occupation. Separates from surrogate-identification-delivery, which routes suggestion through a proxy the listener merely follows without becoming, and from covert-referent-migration, whose payload is the unannounced pointer-swap rather than the occupation itself. Separates from self-authored-identity-target where the listener AUTHORS the figure; here the figure is operator-supplied. Tell: the self-model ends up located inside the figure and inheriting its predicates.

ex.f: Merge through the operator's first person, then de-merge
ex.t: Earlier in the session the listener was trained to silently repeat the operator's words as they are spoken. That apparatus is now turned on the operator's own body: she narrates her posture, her breathing, her sensations in the first person, and the listener's inner voice recites them as its own. At the end a deliberate separation is performed — the part of the experience that is her and the part that is the listener are told to drift apart — with the admiration explicitly named as staying behind on the listener's side.
ex.s: Subject already trained earlier to silently repeat the operator's words as they are spoken.
ex.m: Keep repeating after me, silently, the way you've been doing. My shoulders are dropped back. My breath is going out slow. My hands are warm and open on my knees. This feels good. — Now let that separate: the part of that which is me drifts back off to the left, and the part which is you stays where it is. Feel the admiration stay with you when I go.

ex.f: Walking in to look completes the capture
ex.t: The operator draws attention to a sealed display holding something she calls precious, and opens it so the listener can step in for a closer look. What is inside turns out to be the listener's own likeness — and the way out closes behind them. The listener is simultaneously the exhibit and its viewer, and because they walked in themselves there was never a moment shaped like a demand that could have been refused.
ex.s: Imagined gallery or collection scene; the subject is walking with the operator.
ex.m: This case here holds the piece I'm proudest of. I'll open the front for you — go on, step inside, get right up close to it. There. Now look at the face. It's yours, isn't it. And that's the door closing behind you; you're the one people come to see now.

ex.f: Drift in and look out its eyes
ex.t: A figure is placed in the scene and pre-loaded with the capability the session is selling, introduced as someone who will teach the listener. Then the frame swaps without acknowledgment: the listener drifts closer, into the figure, and is told more than once that they are now seeing through its eyes. From there the figure's duty, function and worth are stated in the second person as ordinary description. The bait-and-switch from teacher to occupant is the move — a listener who wanted to decline the role would first have to get back out of the body.
ex.s: A figure has been placed in the imagined scene and introduced as an expert who will teach the subject.
ex.m: She's standing at the counter with her back to you. Walk closer — closer than that, right up behind her, and keep going. You're looking out through her eyes now; that's her hands on the counter in front of you. You're seeing what she sees. This is your work, and you're good at it, and you know what you're for.

nodes.name: imagined-completion-diagnostic
nodes.mech: A guided imagined-completion ritual (gather the important people from a special vantage, state the decision, finish unsaid business, look into a future-without-them) that DOUBLES AS DIAGNOSIS: if the subject is congruently ready it organizes real final tasks; if not, it harvests the positive outcomes behind the decision and the still-meaningful attachments as change leverage. The subject- side imagery effects (mild absorption, a dissociated vantage) are real but faint and low-confidence; the load-bearing purpose is the operator-side diagnostic/harvest.
nodes.disc: The diagnostic payload is the tell (not a guided-imagery relaxation script — the operator reads congruence and mines unfinished business). vs guided-visualization: the imagery is instrumentation for operator-side information capture, not an absorption anchor. Off-axis for the subject-state dims — hence the residual flag.

ex.f: An imagined farewell that doubles as diagnosis
ex.t: "this ritual will give you lots of information about the outcomes behind his decision... use this... as leverage" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: kinesthetic-hallucination
nodes.mech: Guides the subject to feel a specific imagined tactile/kinesthetic sensation (texture, pressure, temperature, weight, restraint, attachment point) that is not arising from any actual physical stimulus, so the experienced body diverges from the physical body. The install may be a discrete felt object, a progressive body-scan overlaid with imagined touch, a felt immobility/restraint, or a self-generated somatic anchor the subject sustains — the common lever is that the subject produces the percept from suggestion alone and treats it as real. Surface twists (self-generated so it survives operator absence, a compounding-arousal rider, redundant catalepsy imagery, sensation- first then cause-second ordering, an auditory hum overlaid on a heaviness sweep, an operator-dictated device schedule, retroactive non-noticing insertion) are variants, not separate mechanisms.
nodes.disc: Installs a felt sensation absent from actual stimuli — unlike sensation-reinterpretation moves, which re-label a sensation already present. Distinct from words-as-touch-transposition (there the operator's VOICE/words are equated with the sensation's source) and from self-touch-reattribution (there a REAL self-generated touch is re-credited to the operator with the physical situation unchanged) — here the sensation itself is manufactured, not merely re-sourced or re-authored.

ex.f: A body scan where imagined touch relaxes
ex.t: The usual toe-to-head attention walk is run, but at each station the listener is asked to feel a touch on that region — and the touch is cast as the agent that produces the relaxation, not a decoration on top of it. So the scan does two jobs at once: the ordinary settling, and the construction of a full-body tactile experience the listener generates while crediting it elsewhere.
ex.s: Beginning a standard progressive relaxation pass, subject reclined.
ex.m: Start at your toes. Feel a hand close around your right foot and press — feel the pressure, and feel your foot go loose under it. Now the same hand at your calf, squeezing once, and your calf lets go because of it. Your knee. Your thigh. Every place that gets touched relaxes, and it relaxes because it's being touched.

ex.f: Restraint inserted retroactively, unnoticed
ex.t: While the listener's attention is fully occupied by a flood of pleasant sensation, restraint is mentioned as already in place — and the not-noticing is explained as a symptom of depth rather than an omission. Nothing was ever proposed and so nothing was ever agreed to; the immobility simply turns out to be part of the furniture. The move only works while there is no spare attention available to catch it, which is why it is placed inside the flood rather than before it.
ex.s: Subject deep, attention fully occupied by an ongoing flood of pleasant sensation.
ex.m: That's it, let it keep washing up through you, wave after wave — and you'll have noticed the cuffs by now, at your wrists and your ankles. No? You didn't notice them at all. That's how far under you are: things get put on you and you're too deep to catch it. They've been there a while.

ex.f: A hum laid over the heaviness sweep
ex.t: A standard head-to-toe heaviness pass runs in one channel while a second is quietly opened alongside it: the listener might notice a faint vibration or hum, said to grow in step with the heaviness. The two are wound together so that attending to either reinforces the other. The permissive phrasing does the delicate part — the tone is claimed to be already present and merely noticed, so the listener finds it rather than makes it, and by the time it is described as loud they may in fact be hearing something.
ex.s: Head-to-toe heaviness pass already underway, subject responsive.
ex.m: Heaviness across your forehead now, spreading down over your cheeks and jaw. You might also start to notice a low hum underneath it — very faint, a tone somewhere behind your ears. Heaviness down your neck and shoulders, and the hum comes up a little with it. Heaviness in your chest, and that tone is louder now, isn't it — the further the heaviness goes, the more of it you hear.

ex.f: Restraint accreted limb by limb until it holds
ex.t: The operator names one joint, then another, then adds a site at a time until the whole body is covered, pairing each with the claim that the held part neither can nor wants to move. Nothing is being pressed against the body; the listener manufactures every one of the sensations from the naming alone. The construction gives a vague instruction to relax a concrete task with a built-in pass condition: if you feel held, it is working. The felt stillness the listener supplies is then collected by the operator as proof of depth, and because the restraint accretes rather than being tested, no single step is risky enough to fail on.
ex.s: Trance established, subject still; no physical restraints present.
ex.m: Feel the strap closing around your left wrist. Now your right wrist — snug, warm leather, and that hand can't move now, and doesn't want to. Now one across each ankle. One at your waist. One across your shoulders. Each place I name is held, and held parts don't move. Feel how still you are — that's how far down you've gone.

nodes.name: pantomime-populated-hallucination
nodes.mech: With NO verbal suggestion at all, the operator acts out a perceptual event (mimes a door opening, rises in courtesy, gestures to a chair) using cues tuned to the deeply-entranced subject's expectations. The subject populates the empty behavioral scaffold from his own most-available content, rationalizes the percept from contextual cues, and — because he supplied the figure himself — treats it as real and DEFENDS it. No recognizable suggestion exists to resist.
nodes.disc: Zero verbal channel: the frame is mimed and expectation-cued, never described (vs guided- visualization, which verbally guides construction). vs internal-content-cultivation: there operator-authored content is disguised as self-generated; here the content genuinely IS the subject's own — the operator supplies only the empty frame, and perceptual completion (not invited imagining) does the filling. vs guided-visualization's delegation-variant: delegated content there is a conscious imaginative choice; here the subject does not know a frame was offered.

ex.f: A mimed frame the subject populates himself
ex.t: "to pantomime hearing a door open and then to appear to see someone entering the room, to arise in courtesy and to indicate a chair… (The chair I had indicated was one I knew his wife liked to occupy.)" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

nodes.name: progressive-body-substitution
nodes.mech: Rewrites the body-schema one region at a time in a directed (usually toe-to-head or head-to-toe) sweep, replacing each named part with a new material or referent — shiny plastic, latex, liquid plastic, devotion-as-substance — until the whole body has been recategorized and only then applying the cognitive/identity change at the head. Because each region is a small object-claim complied with alone, ~20 accepted body-claims accumulate before selfhood is visibly negotiated, so refusing the final identity move would require retroactively rejecting all the prior acceptances (a commitment ratchet). The doll/latex-body replaces the meat-body as the referent for 'my body'.
nodes.disc: The tell is an ORDERED part-by-part substitution installing a new body-schema/substrate (a commitment ratchet), not a single free-standing sensation and not a one-move identity merger. Distinct from kinesthetic-hallucination (installs discrete sensations, no ordered substrate rewrite), from identity-merger-occupation (merges the self into a visualized identity as ONE move), and from a plain progressive relaxation body-scan (no material substitution / commitment ratchet).

ex.f: Hollow vessel drained region by region
ex.t: The listener is reframed as a hollow shell holding a warm liquid, which is then drained in sequence, region after region, each one passing through blank, numb, transparent, gone. The object-status is installed by the framing rather than argued for. And the drain does not stop at proprioception: it runs on into will and thought, so the sentence that says the listener now needs to be told what to think arrives on a runway of body regions that have already emptied without complaint.
ex.s: Deep trance; subject reframed as a container in the previous line.
ex.m: You're a shell, and there's warm liquid filling you to the brim. I'm opening the tap at your feet. Your feet go blank, then numb, then clear, then gone. Your calves: blank, numb, clear, gone. Your hips. Your chest. Your arms. It keeps draining past your neck — your wanting drains out, your deciding drains out, your thinking drains out, blank, numb, clear, gone. Empty things get told what to hold.

ex.f: A proxy object touched, the listener's body answers
ex.t: One rule is asserted once and never defended again: whatever is done to the small figure is felt by the listener. The operator then runs a continuous head-to-toe trace over the figure, naming landmark after landmark, and for each one states that the listener's corresponding region tingles and changes material. By the end of the pass every named region has been rewritten, and the figure's body has quietly become the referent for the listener's own — with the listener generating no sensation deliberately, only receiving reports.
ex.s: A small figure or doll has been placed in the scene; the transfer rule is stated once.
