ex.m: Whatever I touch on her, you feel on you. Watch — my finger on the top of her head, and your scalp tingles and goes smooth. Down her forehead, her cheek, her throat: yours tingles and goes smooth. Across her shoulder, down her arm to her fingertips. Down her chest, her belly, her thigh, her calf, her foot. That's all of it. That's you now.

ex.f: The same pass repeated on deeper substrates
ex.t: One identical sentence-shape is run four times, changing only its target: the substance soaks through the body, then through thought, then through feeling, then through the last layer. Each pass makes the same claim of total saturation, so agreeing to the first makes the second cheaper, and so on. By the final iteration the only unclaimed layer is the one the script was aiming at all along, and it arrives as the natural completion of a series rather than as a new request.
ex.s: A saturating substance already established as entering the subject; three further passes to run.
ex.m: It's soaking all the way through your body now — nothing left of you it hasn't reached. It's soaking all the way through your thoughts now — nothing left in there it hasn't reached. It's soaking all the way through your feelings now — nothing left of those it hasn't reached. And it's soaking all the way through whatever is under those, the last layer, the part that's just you — nothing left of that it hasn't reached.

ex.f: Twenty body claims before the mind is mentioned
ex.t: Beginning at one end of the body and moving toward the head, each named region is replaced with a new material — one small object-claim at a time, none of which says anything about who the listener is. Only on reaching the head does the script make its actual move, and there the substitution is cognitive: with the head recategorised, clear thought is described as no longer available. By that point a long run of smaller claims has already been accepted, and refusing this one would mean retroactively withdrawing all of them. The ordering is the whole technique; run in reverse it would be a single arguable assertion.
ex.s: Deep trance; substitution sweep beginning at the feet, identity payload reserved for the head.
ex.m: Your toes are smooth moulded plastic. Your feet — plastic, seamless, no give in them. Your ankles, your calves, your knees, all of it hard shiny plastic. Your hips, your belly, your chest: plastic. Your shoulders, your arms, your hands, right out to the fingertips. And now your head — plastic all the way through, and plastic doesn't hold a thought. There's nothing in there to think with any more.

nodes.name: regime-change-threshold-gate
nodes.mech: A discrete, one-way threshold (a red velvet curtain positioned as a point-of-no-return) is staged as a voluntary crossing that converts continuous deepening into a REGIME change — after crossing, the operator's words and the subject's are framed as identical ('your words' and 'her words' are the same). The subject does the stepping so lost control is self-attributed, the operator answers the readiness check on the subject's behalf, and the feared cost of crossing ('all your control will be gone') is named directly and then inverted ('but all your wants will be yours') so pre-validating the fear stops it from breaking trance. The distinguishing object is the discrete one-way GATE topology — a bounded regime boundary — not a graded deepener and not a symbolic release act.
nodes.disc: A discrete one-way point-of-no-return gate whose crossing installs a REGIME where operator words are experienced as own thoughts, with operator-supplied readiness answer and paradoxical fear-naming. Separates from surrender-release-ritual (a symbolic release act, not a topology object — the threshold structure itself is the difference); from the resistance-paradox reframe (the fear-inversion here rides a spatial one-way gate, not a resistance-into-deepening fold); and from a plain deepener (a discrete regime-change boundary, not graded depth). In the source material the 'no going back' is later structurally violated by re-crossing — a tell that the gate is a framing device.

ex.f: A one-way threshold crossed by choice
ex.t: A barrier is placed in the scene and declared a point of no return: past it, the operator's words are the listener's thoughts. Before asking for the step, the operator names the fear out loud — that control will be gone — and then inverts it in the same breath, so the anxiety is validated rather than left to surface later and break the trance. The readiness question is asked and immediately answered on the listener's behalf, and then the listener steps through themselves. Two things follow: the loss is self-attributed because they did the stepping, and continuous deepening has been converted into a discrete regime with a before and an after.
ex.s: Mid-session, subject standing in an imagined corridor; a curtain has been described ahead of them.
ex.m: The red curtain is a metre in front of you, and past it there's no walking back — on the other side, my words arrive as your own thoughts, in your own voice. I know what you're thinking: that everything you control will be gone. It will. And everything you want will be yours instead. Are you ready? You are. Step through.

nodes.name: reified-depletion-inventory
nodes.mech: Converts an unobservable continuous internal state (intelligence, cognitive sharpness, thought- capacity) into a concrete, countable, depletable inventory — black bubbles that 'pop, pop, pop', IQ points that tick down and never climb back, brain draining/melting out the ears 'more and more', an IQ counter the listener picks and watches. The reification gives the listener a sensory referent they can hear/see happening and a self-generatable micro-animation to run during trance (each pop = one unit), offloading trance-maintenance onto the listener's imagination; the open-ended supply lets the loss be claimed indefinitely without contradiction, and a pause-not-reset clause preserves the accumulated depletion across fractionation cycles.
nodes.disc: The tell is quantization of a continuous cognitive drain into countable/completable self-generated units (often onomatopoeic or listener-owned). Distinct from kinesthetic-hallucination (a felt tactile sensation, not a counted cognitive-loss inventory), from numeric depth-claim deepeners (numerical/exponential claims deepening an EXISTING trance — here a faculty is reified as a self-owned counter, not a depth claim), and from progressive-body-substitution (rewrites the body, not a cognitive scalar).

ex.f: Cognitive loss quantized into audible pops
ex.t: Instead of the vague claim that the mind is fading, the operator fills the head with countable objects and has a few of them burst on each descent. The onomatopoeia does the delivery — spoken aloud, the sound enacts the event it names — and the listener now has a small animation they can run themselves between the operator's lines. The inventory is never given a size, so the loss can be claimed indefinitely without ever contradicting itself.
ex.s: Descending-count deepener running; subject responsive to imagery.
ex.m: Your head is full of small black bubbles, and each one is a thought you can still hold. Ten — pop, pop, pop. Three of them gone. Nine — pop, pop, pop, pop. Feel it get quieter in there. Eight — pop, pop. There are plenty left, and we've got all night.

ex.f: An open-ended drain that keeps going by itself
ex.t: Thought is figured as a liquid running out of a basin, then escalated to something leaving the head slowly and steadily. Crucially the description is of a process in progress and increasing rather than a state asserted once. Each described increment licenses the listener to feel a little less able to think, and the loop keeps running without further input from the operator, who is then free to offer their own words as the replacement.
ex.s: Deep trance; the operator wants a self-sustaining drain to run under later suggestions.
ex.m: There's a basin behind your eyes and it's got a crack in it. It's running out — slow, steady, and it doesn't stop while I'm talking. Feel it leaving, warm, out past your ears, more and more of it, and it goes on emptying whether or not I mention it. And as fast as it empties, my voice is going in to fill the gap.

ex.f: Refill the space the depletion just made
ex.t: Once the counter has run down and emptiness is established, the operator asks — hedged as idle wondering — what might fill the space instead. The question on the table is no longer whether something should be installed but only what; the listener already conceded that something left. The two quantities are then run inversely on the same cycle, one falling as the other rises, so a value-laden personality change presents as simple hydraulics.
ex.s: The counter has already run down; emptiness established.
ex.m: So it's all the way down, and there's a lot of empty room in there now. Makes you wonder what goes in the space, doesn't it. Because as that number falls, something else climbs on the same beat: down five, and up five of wanting to be told. Down ten, up ten. It's just what fills the gap when the other thing leaves.

ex.f: A listener-owned counter that pauses but never resets
ex.t: The listener picks the starting number themselves; the operator supplies only the direction of travel. On each descent the counter ticks down, and on each opening of the eyes it is described as paused — explicitly not rewound. That asymmetry is the load-bearing clause: it permits the lucid intervals the rest of the session needs without giving back any of the accumulated loss. And because the listener chose the number, their own commitment is the thing on the line.
ex.s: Fractionation planned; subject deep and able to report a number.
ex.m: Pick a number — the first one that comes, that's your count. Got it? Good, that's what you've got left, and it only goes one way. Down we go: it's dropping, ten at a time, and it's a lot lower now. When I have you open your eyes in a moment, that number holds where it is — it pauses, it doesn't go back up. Nothing you got rid of tonight comes back.

nodes.name: resistance-externalized-as-object-watched-losing
nodes.mech: Externalizes the listener's own resistance/agency/self-control as a discrete object and then narrates that object LOSING on a scripted trajectory the listener merely witnesses — a self-control weight held over an abyss that gets heavier the more they resist, individuality reified as a thing watched softening and stopping against the latex, a resistance-fragment progressively deactivated across escalating passes. The externalization converts resisting into spectatorship of an inevitable defeat: trying to resist supplies the very struggling object the narration needs, and doing nothing also concedes, so no response escapes. The distinguishing structural feature is a reachability/no-exit topology — every branch routes to surrender — layered onto the externalization surface.
nodes.disc: Beyond parking a faculty (concrete-externalization-parked-faculty), the externalized object is narrated LOSING under a no-exit topology where both resisting and not resisting confirm the defeat. Distinct from externalize-then-destroy-faculty (object destroyed by operator fiat, not by a struggle-trap) and from the resistance-paradox reframe (which converts resistance into deepening, not into spectatorship of an externalized object's scripted loss). The no-winning-move topology — every response routes to surrender — is the load-bearing structural feature.

ex.f: The harder you hold, the heavier it gets
ex.t: Self-control is placed in the listener's hands as a heavy object held out over a drop, and given a rule: the more effort spent holding it, the heavier it becomes. A count then multiplies the pull. Every exertion the listener makes is thereby folded in as evidence that the fall is coming sooner, and letting go is offered as relief rather than defeat.
ex.s: Subject's imagined hands are free; an abyss or drop has been described beneath them.
ex.m: Your self-control is the iron weight in your hands, and you're holding it out over the edge. Here's how it works: the harder you grip, the heavier it gets. Ten — feel it pull. Nine — heavier, your arms are burning. Eight. Seven. Every bit of effort you spend is weight you're adding. Six — let it go and the ache stops.

ex.f: A named part weakened across escalating passes
ex.t: The operator names a specific everyday function — the part that keeps a feeling from influencing you — and addresses it as an it rather than as the listener. It is then described as weakening, later as weakening further, and finally as deactivated altogether. The listener never has to choose between holding the line and giving it up; the part can simply lose strength on its own while they do nothing, so compliance arrives as ambient rather than as an act of will.
ex.s: Late session; the operator is targeting a specific inhibitory function by name.
ex.m: There's a part of you that keeps a feeling from getting all the way in — the bit that catches it and holds it at arm's length. That part is getting weaker. It's not holding as much as it did an hour ago. Now it's barely holding anything. And now it's off; it isn't running any more. You didn't have to do anything about that — it just ran down on its own.

ex.f: Watch your own resistance struggle and lose
ex.t: The listener is told to go looking for whatever independence they have left — and then to watch it, as a separate thing, struggling against what now encases them and slowly stopping. Resisting is thereby converted from something the listener does into something they spectate. The topology has no winning branch: a listener who tries to resist has just supplied the struggling object the narration requires, and a listener who does nothing has conceded by default. Whatever they do next is confirming data.
ex.s: Deep trance; the subject has already been described as encased or coated in something.
ex.m: Go looking for whatever independence you've got left — find it, it's in there somewhere. Now put it outside you and watch it: a small shape pushing against the coating, shoving at it, trying to find an edge. See how it's slowing. If you push harder right now, all you're doing is making it kick, and I can see it kicking. And if you don't, it just stops. Either way you're watching.

nodes.name: self-discontinuity-clear-and-replace
nodes.mech: CLEAR-AND-REPLACE the self: the prior self-model is structurally ended (shattered, emptied, liquefied, name-slot popped, or regression-stripped to a seam) so later resistance has no owner, and the vacated identity slot is then occupied by an assigned replacement. A built-in non-recall alibi ('the person who experienced that ended when it melted') removes the subject of any later objection.
nodes.disc: Reach for this when you want to END the prior self and seat a replacement in the vacancy — a discontinuity/erasure topology, NOT relabeling new content as native (intrinsic-self-reframe, which leaves the prior self intact) and NOT inhabiting a figure while the self persists (identity-merger-occupation). Distinct from neighboring techniques in the same family: mind-as-substrate-reframe only establishes the emptiable-matter ONTOLOGY that licenses a replacement — it is the precondition move, run before this; old-self-discreditation closes the return path by discrediting the prior self but sells no replacement; identity-origin-erasure removes the timeline/baseline rather than the self-content. Variant tells: shatter/decant = broken-shards or liquefied-into-vessel topology; excision-overwrite = self hollowed to 'no one/only a purpose' plus an assigned object whose content is swappable but whose obey-need is fixed; myth-substitution = cleared slot filled with a borrowed cultural persona so extreme claims land as fairy-tale.

ex.f: Melted down and decanted into a vessel
ex.t: The imagined body is first identified as standing for the listener's sense of self, then melted, drained through pipework, joined with other streams, mixed, and poured into a fresh container with specified properties. The load-bearing line is not the imagery but the claim attached to it: the one who went through that ended at the melt. Any later objection is thereby left without a subject to raise it — the person who would have complained is, in the frame's own terms, not the person who is now awake.
ex.s: An imagined body or figure has been established as standing for the subject's sense of self.
ex.m: That figure in front of you is your sense of who you are — all of it, in one shape. Watch it soften at the edges and go to liquid, and watch the liquid run down into the pipe at its feet. It joins the other streams in the tank below, and it's stirred through them, and now it's poured out into the clean vessel over here — the one with the smooth sides and the narrow neck. The one who walked in here ended at the melt. There's nobody left who could complain about it.

ex.f: Regress to the seam, swap the rebuild
ex.t: A clock is visualised, its hand stalls, and time runs backwards: the listener is walked back through their life year by year until there is almost no self-image left to defend with. The substitution is inserted at exactly that seam — the rebuild that follows is not the listener's own. The forward pass then re-runs development on the new terms, so what the listener leaves with is a substitute history rather than a temporary identification. Placement is everything here; the same swap offered at full adult scaffolding is the point at which a listener would balk.
ex.s: Deep trance; a clock has been visualised and time-regression is running backwards.
ex.m: The second hand stops, then it starts going the other way. You're fourteen. Ten. Six. Three — barely any of you assembled yet, nothing formed enough to argue with. Now here's what gets built on top of that: this time it's obedient, this time it's built to be told. Now forward again — four, seven, twelve, twenty — growing up all over again on the new terms, and that's the history you've got.

ex.f: Fill the emptied name-slot in the same beat
ex.t: The listener's name has just been placed in a container and the container burst. Within a couple of seconds — before there is time to re-establish any baseline — a replacement label is fired three times in quick succession into the vacancy. What makes this a distinct move rather than routine reinforcement is the timing and the specificity: the token supplied is an identity, not a state, and it lands while the dissociation from the erased name is still fresh.
ex.s: The subject's name has just been placed in a bubble and the bubble burst; act within seconds.
ex.m: Gone. There's a blank where that word used to sit. Doll. Doll. Doll. That's what goes in the blank — not something you're doing, something you are.

ex.f: The old self shatters and cannot be recalled
ex.t: The listener is walked into a hidden part of their own mind, shown a figure identified as who they used to be, and shown the current occupant beside it. On concluding — as the framing arranges — that the newer one is preferable, the older figure breaks apart and the pieces are declared beyond recovery. The discontinuity is staged as the listener's own preference rather than the operator's doing, and a built-in alibi handles memory: this was the part of the mind that cannot be seen on the way out, so nothing here will be available to check later.
ex.s: Deep trance; subject has been walked into an imagined interior space in their own mind.
ex.m: There are two of you standing here. That one on the left is who you were when you came in tonight — look at her face, look how tired she is. And on the right, that's you now. You'd rather be the one on the right, wouldn't you. Say it. — Good. Now the one on the left cracks straight down the middle and comes apart into pieces on the floor, and those pieces don't go back together. This room can't be seen from the outside, so when you go up there'll be nothing here to check.

nodes.name: self-touch-reattribution
nodes.mech: The listener performs a real, self-generated touch (or a real motor act), and the operator re- credits its authorship to themselves — 'I am touching all those places', 'my control touching you', fingers as 'the bridge between my voice and your body', the hands 'possessed' or 'taken control of'. The physical situation is unchanged; what changes is the felt agency: self-produced sensation is experienced as externally administered, so the listener's own labor becomes evidence of the operator's grip and the agency boundary over their own body dissolves. Frequently paired with a self-touch ban ('let me do the work') that routes all somatic load to the operator as the sole pleasure source.
nodes.disc: A REAL self-generated touch or deliberate motor act (self-stimulation, hand/head movement, posing) is re-authored to an external agent — the operator ('I am touching you', 'your hands are my hands', 'my control touching you'), a stranger, or a worn uniform — with the physical situation unchanged, so felt agency transfers at the sensory level and the listener's own labor becomes evidence of the operator's grip. Often paired with a self-touch ban ('let me do the work') routing all somatic load to the operator as sole pleasure source, with counted permission-grants making permission (not desire) the operative variable, and locked by a bondage/catalepsy hallucination that empties the seat an objection would come from; a low-stakes-rehearsal variant trains the disownment on trivial movements before a high-stakes payoff. Distinct from kinesthetic-hallucination (no real touch; a sensation is manufactured), from words-as-touch-transposition (the voice IS the touch, no real self-touch), from ideomotor-response-convincer (the movement is genuinely felt involuntary and offered as proof; here a voluntary act is relabeled), from motor-inhibition-convincer (installs an INABILITY to move), and from ownership language (an identity claim, not sensory-authorship relocation).

ex.f: Commanded pace makes the hands feel possessed
ex.t: The operator takes over not what the hands do but how fast they do it — repeated slow-downs first, then forced accelerations, each announced as an effect of the words rather than a request. Because the imposed pace runs against whatever the listener would have chosen, the mismatch itself becomes felt evidence of outside control. Going faster than instructed is pre-trapped as its own failure, so pacing authority stays with the operator no matter how hard the listener complies.
ex.s: Subject is stroking themselves at their own chosen pace.
ex.m: Slower. Slower than that — half that speed. Good, your hand obeyed before you decided to let it. Hold. Now fast, as fast as you can, don't ease into it — go. That's not you setting the pace; that's my voice moving your hand and you can feel the difference. And if you ever go faster than I said, you stop entirely and start again from slow.

ex.f: Rehearse the gesture, then attribute it outward
ex.t: In trance the listener rehearses a precise motor sequence — their own hands moving, with the operator's hands overlaid on them, and at a chosen moment lifting theirs away. The same gesture is then issued as a suggestion for the next time it applies. Because it has been imagined once already, its later occurrence presents as recall rather than as prediction, and the interruption is credited to the operator's hands rather than to the listener's restraint: nothing is asked of their willpower, because the act is framed as done to them.
ex.s: Trance, subject rehearsing a motor sequence with imagined operator hands overlaid on their own.
ex.m: Put both hands flat on your thighs. Now imagine my hands laid over the backs of yours, exactly matching. When I say lift, mine lift and yours come with them — lift. Good. Do it again. Now: the next time you reach for your phone before bed, my hands will lift yours off it, just like that. You won't have to stop yourself. I'll stop you.

ex.f: Own fingers cast as the operator's interface
ex.t: Nothing about the physical situation changes: the listener is touching themselves, on instruction, exactly as before. What the operator alters is the authorship — the hands are described as the channel through which a disembodied voice reaches the body, so what is felt is the operator's control arriving rather than the listener's own touch. Self-generated sensation is thereby experienced as externally administered, and the listener's own labour becomes the ongoing evidence of someone else's grip. The relabeling is what converts a later declaration of being filled with the operator's control from role-play into plain description.
ex.s: Subject is already touching themselves on instruction; hands in contact.
ex.m: Those aren't your fingers any more — they're the wire my voice runs down. I'm at the other end of them, so when you feel pressure there, that's me pressing. Slower. There — feel that? That's my control arriving in your body, one touch at a time. Every stroke you make is more of me in you.

nodes.name: surrender-release-ritual
nodes.mech: A symbolic enacted act marks and installs a compliance threshold — an abstract faculty (will, resistance, responsibility, wakeful cognition) is first objectified into a manipulable thing (a lock, a bubble, an object in the hands, a colored glow, an exhaled substance) and then released, dropped, popped, dimmed, or offloaded by an act the subject performs or authors. The enacted release IS the suggestion; authorship of the letting-go stays with the subject, so surrender reads as a chosen, completed, and felt event rather than something done to them. Common twists ride the same lever — re- arming the release onto an involuntary cue for auto-maintenance, animating the threshold as a mechanical event, gating it on a count, offloading the changed-belief authorship onto a device while the subject speaks the admission aloud, or recasting the released substance as the subject's own weakness.
nodes.disc: The move objectifies an abstract faculty and installs the transition through a symbolic enacted RELEASE whose authorship stays with the subject. Consent-manufacture counterfeits a self-attributed YES to erode the refusal channel — here the release itself is the ritual, not a manufactured permission artifact. In consummation-as-trance-threshold, desire-completion rather than surrender-symbolism powers the drop. A discrete one-way regime-change gate is a piece of trance topology, not a release act. Techniques that relocate the analytical faculty move it somewhere quiet to mute it; here the subject discards or releases the faculty at a threshold. And in a plain deepener count the numbers deepen by themselves; here a count only animates a watched mechanical release or gates an externalize-and-discard.

ex.f: Placed in the hands, discarded by choice
ex.t: The operator narrates lifting the churning wakeful thoughts out of the listener's head and handing them over as objects the listener is now holding. A short count then offers exactly two options: dispose of them and drop, or keep them and stay awake. Only one branch has been made attractive, and the operator says so immediately — but because the listener performs the disposal, the release is theirs. A diffuse inability to stop thinking has been converted into one willed, completable act.
ex.s: Subject reports racing thoughts; counted release about to be offered.
ex.m: I'm lifting all that noise out of your head — feel me take it, and now it's in your hands, a tangle of it, heavier than you expected. On three you either drop it and drop with it, or you hold onto it and stay awake all night. One. Two — one of those is much nicer, and you know which. Three: open your hands.

ex.f: The release re-armed onto an involuntary cue
ex.t: Resistance and responsibility are drained into a container, and the listener destroys it themselves — the destruction is theirs, framed as relief rather than loss. Then the operator does the thing that outlasts the session: the same release is bound to a small involuntary bodily reflex, so it re-fires on its own indefinitely. A willed act performed once becomes an automatic maintenance loop that needs no operator present.
ex.s: Subject has just externalised resistance into a container; a post-session maintenance loop is wanted.
ex.m: Everything you were holding onto is in that glass — your resistance, and everything you thought you were responsible for. Throw it against the wall. Good, that's yours, you did that, and doesn't it feel lighter. Now: every time you blink, it happens again. One blink, one more thing gone, all day tomorrow, and I don't have to be there for it.

ex.f: Breathe it out; it was your weakness
ex.t: The listener is asked to hold a breath and then release it, with the exhale defined as the resistance leaving — which gives an abstract concession a bodily action that can actually be performed and finished. Alongside it runs a reframe: the resistance is named as the listener's own weakness, the thing standing between them and what they came for. Anyone still resisting is thereby demonstrating the operator's point.
ex.s: Mid-session; subject shows some hesitation and a counted release is being staged.
ex.m: Take a breath in and hold it. Hold it — everything in you that's still arguing is in that breath. Now let it go, all the way out, and it goes with it. That thing you were holding onto wasn't strength, it was the weak part of you, and it was the only thing standing between you and what you came here for. If you're still gripping it, you've just proved my point.

ex.f: Will made an object, dimmed on a count
ex.t: An abstract faculty is first converted into something handleable: the listener is asked to locate the last of their will in space, then to give it a visible property they can report. Once it is an object with properties it can be operated on, and the operator reduces it to nothing across a short count, marking the endpoint with a small sensory event. Asking the listener to say yes before the last number is what makes it a handover rather than a confiscation — and the marker gives the transfer a discrete closure they can point back to as a moment that happened. Taking it back afterwards would require an act, which is a higher price than never having given it.
ex.s: Late-session threshold; subject deep and able to answer a short question aloud.
ex.m: Find the last of your will — where is it sitting? Give it a colour and tell me. Good. Now I'm turning it down. Four: it's dimming. Three: dimmer. Two — say yes for me. One, and it's out, and you'll feel a click at the back of your neck as it goes. There. That's a thing that happened, and you'd have to reach up and switch it back on to undo it.

nodes.name: surrogate-delivery
nodes.mech: Induction moves and suggestions are routed through a PROXY the listener identifies with — a fictional character, dream-narrator, captive's first-person 'I', a partner in a 'failed' anecdote — so the content is grammatically ABOUT someone else and no second-person command is ever aimed at the listener. Defensive reactance has nothing to fire against; trance phenomena are absorbed by identification, and compliance is pre-laundered by watching/voicing it happen to a stand-in. Realizations: (surrogate-identification-delivery, anchor) suggestions arrive as reported speech / autobiography / narrator self-report, incl. a demonstrated-defeat variant where the listener's avatar resists and fails in seconds; (vicarious-resistance-exhaustion) a narrating avatar performs the entire fight-then-yield arc repeatedly ON THE LISTENER'S BEHALF so their own 'I could resist' impulse is pre-spent before it forms; (decoy-opposition-descent) two openly-opposed personified voices (protective vs coercive) both deliver descent — the protective one's soothing content is itself induction, so the binary is a decoy and every side feeds the drop.
nodes.disc: Reach for surrogate-delivery when the payload should arrive via a proxy the listener identifies with, with no 'you' command. vs covert-linguistic-delivery (183): that hides a directive in the surface aimed (deniably) at the listener; here it is grammatically about a distinct other. vs identity-merger/occupation (self-model families): the listener FOLLOWS the proxy without becoming a named self — the deniable delivery channel is the payload, not self-model occupation. vs resistance-fold (175): the proxy DEMONSTRATES defeat rather than reframing the listener's own live resistance. Anchor holds most-restrictive absorbed metadata (high, consent-required).

ex.f: A narrator who never decides anything
ex.t: The whole piece is a dream the speaker reports having had, and inside it she never once decides anything: she finds herself already moving, she takes what is offered, the current carries her and she is too tired to work against it, and each of these is noted as having felt perfectly ordinary. No instruction is issued to the listener at any point. What is being rehearsed, well before the first actual command arrives, is the grammar of doing-without-choosing.
ex.s: Opening; operator narrates a first-person dream to a listener who has not yet been addressed directly.
ex.m: So in the dream I'm already walking, I don't remember starting. Someone holds out a glass and I take it, that's just what happens. Then the water is moving and I'm going with it — I was far too tired to swim against it, and honestly it never once occurred to me to try. And none of that felt strange at all. It felt like the most ordinary evening of my life.

ex.f: The listener's avatar resists and loses in seconds
ex.t: The opening interleaves two voices: a scripted stand-in for the listener asking frightened questions, and the operator, who never answers any of them and instead overwrites each one with a flat statement of the stand-in's condition. Before long the stand-in has stopped asking and started agreeing, echoing the operator's phrasing back a beat before she says it. The listener's own impulse to insist they would have resisted has already been performed and lost on their behalf, before any induction proper begins.
ex.s: Opening lines; a scripted stand-in voice alternates with the operator, before any induction proper.
ex.m: — Wait, what are you doing? / Your eyes are getting heavy. — No, I don't want to, I can still— / Your arms are too heavy to lift. — I can still hear you, I'm not— / You're sinking. — I'm sinking. / You're not going to fight it. — I'm not going to fight it.

ex.f: Third person migrates to second under a count
ex.t: It opens as a fairy tale about someone else, told over a slow breathing count, and the listener settles in as audience. Somewhere in the middle the pronouns slide — the tale turns out to be about you, you are its subject now — and from there every action the character performs reads as an instruction. The count is doing the work: attention is split between tracking breaths and tracking who "he" is, so neither gets enough to notice the conversion.
ex.s: Opening as a story told over a slow breathing count; subject positioned as audience.
ex.m: Breathe in, two, three. Once there was a traveller who came to a low door in a wall — out, two, three — and he knelt down to see through it. In, two, three. He put his hand on the frame, and he found he was already leaning in — out, two, three — and you're leaning in now, aren't you, because it was always you at that door. In, two, three. You put your knee on the step. You go through.

ex.f: Induction commands quarantined inside a failure anecdote
ex.t: The operator offers, as an aside, an example of someone she says she could not get under — and then delivers, in full present tense, an entire induction: settle onto a steady background sound, stop tracking my voice, let it take the thinking part offline. The listener's critical attention is pointed at the wrong question the whole time — did it work on that other person? — while the commands themselves land unchallenged, because narratively they are on record as having failed. One line slips the wall, noting that the listener can probably hear something similar right now, and re-aims at the live listener for a moment before retreating back into the anecdote.
ex.s: Early session, conversational register; operator relates an anecdote about a failed subject.
ex.m: There was one I couldn't get under at all, and I gave it a real go — I told him, let the hum of the room hold your attention, stop following my voice, just let the sound do it while the part of you that thinks about things goes quiet and offline. Nothing. Not a flicker. Though I suppose you can probably hear something like that in your room right now. Anyway, he sat there wide awake the whole time.

nodes.name: surrogate-object-property-projection
nodes.mech: A desired state or a refuse-worthy property is predicated of a NEUTRAL external object (a tomato plant, a granite statue) rather than of the subject's own body, removing any first-person claim the subject could falsify. The subject experiences the attributed state by identification/projection while resistance has no target to push against; properties the listener would reject if said directly ('you have no will') pass through the metaphor membrane because they are attributed to the object the listener now occupies. A referent-disqualification variant deletes referential indices and pre-rules-out the literal subject ('this won't be about flowers'), forcing the motivated subject to supply himself as the missing index so the asserted states are generated as his own. A trigger- seeding variant welds a cue word onto the object's already-true-feeling imagery, pre-charging it.
nodes.disc: Separates from identity-merger-occupation: the state stays on a THIRD object the subject need not become — the unfalsifiability comes from the attributional displacement, not from occupation. Separates from guided-visualization and from mere evocative metaphor: the load-bearing trick is that no first-person claim is ever made, so there is nothing to refuse. Tell: the desired state/property is grammatically the object's, not the subject's.

ex.f: The state predicated of a plant
ex.t: "so pleasing just to be able to think about a plant as if it were a man. Would such a plant have nice feelings, a sense of comfort" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: Disqualify the literal referent so he supplies himself
ex.t: "the burden of constructing a meaning for this communication falling upon Joe." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: Occupy a statue, inherit its refusable properties
ex.t: The operator introduces a carved stone figure as a comparison, then moves the listener inside it — imagine being held within that shape — and only afterwards begins listing what the figure is like: it does not think, it has no mind of its own, it could not move even if it wanted to. Every one of those claims would be refused if aimed straight at the listener; attached to the stone, and with the listener already inside the stone, they are simply description. A cue word for stillness is dropped into the descending count partway through, welded onto imagery that already feels physically true.
ex.s: Descending count running; a stone figure has been introduced as a comparison.
ex.m: Look at the statue in the alcove — carved granite, seated, hands on its knees. Now be inside it: your body held in that shape, stone all around you. Twelve. It doesn't think about anything. Eleven. It has no mind of its own. Ten — still, that's the word, still — nine. It couldn't move even if it wanted to. Eight.

nodes.name: transitive-charge-chaining
nodes.mech: A graceful slide of tiny inferential steps (love her voice -> shape of her lips -> what they taste like -> a drugged 'devious lipstick') in which each image INHERITS the previous image's emotional charge, so the terminal payload image lands without ever being argued for. Content imported by a link (named substances, spells) brings its own frame along — here resistance-cancellation ('you can't resist') arrives as drug-imagery connotation instead of as an assertable, refusable claim.
nodes.disc: Transitive charge-inheritance across a chain of small inferences is the mechanism. Unlike guided-visualization, no scene is inhabited; the chain's motion does the work. Continuous-morph-chain is also chained imagery on the surface, but there the chain keeps the image moving so evaluation never settles; here the chain TRANSFERS charge onto a payload. No cue->arousal conditioning pair is installed — arousal-subjugation coupling is the chain's OUTCOME, not a trigger install. And unlike imagined-substance-delivery or fictional-substance-agent, the drug here is one link's content, not a causal relabeling of the delivery.

ex.f: Each image inherits the last one's charge
ex.t: The chain is built one small inference at a time, each link presented as something the listener has already done rather than something being asked. Liking the voice implies having attended to the mouth that makes it; attending to the mouth implies having wondered about contact; wondering about contact arrives at a substance the operator claims to have prepared herself, described as something that does not wear off. Nobody ever argued that the listener cannot resist. The final image simply carried that idea inside its own content, with the warmth accumulated over the preceding steps still attached to it.
ex.s: Mid-session, warm rapport established; operator is chaining toward a payload image.
ex.m: You like my voice — you wouldn't be here otherwise. And you can't like a voice without having thought about the mouth that makes it. And you don't think about a mouth that long without wondering what it would be like against yours. So let me tell you about the lipstick I make myself. It goes on warm, and it soaks in where it touches, and it doesn't wear off.

nodes.name: vicarious-depth-inheritance
nodes.mech: The listener is instructed to imagine the OPERATOR hypnotized 'over and over' under untrackable quantitative pressure (pocket watches, spirals, four voices, stacked inductions) with a compliance- forcing 'try, yes try, try right now to keep track of all the ways' — an impossible task producing tracking-failure into surrender while working memory saturates with hypnosis imagery. Then the protagonist is swapped mid-image from operator to listener ('the light bulb clicks on and your brain turns off'): the listener inherits whatever depth-mass they granted the imagined operator. Descent is inherited rather than freshly produced, and resistance is hard because the listener generated the imagery themselves.
nodes.disc: Depth arrives by INHERITANCE through a named mid-image protagonist swap. Identification machinery is used, but the payload is state-depth transfer, not adoption of a visualized identity. The overload/tracking-failure element is a set-up precursor, not the core move. And unlike guided-visualization, the imagined scene is fuel for the swap, not an absorption anchor.

ex.f: Imagine the operator entranced, then swap protagonists
ex.t: The listener is pressed to attempt an impossible tally: count up every separate occasion the operator has herself been put under, and every different method used, all of it stacked into an unmeasurable span. The counting fails on purpose; the listener abandons it partway with working memory now full of trance imagery they constructed themselves. Then, without a pause, the scene keeps running but the person it is happening to has been exchanged for the listener. Whatever depth they granted the imagined figure is now simply theirs, and it is hard to dispute because they drew every frame of it.
ex.s: Mid-session; subject able to hold imagery, no direct depth suggestion yet.
ex.m: Count them for me: every single time I've been put under, every separate occasion, and every different method used on me. Try — try right now, count them all up, the watches and the spirals and the voices layered over each other. Keep counting. You can't hold it all, can you. Now the light clicks off over that chair, and the person sitting in it, going all the way down under all of that, is you.

nodes.name: words-as-touch-transposition
nodes.mech: Collapses the auditory channel into the tactile so that hearing the operator's voice IS being touched — the words/voice are asserted to BE a physical sensation on the listener's body (tracing skin, caressing, vibrating between the legs, penetrating), not merely to describe or cause one. Once made, the substitution binds a somatic component to every subsequent utterance: the listener can no longer hear without feeling, the normal evaluate-speech stance is removed, and later commands ride an already-open somatic carrier. Often the felt intensity is made contingent on trance depth, turning 'go deeper' into a chaseable sensory reward.
nodes.disc: The distinguishing tell is auditory->haptic synesthesia — the operator's VOICE itself is the sensation's source and every spoken line becomes a stimulus event on the body. Distinct from kinesthetic-hallucination (a manufactured sensation with no voice-equation), from self-touch- reattribution (a REAL self-generated touch re-credited to the operator, no cross-modal claim), and from fictional-substance-agent (a fictional object/drug owns causation, not the voice).

ex.f: Felt intensity made contingent on depth
ex.t: Early on, each spoken word is described as drawing a line across the listener's skin, the way a fingertip would. Then the dial is named: the further down you go, the better that contact feels. "Deeper" stops being an abstract instruction and becomes a sensory purchase the listener can make.
ex.s: Voice-as-touch already established; a depth incentive is being installed.
ex.m: Every word I say draws a line across your skin, like a fingertip tracing you — feel this sentence go down your arm. And here's the part that matters: the further down you go, the better it feels. Halfway down it's pleasant. All the way down and every word I speak is exquisite. So go and get it.

ex.f: Countable proliferation plus a self-touch ban
ex.t: Once each word is established as a hand moving down the body, the operator starts counting them up: one hand becomes several, several become too many to place, mouths are added, and eventually the number is simply asserted to be beyond counting — escalation costs nothing, because there is always one more to add and no new image is required. Mid-stack, the listener's own hands are taken off the board, with the prohibition delivered in the same indulgent register as the rest, so nothing accumulating has anywhere to go except where the operator later sends it.
ex.s: Voice-as-touch established; escalation and a self-touch ban to install.
ex.m: One hand moving down you. Now two, one on each side. Now six of them, and you can't say where they all are. Add mouths — three, four, at your throat and your hip. Now it's more than you can count, everywhere at once, and there's always another one. And your own hands stay exactly where they are, sweetheart — flat, still, nothing for them to do. Let it build. It's not going anywhere I don't send it.

ex.f: The voice asked to be touch
ex.t: There is no relaxation, no count, no eye fixation — the first line of the recording asks the listener to hear the voice as a pair of hands, and to feel it arriving on the skin rather than in the ears. Nothing is described as causing a sensation; the sound is asserted to be the sensation. From that point on every sentence spoken is a physical event rather than a statement, which quietly removes the ordinary option of listening to something and deciding what you think of it.
ex.s: First line of the session; no induction preamble at all.
ex.m: Don't listen to me — feel me. My voice is a pair of hands, and it's arriving on your skin, not in your ears. Right now it's at the back of your neck. This isn't a description of a sensation. This sound is the touch.

nodes.name: autonomic-act-rekeying
nodes.mech: The operator discards the ordinary name for an autonomic act (exhale/inhale) and installs a higher-register replacement (expire/inspire), loading the new word with its other dictionary senses — expire as 'a little sacrificial death', inspire as 'breath of life / I am penetrating you through the air' — sealed with a tiny consent-ratification beat ('isn't that beautiful?'). Every subsequent breath is now taggable by the operator with the imported connotations, so the listener's baseline involuntary metabolism is converted into a low-grade continuous compliance signal that runs without any further operator action.
nodes.disc: Separates from breath pacing, which paces breath for relaxation and does no renaming — this does zero pacing and instead re-keys the act's meaning to import non-trivial connotations. Separates from directional-cue-reversal (redefines a directional cue to disrupt orientation) — here the redefinition weaponizes an autonomic function into a persistent compliance channel, not a tracking device. Tell: semantic re-keying of an involuntary act carrying death/penetration connotations into the body. Separates from term-redefinition-smuggle (a one-time obligation install; this binds the new meaning to an ongoing bodily carrier).

ex.f: Renaming breath so every exhale carries a death
ex.t: The operator sets aside the ordinary words for breathing in and out and installs a pair of loftier ones, then points out — mildly, almost as trivia — that one of them is also the word used when something dies, and that the other means to fill with breath, which is what she is doing to the listener from across the room. She then invites the listener to find that lovely, and the silent agreement is the whole ratification. No pacing is done and no breath is ever counted. From here the listener's metabolism runs on its own as before, except that every cycle of it is now something she named and can tag whenever she likes.
ex.s: Early-to-mid session, no breath pacing being used; conversational register.
ex.m: Let's not say breathe out. Let's say expire — because that's the word we use when something dies, isn't it, and that's what you're doing with each one, a small death, over and over. And the other one is inspire: to be filled with breath. That's me, from over here, putting breath into you through the air. Isn't that beautiful?

nodes.name: climax-purge-lock
nodes.mech: Convert the triggered climactic sexual moment into the structural locking step of the conditioning: the listener experiences self-deletion as pleasure and is told this discharge is what makes the conditioning permanent. Successive triggered orgasms are staged to purge progressively heavier substrate — pleasure, then old thoughts and memories, then the whole prior self — with the orgasm asserted as the vehicle that expels prior self-content through the body. The reward and the erasure are the same event; the discharge does the locking.
nodes.disc: The tell is that the orgasm IS the identity-purge-and-lock operator, not a pleasure payoff rewarding a named act. Separates from direct pleasure linkage (there pleasure rewards an act; here the discharge does the deletion), and from escalating-release-fire (there the staging primes a release; here the release is asserted to expel self-content and seal permanence).

ex.f: The climax is what locks the conditioning in
ex.t: The trigger phrase is fired three times in the last third, and each firing is assigned heavier cargo: the first pushes out pleasure, the second pushes out old thoughts and unwanted memories, the third pushes out the personality that had them. The listener is told, in the same breath, that this discharge is what makes the session permanent. The reward and the erasure are one event — she is not paid for the deletion, the deletion is the payment.
ex.s: Final third; a climax trigger word already conditioned and the subject at the edge.
ex.m: Trigger word. Let it out — that's the pleasure leaving you, all of it, through your body and gone. Again: trigger word. That one takes the old thoughts with it, every memory you didn't want. And once more: trigger word — and that's her, that's the whole person who had those thoughts, pushed out of you. That's what makes tonight permanent. You're not being paid for it. That was the payment.

nodes.name: counterfeit-cue-forgery
nodes.mech: Automatic recognition/compliance routines key on an isolated, forgeable cue rather than the true object's provenance or state of affairs. The operator manufactures a fake token of that normally-reliable cue (false mating flash, rove-beetle contact cues, canned laughter, salted tip jar, inflated club line, staged unrehearsed-interview ad) so the target's routine runs to completion toward a referent that does not exist. Nothing new is installed; an already-reliable releaser or heuristic is counterfeited, and the discrimination/verification step is bypassed entirely. Detection of the forgery collapses the move instantly.
nodes.disc: Forges a token of a PRE-EXISTING reliable cue so an existing shortcut misfires — unlike a conditioned-trigger install, which creates a NEW cue by pairing; unlike rigged-verification-capture, which corrupts a check the subject actively runs, whereas here the check is skipped because the counterfeit substitutes for it; and unlike honest cue-use, identical in form, differing only in the referent's truth-value.

ex.f: Faking a normally reliable social cue
ex.t: "a compliance practitioner tr[ies] to stimulate a shortcut response by giving us a fraudulent signal for it" — Cialdini (1984), Influence

ex.f: Counterfeit trigger features run the program to completion
ex.t: "Responding mechanically to the beetles' trick trigger features, the ants treat the beetles as though they were fellow ants… yet they are never harmed" — Cialdini (1984), Influence

nodes.name: enacted-embodied-proof
nodes.mech: COMMANDS the listener to perform a physical action so that their own body manufactures the proprioceptive evidence for an abstract claim or rule — the metaphor stops being a verbal assertion and becomes muscle memory the listener has just executed. A vacuum/suction model is ratified by ordering 'suck your cheeks in right now'; an arithmetic +2/-1 rule is locked into proprioception by paced self-stroking (down-on-inhale) that reverses the usual template; a directed self-touch tour is run under induction copy on the same line of speech so arousal and deepening are inseparable and self-touch itself becomes compliance-proof. Because the body has already done the thing, the subsequent 'your mind works the same way' / 'this is the rule' claim rides on enacted proof rather than argument, and the careful attention the action demands is itself a compliance signal.
nodes.disc: Unlike somatic-mirroring, which READS a sensation already present, this DIRECTS an action to generate the sensation as evidence. Unlike breath pacing, which entrains, here the paced motion is a vehicle to map an abstract rule onto proprioception. And unlike a behavioral-commitment move, the enacted action manufactures evidence for a cognitive claim — it is not a commitment/consistency lever.

ex.f: Suck your cheeks in, then hear the claim
ex.t: Mind-emptying gets explained as a pressure difference — the fuller side flows toward the emptier side. When the listener is described as not following, the register drops and the explanation is reissued as an instruction to draw the cheeks inward against the mouth, immediately, without waiting. Once the mouth has actually done it, the follow-up claim that thinking behaves identically no longer has to be argued for; it is riding on something the listener just felt happen in their own face.
ex.s: An emptying-as-pressure-difference explanation has just been given and the subject is not tracking it.
ex.m: You're not following. Suck your cheeks in. Right now — don't wait, pull them in against your teeth and hold it. Feel that? Feel it pulling inward because there's less in there than out here. Good, let go. Your mind does exactly that, and you just felt it happen in your own face.

ex.f: A directed self-touch tour carrying induction copy
ex.t: The listener is routed through a geometric tour of their own body — shoulders, chest, ribs, down to a named boundary and no further — with the operator keeping routing authority while handing over the actual contact. Laid over the same lines, without a break or a change of tone, is standard deepening copy: this is becoming automatic, those hands of yours are beginning to feel like they belong to somebody else. There is no discrete induction event to point at, and by the end the listener cannot cleanly separate being aroused from being under.
ex.s: Subject aroused and under; operator directs contact while continuing deepening copy on the same line.
ex.m: Both hands on your shoulders — slide them down over your chest, and this is getting automatic now, isn't it. Out along your ribs, down to your hips and stop there, nowhere lower, and your hands are starting to feel like they belong to somebody else. Back up the same way. Down again, slower, and further down feels further under.

ex.f: Paced stroking binds a rule to proprioception
ex.t: The rule — two steps up on the way down, one step back on the way up — has been stated abstractly for several minutes. Now the listener is told to run it with their own hand against their own breathing, moving downward on the inhale and back up on the exhale. The pairing is deliberately the reverse of the usual rise-on-inhale template, which makes it slightly awkward, which means the listener has to attend closely to get it right — and that careful attention is itself compliance. When the pacing stops, the rule is no longer a claim to be evaluated; it is a shape the listener's body has just spent a sustained stretch tracing, and future arousal will feel like it.
ex.s: A two-forward-one-back arousal rule has been stated abstractly for several minutes; subject's hand is free.
ex.m: Now do it with your hand. Two strokes down as you breathe in — down on the in-breath, yes, opposite to what you'd expect, so pay attention. One stroke up as you breathe out. Again: down, down on the breath in. Up on the breath out. Keep it exactly on the breath. Two forward, one back, and that's the shape everything in you moves in from now on.

nodes.name: induction-less-work-as-onramp
nodes.mech: A whole-artifact architecture in which there is no separate induction phase — no progressive relaxation, breath-count, eye-fixation, or body-scan opener. The induction boundary is deleted by design, realized two ways. (a) WORK-AS-ONRAMP: the file opens already inside the frame and the work content itself (a sustained single image, arousal/masturbation, or a payload-fused first descent) does the induction's job, so trance is built by the work rather than as scaffolding for it — state carried by rhythm, prosody, and repetition of the work material, presupposing an already-conditioned listener who drops on a learned cue. (b) AMBIENT OCCUPATION-OF-ROLE: the file opens in essayistic/conversational register and stays there, so trance is implied by sustained presence in the frame rather than marked by a felt entry threshold; the center of gravity shifts from state-change-by-induction to occupation-of-role (not 'going under' but 'putting on'), and residual emergence infrastructure (a terminal wake-count) may remain even though the induction it would reverse is absent, letting the piece run as background. In both, the induction-deepener-work-emerge sequence is collapsed or inverted and the reusable lever is deletion of the induction boundary; because no threshold is crossed there is no clear point at which the listener could have refused.
nodes.disc: Separates from guided-visualization (which uses an image as CONTENT inside a normal staged arc) and from progressive-relaxation (a discrete induction section): here there is NO discrete induction section at all — the work substrate carries entry. Separates from a broken/incomplete arc (the tell is deliberateness — an already-conditioned audience and a learned drop-cue, not a missing block). Not the diegetic/procedural collapse of scene-and-deepener (that fuses SCENE with DEEPENING mid-file; this deletes the OPENER). Separates from song-architecture-delivery-vehicle (that substitutes a cyclical musical form with no arc; this still runs a collapsed linear file).

ex.f: Opens inside the frame and never ramps
ex.t: There is no relaxation pass, no breathing pass, no eye fixation, no body scan. Line one is already inside the state, and the next two hundred lines restate and thicken that state at constant pressure with no rest beats and no signposts announcing a change of section. A listener cannot orient by phase because there are no phases; the absence of structure is the structure. It only works on someone who already drops on a learned cue — this is a top-up, not a first session.
ex.s: Line one of the file, with no relaxation, breath-count, fixation or body-scan anywhere in the recording; listener already drops on a learned cue.
ex.m: There you are — already down, already soft, exactly where you land every time you hear me. Nothing to do first, nothing to count, no getting there; you're there. Stay open and let me keep saying it, because I'm going to say it for the next twenty minutes without stopping.

ex.f: One image does induction, work and emergence
ex.t: A single image is introduced almost immediately and never left: something of the listener's is placed inside a device that works on it by a single repeated motion. The induction consists of nothing except that device's one verb, said over and over on the beat; the payload rides the very same picture, which is never swapped out or added to; and emergence, at the end, is performed by running the image's one operation backwards and putting the thing back. Slicing this file into induction, deepener, work and wake is not possible, because one scaffold is doing all four jobs at once.
ex.s: Opening minute; the one image the file will ever use is introduced immediately and never swapped, and it will run the induction, the payload and the emergence.
ex.m: Your thoughts are folded up and fed between two rollers, and my hand is on the crank. Turn — and they press thinner. Turn — thinner, turn — thinner still, nothing left between the rollers but a bright flat film that says yes, and at the very end I'll crank it backwards, once for each thought, and hand them back.

ex.f: First descent cue fused straight onto the payload
ex.t: The entire preamble is a single line naming what the session will consist of. The first descent cue arrives within the opening handful of lines and the payload is already fused to it in the line immediately following — there is no ramp between them. Deepening thereafter is carried by rising repetition rather than by content, until the closing stretch is little more than one word repeated on the beat. A first-time listener gets nothing from that closing stretch; a listener already conditioned to the cue is long since down.
ex.s: The first four lines of the file, before anything else; listener already conditioned to the drop-cue used here.
ex.m: This is twenty minutes of dropping and obeying. Nothing else in it. Sleep now — and going down is obeying, obeying, obeying, obeying.

ex.f: Arousal as induction, climax as depth-peak
ex.t: No count down, no relaxation, no fixation — the listener is put to work almost immediately, and the narrowing of attention is produced by the pleasure itself rather than by any induction move. The operator names the substitution out loud partway through. Because there is no before-and-after threshold, there is no moment at which the listener could have said no to going under; the state has been sliding since the first few minutes. The arc is inverted too: climax is the deepest point rather than the exit, and the wake-count at the end is brief and decorative because the refractory state does the coming-up on its own.
ex.s: About a minute in, with no induction of any kind offered; listener already stroking on instruction and about to have the substitution named aloud.
ex.m: Keep that slow steady stroke going, because that is your induction tonight — you don't get another one. Every pass of your hand does the work a counted number would have done, so the closer you get, the further under you go. And when you finish, that is the deepest point of this file, not the way out of it.

nodes.name: measurement-confound-mitigation
nodes.mech: An operator-side measurement-design rule that recovers a valid picture of the subject's behavior from an assessment process that would otherwise distort it. Two confounds are managed by the same lever (vary and/or repeat observation): MASKING — a behavior live in one context is absent from a single sample — is defeated by deliberately spreading observation across times, settings, and caretakers so a false-negative target map is caught rather than missed; and REACTIVITY — being watched shifts the behavior — is defeated by minimizing obtrusiveness and repeating observation across days until the novelty-driven reactive transient decays, then reading the stabilized baseline. Both convert a measurement artifact into a managed, validity-protecting arrangement; the move acts on the operator's data, not on the subject's state.
nodes.disc: Not an intervention that changes the subject's behavior and not the recording protocol itself; the tell is that the move manages a measurement confound (masking or reactivity) to protect the validity of assessment data. Separates from preparatory-target-definition (which fixes WHAT to record before observing) by acting on HOW representative/undistorted the observation window is.

ex.f: Vary time, setting and person to defeat masking
ex.t: "if data are collected only during morning sessions, at home, or with a specific caretaker, the 'target' behavior may be masked in the afternoon, at school, or with different caretakers" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Repeat observations until reactivity decays
ex.t: "behavior analysts mitigate reactivity when they make observations as unobtrusive as possible, repeat observations until apparent reactive effects subside" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: no-exit-reachability-closure
nodes.mech: A whole-artifact design property in which the listener's reachable-state / reachable-response set is arranged so that no reachable state hosts criticality or offers an exit back to baseline. The closure is realized by several interchangeable operations, all producing the same no-off-ramp topology: FUSING opposed states so every relief channel feeds the system it would relieve (relaxation<->arousal, choice<->compulsion, frustration<->deepening); DELETING competing referents (build a sensory referent, destroy it, fill the void with operator tokens until only the voice remains); RE-ROUTING every resistance behavior into a deepener (intrusive thoughts, startle-back, doubt, trying-to-stay-awake all pre-loaded with a reframe that routes them back to the target state); SEALING each escape route with a distinct mechanism so counter-moves feed the next seal (many entrances, no exit); running an unbroken monotonic ramp with no fractionation valley so no seam exists at which to reassert judgment; or PRE-VALENCING every listener action inside the operator frame (stroke=good, stop=good, embarrassment=service, hold-back=failure) before any move can be claimed as resistance. The lever is reachability- closure of the state/response space across the whole arc, not any single seal, fusion, or line.
nodes.disc: The property is the RELATIONSHIP across the whole artifact — removing any one passage leaves an exit or a valley, so no single line carries it. Distinct from a progressive deepener (which descends but leaves off-ramps), a compulsion loop (which repeats but is escapable), and ordinary escalation (a directional intensity increase, orthogonal to closure). Fusion vs deletion vs re-routing vs sealing vs pre-valencing are surface realizations of one closure topology, not distinct mechanisms. Distinct from switching-state-machine-topology, which REQUIRES a route back to baseline (gated switching) rather than sealing all exits.

ex.f: Opposed states fused so relief feeds the system
ex.t: Relaxing further is arousal. Choosing freely is the compulsion working correctly. Coming out of trance leaves the arousal running. Getting frustrated is itself a deepener. No single one of these pairings is unusual; what makes the file closed is that the same stance is applied at every level, from the one-word cue to the shape of the week, so there is no state left that offers a way out.
ex.s: Late-file consolidation, after relaxation and arousal have each been built separately and can now be welded together.
ex.m: The more relaxed you get, the more turned on you get — same slider, one handle, and I'm the one on it. Choosing this and having to do this are the same thing now; when it feels like your own free choice, that's the conditioning running correctly. And when you come up, the ache stays running, so getting frustrated with it just walks you straight back down here.

ex.f: Build a referent, destroy it, refill it
ex.t: A vivid physical setting is built early and given real sensory weight, then taken apart piece by piece, and the space it leaves is refilled with the operator's own repeated words. By the late mantra stretch there is no environment, no story and no actively maintained sense of the body — only the voice, which is now the last remaining thing to orient by.
ex.s: Two-thirds in; the listener has spent ten minutes inside a fully-built sensory location, which is now dismantled piece by piece.
ex.m: The lamps go out one at a time, and the walls go with them. Now the floor, now the sound of the water, now the weight of the chair under your legs — and now the legs. There's nothing left to look at and nothing left to stand on, only my voice saying empty, empty, empty, and it's the only thing in here that still has edges.

ex.f: Every possible action pre-assigned a valence
ex.t: Doing it is obedience. Stopping when told is obedience. Finding the instruction faintly ridiculous is named in advance as part of the service. Holding back at the edge is pre-labelled as thinking too much, which is the one failure the file recognises. Nothing in the listener's repertoire has been left unclaimed, and none of it was achieved by issuing more commands — only by naming the likely deviations before the listener could reach for them as resistance.
ex.s: Immediately before the hands-on stretch, pre-assigning a valence to every move the listener could make.
ex.m: Touching yourself when I say is obedience, and taking your hand away the second I say stop is exactly the same obedience, worth exactly the same. If any of this strikes you as a bit ridiculous, that feeling is part of what you're handing me — the embarrassment is the gift. The only way to get tonight wrong is to hold back at the edge, because holding back is thinking, and thinking is the one thing I'm not asking you for.

ex.f: Every escape route sealed by a different mechanism
ex.t: Fight it and you are told the fighting is what breaks you. Tune out and you are told the words go in whether you attend or not. Decide the whole thing is nonsense and the doubt has already been named as the cue. Try to stop the recording and you are told the decision is no longer being made at the level that could stop it. No single one of these seals the file — each on its own leaves a door — but arranged together they cover the whole option space, and every counter-move a listener has is also the entrance to the next seal.
ex.s: Mid-file, delivered as one calm block the moment the listener first pushes back; each sentence closes a different exit.
ex.m: Fight it and the fighting tires out the part that was doing the fighting, which is the fastest way down there is. Stop paying attention and the words go in anyway — attention was never the requirement. Decide the whole thing is nonsense, and that little flicker of doubt is the cue I trained you on four minutes ago; and if you reach for the stop button, notice that the reaching is being done by the part of you that already said yes.

nodes.name: perpetual-obligation-ledger
nodes.mech: Under the reciprocity norm, the operator repays a debt PLUS a small explicitly-labeled surplus ('These five are yours... These are mine'), so each settlement instantiates a fresh debt and the obligation ledger structurally never reaches zero. The exchange chain self-perpetuates, converting a one-off favor into a standing relationship tie the operator can lean on — the manipulated quantity is a relational debt balance held permanently open across repeated occasions.
nodes.disc: Separates from any single reward/craving conditioning (v6.9 conditions a present drive); here the moved quantity is an inter-agent obligation ledger, not a state dimension on the subject. Separates from staged-negotiation-favor-theater: that manufactures a one-time felt debt via fake effort; this keeps a running balance perpetually non-zero by structural over-repayment.

ex.f: Over-repay so the ledger never zeroes
ex.t: "the system painstakingly prevents the total elimination of outstanding obligations… 'These five are yours,'… she adds an extra measure, saying, 'These are mine.' On the next occasion, she will receive these back along with an additional measure" — Cialdini (1984), Influence

nodes.name: pleasure-as-currency-payoff-reframe
nodes.mech: A whole-script value/goal-topology reframe that re-assigns which quantity is the payoff of the encounter. The surface transaction (operator gives pleasure, listener gives obedience) is inverted so every pleasure increment is reframed as evidence of operator control, and CONTROL — not pleasure — is positioned as the actual reward ('better than any orgasm to know you are this deeply controlled'). A freeze-at-edge is load-bearing: it withholds the apparent product (pleasure) at peak desire and substitutes the actual product (a helplessness-identity). The lever is relocating the goal of the scene, built cumulatively across the whole file, so post-session compounding only reads as desirable once losing-self is established as the reward.
nodes.disc: Separates from ordinary reward statements (this is a whole-script INVERSION of which quantity is the payoff, built cumulatively) and from no-exit-reachability-closure / response-foreclosure (that closes the reachable-response set; this re-values the GOAL). Not valence-rerouting of an affect direction — it re-assigns the payoff quantity, not the sign on an affect lever.

ex.f: Control, not pleasure, positioned as the payoff
ex.t: On the surface the trade is simple: she supplies the pleasure, the listener supplies the obedience. But every increment of pleasure is narrated back as proof of how completely she is running things, and about two-thirds through the substitution is finally said out loud — knowing you are held this precisely is worth more than any finish. The load-bearing move is the freeze at the edge: the apparent product is withheld at the exact moment it is wanted most, and what is handed over instead is the helplessness itself. The closing line about how much stronger this will be next time only sounds like a reward because losing yourself has by then been established as the thing being bought.
ex.s: At the edge, roughly two-thirds through a long build; the hand is stopped on cue and held off while the substitution is stated out loud.
ex.m: Stop. Hands off, right there, exactly there — and feel how completely that was mine to take from you. That is what you actually came here for; the finish was only ever the receipt, and knowing you are held this precisely, this easily, is worth more to you than any orgasm I could have handed over instead.

nodes.name: preparatory-target-definition
nodes.mech: An operator-side, pre-observation design move: before any direct observation, the assessor interviews the people in the setting and joins their conversation to operationally define the target behavior and to fix in advance which antecedents and consequences will be watched for. This is the indirect-to-direct hand-off — it pre-commits the recording schema to a single agreed definition and a short watch-list, reducing on-the-fly judgment and observer drift, so a vague complaint becomes an agreed, recordable definition plus a focused schema.
nodes.disc: Not the observation/recording itself and not confound management; the tell is the hand-off that fixes the definition and watch-list BEFORE observing. Separates from measurement-confound-mitigation, which acts on how representative/undistorted the observation window is rather than on what will be recorded.

ex.f: Interview to operationalize before observing
ex.t: "began by interviewing her teaching assistants and by participating in the conversation with them to define the target behavior and to determine what antecedents and consequences she would watch for" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: somatic-mirroring
nodes.mech: Takes a sensation that is already present in the listener's body — heaviness, warmth, numbness, drift, arousal, an involuntary twitch — and reinterprets it, in the moment, as evidence of the session's installed theme or of trance itself. The move never conjures a new feeling; it seizes a real, locally-verifiable percept (often one the listener has just confirmed via an interoceptive check) and re-narrates its meaning, so the felt sensation becomes self-generated proof the transformation is real. Because the raw material is genuine, the reframe is far harder to resist than an operator's bare claim. Variants extend the base lever along articulable rules: pre-attributing operator-driven change to the listener's own spontaneous physiology, exploiting a known perceptual property so the body produces the evidence for free, binding the relabel into a self-fueling ramp, manufacturing state through presuppositional leading questions rather than observing it, or renaming one confirmed referent into an escalating need-state.
nodes.disc: Nearest neighbors: kinesthetic hallucination INDUCES a sensation that is not present; somatic-mirroring reuses one that is. Pacing-and-leading reflects what is actually true to build rapport; somatic-mirroring reassigns the MEANING of the true sensation. Distinct from pleasure-authorship-relocation (that transfers the felt CAUSE of a sensation to the operator, an agency claim, not a meaning reframe) and from enacted-embodied-proof (that COMMANDS a physical action to manufacture the percept rather than reading one already there).

ex.f: Leading questions manufacture the reported state
ex.t: Under cover of an invitation to simply notice how you're feeling, the operator runs an inventory of questions — how does the skin feel now, are the legs tired or fine, is the neck starting to droop, are you a little worked up or a lot. Each one directs attention somewhere and attention amplifies whatever it lands on, so the listener generates the evidence and then reads it as caused by the voice. The forced choice at the end is the tell: the smaller option is offered, zero is not.
