ex.s: First two minutes, framed as an ordinary check-in; listener able to answer aloud or nod, and every question presupposes some amount of the state.
ex.m: Just notice how you're doing for a second. How's the skin on your forearms right now — heavier, or more like warm? Are your legs tired or fine, is the neck starting to droop a little, and are you a bit worked up, or a lot?

ex.f: Pre-attributing the change to the listener's own body
ex.t: Each change is credited to the listener's physiology before it is asked for: the breathing begins to slow around now, and there is nothing unusual about that; when someone is well under, the body tends to shift a little to find a better position. Anyone lying still will do both of those things anyway. So the ordinary drift of a resting body arrives already labelled as evidence of trance, and the listener experiences relaxing on their own rather than being relaxed by someone.
ex.s: Three or four minutes in, listener lying still, with no relaxation instruction yet given and none about to be given.
ex.m: Your breathing is slowing down around about now, all on its own — perfectly ordinary, nobody has to do that for you. And in a minute your body will shift a little to find a better position; that's just what a body does once someone is properly under. None of that is my doing.

ex.f: One confirmed referent renamed into a need-state
ex.t: First a neutral, entirely expected trance sensation is seeded — a warm settling somewhere around the stomach — and the listener is given time to find it and agree that it is there. Then, over a few lines, the same unchanged sensation is renamed: it's almost like being hungry, and then very hungry, and then hard to think about anything else. Nothing in the body was altered; only the label moved, which is exactly why the resulting craving feels like it came from inside.
ex.s: Mid-trance, after a neutral warm settling has been seeded and the listener has confirmed finding it; nothing in the body changes from here, only the label.
ex.m: That warm settled weight just under your ribs — you found it, it's yours, it's been there a couple of minutes. It's almost like being hungry, isn't it. And now it's very hungry, and now it's the kind of hungry that makes it hard to hold on to anything else you were thinking about.

ex.f: A sensation you confirmed, re-narrated as the theme
ex.t: Warmth belongs to the surroundings at first — the room, what the listener is wrapped in, what they are holding. Then it is offered as a shared observation rather than an instruction: are you getting that as well, the warm patch low in the torso, the one that gets stronger the longer you look at it. The listener checks, and finds something, because attention on a body part reliably produces something. Once the warmth is theirs and self-verified, it is tied to a second thing — warm places always make me drowsy — and the sensation they confirmed for themselves is now the evidence that they are going under. Refusing requires denying a feeling they have already half-reported.
ex.s: Early, listener settled and quiet, with something genuinely warm present — a blanket, a mug, a heated room — and able to nod or answer.
ex.m: It's warm in here tonight, isn't it — the blanket, the tea. I'm getting it too, that warm patch low in the belly that gets a little stronger the longer you keep your attention on it; have you found it yet? Warm places always make me drowsy — and there it is doing exactly that to you, and you found it yourself, I didn't put it there.

nodes.name: song-architecture-delivery-vehicle
nodes.mech: A whole-artifact delivery-vehicle property in which the conditioning payload is carried by a musical/song architecture rather than a linear induction-to-trance-to-wake arc: layered tiers (minimal repeating mantra hooks, a rhyme-locked sung chorus, and a spoken 'spacy recital' narrative) each operate at a different cognitive depth, and the piece is built for exposure-over-repetition (designed to be replayed) with no wake or emergence. A familiar pop sample in the carrier register lowers analytic guard by delivering the content as passively-consumed entertainment. The reusable lever is the artifact FORM (music-first, cyclical, replay-looped) as the conditioning substrate.
nodes.disc: Separates from the induction-less onramp candidate (that deletes the induction stage but still runs a linear file; this substitutes a cyclical MUSICAL form with no arc at all) and from carrier-medium-binding of a single trigger to a tone (this is whole-artifact song composition, not one binding). The tell is the tiered mantra/chorus/recital structure plus stated replay-loop intent, not any single passage.

ex.f: Song form as the conditioning substrate
ex.t: The piece is built in three tiers that work at different depths at once: a handful of short mantra hooks light enough to run in the background all day, a rhyming sung chorus carrying the actual conceptual payload, and spoken drifting passages that supply the elaborated story for the lowest-guard stretches. There is no induction, no wake and no arc — it is cyclical, and the lyrics themselves state the intent to replay it daily. A recognisable pop sample sits in the middle of the carrier, which delivers the content in the register of entertainment the listener already consumes without evaluating. What does the conditioning here is sheer accumulated exposure, rather than how far down any one sitting goes.
ex.s: Writing the track itself: three tiers over one loop, no induction, no wake, and the replay instruction stated inside the lyric.
ex.m: Hook, four times over the loop, light enough to hum at work: "empty head, easy yes." Chorus, on the sampled melody everybody already knows: "play me in the morning, play me every day / thinking's getting quieter and I like it that way." Then the spoken verse, half-time over the same bars, unhurried: "you don't have to follow this one, you only have to leave it running…"

nodes.name: staged-negotiation-favor-theater
nodes.mech: The operator, already knowing the outcome, stages a visible costly struggle with an off-stage authority (a 'battle' with the sales manager that never actually happens) and returns bearing fatigue signals — disheveled, weary, loosened tie, elapsed time — presenting the predetermined deal as a hard-won concession. The manufactured effort makes the target revalue an unchanged offer as a costly favor, manufacturing felt indebtedness and aligning the target emotionally with the operator ('he's on my side') against the fabricated adversary, which suppresses resistance.
nodes.disc: Separates from perpetual-obligation-ledger: that keeps a running debt balance open via over-repayment; this manufactures a single felt debt from theatrical effort with no real ledger. Distinct from a genuine negotiation — the outcome is predetermined and the cost-signal is theater; it collapses if the target glimpses the empty office.

ex.f: A staged battle with an off-stage authority
ex.t: "the salesman would loosen his tie and return to his customers, looking weary but carrying the deal he had just 'hammered out' for them—the same deal he had in mind before entering the boss's office." — Cialdini (1984), Influence

nodes.name: switching-state-machine-topology
nodes.mech: A whole-script install shape that builds a two-state machine (e.g. normal / bimbo) with explicit gated transitions and an accumulation rule biasing drift toward the target state over repeated cycles — rather than pushing toward a single permanent end-state. It requires the listener to spend most time in the vanilla state and enter the target state only on cue; a protective amnesia rule shields the vanilla state from contamination so the script is re-runnable rather than one-shot. The on-trigger is the ongoing operational interface; the script itself is a one-time installer for repeated cross-session use. The lever is the state-space topology (switching with a drift bias), not a directional intensity push.
nodes.disc: Separates from a destination-installer ('you are now permanently X') because the design deliberately keeps the listener mostly in the baseline state and gates entry to the target state — the tell is the two-state gated topology with an accumulation/drift rule and protective amnesia enabling re-runs. Distinct from no-exit-reachability-closure, which seals ALL exits; here exit back to baseline is REQUIRED by design.

ex.f: Two gated states with a drift bias
ex.t: The file does not aim at a destination. It builds two states with a named cue for entering the second and a named cue for returning to the first, plus a rule that each visit makes the next one easier — a drift bias rather than a one-way push. It assumes the listener spends most of their life in the ordinary state, and an amnesia rule keeps the second state's content from bleeding back, which is what makes the thing re-runnable. The recording is a one-time installer; the cue is the interface that gets used from then on.
ex.s: Install section of a one-time file, after both states have been demonstrated once each; the recording will not be replayed, the cues will be used from now on.
ex.m: When you hear me say pink light, you become her — playful, easy, empty; when you hear clear, you're yourself again and back to your afternoon. Every time you cross over, the crossing gets quicker and the state gets a little wider, so next time takes less of the cue than this time did. And what she does stays with her: you come back knowing you were away and not much more, and that is what makes this safe to run again next week.

nodes.name: valued-channel-induction
nodes.mech: The operator selects the induction channel matching the subject's strongest/most-valued representational system (read from predicates) and issues an opening task that PRESUPPOSES that channel. Because the task is one the subject executes fluently and without effort, executing it IS the entry into trance — processing transfers off the verbal/analytic track with near-zero friction. A failed induction is reframed as wrong-channel choice, not subject resistance.
nodes.disc: The channel is SELECTED from the subject's read valued system and the task PRESUPPOSES it rather than requesting it — the tell that this is not generic vivid-imagery rapport. Pacing-and-leading reflects the subject's CURRENT experience then leads; this instead matches the subject's channel CAPACITY and makes task execution itself the entry. Unlike guided-visualization, no scene is built; the channel choice is the mechanism. Unlike overlap-bridging, it stays INSIDE the strong channel; bridging deliberately crosses to a weak one.

ex.f: Match the induction to the subject's valued channel
ex.t: "By bringing the client to a task which presupposes a visualization capacity, the hypnotist facilitates the transfer of control..." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

nodes.name: crisis-induction-live-readout
nodes.mech: The operator deliberately names the group's most taboo material (even insulting a member) to detonate the habitual interaction sequence, then withholds all content engagement and observes, re-igniting with trigger mentions when it slows. The real, un-self-conscious sequence exposes who-triggers-whom that a polite session hides; fatigue and lowered later resistance are side effects, not the point.
nodes.disc: Operator stays a non-engaging igniter/observer harvesting a structural read-out - not arguing content, not running a covert-induction pretext, and not handling resistance: the provocation is diagnostic and resistance-lowering is only a byproduct. Sibling stage to influence-topology-node-selection, whose node choice the live read-out feeds.

ex.f: Detonate the group, then read it
ex.t: "I sit back and observe… If it starts to slow down, then I step in and kick it to get it going again." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: target-selection
nodes.mech: Design-time selection and operationalization of WHICH behavior/target the intervention will aim at, decided before anything is done to the subject; the payoff is the operator's target list, not any subject state. The variants are the selection criteria a writer chooses among: (a) FORWARD LEVERAGE — privilege behavioral cusps whose change unlocks disproportionate downstream contingency space, so one trained behavior cascades into untrained learning; (b) STANDING-CONTINGENCY MAINTAINABILITY — keep only targets the post-instruction environment will already catch and reinforce (and reject age-/community-atypical targets that suppress natural reinforcement), shifting the maintenance burden off the operator; (c) PRODUCING-BEHAVIOR VALIDITY — refuse to hang the contingency on an outcome or mere correlate; decompose the stated result into the definable behaviors that produce it and place the contingency there (named failure: contingency-on-the-product programs fail); (d) GOAL-PROXIMAL DIMENSION — operationalize the vague goal as one specific measurable dimension (rate, duration, latency, magnitude, topography) moved in a named direction, chosen by which dimension most directly advances the actual goal (calories, not bites); (e) TRAIT-TO-BEHAVIOR DECOMPOSITION — meet every intrinsic-trait label ('lazy','fearful') with 'what does X DO?' to dissolve the internal-cause attribution into a countable, environment-linked, targetable behavior; (f) STRENGTHS-FIRST BALANCE — force a fixed-count strengths inventory ahead of an equal-count deficit list at intake so the target pool tilts toward building, not only suppressing.
nodes.disc: Reach for target-selection when the writer's question is 'what should the intervention aim at?' — a design-time filter/operationalization on the operator's target list, nothing enacted on the subject. Pick the criterion by the sub-question: downstream leverage (a), will-it-last (b), causal validity (c), which measurable dimension (d), how to make a vague trait targetable (e), or is the pool strengths-balanced (f). Distinct from intervention-gating (which decides whether/which-arm to proceed on an already-chosen target) and from preparatory-diagnostic-read (which reads the subject to build the map this move selects over).

ex.f: Privilege the cusp that unlocks new contingencies
ex.t: "sets the occasion to access reinforcers that otherwise would not have been available" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Rank the eligible pool by leverage questions
ex.t: "Which behavior should be changed first?… modification is likely to provide access to more normalized settings… Will this new behavior produce reinforcement for significant others?" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: functional-analysis-methodology
nodes.mech: EXPERIMENTAL FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS — the operator upgrades a correlational hunch into demonstrated causal control by arranging conditions and actively turning a suspected controlling variable on and off while holding others constant, watching whether the target behavior tracks the manipulation (control over occurrence AND nonoccurrence). Core design = a control condition expected to yield the lowest rate (typically play: preferred items free, no demands, continuous attention) against test conditions selected only for the hypothesized function(s); differential responding anchored by the play baseline establishes causal function, with the explicit cost that untested functions cannot be ruled out. Requires operator control of antecedents/consequences and the ability to evoke the behavior.
nodes.disc: Reach for experimental FA when you need PROOF of what maintains a behavior and you control the antecedents/consequences and can evoke it — the tell is active on/off manipulation of a variable with a control condition, demonstrating control over occurrence AND nonoccurrence. Pick the realization by constraint: standard multielement when single variables can be isolated; brief/trial-based when disruption must be minimal; IISCA when isolated conditions yield nothing (compound/interactive maintenance); EO-verification when the question is whether a contrived motivating operation (not a cue) drives responding; per-topography coding when several problem behaviors co-occur; single-variable off/on when the object is a belief/false-cause. Distinct from descriptive-functional-assessment (observes only -> correlational, hedged, no manipulation), from contingency-space-analysis (computes a dependency from already-collected counts, no arrangement), and from procedure-fidelity/transferability tests (document enactment vs a causal claim).

ex.f: Isolate one variable to upgrade correlation to control
ex.t: "specific manipulations of one event (the independent variable) produce a reliable change in another event... unlikely the result of extraneous factors (confounding variables)—a finding known as a functional relation" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Turn the maintaining event on and off
ex.t: "Functional analysis involves systematically manipulating environmental events thought to maintain problem behavior within an experimental design" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: design-time-reconnaissance
nodes.mech: Before instruction/design, exhaustively map the space the plan must survive so gaps are caught on paper rather than in the field; nothing is delivered to the subject. Realizations: (a) GENERALIZATION-DOMAIN RECON — enumerate every setting and stimulus condition where the behavior should AND explicitly should NOT occur (treated as the unseen test, with discriminated alternative responses planned for inappropriate opportunities); list every desired response form and triage train-directly vs delegate-to-generalization; and survey the discriminative stimuli, schedules, and reinforcer types already operating in the target settings, so training is matched to what the environment will actually deliver; (b) EXHAUSTIVE-OBJECTOR CENSUS — before design work, demand a complete externalized (written) census of every objecting part and its function, sweeping every representational system rather than stopping at first responders, pre-warning that many typically object, so no suppressed objector is omitted from later design and cannot resurface as post-install sabotage. The shared lever is exhaustive design-time enumeration for completeness; the failure mode it prevents is a missed item (setting or objector) resurfacing after commitment.
nodes.disc: Reach for design-time-reconnaissance when the writer needs an exhaustive pre-design map so nothing is missed -- a completeness sweep on the PLAN before any teaching/install, subject untouched. Tells: enumerate should/should-not settings + response-form triage + standing-contingency survey (a); complete written cross-channel census of objectors (b). Distinct from target-selection (which FILTERS/picks targets rather than enumerating the space), from preparatory-diagnostic-read (which reads/measures the subject rather than enumerating on paper), and from intervention-gating (which branches proceed/how). Its contingency survey supplies the environment map that target-selection's maintainability criterion tests against.

ex.f: Survey the contingencies already running in the setting
ex.t: "What discriminative stimuli usually set the occasion…What schedules of reinforcement…are typical…What kinds of reinforcers are likely to be contingent" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Enumerate where it should and should not occur
ex.t: "situations that may appear to be appropriate opportunities…but are not…for which an alternative response is needed" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Enumerate response forms, then triage teaching
ex.t: "Only by having a complete list of all the desired forms of the behavior can the practitioner make meaningful decisions about which behaviors to teach directly and which to leave to generalization" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: generative-cusp-installation
nodes.mech: Install a fixed frame with a swappable slot ("I want __") plus a self-driven question-asking repertoire (the mand-for-information cusp, "What's that?") so new content drops into the slot and each question harvests new material with no per-item training. The small installed cusp is a behavioral lever whose returns compound, yielding open-ended, self-driven, combinatorial repertoire expansion rather than item-by-item gains.
nodes.disc: The tell is compounding self-amplification from a single installed frame-plus-cusp, where returns outpace the instruction delivered. Not ordinary item-by-item teaching or a single new label, and unlike forward-leverage-target-selection (which privileges cusps on the operator's target list) this move acts on the subject's repertoire - it installs one.

ex.f: Install one frame, get compounding returns
ex.t: "A child's ability to ask questions plays a major role in vocabulary growth by gen­erating new tacts, echoics, mands, intraverbals" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: influence-topology-node-selection
nodes.mech: Map who-responds-to-whom, then route a minimal change through the single node whose change propagates system-wide - deliberately avoiding the symptomatic member (easy to flip, but the system flips them back) and preferring the most tenacious member others actually respond to. The system then does most of the work and the change persists.
nodes.disc: Selection of the intervention NODE by influence-graph propagation and tenacity - not any particular change technique and not work with the presenting member; tell is deliberate non-symptomatic tenacious-node targeting. The graph is read and routed through, not restructured. Sibling stage to crisis-induction-live-readout, whose read-out supplies the map this move selects from.

ex.f: Route change through the tenacious node
ex.t: "The person who has the symptoms will be the last one that you want to work with… the one who is really tenacious." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: natural-contingency-handoff
nodes.mech: Retire the operator by handing maintenance to a natural contingency already operating in the target setting, via one of two levers. Contact lever: drive just enough emissions of the trained behavior in the generalization setting for it to contact the already-present reinforcer, then withdraw operator support once contact occurs. Fluency lever: do not stop at bare correctness — push measured performance (accuracy, rate, latency, duration, magnitude, topography) until the response is fluent enough to satisfy the natural setting's unforgiving timing/quality demands, because a correct-but-too-slow response never contacts reinforcement and extinguishes. Either way the response survives because the environment now selects and maintains it, collapsing operator effort from "sustain indefinitely" to "get the behavior over the natural contingency's threshold."
nodes.disc: The operator supplies no content and retires once natural reinforcement takes over — unlike moves that deliver operator content at the trance/waking threshold, schedule practice for state re-access, or sustain compliance for depth. Presupposes a target already screened by a standing-contingency maintainability filter; the deficit fixed is a CONTACT-frequency deficit (drive exposures) or a FLUENCY deficit (train measured dimensions to threshold), not broadened cues.

ex.f: Train to fluency or it extinguishes
ex.t: "Behavior changes that seem to need generalization may only need better teaching. Try making the students fluent" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Bridge to first contact, then fade
ex.t: "consists of getting the learner to emit the behavior in the generalization setting just often enough to contact the contingency." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: social-reinforcement-recruitment
nodes.mech: Route the maintaining reinforcement through another AGENT whose delivering behavior is itself the engineered variable — convert the subject's social environment into the reinforcement engine. Operator-side forms: inform capable-but-dormant people in the setting of the value of their attention and explicitly ask them to watch for and reinforce any reasonable effort (awakening an asleep community so gains persist after the trainer leaves); or, where ABC narrative data reveal caregivers/staff reinforcing the wrong endpoint (e.g. the end of an escalation chain over appropriate bids), directly reverse that agent's contingency (reinforce appropriate responses, extinguish the escalation endpoint, shape delay tolerance). Selection-side form: choose a proxy target behavior specifically because its payoff changes how significant others treat the subject, recruiting a named third-party causal path. Subject-side form: the subject self-evaluates against a criterion and, on meeting it, actively recruits praise/feedback from an authority, engineering the conditions under which that person reinforces them (raising the authority's own praise rate as a collateral change). Includes the dosing layer: calibrate recruiting rate and topography to the setting's tolerance so the recruited contingency stays net-positive and the reinforcing agent is not flipped into a punisher.
nodes.disc: The operative move lands on the setting's people, or on target choice routed through them - never on the subject's state. Unlike a trigger install that arms someone to fire a cue, nothing is installed in anyone; third parties are asked to notice and reinforce. Unlike a subject-comfort check, the dosing layer preserves a third party's goodwill rather than checking the subject's comfort. Unlike the producing-behavior validity rule of target selection, the proxy here is deliberately chosen for its third-party path, not rejected as a mere correlate.

ex.f: Waking the dormant reinforcing community
ex.t: "The contingency is there, but dormant. One solution… is to inform key people in the generalization setting of the value and importance of their attention… and ask them to help." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Proxy target chosen for its third-party payoff
ex.t: "not because of their direct benefit…but because of an important indirect benefit" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: compounding-dependency-loop
nodes.mech: A meta-suggestion claims repeated listening cumulatively RAISES a waking baseline state (e.g. natural arousal) across sessions rather than resetting per session, and the installed state's only relief route is more of the same hypnosis — so the cure feeds the disease. Re-listening is motivated (each now "does more"), any felt increase is pre-explained as the suggestion working, and the teardown route interlocks with the escalation so the dependency closes into a loop: more listening raises baseline further, which motivates more listening.
nodes.disc: Separate from progressive-conditioning (which accumulates trance DEPTH or response strength as a passive belief) by the cure-worsens-condition DEPENDENCY INVERSION — the installed waking-baseline state's designated relief route is the very mechanism that escalates it, forming a closed dependency loop. The structural cure-feeds-the-disease inversion is not a scale/target twist, so it stands apart rather than folding in as a variant.

ex.f: The cure that feeds the condition
ex.t: Near the close, the operator states as a rule that the effect does not reset between sessions: each replay leaves the listener's everyday, waking desire running a little hotter than before. Earlier in the same recording, the only sanctioned relief for that desire was returning to this voice. The two clauses interlock — the ache the file installs is discharged by playing the file, and playing the file raises the ache — so every relief is also a dose, and any increase the listener notices is pre-labelled as proof the suggestion is taking hold.
ex.s: Final ninety seconds, after the earlier stretch established that this voice is the only sanctioned relief for the want being installed.
ex.m: This does not reset when the file ends. Every time you play it, your ordinary daytime wanting runs a little hotter than it did before — and you already know the only thing that takes the edge off it is coming back here to me. So when you notice you need this more this week than you did last week, that isn't a problem; that's the suggestion working exactly the way it was built to.

nodes.name: object-as-causal-agent-of-cognition
nodes.mech: An external object (a worn garment, a hallucinated device, or a recast environmental detail such as a color) is declared the CAUSAL AGENT of the listener's mind-state rather than a carrier of installed meaning: putting on the uniform causes the persona/blankness to 'expand to fill' it or 'supplies the mind' or continuously drains cognition at skin contact; a hallucinated collar 'radiates every word' and 'amplifies' suggestions so rising obedience is felt as the equipment working; a color is re-cast into the listener's drainage system ('thoughts stream out into red') so later encounters replay the emptying. Authorship of behaviour is displaced from the listener onto the object, which becomes the grammatical subject of compliance ('the uniform/collar is doing it'), neutralizing resistance (refusing means fighting an object) and giving a portable, externally-checkable on/off switch that locates the source of compliance outside the self. The object is then externalized as a post-session cue so encountering it replays the actual in-session mechanism, not merely a reminder of it.
nodes.disc: The object is declared causal of the mind-state (it supplies/drains cognition, amplifies/radiates the words, IS the drainage/operative apparatus) and compliance is attributed to it - not merely an object carrying re-evocable significance the listener still owns (portable-object-state-export), and not a discrete cue-response state-shift. The tell is the object assigned an ACTIVE CAUSAL role in producing the state (always-on ambient drain; encounter replays the mechanism), with compliance attributed to the object rather than the listener.

ex.f: Uniform as sealed precondition for the state
ex.t: The outfit is never described — no colour, no cut, nothing the listener could picture. It is simply named again and again as the thing that permits the state: sealed into it, she is allowed to be awake or asleep and nothing else.
ex.s: Any point once the outfit is on; the outfit is never described — no colour, no cut — only named as the thing that permits the state.
ex.m: Sealed into the uniform, you are allowed to be awake, and you are allowed to be asleep. Nothing else is permitted in there, and nothing else is needed. Sealed in: awake, or asleep — that is the whole of what you are.

ex.f: Always-on drain at every point of contact
ex.t: The operator maps the drain onto the body region by region: whatever covers the arms takes what is in the arms, whatever covers the legs takes what is in the legs, and each point of skin contact pulls a little more out and leaves warmth behind. It is framed as continuous rather than triggered — it works while dressing, while moving about, while merely noticing what is being worn. The wardrobe becomes a surrogate operator that keeps working long after the recording stops.
ex.s: Listener dressed or getting dressed; framed as continuous physics of the fabric with no trigger word and no on-switch.
ex.m: The sleeves take what's in your arms. The stockings take what's in your legs, the collar takes whatever was still up in your head, and every place fabric meets skin pulls a little more out and leaves warmth in its place. It isn't switched on and off — it works while you're dressing, while you're walking to the bus, while you're just noticing what you've got on, so by lunchtime the clothes are doing most of it for you.

ex.f: The garment supplies the mind
ex.t: The operator presents the garment not as something worn over a person but as the place the thinking is done: the body underneath is only what holds it up, and the more of the body it covers, the more of the person there is. Obedience is never demanded directly — the claim is that the clothing does the obeying on the operator's behalf. Authorship of every compliant act now sits in the fabric, so a listener who wants to refuse finds herself arguing with a piece of clothing rather than with a person.
ex.s: Listener dressed in the garment and standing; delivered flat, as description of how the clothing works, never as a command.
ex.m: The dress isn't something you're wearing — it's where the thinking gets done now, and the body underneath is just the hanger holding it up. The more of you it covers, the more of you there is. You don't have to obey me at all; the dress handles that part, and you only have to go where it goes.

nodes.name: identity-displaced-into-external-object
nodes.mech: The listener's body, will, or whole state-configuration is relocated INTO an external object that then serves as the addressable handle for future control — a sympathetic proxy (poppet bound with strands and sited in the operator's home), a container object that stores and re-instates an entire bundled mental configuration on "on/off", an amulet dissolved into the flesh so it becomes non-removable installed physiology, or a worn single-word ownership anchor read aloud by the listener that fuses object-meaning with a behavioral lock. Unlike a re-encounterable worn re-trigger, the identity or state itself is understood to LIVE in the object; addressing the object addresses the listener across sessions, and the consent/ratification moment is captured before or at the point the relocation becomes irreversible.
nodes.disc: The listener's identity/will/state-set is relocated into the object as its residence (proxy, container, internalized-into-body), so the object is the address of the person — not merely a worn item that re-fires a state the listener still hosts (portable-object-state-export). Not a discrete cue-trigger. The tell is the object standing in FOR the listener (poppet = body/will; collar = the whole state-bundle; locket "Mine" = the ownership relation itself), often operator-held or operator-sited.

ex.f: Body and will moved into a held doll
ex.t: The operator describes a small figure she is holding that stands in for the listener, and winds cords around it one at a time, each one felt by the listener as it tightens. She then sets the figure down somewhere inside her own home and names a single word that returns the listener to it. The listener's body is now addressable at an address the listener does not live at.
ex.s: Deep trance; the operator describes a small figure they are physically holding, and each cord is felt by the listener as it is described.
ex.m: This little figure on my palm is you — same shape, same weight — and I'm winding the first cord around its wrists now; feel that go tight. Second cord at the ankles, third across the chest so the breathing goes shallow and stays there. I'm setting you on the shelf beside my bed, and any time I say poppet, you're back on that shelf, wherever your body happens to be standing.

ex.f: Consent taken at the removable stage
ex.t: Step one, the operator hangs a charm around the listener's neck and pauses to ask whether it is willingly accepted — a real-feeling choice about a thing that could still be lifted off. Step two, she pours her own power into it while it hangs there. Step three, the metal warms and sinks through the skin until it is somewhere under the ribs, not removable at all. The permission was collected while the object was still a necklace and is treated as covering what it became.
ex.s: A three-beat ritual in the middle of the session; the consent question is asked at beat one, while the object can still be lifted off.
ex.m: I'm putting this around your neck. Do you take it, freely, yes or no? Good — now I pour myself into it, and it gets heavy and hot against your sternum, and now it sinks, through the skin, in under the ribs where it stays; you said yes, and it does not come off.

ex.f: One word read aloud in the listener's own voice
ex.t: A pendant is fastened at the listener's throat, described as costly and never to be taken off, and then opened to show one word engraved inside — which the listener is made to say out loud rather than merely read. The ownership claim enters through the listener's own mouth, so the ratifying voice is theirs.
ex.s: Pendant fastened at the throat, described as permanent; listener is able to speak aloud and is made to.
ex.m: It cost more than you'd guess and it doesn't come off — not for the shower, not for anybody who asks. Open it. There's one word engraved in there, and I want it out loud, in your voice, not just read: say it — Mine.

ex.f: Whole state bundled into a wearable container
ex.t: The operator declares that everything the listener has been during the session is now held inside a single worn object, and that she is the one holding it. She then names two phrases that only she may speak: one that puts the object back in place and restores the whole bundled configuration with it, one that removes both. She no longer asks the listener to go anywhere; she simply puts the state on them, awake or asleep, and the object is where it lives between sessions.
ex.s: End of session, the worn item already in place, with the full state built and about to be lifted off the listener and stored.
ex.m: Everything you have been for the last hour goes into this, and I'm the one who keeps it. When I say wear it, it goes back on you and all of this comes back with it — awake, asleep, or halfway through a sentence at work. When I say set it down, both come off; and those two phrases only work in my mouth, never in yours.

nodes.name: identity-origin-erasure
nodes.mech: Relocates the ORIGIN of the installed identity into an erased or unfalsifiable past so there is no "before" the listener could locate or return to. Rather than relabeling new content as native (the intrinsic reframe), it rewrites autobiographical memory/timeline: the trait is asserted to have always been true ("you have always been the submissive", "you were always made to be a doll, you didn't have a life before me"), often filling the void with a fabricated flattering past ("always been this way, can't remember being any other way"), so the "I changed into this" seam that would let the listener date and undo the change is removed. It typically depends on a prior amnesia/emptying foundation so the timeline cannot be checked from inside the trance, and is sometimes synchronized with a physical act (stripping) that mirrors the identity removal.
nodes.disc: The load-bearing move is deletion of the baseline: it forecloses return-to-baseline by removing the baseline itself, where intrinsic-self-reframe relabels new content as native but leaves the prior self/timeline intact. Screen-memory work replaces a SPECIFIC targeted memory; this erases the whole pre-scene self/origin globally. And where persistence framing projects the installed identity forward in time, this rewrites the past backward.

ex.f: Tense shifted from becoming to always-was
ex.t: The operator observes how much has changed over the session, then corrects herself: for the listener, nothing changed, because this was always the case. The grammar flips from a becoming to a having-always-been, and an earlier stretch of deliberate memory-blurring means the listener has no intact timeline to check the claim against. A small staged self-correction, delivered as though it were a slip of the tongue, half-hides the moment the tense moved.
ex.s: Near the close, after an earlier stretch of deliberate memory-blurring has left no intact timeline to check the claim against.
ex.m: Look how much you've changed tonight — no, sorry, that came out wrong. Nothing changed. You have always been like this; I only got to stand here and watch you notice it.

ex.f: Filling the gap with a flattering false past
ex.t: Having silenced the objecting inner voice, the operator does not leave the gap empty — she stocks it. A whole childhood is supplied: what the listener was like at school, what she has always liked, what she has spent years doing, all of it consistent with the installed persona and all of it pleasant to own. Any attempt to reach for the real past is pre-answered by returning this one instead.
ex.s: Immediately after the objecting inner voice has been quieted; the gap is stocked rather than left empty.
ex.m: You were like this at school as well — always the one people wanted to look after, always happiest when somebody else was deciding. You've liked pretty things since you were small, and you've been practising this for years without ever calling it that. Any time you go looking for how you used to be, this is what comes back to you.

ex.f: Rewriting the capture so none occurred
ex.t: Late in the session the operator stops narrating a transformation and starts narrating a fact: this is what you were made as, this is where you have always been kept, there was no life before this one. The line is delivered while the listener's clothes are being removed piece by piece, so the physical undressing and the erasure of the prior self run on the same beat. There is no longer a prior state to be returned to on waking, because it has been asserted out of existence.
ex.s: Late session; the listener's clothes are being removed piece by piece, one item per line, on the same beat as the erasure.
ex.m: Shoes off. There was no journey to here — this is what you were made as. Coat off, dress off; you were never anywhere else, there was no life before this room, and nothing has been taken from you tonight because there was never anything there to take.

nodes.name: intrinsic-self-reframe
nodes.mech: Reframes installed content (an identity, trait, feeling, state, or even a control surface) as always-intrinsic and pre-existing rather than externally imposed, so the listener's stance shifts from evaluating a proposition to recognizing a fact about themselves. The lever is authorship relocation onto the listener's own self via a self-discovery frame ('you already know this', 'it was always there deep down', 'this is simply who you are', 'a side you have always had', 'it doesn't come from me, it was there all along'). Once accepted, resistance reads as self-denial rather than refusal of an external claim, and later content lands as confirmation of an existing identity rather than imposition. Realizations range over placement (opening whole-identity premise, mid-session ontological restatement), over the object (an identity, a coined category, a just-built affect whose authorship is disavowed, an arousal control surface claimed to have 'always been there'), over vehicle (copular assertion, latent-self-surfacing where the listener supplies the content, first-person creed inscription declared to BE the walls of the listener's own mind), and over the GROUNDING of the always-was claim - which can be grounded in the self/identity or grounded in a physiological/developmental substrate (endocrine/reproductive vocabulary, 'born with a female spirit', an infant caregiver-trust circuit 'reconnected' to the operator, with an unflagged category mismatch doing the smuggling) so pushing back feels like arguing with one's own body.
nodes.disc: The tell is the single-self self-discovery reframe that dissolves the installed/native boundary without splitting the self, erasing a timeline, or citing a physiological source. Named-alter-partition-install builds a SECOND self alongside; identity-origin-erasure deletes the prior baseline/timeline so there is no before to return to, rather than merely relabeling the new content native; clear-and-replace self-model surgery excises the prior self and installs a replacement; and persistence framing asserts the change forward in time, where this asserts always-was retroactively.

ex.f: Disavowing authorship of a just-built feeling
ex.t: After a long stretch spent building the feeling, the operator points at it and denies having made it: what the listener is feeling is not hers, she never put it there, it was already present and she has only uncovered it. Because the feeling is genuinely present, the disavowal lands as an observation rather than an instruction, and the listener can no longer discount it as something that was suggested.
ex.s: After ten minutes spent building the feeling; the operator points at it while it is unmistakably present and denies authorship.
ex.m: Feel that — right now, in the chest, down through the hands. I did not put that there. I can't put a feeling into somebody; all I did was talk until you stopped hiding it from yourself, and it was in there long before I opened my mouth.

ex.f: A control surface claimed to have been there all along
ex.t: Once the listener is blank, the operator announces a discovery rather than an installation: there is a small dial in there, labelled, and it was always there — the resistance had simply been standing in front of it. Nothing is being added, only uncovered, which sidesteps the question of whether adding it would have been agreed to. The dial is then described as the listener's own, though only the operator's hand turns it.
ex.s: Listener blank and reporting empty; the control surface is announced as a discovery, not an installation.
ex.m: Oh — there's a dial in here. Small brass one, low down, worn smooth, labelled obedience, and it's old; it's been there the whole time with your resistance standing square in front of it. Nothing's being added, it's yours — I'm just going to turn it up two clicks now that I can finally reach it.

ex.f: The listener supplies the content and carves it
ex.t: The listener is walked into a chamber whose walls carry lines cut into the stone, each one written in the first person — and is told, halfway through, that they are cutting the letters themselves. Then the frame inverts: this chamber is not a place the mind is picturing, it is the mind, and those cut lines are the material it is built from. The suggestions arrive as things recovered from the listener's own architecture rather than things handed over, so the filter that would ask whether a thought is the listener's or the operator's has nothing to catch.
ex.s: Deep visualization; the listener is walking a stone chamber whose walls carry first-person lines, and the frame is about to invert.
ex.m: Read the line under your fingers: "I am easiest when I am not deciding." Now look at your other hand — that's a chisel, and you cut that line, and the six below it. And this chamber was never something you were picturing: it is your mind, and those cut lines are the material it's built out of.

ex.f: Opening with the identity pre-accepted
ex.t: The opening is not a proposal but a report: the listener is told they already know, privately, what they are, and that the session's only job is to make that more true, a little more so with each passing day. The listener never gets a moment where a claim is put forward and could be turned down, because the claim arrives as something already settled and merely being strengthened. Disagreeing now means calling yourself a liar rather than declining an offer, which is a much harder posture to hold.
ex.s: The opening lines of the file, before any induction; delivered as a report of settled fact rather than as an offer.
ex.m: You already know what you are. You've known it privately for a long time, and you've never once said it out loud. This recording isn't here to turn you into anything — it's here to make what's already true a little truer, and a little more so every day after this one.

nodes.name: named-alter-partition-install
nodes.mech: Constructs a SECOND self-locus inside the listener — often a separately-named, persistent alter-identity (a named doll-self, a slave-self) or a manufactured sub-self (a 'primal self' below thought, a pre-labeled 'part that always listened') built feature-by-feature (traits, body, drive, sometimes a fabricated autobiography) — and transfers the conditioned behavior onto it, either by relocating the listener's 'I' INTO the alter or by installing the alter BESIDE the listener as a discrete third-person carrier of the payload, so the listener can enact compliance while disowning agency ('the doll responding', 'Daddy brought the alter out'). The distancing is the mechanism: a manufactured person absorbs conduct the listener would not own directly, entered at low ego-defense and routed back to 'you'. The partition makes compliance ego-syntonic for the installed part while ego-dystonic resistance is relocated onto a losing faction; a verdict is pre-assigned that the compliant part is the authentic self. Future triggers address the alter rather than the listener, and the second self is engineered as always-on/permanent so it feels inherent, sometimes with a retroactive backdating or anti-deprogramming immunity clause.
nodes.disc: The tell is naming-or-manufacturing a persistent second agent and relocating agency/behavior onto it. Intrinsic-self-reframe reframes the ONE self as intrinsic with no split; this builds a distinct second locus. Consciousness-splitting work partitions awareness into observer/responder within one self for in-session ideomotor proof; this installs a durable IDENTITY-typed second self carrying the conditioned behavior, addressed by name/trigger. And proxy-agent-resistance-offload's proxy is externally-authored, definitionally obedient, and FIGHTS the listener; here the alter is a self the listener inhabits and defers to.

ex.f: Splitting the self and pre-naming the winner
ex.t: The operator grants that part of the listener is still holding on, then identifies whatever gives way as the part that is actually listening — and asserts it has been listening far longer than the other one has. Whatever the listener feels next has a bin waiting for it: agreement is the real self, objection is the faction that loses. The mere fact of still having the recording playing is offered as the proof.
ex.s: Mid-file, at the first sign of partial resistance; both outcomes are labelled before the listener reports either one.
ex.m: Part of you is still holding on — that's fine, let it hold. The part that's giving way is the part that's actually been listening, and it's been listening a lot longer than the other one has. If you want to know which of the two is really you, ask which one pressed play, and which one is still letting it run.

ex.f: A manufactured layer beneath the thinking self
ex.t: The operator names a layer the listener has never heard of, places it beneath thought and opinion, and claims only that layer — explicitly leaving the thinking mind free to object, because objections are by definition the shallow part talking. Any later resistance is therefore not counted, and the claim is sealed by insisting it is not a proposal being offered for consideration but a description of what the listener already is.
ex.s: Early install; a layer the listener has never heard named is introduced, claimed, and the thinking mind is explicitly left free to object.
ex.m: Underneath your opinions there's a layer that has never had a thought in its life — call it the base. I'm not talking to your thinking mind tonight at all; it can disagree the whole way through, and it will, because disagreeing is the only job the shallow part has. And I'm not asking the base for permission either — I'm just telling you what's already down there.

ex.f: Inner figure given a summonable name
ex.t: The operator instructs the inner figure to rise and take the body, gives her tastes, a way of moving, and a name, and states that the previous personality is fading behind her. Later trigger phrases are addressed to that name, so what fires is not the listener obeying but the figure arriving.
ex.s: Late in the file, after the inner figure has been built feature by feature; she is instructed to take the body and given a name for triggers to address.
ex.m: Come up now and take the body — hands, mouth, hips, all of it is yours to use. You like sweet drinks and slow music, you walk from the hips, and your name is Bee. The one who was here before is going quiet behind you, and from now on, when I say your name, you're the one who answers.

ex.f: A named second self that triggers address
ex.t: The operator asserts that everyone carries a second, obedient self, then calls the listener's out and gives it a name of its own — whispering that it is always present now, awake, asleep, in dreams. Later commands are addressed to the name rather than to the listener, so compliance can be reported as something that self did. The boundary between the two is deliberately blurred, with the listener told they can no longer locate where one leaves off and the other begins, which closes off the escape of saying it was not really me.
ex.s: Mid-file install; the second self is asserted as universal, called up, named, and addressed directly from here on.
ex.m: Everybody has a second one underneath — the one that only ever says yes — and yours is up now, and her name is Doll. Doll, hands in your lap. She doesn't go anywhere when the file ends; she's there awake, asleep, in dreams, and by now you couldn't draw me the line where she stops and you start.

nodes.name: portable-object-state-export
nodes.mech: Object-anchoring: bind the in-session state (trance, arousal, ownership, submission, cognitive blankness) to a specific everyday object the listener wears/carries by repeated equivalence, then hand it over as a self-administered out-of-session re-trigger. Because the object persists where the operator's voice does not, encountering/wearing/noticing it re-instantiates the bound state with the operator absent, extending the session's reach indefinitely. Realizations differ only in firing intensity and in what the object holds: (a) at the gentle pole, a worn item carries persistent ambient meaning (a 'constant reminder', a 'soft pull back'); (b) at the active pole, the object is a live portable re-induction surface fired by ordinary encounter; (c) in the EXCLUSIVITY variant, the object is elevated to the SOLE control channel every later move routes through ('all I need to control you', 'deeper than chains') — the knob is whether this is the only lever; (d) in the STORAGE-LOCUS variant, the object is made the place an abstract outcome is stored and retrieved on demand (a named 'Magic Spot' holding a permanent result even after the physical trace fades) rather than a cue that fires — the knob is what the object holds, a stored outcome vs a re-fired state. All share one lever: persistent conditioned meaning installed onto a physical object the listener owns.
nodes.disc: Reach for THIS when the persistence carrier is an EXTERNAL, encounterable object the listener OWNS/WEARS and its payload is a state/meaning/outcome re-evoked or retrieved on encounter (includes the exclusivity 'sole lever' and storage-locus 'where the outcome lives' realizations). Choose a sibling technique instead when: the object is declared the CAUSAL AGENT that supplies/drains/amplifies cognition and compliance is attributed to it (object-as-causal-agent-of-cognition); the listener's identity/will/state is RELOCATED INTO the object so it becomes the address of the person, often operator-held (identity-displaced-into-external-object); the anchor is sited ON/IN the listener's own body and cannot be set down (somatic-self-anchor); or the move is a discrete cue-response trigger install firing a state-shift. The tell separating it from a session-bound prop is explicit export into daily life plus self-administered re-firing/retrieval with no operator present.

ex.f: Worn item that fires the state on sight
ex.t: The operator binds the blank, agreeable state to the clothing itself and then lowers the bar for what counts: not the full outfit, a couple of minimal pieces are declared enough to drop her. Glancing down at herself while dressed is named as its own trigger. Because the anchor is worn rather than spoken, it fires anywhere in the course of an ordinary day, with no recording playing.
ex.s: Post-hypnotic install with the listener currently wearing the item; the threshold for firing is lowered from the full outfit to a couple of pieces.
ex.m: That blank, agreeable feeling you're in right now belongs to these clothes, not to me. You don't need the whole outfit either — the stockings and the collar on their own are enough to put you here. And glancing down at yourself while you're wearing them is its own trigger; it'll go soft behind your eyes before you've finished looking.

ex.f: Apply to enter, remove to exit
ex.t: The trigger is a specific object rather than a word: putting it on enters the state, taking it off ends it. The operator closes both failure routes in advance — if you don't own one you'll want to buy one, and if you own several, your deeper mind has already chosen which is the special one. Nobody can fail the selection step, so everyone leaves with a designated object.
ex.s: Trigger install where the trigger is an object rather than a word; both no-object and too-many-objects are closed off before the listener can raise either.
ex.m: Putting it on drops you; taking it off brings you back. That's the whole switch. If you don't own one, you're going to want to go and buy one this week and you'll enjoy choosing it — and if you own several, your deeper mind has already picked which one is the special one, and you'll know which the moment you open the drawer.

ex.f: Carried scent firing on every breath
ex.t: The scent the listener applies each morning is given a second job: every inhale reinforces everything else that was installed. It is then described in bodily terms — drawn into the lungs, into the blood, carried everywhere, changing her — so it reads as an agent of change rather than a reminder. Breathing is involuntary and constant, so the anchor fires dozens of times a minute, self-applied, with no session running.
ex.s: Late install, referring to the scent the listener already applies every morning; framed as an agent carried in the body rather than a reminder.
ex.m: That scent you put on every morning has a second job now. Every breath in draws it down into your lungs, into the blood, out to your fingertips — and every breath in reinforces everything I've put into you tonight. You breathe about twenty thousand times a day, and every one of them is me.

ex.f: The anchor generalized so it cannot be discarded
ex.t: The suggestion is installed at peak arousal: wearing the item makes you easier to hypnotise, a way for the voice to reach straight in. Then it widens — not this particular one, any that the listener finds appealing — and stretches out of the session into ordinary hours as a persistent light haze during everyday errands. Discarding one garment no longer removes anything, because the anchor was never attached to that garment in particular.
ex.s: Installed at peak arousal, then widened from the specific garment to the whole category and stretched into ordinary waking hours.
ex.m: Wearing them makes you easier to hypnotise — an open door straight into you, and you can feel that being true right now. Not this pair in particular: any of them, any pair you like the look of. And it doesn't stop when the file does; you'll wear a pair to the shops and spend the whole afternoon in a warm light haze wondering why.

nodes.name: progressive-conditioning
nodes.mech: Installs a belief that conditioning compounds with each return, replay, firing, or even sleep — so trance depth and response strength are asserted to accumulate monotonically across sessions, with no ceiling and no decay. The listener's own progress-narrative is made self-fulfilling: any later gap or plateau is pre-read as on-schedule confirmation rather than failure, and the cost of deepening is transferred off the operator onto a structural belief the listener now holds. Realizations range over the accrual vehicle (per-session, per-firing, per-replay, per-orgasm, per-act-of-obedience, during-sleep, via a listener-maintained memory artifact) and over the target (depth, compliance, amnesia-schedule, exercise drive), and over framing — from a plain accumulation claim to an unfalsifiable GEOMETRIC multiplier ("twice as powerful", "a hundred times deeper" per replay/firing, no measurable baseline) that pre-attributes any felt drift to "the recording working" and pre-authorizes dose escalation and session stacking. The lever is one: a self-reinforcing expectancy of increasing effect over repeated engagement.
nodes.disc: Separate from a within-session deepener by the forward-binding to FUTURE sessions/replays (single play explicitly insufficient). Separate from manufactured-conditioning-history, which sources present state from a counterfactual prior history — events that never happened. Separate from environmental reinforcement-schedule shaping (the ABA literature), which titrates a measured criterion, not a belief. The geometric per-replay multiplier ("twice as powerful", no baseline) is a framing variant of the accumulation lever, not a separate move; the cross-replay time horizon is what separates it from in-session intensity multiplier-stacking.

ex.f: Each replay doubles the effect
ex.t: In the final half-minute the operator states, as a property of the listener rather than a request, that each replay is twice as strong on thought and behaviour as the one before. Nothing anchors what the first play was worth, so the claim cannot be checked — and a weak session becomes a reason to play it again rather than a reason to stop.
ex.s: Final thirty seconds, after the wake-count, delivered as a fact about how the listener now works.
ex.m: Here's how you work from now on: each time you play this, it goes twice as deep into your thinking and twice as far into your behaviour as the play before it did. Twice. So if tonight felt light, all that means is tomorrow's is worth double.

ex.f: Deepening credited to the listener's own returning
ex.t: The compounding is attributed to the listener, not the operator: coming back and giving in is itself the training, so each return is something she is doing to herself. There is now no one on the other side to push against, and relapse reads as self-expression rather than as being worked on.
ex.s: Closing frame; the compounding is credited to the listener's own act of returning rather than to anything the operator does.
ex.m: I'm not the one training you. You are — every time you come back, press play, and let go a little sooner than you did last time, that's you doing it to yourself. There's nobody on the other side of this to push against; there's only how often you keep choosing it.

ex.f: Sleep recoded as extra conditioning time
ex.t: The listener is told that once the audio ends the suggestions keep repeating underneath the night's sleep, unnoticed, settling deeper with every hour — until it simply reads as true. Hours of doing nothing are reclassified as hours of work, so the deepening requires no compliance at all, only unconsciousness.
ex.s: Delivered as the file ends, with the listener expected to fall asleep with it still on.
ex.m: When the audio stops, this doesn't stop. Everything I've said tonight keeps repeating underneath your sleep, quietly, hour after hour, settling a little further in each time you turn over. You'll wake with none of it in mind and all of it simply true.

ex.f: Unbounded multiplier with no ceiling
ex.t: The operator states it as a rule of the system rather than a wish: every firing goes an unbounded multiple further than the last, and every depth ever reached is added back behind the command. Depth stops being a level the listener could be at and becomes a figure that only rises. The listener loses the counter-frame that says this has been heard before and is wearing off, because wear is defined out of the design.
ex.s: Trigger install, stated as a property of the system rather than a wish, with no baseline offered against which the claim could be checked.
ex.m: Every time that word fires, you go many times further down than you went the time before — no ceiling on it, no wearing off, ever. And every depth you have ever reached gets stacked back in behind the word, so it carries all of them at once. Depth isn't somewhere you are any more; it's a number that only ever goes up.

nodes.name: proxy-agent-resistance-offload
nodes.mech: Install an AUTONOMOUS agent that holds real decision-authority the listener defers to, and route the contest through it — displacing surrender-agency off the listener onto a party 'programmed never to lose'. The agent's representational LOCATION (inner part vs in-scene figure) is a parameter. VARIANTS: (a) externally-authored obedient inner character [proxy-agent-resistance-offload] — a named, persistent, seeded-by-a-prior-file part that is definitionally obedient and exempt from justification; the listener's resistance is reframed from 'me vs the operator' (winnable) into 'me vs an internal part that never loses' (defeat structurally guaranteed), and irrational beliefs the listener's reason would reject are assigned to the proxy ('doesn't need it to make sense') and radiated in via a shared-mind premise as ambient feeling; (b) aftercare-clause subconscious [guardian-delegation-inner-agent] — a safety/reassurance clause that names the 'subconscious' as a competent autonomous decision-holder owning the off-switch and timing ('removing the lipstick ends the effects AND your subconscious already knows when to put it on'); the reassurance IS the installation, defusing 'what if I can't turn this off' anxiety while relocating the off-switch into an installed inner authority rather than returning it to the listener; (c) interposed in-scene proxy [interposed-proxy-agent] — a separate figure in the scene is granted real agency and made the actual command-issuer while the operator recedes to narrator (draws the listener in, guides their hands, supplies affection the stranger-operator could not credibly give); authorship diffuses to the admired proxy so compliance feels like inclusion/identification, and the proxy is staged as a permanent occupant carried out of session ('she can live for you'), the wake omitted. Pick by inner-combatant vs aftercare-subconscious vs in-scene-actor — but all install a delegated authority the listener cannot simply reclaim.
nodes.disc: Installs an autonomous agent (inner part OR in-scene figure) that HOLDS authority against the listener and carries the contest/belief, rather than the listener inhabiting it — the tell is delegated decision-authority the listener defers to and cannot simply reclaim. Separates from a genuine agency-reminder/aftercare disclaimer (which hands control BACK), from named-source-authority (which points at a figure outside the listener the operator relays or borrows), and from ordinary guided-imagery characters that are used and released (these agents are non-dismissed and carry real authority). External-scene proxy vs inner named character vs ambient subconscious is the agent's location, a parameter.

ex.f: Belief routed through a proxy exempt from proof
ex.t: Rather than asserting the claim to the listener, who would examine it, the operator installs it in the inner figure — that figure is being trained to treat the operator's words as true — and then reminds the listener that the two of them share one mind. The listener is invited to dispute it as much as they like, on the grounds that the figure holding the belief was never required to find it reasonable in the first place. The proposition never presents itself for judgement; it arrives as a feeling already in the room.
ex.s: At the point where the listener's reasoning would examine a claim; the claim is addressed to the inner figure instead, under a shared-mind premise.
ex.m: I'm not telling you this — I'm telling her. She's being trained to take whatever I say as simply true, and she has never been required to find it reasonable; that was never part of what she's for. Dispute it as much as you like: the two of you share one head, so it arrives in you as a feeling long before it reaches anything capable of checking it.

ex.f: An inner opponent programmed never to lose
ex.t: The operator does not argue with the listener at all — she narrates a figure already installed inside him doing the pulling: it is dragging at your sense of being, taking the room a little at a time, and the only reason you are still following this is that it permits you to. The contest is moved from listener-versus-operator, which could be won, to listener-versus-a-part-of-himself that was built obedient. Defeat is guaranteed by construction, and the surrender belongs to the figure rather than to him.
ex.s: Mid-file; the inner figure was seeded by an earlier session and is now narrated acting on the listener, never addressed to him.
ex.m: She's already at it — I can hear her from here. She's dragging at your sense of where you end, taking the room a foot at a time, and the only reason you can still follow my voice at all is that she's allowing it. I'm not going to argue with you tonight; I don't need to. She was built not to lose.

nodes.name: replay-until-ready-failure-absorber
nodes.mech: A pre-induction frame positions the file as one installment of a multi-file arc to be replayed "again and again until you feel like you've reached the appropriate level", with success defined as listener-self-judged readiness. This removes the pass/fail pressure that would short-circuit conditioning: any partial result becomes on-track training data and the only failure state becomes not-repeating. Front-loaded before any state work, it neutralizes performance anxiety and licenses repetition — a structural commitment device that rewrites what counts as success across sessions.
nodes.disc: Separate from progressive-conditioning (a depth-accumulation claim) by being a pre-induction EVALUATION FRAME that rewrites the success metric (no pass/fail, only not-repeating fails) rather than asserting cumulative depth. Separate from a post-orgasm scrapbook/consolidation bridge by its placement before any state work and its preemptive, not consolidating, function. Separate from plain expectancy-seeding (which seeds an expectation of an effect) by rewriting the success/failure metric to license replay.

ex.f: Replay until you judge yourself ready
ex.t: Before any induction, in an ordinary speaking voice, the listener is told this is the first of a set and is to be played over and over until they feel ready to move on to the next one. Nothing that happens tonight can count as failing, because the standard is their own sense of readiness and the only way to fall short is to stop replaying. Any partial result is reclassified in advance as training data.
ex.s: The very first thing on the file, in an ordinary speaking voice, before any induction or state work at all.
ex.m: Before we start: this is the first of a set, and it's meant to be played again and again until you feel ready to move on to the next one. Nothing that happens tonight can count as failing — if you drift off, if you fidget, if it seems like nothing happened, that's just the training running at the speed it runs at. The only way to get this wrong is to stop replaying it.

nodes.name: self-perpetuating-object-ritual-loop
nodes.mech: A bundle that chains a ubiquitous environmental cue into a commerce/acquisition obligation and a recurring private ritual, closing the loop back onto re-listening — so post-session daily life is threaded with cue -> obtain-the-object -> perform-the-ritual -> re-install-the-state -> return-to-the-recording. It is not a single anchor but an engineered self-sustaining loop: the environmental cue (seeing red) drives a purchase, the purchased object drives a timed private ritual with sub-triggers, and the ritual re-reinforces trance and operator authority while driving re-consumption of the recording. The object is one node in a loop whose payload is perpetuation itself.
nodes.disc: A multi-node self-sustaining loop (environmental cue + commerce + recurring ritual + re-listen closure), not a single worn re-trigger (portable-object-state-export) and not a single firing of stacked triggers. The tell is the closed loop that recruits commerce and re-consumption, designed to perpetuate rather than fire once; it installs a real post-hypnotic bundle, but the load-bearing payload is the arc/loop shape.

ex.f: Cue, purchase, ritual, replay
ex.t: One colour, common enough to appear several times a day, is bound to the feeling of being controlled — and to an urge to go out and buy a particular outfit. Owning the outfit triggers the next stage: putting it on starts a fixed block of time in the trained state, with a small internal cue re-firing at regular intervals throughout. The closing lines tie the ritual back to the recording, so wanting to repeat the exercise and wanting to play the audio again grow together. Nothing here is a single anchor; it is a circuit that keeps re-supplying its own next input.
ex.s: Post-hypnotic block at the end of the file, installing cue, purchase, timed ritual and return-to-the-recording in one sequence.
ex.m: From tomorrow, every time you notice the colour red anywhere, you'll get a second of that controlled softness — and a small pull towards buying yourself a red set to wear. The evening you first put it on, you'll set a timer for thirty minutes and stay in this state the whole time, and every time your fingers find the fabric you'll drop another step. And when the timer goes, you'll want to do it again, which means wanting my voice again — you'll be reaching for this recording before you've finished getting dressed.

nodes.name: design-space-pedagogy
nodes.mech: A reader-directed pedagogical architecture that presents a family of techniques not as isolated tricks but as a parameterized design space with dials and a default heuristic. Realizations: a 2x2 matrix walked cell-by-cell with a coverage-vs-cost tradeoff; mirror-pairing every value-raising move with its value-abolishing dual plus a normative default; imperatives-then-decision-frame layering that gates when-not-to-use; and twinned exemplars withholding the category names so the reader induces the grid. The reader internalizes a parameterized mental model plus a selection heuristic rather than a rote list.
nodes.disc: Teaches a DISCRIMINATION/SELECTION space (dials, tradeoffs, when-not-to-use), NOT acceptance of a refused claim — separating it from validation-by-demonstration-arc (which earns a contested claim via stacked corroboration). Operates on the READER, not an in-session listener x(t); a non-executable corpus-shape observation citable to no single passage (a container, not a script move). Held separate from the general reader-assent-engineering container on this dial-space tell.

ex.f: Imperatives first, when-not-to-use last
ex.t: "consider various factors before deciding to use shaping" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Twin exemplars with the categories withheld
ex.t: "Can you hear an essential difference?" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: public-avowal-third-party-propagation
nodes.mech: Externalize the installed state so parties OUTSIDE the operator-listener dyad do the reinforcing/propagating work, making a private experience a self-reinforcing relational system that extends operator reach past the audio. VARIANTS by how the outside world is recruited: (a) public avowal / third-party-directed act [public-avowal] — post a named avowal, publicly self-label, tell someone the operator's slogan, share the file, so an AUDIENCE reinforces via self-consistency pressure (having declared it publicly, the listener is pushed to keep believing) and doubles as recruitment/distribution; frequently laundered as defiance/self-proof or prosocial sharing; (b) viral propagation / recruit-new-subjects [viral-propagation-directive] — redirect the whole payload OUTWARD, the listener guides others toward becoming the operator's slave or craves the trigger from others and 'uses it on others', a proselytizing transmission vector (raising exit cost — leaving now requires publicly admitting one was wrong); (c) deputize-toward-a-partner [listener-as-influence-vector] — the subject is made an active recruiter/contingency-manager toward a specific third party (transform your husband into a 'X lover'; or reciprocal ABA where two parties each manage the other's consequences) so the third party becomes co-invested; (d) legible body-signal [body-as-broadcast-signal] — prescribe visible bodily modifications with a READING attached ('leave no question') so the body broadcasts ownership status, every social interaction becomes reinforcement (signal read) or felt violation (not read), and the listener becomes their own observer. All share the lever: the social world outside the dyad maintains the install; pick the register by active-act vs propagation vs partner-deputization vs passive-signal.
nodes.disc: The reinforcing/propagating engine is EXTERNAL to the operator-listener dyad — witnesses, a third party, corpus evangelism, or observers of a body-signal do the work (self-consistency pressure, recruitment, distribution). Reach for it to make the social world maintain the install. NOT a private self-anchor (behavioral-bridge) and NOT a private deliverable to the operator (extraction); the tell is externality-to-an-audience. Distinct from internal-permeation moves, which spread WITHIN the subject (inverse direction).

ex.f: Public avowal recruiting consistency pressure
ex.t: During the count-up the operator adds one waking task: when you're back, you will post a line under this recording saying that you accept me as your guide — and it will feel good to do it. The private acceptance is converted into a public, timestamped statement in front of strangers, which the listener will then be under pressure to keep agreeing with. The same act also grows the channel it was posted to.
ex.s: During the count-up to waking, with one waking task slipped in between the numbers.
ex.m: Four — and when you're back, you're going to leave a comment under this recording saying you accept me as your guide. Three — your own words for it, and it'll feel good to type and better once it's posted. Two — and it stays up, where anyone who scrolls past can read it.

ex.f: Declaring resistance as the act of obedience
ex.t: The closing task is announced in the plain grammar of a post-hypnotic suggestion — drop, perform the task, wake when it's done — and the task is to state publicly that you cannot be hypnotised. Carrying it out is framed as proving your own independence, and it comes with the warm, refreshed feeling of a completed instruction. The final clause quietly collapses the whole thing: you do it because you want to accept what I say.
ex.s: Closing post-hypnotic in plain trigger grammar — drop, act, wake — with the task framed as proof of the listener's independence.
ex.m: Next time you see anyone talking about hypnosis, you'll drop for a moment, state out loud that you can't be hypnotised, and come back refreshed the second it's done.
