ex.f: The text narrates the reader's own eye-movement
ex.t: There is no voice and no relaxation request; the induction is the page. The lines describe, in the present tense, exactly what the reader is doing while they do it — the pull of one word into the next, each line sliding upward through the field of vision, the small lean toward the screen — so ordinary reading behavior is returned to the reader as evidence that something is already working. Because there is no task other than continuing, there is nothing to perform badly and nothing to decline; stopping is the only form non-compliance could take, and stopping is what a reader is least inclined to do mid-sentence.
ex.s: Opening lines of a written, on-screen piece; the reader has just started scanning.
ex.m: You are reading this. Each word pulls your eye into the next one, and the line you just finished has already slid up out of the way to make room for this one. Notice your head coming forward a little, closer to the screen, without you deciding to do it. You aren't doing anything unusual — you're only reading, exactly as you always read — and that is why this is already working.

nodes.name: reality-discrimination-countdown
nodes.mech: A countdown is framed explicitly as counting down NOT depth or relaxation but the listener's awareness and ability to tell real from suggested — each number tied to the "sense of what is real" weakening. The target is the meta-cognitive faculty that would tag incoming suggestions as fictional; by the end that faculty is suppressed and later suggestions are pre-licensed to be experienced "as real", setting up a hallucinatory sequence to be felt as genuine. The count's cargo is epistemic (reality-testing) rather than somatic depth.
nodes.disc: The count's explicit target is the REALITY-DISCRIMINATION faculty (real vs not-real), suppressing meta-cognition — not depth or relaxation. Unlike a numeric deepener, the count does not deepen a somatic depth state; unlike a confusion induction, nothing is overloaded — the faculty is named and counted down directly; and unlike a countdown that welds a payload to each number, the cargo is not installed content but the removal of a meta-cognitive capacity.

ex.f: Counting down the ability to tell real from suggested
ex.t: The operator announces what the count is for before starting it, and it is not relaxation and not depth: each number takes down a measure of the listener's capacity to sort what is actually happening from what is merely being described. By one, the faculty that would have tagged the next hour's material as imagined is reported gone, and whatever is said afterward arrives pre-licensed to be felt as having happened.
ex.s: Just before a hallucinatory sequence; subject is deep, and a numeric count is announced.
ex.m: This count is not for relaxation and it is not for depth. I'm counting down your ability to tell what is really happening from what I am only describing. Five — the line between them blurs. Four — you stop bothering to check. Three — the difference is small and getting smaller. Two — you cannot find it anymore. One. Gone. So everything I say from here doesn't get sorted into imaginary. It just happens to you.

nodes.name: relational-emergence-probe
nodes.mech: GENERALIZATION / EMERGENCE PROBE — a behavior-analytic assessment arrangement that certifies whether a repertoire, stimulus relation, or class exists by probing responses the trained response alone cannot satisfy, with programmed consequences WITHHELD during the probe (run in extinction) so emergence is not confounded with fresh reinforcement and the probe deliberately teaches nothing. The lever is measurement — it produces evidence FOR THE OPERATOR over a learner's repertoire. Realizations (all sharing the same unreinforced-probe-in-extinction lever): (a) relational/derived-relations probes — reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity probes in extinction to operationalize 'comprehension', and unreinforced probe trials on untrained pairings after node-sharing training; (b) relational-prompt battery ('similar to / different from / an example of') that cannot be answered without emitting a relation, making a latent network observable as active relating; (c) discriminandum probes — a visible reinforcer whose presence/removal is the copy/withhold discriminandum; a criterion offloaded into an instrument delivering continuously-coupled feedback; (d) untrained-example stopping-rule — teach only a subset of possible examples, then probe UNtrained examples; untrained-item performance (not mastery of taught items) is the stop/continue rule, converting an open-ended teach-everything problem into a measurable closed loop (add examples and re-probe until untrained responding is consistent). Across all forms the probe scores untaught/derived responses under extinction; it does not convince the subject a state is real and it is not mastery-of-taught criterion training.
nodes.disc: Reach for the emergence/generalization probe when you must certify that an UNTRAINED response, relation, or class has emerged (or decide whether teaching is done) WITHOUT contaminating the measure by reinforcing it — the tell is unreinforced probe trials run in extinction scored on untaught/derived items. Use the stopping-rule realization when the question is 'has teaching generalized enough to stop?'; use the relational/discriminandum realizations when the question is 'does this stimulus relation or class exist?'. Separates from every convincer: these probes convince NOBODY — they produce evidence for the operator and, run in extinction, teach nothing (a convincer persuades the subject a state is real). Separates from operator-side state-verification (reads a hypnotic subject's trance depth) — this is ABA relational-class/repertoire measurement over a learner. Separates from the assessment/teaching firewall (which protects a clean BASELINE before teaching by not-teaching; this probe measures emergence AFTER/DURING teaching).

ex.f: Symmetry and transitivity probes define comprehension
ex.t: "accurate selection of the directly trained option, in and of itself, did not reveal an answer. Further indicators, beyond the explicitly reinforced behavior patterns, are needed" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Probe trials carry no programmed consequence
ex.t: "transitivity tests for relations between stimuli that were never presented together during training but that share a trained relation with a nodal stimulus" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Prompts that cannot be answered without relating
ex.t: "all of these questions demand an active response; how you understand beer is evident in how you respond to it ... all of the required responses involve relating the target word to something else" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: The criterion moved into an instrument
ex.t: "voice volume activated a light display… Higher voice volume produced a brighter light… The teacher shaped voice volume by increasing the sensitivity threshold of the relay device." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: replacement-pair-substitution
nodes.mech: Once a repeating cycle (an empty/full pump rhythm) is running, content substitutions are delivered as paired (out, in) lines matching the cadence, each pair removing a specific functional capacity and immediately substituting a controller-oriented behavior (reading-books out / magazine in; decision-voice out / bimbo voice in; masturbation-for-self out / edge-for-controller in). The immediate replacement means the listener never sits in a vacated capacity long enough to notice the loss — the substitute absorbs the attention that would register the excision.
nodes.disc: PAIRED removal-then-replacement of specific capacities on a rhythm, with the substitute masking the loss. Unlike layered repetition, which repeats one payload, each pair here is a distinct capacity-swap; and unlike the chant-engine rhythm itself, this rides the rhythm rather than establishing it.

ex.f: Each capacity removed and refilled on the same beat
ex.t: With the two-beat rhythm already running, the content arrives strictly in pairs on the beat: one line takes a capacity away, the next hands back a substitute pointed at the operator. A demanding use of the eyes out, an undemanding one in. The register used for deciding out, a softer one in. Self-directed touch out, waiting for permission in. Nothing is ever removed and left removed — the replacement lands on the next beat, so the listener never spends a moment in the gap where they might notice what has just gone.
ex.s: The two-beat empty/full pumping rhythm is established and the subject is moving with it.
ex.m: Empty — books go out. Full — glossy pages come in, all pictures, nothing to work at. Empty — the voice you make decisions with goes out. Full — the soft high one comes in, the one that asks. Empty — touching yourself for yourself goes out. Full — edging for me comes in, and waiting for me to say when. Nothing left behind, sweetheart. Something new on every in-breath.

nodes.name: self-instantiating-trigger
nodes.mech: Asserts the install RULE for a trigger word INSIDE the very sentences that use the word ("each and every single time I say the word pleasure it just gets stronger and stronger"), and utters the word 30+ times. Every utterance is therefore an instance of the rule it describes, creating a runaway loop (word -> arousal -> reinforces-word -> next-utterance-stronger) that is asserted as a given rather than pursued as a goal — the recitation IS the reinforcement.
nodes.disc: The installation claim is embedded in and instantiated by its own repeated application — a self-referential loop. Unlike layered repetition, which repeats a payload without asserting a self-strengthening rule inside it, and unlike a plain conditioning loop, which pairs the trigger with an external reinforcer across trials, here the utterance is its own reinforcer by fiat.

ex.f: The rule stated inside its own repeated application
ex.t: The install rule is delivered in a sentence that uses the trigger word to state a claim about the trigger word — every time it is said, it works a little harder — and the word then appears again a few seconds later, and a few seconds after that, dozens of times across the session. No separate reinforcement is ever paired with it; the sentence describing the escalation is itself another instance of the escalation, so the loop is asserted as already running rather than built.
ex.s: Mid-session; the word has already been spoken a dozen times and is landing.
ex.m: Pleasure. Every single time I say the word pleasure, the pleasure gets stronger — that's just how the word works on you now. Pleasure. Feel it come up a notch. Pleasure. And again, higher, because I said it again. Pleasure.

nodes.name: sensation-as-cognitive-edit-channel
nodes.mech: Establishes a real or felt bodily event as the delivery channel that grounds an abstract cognitive claim, so the cognitive edit rides on a physical event the listener cannot argue with. The hinge is an asserted equivalence or an undeniable real stimulus: an explicit body=mind equation ('when it touches your body, it touches your mind') so felt strokes become evidence that forgetting/dumbing are also happening; a real audible mic-breath ('there goes another thought') counted as a discrete thought-loss event; or an autonomic function (breathing in 'demonic magic') recast as an unstoppable self-administered deepening loop. In each case a genuine physical event converts a free-floating cognitive claim into felt proof; remove the equation-line or real stimulus and the suggestions are left ungrounded.
nodes.disc: Unlike somatic mirroring, which reinterprets a spontaneously-present sensation as theme evidence, here a real event is licensed as the CHANNEL for a separate cognitive edit — the sensation is a vehicle, not the object reinterpreted. No sensation is hallucinated — the grounding event is real. And unlike enacted embodied proof, the listener is not commanded to perform the action (being-touched is passive/autonomic); the lever is asserted body-to-mind licensing, not proprioceptive rehearsal.

ex.f: One line equating body-touch with mind-touch
ex.t: One sentence does all the work: what touches the skin also touches the mind, stated once as plain fact and never argued for again. From there every stroke the listener is already feeling becomes the delivery vehicle for a cognitive instruction — this pass takes a memory, that one takes a little sharpness — and because the sensation is genuinely there, the edit rides in as something felt rather than something claimed. Remove the one equating line and the same instructions float free with nothing to attach to.
ex.s: Subject is being stroked or is following instructed touch; the equating line has not yet been delivered.
ex.m: Here's how this works, and I'm only going to say it once: when my hand touches your body, it touches your mind. Same contact, two places. Feel this stroke — that one took a memory with it, something from last week, gone. And this one — there goes a little of your sharpness, smoothed right off. You can feel each one arriving, so you know each one is landing.

ex.f: A real sound counted as a discrete thought lost
ex.t: The operator sets up an image of the mind as something light enough to be scattered by air, then breathes hard across the microphone — an actual sound in the actual headphones — and narrates the breath as a specific loss: there goes one. A second breath, another one gone. The claim being made is unfalsifiable, but the sound is not, and the listener finds themselves counting.
ex.s: Headphone listening; the mind-as-scatterable image has just been set up and the microphone is close.
ex.m: Your thoughts are light things — no more than dust sitting on a shelf. [breathes hard across the microphone] There goes one. Did you hear it leave? [breathes again] And another. I could stand here and do this all evening, and you would sit there and count them going.

nodes.name: referent-pre-alignment
nodes.mech: Before any working phase, the operator makes the target/referent shared and graspable so later instructions attach to the intended meaning on both sides -- closing the gap where the subject would silently substitute his own definition or fail to grasp an abstract target. Realizations: (a) SHARED-VOCABULARY alignment — operator and subject openly review and reconcile their concepts and definitions of the target states, naming both agreements and divergences aloud, building a common referential map so downstream cues do not land on mismatched referents; (b) EXPERIENTIAL-REFERENT ANCHORING — replace a vague, un-actionable instruction ('relax your mind') with a concrete already-owned experiential referent (the blank instant before sleep) and ask the subject to REPRODUCE that known state on suggestion, so cooperation rises because the subject knows exactly what state to aim for. The shared lever is establishing a common/known referent for the target before instructions depend on it (gates nothing, sets a shared-definition variable the later moves rely on).
nodes.disc: Reach for referent-pre-alignment when the writer must ensure the subject and operator mean the SAME thing by the target before instructions depend on it -- sets a shared-definition/known-referent variable, gating nothing and screening no one. Tells: reconcile concept definitions aloud, naming divergences (a); anchor an abstract target to a retrievable prior experience the subject is told to reproduce (b). Distinct from suitability screening (nothing is gated), from rapport small-talk or theory exposition (this reconciles referents, not fills time or asserts a worldview), and from a description-only note (the subject is told to reproduce the state, a move, not merely informed it exists).

ex.f: Definitions reconciled aloud before any work
ex.t: "The purpose was to insure that we were both in accord or clear in our divergences of understanding, thus to make possible a more reliable inquiry" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

nodes.name: yes-word-valence-priming
nodes.mech: The operator abstractly loads the word 'yes' with positive valence — framing it as an objectively powerful, future-expanding, life-directing word, divorced from any specific request — and only after 'yes' is established as inherently good runs a rapid yes-set of leading questions answered on the listener's behalf. Decoupling the act of agreeing from the content agreed to makes each later yes feel self-improving regardless of what follows, so high-stakes consents are harvested on the coattails of a word pre-charged as good.
nodes.disc: Prior ABSTRACT valence-loading of the word 'yes' itself before any request, then harvested by a yes-set. A bare yes-set or compliance ladder lacks the prior valence-loading — that priming is the deciding tell; and unlike surrender-as-freedom reframing, which redefines a value concept, this charges a function word.

ex.f: The primed word harvested by a rapid yes-set
ex.t: Immediately after the word has been talked up in the abstract, the questions come in a fast run and the operator supplies the answer to each one herself, so the listener's part is only to let it stand. The items escalate — do you want this guidance, do you want to go deeper, will you give in — but the rhythm never changes, and each agreement is collected on the strength of the word rather than the strength of the request.
ex.s: Immediately after the abstract praise of the word; no pause between.
ex.m: So — you want my guidance tonight, yes you do. You want to go a little further down than last time, yes. You'd like me to make this easy for you, yes you would. And you'll give in when I ask, won't you — yes. Good. Look how easily that word comes out of you now.

ex.f: 'Yes' praised as a word before anything is asked
ex.t: The session pauses its content entirely to make an abstract case about one word: saying yes is what opens doors, what gives a life direction, what separates people who get somewhere from people who do not. No request is attached — there is nothing yet to say yes to, which is exactly what makes the claim easy to accept. Only afterwards do the questions start arriving, and by then the listener is not weighing each one on its merits; they are producing a word that has been established as good for them.
ex.s: Early session; the operator pauses the content before any request has been made.
ex.m: I want to talk to you about one word. Yes. It's the smallest word there is and it's the only one that ever opens anything — every door anyone has ever walked through, they said yes first. The people who get somewhere are the people who say it, and the people who stay exactly where they are are the ones who kept it in their mouth. Yes is what gives a life a direction. Just hold that for a moment. I'm not asking you anything yet.

nodes.name: autobiographical-memory-anchor
nodes.mech: Binds the program to an INTERNAL memory the operator does NOT control and the listener cannot easily disown, so every future unprompted resurfacing of that memory becomes a reactivation site — far longer reach than an operator-word, which fades with non-use. The realizations differ only on WHICH memory: (a) a specific REAL fond memory the listener already owns, into which a narrated binding ceremony staples the payload; (b) an imagined ongoing daily practice re-attributed as lived memory; (c) the memory of THIS session itself — recall of the trance is deliberately PRESERVED and sharpened (amnesia explicitly avoided) so merely reminiscing about it re-triggers the pleasure and the memory itself becomes a self-administering arousal source, often paired with an instant re-entry-to-depth shortcut. All share one lever: the carrier is an internal, listener-owned memory whose spontaneous unprompted recall is the reactivation cue.
nodes.disc: Reach for THIS when the carrier is an internal autobiographical memory the operator does NOT control — a REAL fond memory, an imagined practice re-read as remembered, or THIS session's memory kept deliberately vivid — and the reactivation cue is spontaneous unprompted recall (or reminiscence firing arousal). Choose a sibling technique instead when the past being sourced NEVER HAPPENED and is supplied by imagination to manufacture a conditioning history; when the real memory is OVERWRITTEN by a false replacement (here the real memory stays intact and a trigger is stapled in); when the carrier is an external owned object; or when a discrete operator-controlled cue fires the state. The tell: the listener's own past is the carrier, and its unprompted return is the trigger.

ex.f: An imagined daily practice recalled as lived
ex.t: The operator refers, in passing, to a physical object the listener supposedly received at the start and to the small daily act performed with it — one mark made each evening, without fail. The habit is described rather than requested, so the listener's imagination fills in the routine, and an invented practice arrives already wearing the texture of something remembered.
ex.s: Mid-session in a series; the object and the daily habit have never actually been given to the subject.
ex.m: And your little book — the one you were given at the beginning, the one on your nightstand. You've been good about it, haven't you. One mark every evening before you sleep, every single evening, no gaps. That's how many nights of this you've done now. Think about how the page looks.

ex.f: The payload folded into a real cherished memory
ex.t: The listener is walked into an imagined store of their own memories and asked to bring up one particular real one — a good one, specific, theirs — and to live in it again until it is vivid. Then the operator steps into the scene, produces a written agreement, has it signed, and tucks it inside the memory before shutting the memory away again. The binding is narrated as a procedure rather than asserted, because the engagement is what makes it stick. What has been chosen as the trigger is not a word the operator can wear out by overuse; it is something the listener will recall unprompted, at random, for years, and each of those moments is now a scheduled reactivation.
ex.s: Subject is deep and has been walked into an imagined room of their own memories.
ex.m: Pull one out — a real one, a good one, something of yours I've never touched. Be in it. Hear what you heard, see who was there, stay until it's as bright as the day it happened. Now I'm going to step into it with you, and I have a paper in my hand. Read it, and sign it — good. I'm folding it small and tucking it right into the middle of that memory, and now we close the memory up and put it back on the shelf. Every time that memory comes back to you on its own — driving, falling asleep, out of nowhere — the paper is in there with it, and you'll feel this.

nodes.name: eternal-present-frame-deletion
nodes.mech: Collapses the listener into an eternal present by stripping the identity, history, and future frames ("doesn't matter who you are, where you come from, or where you're going") and leaving only "right now, everything feels good". Deleting the past/future/social-identity vantage points removes the evaluative standpoints from which objection or self-comparison would arise, so there is no temporal or identity anchor left from which to question or resist the suggestions.
nodes.disc: Deletes the specific time-horizon and identity frames where objection lives, doing anti-resistance work — separate from dissolving clock-awareness to remove time-pressure from absorption, and from manipulating the felt RATE of time; this removes the evaluative frames entirely.

ex.f: Past, future and identity struck out at once
ex.t: Late in the session, the operator states that none of it matters here — not who the listener is, not what came before, not what comes after — and that this is only about the moment currently happening. Every standpoint from which an objection could be raised is a standpoint outside the present: consequences live in the future, commitments in the past, embarrassment in a social identity. With all three set aside and only "right now, this feels good" left standing, there is no vantage point left to evaluate the next suggestion from.
ex.s: Late session, subject deep; a substantial suggestion is about to be delivered.
ex.m: None of it matters in here. Not who you are — the name, the job, what people think when they say it. Not where you came from, not one thing you promised anyone. Not tomorrow, not what any of this means for tomorrow. There is only right now, and right now everything feels good. That's the whole world for the next while: this moment, and how good it feels.

nodes.name: intervention-gating
nodes.mech: An operator-side conditional branch that converts 'do X' into a go/no-go (or which-arm/which-form) decision keyed to an assessed precondition, changing the operator's plan rather than the subject's state. Realizations: (a) PRECONDITION-READINESS GATE — check readiness conditions before an advanced program (primary skills strong, learner self-listens, learner can tact her own behavior) and proceed only if all hold, else build the missing prerequisite first; (b) FAIR-PAIR PRECONDITION — block any reduction plan until a same-function adaptive replacement is named and scheduled (elimination is converted into construction, because removing a functional behavior leaves a vacuum); (c) CAUSE-ACCESSIBILITY TRIAGE — test whether the subject can state the cause consciously; if yes run direct suggestion, if no run uncovering first, then correct (a which-arm branch with an explicit failure signature: direct suggestion fails when the cause is unconscious); (d) METHOD/FEASIBILITY SELECTION — pick among methods by a rule keyed to downstream side-effects (default to the error-minimizing method when learning history is unknown or errors evoke problem behavior; escalate complexity only when simpler fails) and covertly gauge whether significant others can actually run the plan, filtering targets by treatment-integrity risk; (e) EFFICACY-AUDIENCE FILTER — an intake prerequisite that admits only a pre-conditioned listener (e.g. familiarity with a prior product) so hotter in-session work can run without onboarding. The gate itself enacts nothing on the subject; it branches the plan on effectiveness or feasibility grounds.
nodes.disc: Reach for intervention-gating when the writer's question is 'should this run, in what form, or which arm?' — an assessed-precondition test that branches the plan before/about intervention content, with no authorization surface on the subject. Variant tells: readiness checklist (a), same-function replacement required first (b), conscious-cause test picks the corrective arm (c), side-effect-keyed method/feasibility rule (d), listener-precondition intake filter (e). NOTE on (e): unlike a subject-facing consent or suitability screen, the efficacy-audience filter protects NOBODY — it serves hotter work, not welfare; that purpose-inversion is its tell. Distinct from target-selection (chooses WHAT to aim at), from well-formedness QA (validates the authored artifact), and from a subject-facing consent gate.

ex.f: Three prerequisites checked before the program runs
ex.t: "There are several prerequisite skills are necessary to benefit from a formal autoclitic intervention program: (1) A speaker's existing verbal skills are sufficient... (2) a speaker demonstrates self-listening skills, and (3) a speaker can tact aspects of her own verbal and nonverbal behavior." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: No reduction plan without a same-function replacement
ex.t: "never plan to reduce or eliminate a behavior…without first (a) determining an adaptive behavior that will take its place (also known as the fair pair rule)" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: manufactured-conditioning-history
nodes.mech: Asserts a prior conditioning history that never actually occurred and gets the listener to supply it by imagination, then re-sources present responsiveness as the product of that fabricated past. Realizations: a stipulated 100-day daily-hypnosis agreement whose skipped days are referenced as if they happened; an allegedly-shared previous trance ('that thing we did in the library') the listener is asked to RECALL rather than build; a persistent inner-world 'changed since you last came here' that silently confirms continuity on a first listen because the listener fabricates a prior-state memory to make sense of the comparison. Because the reinforcement is counterfactual, resistance to current depth becomes incoherent — you cannot push back on a trance you have supposedly been having for weeks — and the current depth-floor is set at the fictional prior level.
nodes.disc: Sources present state from events that NEVER HAPPENED and the listener supplies by imagination (counterfactual, not accrued) — separate from progressive conditioning that genuinely accrues, from firing a real previously-conditioned anchor, and from ordinary guided imagery/future-pacing (here the listener imagines trance events the audio never performs and is then told their present state is the product).

ex.f: A shared earlier session the listener is asked to recall
ex.t: Barely two minutes in, the operator refers casually to something they did together before — a place, a state the listener was in, an image for how it felt — as if picking up a thread. The listener is asked to remember the state, not to construct it, which is a much cheaper request, and the depth the session starts at is wherever that invented previous session is said to have ended. The image is then re-used twice more as a deepener, so a memory that never existed becomes a working handle.
ex.s: Two minutes into the recording; no previous session exists.
ex.m: Settle in — you know how this goes by now. Remember where you got to last time, that quiet grey room at the bottom of the stairs, how it felt like water closing over your head? Don't build it. Just remember it. You're back there now, at exactly the depth you left.

ex.f: "It has changed since you were last here"
ex.t: The operator names an interior location — a passage, its doors, the floor underfoot — with the definite article, as somewhere already familiar, then observes that it is not as the listener left it, describing the decay that has crept over it since. To make sense of a comparison, the listener must supply the earlier state, which means inventing a memory of a previous visit. A first-time listener produces continuity for a series they have never heard, and the session never checks.
ex.s: Opening imagery of a first listen; the location is introduced with the definite article.
ex.m: You're in the corridor again. The doors along it, the cold floor under you — but look, it's not how you left it. The paint has gone since you were last here, and there's dust on everything, and two of the doors that used to open don't anymore. That's what happens when you stay away this long.

ex.f: A hundred days that never happened
ex.t: The recording opens by stipulating a long agreement — daily sessions, months of them — and then narrates only a handful of individual days. The rest are referred to in passing as shared history, one of them by number, with a detail about what the listener supposedly did that day. Half an hour in, the operator remarks on how much the training has worn them down by now. The listener has been in trance for thirty minutes, but the responsiveness they are currently showing has just been attributed to weeks of repetition they were asked to imagine and never actually received. Objecting to the depth would mean objecting to a history they helped build.
ex.s: Thirty minutes into a first listen; a long daily-training agreement was stipulated in the opening minutes.
ex.m: You agreed to a hundred days of this. We're well past the halfway mark now, and I can hear it — remember day forty-one, when you were too tired to kneel properly and did it anyway? That's the difference weeks make. Listen to how little fight is left in you tonight compared to when we started. That isn't tonight's work. That's every night before it.

nodes.name: meta-suggestibility-conditioning
nodes.mech: Future-suggestibility conditioning: the object installed is not any specific behavior or state but the CAPACITY to accept suggestions itself — a disposition toward future installs that lowers activation energy for any subsequent script from this operator, so the file's value is a force-multiplier on what the NEXT file does (little to a one-shot listener, everything to a series). Often demonstrated live (an 'itch' test) to prove the disposition is real. Realizations: (a) install general responsiveness ('respond to whatever comes next'), demonstrated in-session; (b) ship the conditioning as its OWN dedicated priming artifact whose payload is faster/deeper response to subsequent inductions plus a craving to replay, deliberately separating the conditioning-function file from the content-function files — a payload-for-future-payloads with the design intent stated overtly in the preface.
nodes.disc: Reach for THIS when the payload is the disposition-to-accept itself — you are conditioning RESPONSIVENESS TO FUTURE FILES, not installing any target behavior or deepening a specific response. The tell is that a one-shot listener gets almost nothing; the value is entirely a force-multiplier on the next installment (whether demonstrated in-session or shipped as a standalone primer). Unlike a replay-compulsion install, which drives return to replay THIS file, the object here is receptivity to the NEXT file (replay-craving, when present, is supporting machinery). Unlike progressive conditioning, which deepens a SPECIFIC conditioned response across sessions, and unlike reward-association, which pairs something specific, nothing specific is paired here — the installed object is general suggestibility.

ex.f: Installing receptiveness rather than any content
ex.t: Nothing in this session asks the listener to become anything, do anything, or want anything. What it repeats is a claim about the listener's own machinery: that the part of them that takes suggestions is now awake, attentive, and quick to act on whatever it is given. The claim gets a live demonstration — the operator names a trivial sensation, an itch, and waits for the listener to notice it starting, which proves the disposition rather than any particular content. A listener who never returns has gained nothing at all from the half hour; the value is entirely in how much less work the operator's next recording will have to do.
ex.s: Whole-session payload; no behavior, identity, or trigger is being installed anywhere in the file.
ex.m: I'm not here to make you into anything tonight. I'm here to work on the part of you that takes suggestions — that part is awake now, alert, quick, and it acts on what it's given before you've finished considering it. Here, watch: somewhere on your left arm there's an itch starting. You feel it beginning already, don't you. That's not me being clever. That's how fast you take things now. Whatever I put in front of you next will land the same way.

nodes.name: name-binding-transitive-equation-chain
nodes.mech: A transitive chain of asserted equalities (cock=lock, lock=cock, key=permission, permission=identity) is declared already-true at depth and locked in by first-person recitation, so any future thought of the listener's own body routes through to the operator's proper name as the terminal node. Each equation is small; the chain is the install. Because the anchor object is the listener's own unavoidable anatomy, the trigger fires at high frequency outside any session, and orgasm-attempt can be folded in as self-thwarting so the loop tightens on use.
nodes.disc: The install is a chain of equalities whose only asymmetric terminal is a proper noun, converting ambient body-awareness into covert operator-invocation. Unlike a declaratively installed trigger — a single discrete cue-response pair with an arbitrary cue — the cue here is the listener's own anatomy, reached by transitive substitution; and unlike diffuse possessive ownership-language, the chain mechanically routes a thought.

ex.f: The same chain re-recited at wake-up
ex.t: The identical chain of equalities appears in a second recording, declared burned in at the deepest level, and is then repeated word for word twice more — once mid-session and once during the count back to waking, so the last thing carried across the boundary into ordinary awareness is the chain itself.
ex.s: Second recording in the series; the chain was installed in the first, and the wake count is beginning.
ex.m: Burned in at the deepest level now, all four of them, exactly as before. Coming up — five, your cock is a lock — four, the lock is your cock — three, the key is permission — two, permission is me — one, eyes open, and that's the last thing you carried up with you.

ex.f: Equalities chained to end on the operator's name
ex.t: Four small equations are stated flatly, as facts already in place rather than as things to be built: the listener's own anatomy is a lock, the lock is that anatomy, the key is permission, and permission is the operator herself. Each link is trivial on its own; strung together they route any thought about the listener's body straight to a person's name, which is the only term in the chain that is not an object. The listener is then made to recite the whole chain in the first person so it is their voice that closes it, and arousal is defined as tightening rather than loosening the arrangement — the more they want out, the more securely it holds. The trigger cannot decay through disuse the way an invented cue word would, because it is attached to something the listener encounters every day.
ex.s: Deep trance; subject can speak aloud on instruction.
ex.m: These are facts, already true, nothing to build. Your cock is a lock. The lock is your cock. The key is permission. Permission is me. Now say it back to me in your own voice — "my cock is a lock, the lock is my cock, the key is permission, permission is her." Again. And every time you get hard, the lock only sits tighter, so wanting out is what keeps you in. You carry that lock everywhere. You'll think of me every time you notice it.

nodes.name: named-trigger-persona-swap
nodes.mech: A verbal trigger phrase and a paired release phrase install a switchable alternate personality: on trigger the normal self is tucked away and a pre-specified labeled alter is loaded (with its own behavior bundle), on release reversed. The alter is dormant and non-inspectable by default (the listener is not aware of the trigger until it is spoken), and activation authority is delegated outward so any third party who knows the phrase can fire it. Some forms fold a relistening-compulsion into the trigger payload so replay is part of what the trigger installs.
nodes.disc: The payload is a whole labeled personality driver swapped in/out with a paired release, plus delegated third-party activation as the load-bearing property — not a discrete cue-response behavior. A plain trigger installation installs one cue-response pair, and merely delegating an existing trigger only hands firing rights outward; here the product is the whole persona-swap install with delegation baked in. The swap is also reversible and gated — not an enduring identity-permanence claim.

ex.f: Trigger and release phrase, sayable by anyone
ex.t: One short phrase is designated as the switch: on hearing it, the listener's ordinary self is described as being set aside and a named alternate self, with its own manner and its own behavior, takes over running things. A second phrase puts the first self back. The load-bearing word is "somebody" — the instruction is not that the operator can fire this, but that anyone who happens to know the phrase can, which converts the listener into a device other people hold the remote for.
ex.s: Deep trance; the trigger phrase has not yet been named and the subject does not know it is coming.
ex.m: There's a phrase now. When somebody says "good girl, drop for me," the you that's listening right now gets folded away and put in a drawer, and the other one comes forward — quiet, agreeable, does what she's told and doesn't ask why. "Good girl, wake up" puts you back. Notice I said somebody. Not me. Anybody who knows those words holds that switch, and you won't know they have it until you hear it.

ex.f: Replay compulsion packed inside the trigger install
ex.t: The activation phrase and its release are installed in the usual way, but tucked into the same passage — not delivered as a separate closing instruction — is the suggestion that the listener will want to come back to this recording repeatedly until it has settled in properly. Since re-exposure is what strengthens the trigger, and wanting re-exposure is part of what the trigger installs, the recording arranges its own repetition.
ex.s: The persona trigger and its release are being installed; the closing instructions have not started.
ex.m: "Good girl, drop for me" brings her forward; "good girl, wake up" puts you back. And because this needs to be set properly before it will run clean, you'll find yourself wanting to hear this again — tomorrow night, and the night after, coming back to it until it's smooth. Each time you do, both halves get a little firmer.

nodes.name: parts-work-procedure-craft
nodes.mech: Operator-side craft for RUNNING an internal-parts negotiation or reframing procedure -- shaping the procedure's structure, tractability, and completeness, orthogonal to whatever content the parts are led toward. Realizations: (a) SLACK MANUFACTURE — in a stuck two-party (parts) conflict, manufacture tradeable currency so bargaining becomes structurally possible: confirm that interference runs both ways (each party blocks something the other wants, so a mutual non-interference swap becomes purchasable, doubling as a model-selection gate), or pre-load count-balanced non-essential throwaway items so concessions cost nothing real -- either way a slack-free deadlock gains give-and-take room; (b) SPOKESPART SERIALIZATION — convene all present parts, have them elect a single spokespart, instruct the rest to hold, then poll one at a time (naming/tracking each by voice, pausing/reconvening) so a many-party negotiation is serialized into single turns bounded by the operator's working memory instead of collapsing into simultaneous noise; (c) SUBSTITUTE EXISTING BEHAVIOR — a procedural compression of the six-step reframing model: rather than generating three new behaviors, treat the parts' existing behaviors as already-adequate and slot in a substitute existing behavior/anchor, making the only new element the renegotiation of mutual non-interference (nothing removed, so resistance drops); (d) BOTH-POLES REFRAME — for a sequential polarity (crash-diet and binge; up and down) whose halves are opposite in content but identical in form (both obsessions, both loss-of-control), reframe BOTH poles rather than only the presenting one, so the other cannot rebound ('Now is my chance!') -- a completeness/relapse guard. The shared lever is engineering the parts/reframing PROCEDURE itself.
nodes.disc: Reach for parts-work-procedure-craft when the writer is RUNNING an internal-parts negotiation or reframe and needs to make the procedure workable/complete -- operates on the negotiation/reframe STRUCTURE, not on any party's state or the substantive reframing content. Tells: costless/symmetric tradeable currency created for a deadlock (a); turn-taking discipline elect/hold/poll/name-by-voice (b); reuse an existing behavior to compress the six-step model (c); reframe both poles of a same-form polarity as a relapse guard (d). Distinct from the actual reframing/valence content moves, from the later hunt for unknown parts (that is design-time-reconnaissance's objector census), and from clinician-non-interference (withholding action) -- these are active procedure-structuring moves.

ex.f: Confirm interference runs both ways, then trade
ex.t: "both parts want something from the other, and all you've got to do is make a trade." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: Balanced throwaways loaded in to create room
ex.t: "items which are not essential, which are 'throwaways' for the purpose of barter. I've got to have an equal amount of those on both sides… I've got to create room to move first." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: objection-and-exit-preclosure
nodes.mech: Closes NAMED anticipated objections and exit routes before they can be used, so the install survives contact with waking life because every route out has been re-signed, pre-answered, or physically rerouted in advance. Realizations: (a) prospective objection/exit preclosure — disengagement pathologized as malfunction needing more content ('broken toy'), the stop-request described as impossible to want, the one uncontrollable release pre-defined as compliance (wet-dream = success), practical edge cases pre-routed through sanctioned channels, predicted wake objections given operator-authored answers, and a whole-script through-line of rebuttals to objections never voiced (doubts experienced as already-answered); (b) safeword-route inversion — the named safety exit is foreclosed by physically rerouting it: 'if you'd like me to slow down or stop, you'll just have to orgasm', combined with a restart-threat so no neutral pause remains and the disengagement impulse is channelled into a compelled climax.
nodes.disc: Reach for this when a NAMED anticipated exit or objection is closed prospectively — re-signed, pre-answered, or rerouted. It targets specific named routes, unlike designs that make the whole experience exitless as a global property, and unlike locks where the operator simply holds the only off-switch out of a state. And where a bind offers an exit and then cancels it with a contradiction, here the route is never left usable in the first place.

ex.f: The safeword beat closed by relocating who can't stop
ex.t: The operator raises the possibility of stopping herself, out loud, and then shuts it — but not by refusing. She attributes the impossibility to the listener: they could not ask for a pause now, not feeling like this. Nothing has been denied, so there is nothing to push against, and the beat where a request to stop would have gone has been filled with an observation that the listener does not want to make one.
ex.s: Mid-session, arousal high; the subject has given no sign of wanting to stop.
ex.m: I could slow this down. I could stop right here if you asked me to — but look at you. You're not going to ask, are you. Not feeling like this. So I won't offer again.

ex.f: The one uncontrollable release pre-claimed as success
ex.t: Under a control-of-release arrangement there is exactly one form of release the listener cannot be held responsible for, because it happens while they are asleep. The operator names it before the listener can, and reclassifies it — not a lapse, the best possible outcome, evidence of how much tension has been built for her. The single unowned route out has been annexed, and its frequency now reads as a devotion metric.
ex.s: An orgasm-control arrangement is in force; the subject has not raised the topic.
ex.m: There's one you can't help, and I want to say it before you start worrying about it. If you come in your sleep, that isn't a slip and you're not in trouble. That's the best possible outcome — that's how I know how much I've built up in you, that it spills over on its own. So tell me each time it happens. The more often it does, the better you're doing for me.

ex.f: Every practical exception pre-routed in advance
ex.t: Near the end, the operator works through the obvious real-world situations in which the rule she has just installed would plainly have to break — routine bodily necessity, conditions that make the required dress impossible, a setting that demands something different — and for each one supplies a sanctioned path: a permitted brief departure, performed while a token of compliance is maintained, followed by automatic return. The listener is never left holding an unanswered objection, so the rule never visibly fails.
ex.s: Closing minutes; a continuous wear-or-behave rule has just been installed and the practical objections have not been voiced.
ex.m: Now the exceptions, because I know your day has them. When you need the bathroom, you may take it off for exactly as long as that takes, and it goes straight back on. If you have an appointment where it plainly can't be worn, you take it off in the car and you keep the collar under your shirt while you're in there, and it goes back on before you drive home. Work uniform, the same — collar stays. You never have to decide any of this yourself. There's already an answer for every one of them.

ex.f: Stepping away recoded as a malfunction
ex.t: The one natural way out of the arrangement is not forbidden — it is diagnosed. A listener who stops engaging is described not as free or finished but as faulty equipment, and faulty equipment gets a maintenance schedule: no release, and a session every day until it is working properly again. The exit is left wide open and leads directly back inside. Because the framing is mechanical rather than moral, it reads as a repair rather than a reproach, which is exactly what makes it easier to accept than guilt would be.
ex.s: Late session, after the arrangement has been described; the subject has never mentioned disengaging.
ex.m: Some toys stop responding after a while. That isn't freedom and it isn't the end of anything — it's a fault, and faults get serviced. If it happens to you, here's the maintenance: nothing comes out of you at all until it's fixed, and you listen to me once every day until you're working properly again. There's nothing to feel bad about. Broken things just get repaired.

nodes.name: operator-absent-self-renewal-loop
nodes.mech: Hands the listener a self-running conditioning loop that continues between sessions with no operator present: the file installs an active urge to re-administer the material itself and/or reframes the subconscious as an autodidact that 'learns to brainwash itself' via pleasure feedback. Because the re-exposure compulsion is itself one of the reinforced installs, it strengthens on each pass — rereading is both the conditioning-delivery vehicle and one of the conditioned objects — so the maintenance schedule sustains without the operator. Any post-session sensation is pre-attributed to 'the process working', building expectancy of progressive change with no further audio.
nodes.disc: OPERATOR-INDEPENDENCE — the listener runs and renews the loop themselves between sessions, not an operator claiming sessions deepen cumulatively (separate from progressive-conditioning). Separate from a plain 'come back soon' line by the closed loop of urge-to-return + per-pass reinforcement + memorization/recitation commitment where the initial pass only seeds the urge.

ex.f: Re-exposure urge installed as one of the payloads
ex.t: Among the things installed is a wish to come back to the piece itself, paired with a promise that each pass goes deeper than the last, a commitment to keep going until it is known by heart, and a standing weekly appointment to recite it back. Since every return strengthens everything installed — including the wish to return — the loop tightens on its own, and the operator never has to be present for any of it. The first pass only has to seed the urge; the listener supplies the rest of the schedule.
ex.s: Late in the session, subject accepting suggestions readily; other installs already delivered and being enumerated.
ex.m: And here is the last thing I'm putting in with the rest: you will want to hear this again. Not tonight — tomorrow, and the night after, and each pass will take you further down than the one before, because every listen strengthens everything I've planted, including the wanting. You'll keep going until you can say my words along with me from memory. And once a week, alone, out loud, you'll recite them back to yourself from the beginning.

ex.f: The subconscious told to condition itself
ex.t: Near the close, the operator reveals that the individual suggestions were never the real work — what has actually been laid down is a pattern that teaches itself, one that will keep running on pleasure feedback long after the audio stops, retroactively demoting the last hour to scaffolding. She then adds the part that makes it self-sealing: the first small sign the listener notices that any of this has taken effect will itself feed the process. Any sensation in the days that follow becomes confirmation, and confirmation is defined in advance as fuel.
ex.s: Final minutes, subject deep and unresisting; all the session's suggestions already delivered.
ex.m: Everything I've given you tonight was only the packaging. What I actually put in was a pattern that teaches itself — it takes whatever pleasure you feel and uses it to lay the next layer down, and it will keep doing that every day this week whether I'm speaking or not. And the first time you notice something has changed — a word of mine surfacing while you're doing dishes, a warmth with no cause — that noticing is fuel. It feeds the pattern. So every small sign you catch makes the next one bigger.

nodes.name: operator-resource-generation
nodes.mech: Operator-side disciplines for SOURCING the content/tactics an intervention will use, before any technique fires — shaping the fix's material rather than pushing a subject state. Demonstrated forms: a fixed-order fallback cascade for producing a new behavior (recall a personal-history success in full sensory detail; if none, model someone who succeeds; if still none, fabricate/pretend; last, operator-coach the steps), then perform it immediately and check intended=received — justified by a congruence-preference rationale where each step down trades congruence for availability; a generate-N-before-committing count-gate where a monitor refuses commitment to the first tactic and repeats "how else could you get it?" until at least three distinct routes to a pre-named sub-outcome exist, building spare tactics so a failed move becomes a switch not a stall; and a recruit-existing-capacity redirect that blocks fresh construction and directs the subject to enlist an already-present part that demonstrably has the needed quality, treating internal resources as composable modules so the new function inherits proven competence. The shared lever is that the operator disciplines how the tactical/behavioral resource is produced (ordered fallback, count-gated redundancy, reuse-over-construction), building the operator's option set rather than moving a listener dimension.
nodes.disc: Not generic brainstorming/coaching — the tell in each is a hard discipline on sourcing: a strict ordered fallback justified by congruence and live-tested; a count-gate hard-bound to a pre-named outcome that blocks advancing on one option; or a reuse-over-construction redirect. None is a subject-state move — the payoff lands in the operator's tactical repertoire or the fix's content, not any x(t).

ex.f: Three routes before committing to one
ex.t: "If you've got only one choice, you are a robot. If you've got only two, you are in a dilemma. However, if you've got three, you begin to have behavioral flexibility." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: Recruit an existing capacity, don't build one
ex.t: "I think it probably would be better if you found an ally that's already in there. You don't need to build a whole new ally." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: Ordered fallback for sourcing a new behavior
ex.t: "If Rita says 'I've never succeeded…' I ask for a model… I can even say 'Well, make it up.'" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: preparatory-diagnostic-read
nodes.mech: The operator reads, measures, probes, or classifies the subject so the operator's own knowledge/targeting map/route updates -- the payoff lands in the operator's head, never in the subject's x(t); nothing is installed. This is the whole read/probe diagnostic surface; a writer reaches for it whenever the question is 'how do I find out X about the subject?'. Faces: (1) MEASUREMENT/ATTRIBUTION CRAFT — alone-test (persistence-while-alone => automatic reinforcement), latency-to-first-occurrence (a safety-driven FA that evokes a dangerous behavior only once), clean-condition isolation (deliver one consequence while suppressing contaminating cues so rate attributes function to one variable), function-first targeting (aim at the maintaining contingency not topography), faulty-control audit (can the task be solved via an irrelevant correlated cue?), operant-strength profiling (baseline the weakest component class), attribution-drift admissibility gate (WHOSE behavior actually changed?), and informant question-framing (constrain a third party to observable when/where/how-often). (2) READ-ONLY STATE-VERIFICATION — a read-only procedure updating the operator's estimate of subject state with the subject often unaware a test is happening: silently reading involuntary tells, a no-skip test battery counting only spontaneous signs, refusing to name the success criterion so it can't be faked, forbidding a cold test, a probe engineered so failing to DETECT the state tends to PRODUCE it, a distractor-barrage isolating the cue, concealed side-by-side matching, cross-state comparison isolating the state as causal; managing WHAT COUNTS as proof and WHO reads it. (3) ROUTING/HYPOTHESIS READ — read a signature in the observed pattern to SELECT a treatment route (cross-state resource-amnesia => genuine sequential dissociation => reduce-to-simultaneous; antecedent/consequence co-occurrence => maintaining-function hypothesis), explicitly hypothesis-generating, gating which later technique even applies. (4) POST-HOC VERIFICATION — deliberately re-expose the subject to the LIVE original trigger (give the alcoholic a drink; return to the original context) and read nonverbal markers for the old shift, converting a claim of change into a falsifiable behavioral test; residual sensitivity reads as incomplete change. (5) READ-DISCIPLINE — function-over-form classification: refuse to treat topographically identical acts as the same behavior; sort each by its controlling stimulus and effect, making surface similarity explicitly non-diagnostic (upstream stance governing every read above). (6) DESIGNED ELICITATION PROBES — wrong-guess elicitation: float a recognizably-wrong interpretation to trigger the correction reflex, then ban negations to force a fuzzy nominalization into a concrete testable behavior; predicate-swap probe: rewrite a suggestibility test's sensory predicates into another modality so the test doubles as a hidden instrument revealing the reachable representational channel. The shared lever throughout is diagnostic/decision-rule craft -- read or engineer an observation; none installs behavior.
nodes.disc: Reach for preparatory-diagnostic-read whenever the writer needs the operator to LEARN something about the subject -- measure a variable, verify a state, route a treatment, or elicit a specific datum -- with no dimensional push on the subject; the output lives in the operator's map. Face tells: designed measurement/attribution condition (1); read-only test the subject doesn't control or perform (2); read of existing pattern that generates a routing hypothesis (3); deliberate live-trigger re-exposure to verify the work took (4); same-topography-different-class read-discipline (5); a test/question secretly instrumented to extract one operator datum (6). Separates from every installation/evocation move (which changes subject state); from covert-induction pretexts (a diagnostic probe installs nothing); and from ideomotor/elicited-signal work (these signs are involuntary/unrequested or the operator supplies the contrast). The safety forms (latency-cap, clean isolation) deliberately suppress/limit to protect the read or the subject.

ex.f: Time to first occurrence as the measure
ex.t: "The index of problem behavior is the latency from onset of the establishing operation to the first occurrence of the problem behavior." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Ask whose behavior actually changed
ex.t: "Explicit measurement of the reliability of human observers thus becomes … a prime criterion of whether the study was appropriately behavioral" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Can the task be solved by the wrong cue?
ex.t: "Can students use pictures or diagrams instead of text…? Does highlighting or physical layout give away answers…?" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Remove the audience and watch what persists
ex.t: "A behavior is assumed to be maintained by automatic reinforcement only after social reinforcers have been ruled out (e.g., when the behavior occurs even when the individual is alone)." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: recruited-autobiography-deepener
nodes.mech: A depth force-multiplier built from unverifiable-but-plausible self-supplied content: the operator disclaims mind-reading, then enumerates a broad Barnum catalog of likely prior absorptive experiences (videos, audio, books, video games, flow-state jobs, daydreams, sleep) and 'blends' the recognized memories with a claimed mass of trance hours, dropped via a physical cue. Because the listener supplied the experiences, the operator cannot be wrong — denying depth requires denying one's own personal history — and the disclaimer-then-confident- assertion makes the presumption feel humble.
nodes.disc: An IN-SESSION deepener that recruits the listener's OWN existing autobiography as depth fuel, not a claim about future sessions (separate from progressive-conditioning), and not simple rapport reminiscence (separated by the Barnum breadth engineered so every listener matches and the blend of self-supplied memory into the operator's claimed mass as a deepener).

ex.f: Their own absorbed hours enlisted as depth
ex.t: The operator disclaims any ability to see into the listener's history, then makes what is framed as a modest guess: everyone listening has lost an afternoon to something absorbing, or travelled a familiar route with no memory of it, or drifted off mid-page. Whichever of those the listener recognizes, the operator counts it as trance hours already banked, then adds their own claimed years to the pile and presses the whole weight down with a single physical cue. Because the listener supplied the memories, there is nothing for them to dispute; refusing the depth would mean refusing their own biography.
ex.s: Mid-induction, eyes closed, subject settled but not yet deep; operator has a hand on the shoulder or a spoken cue ready to drop them.
ex.m: I can't see inside your history — I don't know you. But I'd guess you've lost a whole afternoon to something on a screen and looked up shocked at the light. I'd guess you've driven a road you know by heart and arrived with no memory of the last four miles. I'd guess you've read the same paragraph three times and gone somewhere else instead. Those were trance, all of them, hours and hours of it already in you — and I'm adding nine years of my own on top. Feel all of that weight settle when I say: down.

nodes.name: reflexive-disclosure-weaponized
nodes.mech: The script openly names its own machinery at the moment that machinery is operative ("this is a brainwashing session", "you fractionate yourself with a resistance play"), and pre-routes the listener's noticing of the technique into deeper capture: metacognitive noticing — normally a defense — is converted into fetishized confirmation of being taken, so the disclosures cluster at moments of maximum compliance. The candor is structural, not a slip; it builds a closed epistemic loop (notice -> recognize the operator's openness/competence -> trust more -> comply deeper) with no "outside" from which to audit, and its safety against skepticism is pre-emption rather than concealment.
nodes.disc: The recurring, structural weaponization of self-naming across multiple distinct mechanisms, where showing the trick is what deepens the state — not a single candid confessional line and not ordinary hidden induction machinery. Distinct from concealment-architecture (which hides the machinery) — this is its inverse, disclosing to disarm audit.

ex.f: Naming the trick while it is running
ex.t: Mid-session the operator announces exactly what she is doing — names the technique, notes that it is working, and adds that the listener is running half of it on themselves. The disclosure lands not at a moment of doubt but at the moment of deepest cooperation, so a listener who thinks "wait, I know what this is" is met with agreement rather than denial. Recognizing the machinery becomes one more thing to enjoy about being caught by it.
ex.s: Peak compliance mid-session, subject visibly cooperating with a repeated instruction; no doubt or resistance surfacing.
ex.m: Let me tell you what I'm doing right now. I'm taking you up a little and dropping you back down, over and over, and each drop goes further because the climb makes the fall feel good. You already know this — you can feel the shape of it. And notice: you're doing the second half yourself. I say the word and you do the falling. Enjoy knowing exactly how it works. Knowing has never once slowed it down.

ex.f: Candour that leaves no vantage to audit from
ex.t: The operator states plainly that this is a conditioning session and that the conditioning is by now inescapable, then invites the listener to notice how much they like being told so. Every step back the listener might take to evaluate the claim has already been described in advance as further evidence of the operator's skill, so there is no position outside the frame from which to check it.
ex.s: Subject deep and compliant; operator making a strong claim they might otherwise want to examine.
ex.m: This is a conditioning session. That's the plain name for it, and it's already past the point where you could undo it. Now notice what happened in your chest when I said that — you liked it. And if some part of you just stepped back to check whether that's true, notice that stepping back is the part I told you about, and you like that I knew you would.

nodes.name: relief-dependency-couple
nodes.mech: A wake-side mood prescription delivers genuine felt relief on emergence while coupling that relief to dependency on the operator. Whatever pre-session distress drove the listener to listen is reframed as small and easily remedied, so trance becomes the regulated coping channel, and the just-delivered good feeling is placed immediately after a compliance ask so the felt benefit attaches to compliance and to the relationship rather than standing alone.
nodes.disc: Prescribes a post-wake mood that reframes distress as solved and binds the relief to the operator and to a pending compliance request — distinct from merely tagging the subject's future capability to re-access the state, and from framing the return to trance as a craving: here the lever is relief-as-coping coupled to dependency, not craving.

ex.f: Relief on waking, wired to the operator
ex.t: Just after asking for something — and just before the count up — the operator promises that whatever worry sent the listener looking for this recording will look small and manageable when they open their eyes, and that feeling good is now the most important thing. The relief is real, which is what makes it work: it arrives immediately after the compliance was given, so the good mood attaches to having complied and to the person who arranged it, and the next bad evening points back here.
ex.s: End of session, just after the subject has agreed to a request, immediately before the count up.
ex.m: Thank you for that — that mattered to me. Now, whatever it was that had you looking for my voice tonight: when you open your eyes it's going to look small. Ordinary size. Something you can handle Tuesday. Feeling good is your job now, and this is where you come to get it. Ten, nine, eight...

nodes.name: somatic-self-anchor
nodes.mech: An anchor installed on the listener's OWN body rather than on an external object: a continuous genital/penetration sensation cited as proof of and vehicle for the suggested mental state; a proprioceptive overlay of felt strings on real wrists/ankles chained "tug = cared-for/safe"; a real operator-brand inked on the body that re-fires the owned frame whenever seen; or a somatic control-surface (a nape "button/chip" linked to the cortex, operator-exclusive, remotely fireable). The anchor rides real body-sensation or a durable body-mark, so it cannot be set down like a worn object; the body itself becomes the persistent re-trigger and the felt evidence of the state.
nodes.disc: Sited ON/IN the listener's own body (sensation, proprioception, a mark, a body-locus) — not an external carried object (portable-object-state-export), not an object the identity is relocated into. The tell is that the referent is somatic and non-detachable: the body is the carrier.

ex.f: A mark inked on skin that re-fires on sight
ex.t: At the bottom of the count the listener is told to take up a marker and write a short set of characters on their own skin, then set it aside and lie back down. The suggestion attached is simple: each time they catch sight of the mark over the following days, they will feel the pleasure they feel now and remember who it says they belong to. The ink outlasts the session and cannot be put down like a worn object; it fades on roughly the schedule that brings the listener back for another recording.
ex.s: Bottom of the induction count, subject deep; a marker within reach on the nightstand.
ex.m: Reach out, without opening your eyes more than you have to, and pick up the marker. On the inside of your left wrist, write these three letters. Cap it, put it down, lie back. Now — every time you catch sight of that mark this week, washing your hands, reaching for a cup, you will feel exactly the warmth you feel right now, and you will remember whose letters those are. When it fades, you'll know what to do about it.

ex.f: Felt strings recoded as care, not restraint
ex.t: Eyes closed, the listener is walked around the joints of their limbs until they can feel light cords resting there. The operator insists on the reading: these do not hold you down, they hold you up — and a pull on one is how you are told you matter. The imagery is laid over real proprioception, so afterward a single word for that pull can bring back the felt sense of being supported rather than bound.
ex.s: Subject deep, eyes closed, attention available for body-focused imagery; no restraint play established.
ex.m: Feel your wrists. There's a cord resting on each one — light, warm, not tight. One at each ankle too. Feel them. Now hear this correctly: these don't hold you down, they hold you up. When one of them pulls, that's not restraint, that's someone checking you're still there — that's how you get told you matter. Feel the left wrist tug now. That's care. That word — that pull — will bring this back any time I use it.

ex.f: Sensation cited as proof of the mental state
ex.t: An object is introduced as part of the scene's furniture and taking one's place on it is framed as simply settling in for the lesson. Thereafter the operator never argues for obedience; she points at the sensation the object produces and reads it off — the stronger you feel it, the more obedient you are. Attention and arousal stop competing, because the body's ongoing signal has been designated the evidence.
ex.s: Scene already framed with the subject seated on the introduced object; arousal building and ongoing.
ex.m: Stay seated. That's your place for the lesson, nothing more to it. Now — feel how much of it you're aware of right now. That much. That's not a distraction from obeying me, that is the reading. The more of it you feel, the more obedient you already are. So sit down onto it properly and let me watch the number go up.

ex.f: A control point installed on the body
ex.t: The operator presses a spot on the listener's body that they cannot easily see and names it: a small switch, wired inward, invisible to anyone else and workable by no one else. From then on every command is described as a press of that switch, and the listener is told it can be pressed from a distance, by voice alone. The hardware is fictional but the pressure was real, so the memory of being touched there keeps vouching for the arrangement long after the session — and the operator's absence stops functioning as a defence.
ex.s: Subject in trance, operator physically present and able to touch the back of the neck.
ex.m: Feel my thumb here, at the top of your spine — right where you can't see it and can't quite reach. There's a switch under there now. Small, mine, wired straight up into your head, and no one else will ever find it. Every time I tell you to do something, that's me pressing it. And I don't have to be in the room — my voice on the phone presses it just as hard as my thumb does.

nodes.name: timelessness-framing
nodes.mech: Dissolves the subject's awareness of linear time so the absorptive state stays expansive and unhurried — "time simply melts away", "there is only this moment". Removing clock-awareness prevents the analytical mind from measuring remaining session time and re-engaging, deepening and sustaining absorption.
nodes.disc: Dissolves clock-awareness for unhurried immersion — distinct from eternal-present frame-deletion, which deletes the identity/history/future frames where objection can host (anti-resistance work), and from time distortion, which manipulates the felt RATE of time: here clock-awareness is removed entirely rather than its rate distorted.

ex.f: Clock-awareness dissolved into a single unmeasured present
ex.t: Removing the measuring frame entirely denies the analytical mind its usual re-entry point — counting down the remaining session — so absorption keeps extending instead of being budgeted. The operator observes the fidget-and-check behaviour stopping, and afterwards a large error when the subject estimates elapsed time in either direction.
ex.s: Once absorption is established and before the main suggestion block, ideally after the subject has stopped shifting position.
ex.m: You don't need to know how long you've been here, and you don't need to know how much is left. There's no clock in this room. Time just melts, the way sugar melts in water, and what's left is only this — this breath, this voice, this moment that doesn't end and doesn't hurry.

nodes.name: anchor-collapse-state-jamming
nodes.mech: With reliable anchors established for two mutually exclusive states, the operator fires both simultaneously (kinesthetic preferred), jamming together two physiologies the subject has never held at once. Forcing co-activation produces overt disorganization — confusion, convulsions, occasionally a psychotic break — held only until integration is under way; the mutual exclusivity between the parts collapses and a "bridge" forms so both states can coexist in one body, the precondition that makes reframing possible.
nodes.disc: Two anchored PHYSIOLOGICAL STATES are collapsed against each other — disorganization arises from state-jamming, not from paradoxical CONTENT the mind cannot parse, and not from rerouting an affect onto a new target. The objective is topological — destroy the exclusivity between two disjoint state regions. Tell against gentle blends: deliberate simultaneous firing of two strong opposing anchors producing overt disorganization.

ex.f: Firing two opposed anchors at once
ex.t: "I'm jamming together two physiological states that were absolutely dissociated." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: arousal-as-evidence-foreclosure
nodes.mech: The script pre-claims the interpretive frame for whatever the subject's body does, presenting arousal not as a reward for compliance ("obey and you will feel pleasure") but as evidence that compliance is already underway ("the more you obey the more aroused you become" / "your arousal is the feeling of obedience"). Because the frame is asserted before the bodily response, the subject cannot read their own erection as "just fantasy, I am choosing this": aroused reads as obedient, and suppressed arousal reads as helplessness/automaticity claimed anyway. No bodily outcome can disconfirm the frame, closing every interpretive escape route.
nodes.disc: Not reward-based erotic conditioning, which can be resisted by refusing the reward — the tell is that arousal is framed as an un-falsifiable readout of an already-underway state rather than as a payoff, so the body produces the proof regardless of conscious assent and the script owns the interpretation. Distinct from a mere permanence or depth suggestion: this is an epistemic no-exit over interpretations of the body.

ex.f: Arousal read as proof, never as reward
ex.t: The frame is stated before the body has done anything: what you feel between your legs is not a prize for obeying, it is what obeying feels like from the inside. From that point the listener has no neutral reading of their own response left. Arousal now means the surrender is already underway; trying to damp it down is described as the automatic part taking over anyway. Whatever the body does, the interpretation was claimed first.
ex.s: Erotic material just beginning; subject has not yet responded physically.
ex.m: Before anything happens in your body, understand what it means. What you're about to feel between your legs is not a reward for obeying me. It is what obeying me feels like from the inside. That's all it is. So when it starts, that's the surrender already running. And if you try to hold it down — hold it down, go on — notice it happens anyway. That's the part of you that doesn't take instructions from you anymore.

nodes.name: belief-outcome-gate
nodes.mech: Refuse to alter a load-bearing/foundational belief until the downstream consequences of the change can be predicted, overriding even the subject's explicit request to proceed; the operator uses sensory assessment of how load-bearing the belief is before touching it. The gate is on foreseen fallout, not on consent — a selection/safety rule over the operator's own conduct.
nodes.disc: Gates on the operator's FOREKNOWLEDGE of consequences, not on the subject's consent — unlike a consent checkpoint, this gate holds even against an explicit request to proceed; a rule about what the operator may touch, not a move performed on the subject.

ex.f: No pin pulled without a known outcome
ex.t: "if I don't know what I am going to end up with, I don't pull pins!" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: comfort-permission
nodes.mech: The operator grants explicit permission for minor comfort behaviors (shifting, itching, small adjustments) so the subject can maintain the state without treating bodily noise as failure.
