nodes.disc: Depth is chosen to match the target material's original encoding state (retrieval-keyed depth) — distinct from a false-bottom deepener (which intensifies state for its own sake), from numerical counting deepening (a delivery form, not a depth TARGET), and from amnesia installation (here the amnesia already exists, and depth is navigated to reach material encoded inside that window). With no state-bound target the escalation has nothing to unlock.

ex.f: Going deeper to reach a state-bound memory
ex.t: "I decided to get the woman into a much deeper phase of hypnosis. I call this phase hypno-sleep ... It was in this deep state of hypnosis that I had the patient relive her experiences as she was being taken to the operating room." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

nodes.name: description-as-installation-register
nodes.mech: The operator speaks about the listener in the third person ("the persona," "she") and describes her responses as ongoing accomplished facts, never addressing her as "you" and never issuing a second-person command. This sidesteps the listener's normal command-evaluation interface — a listener can refuse a command but cannot refuse a description of a self she is already inside — and positions her as overhearing her own conditioning, which is itself mildly dissociative. The install lands as reportage of what is already true rather than as an instruction to be weighed.
nodes.disc: The tell is the systematic zero-occurrence of second-person "you" across the whole file, with the listener rendered as a described third-person object whose responses are stated as facts. Distinct from ordinary persona voice (which still commands in second person) and from dissociative-distance deepeners (which move the listener's vantage but keep addressing her). It is the REGISTER — describe-don't-command — that is the lever, not any single line.

ex.f: Described in the third person, never addressed
ex.t: Nothing in the recording is aimed at "you." The operator talks about the listener instead, in the third person and in the present tense, as a matter of record: she settles easily now, she doesn't hold on to thoughts any more, she likes the sound of that word. Over a whole file the pronoun that would let the listener answer never appears once. There is no command to weigh, so the ordinary reflex of accepting or declining an instruction never fires — and refusing a description of yourself that you are apparently already living out has no obvious grammar. It also seats the listener slightly outside herself, overhearing her own conditioning being discussed by someone else.
ex.s: Mid-session, any point after settling; the operator has not used the word "you" once and will not.
ex.m: She's settled now — her breathing has gone slow without her arranging it. She doesn't hold on to thoughts the way she used to; they arrive, and she lets them go past. And she likes the sound of that word. She likes it more each time it's said near her.

nodes.name: dissociative-memory-vault
nodes.mech: Builds a persistent in-trance dissociative custodian construct — a personified reflection, inner self, or vault — assigned the role of safekeeping trance content, framed as retrievable any time. The payload is a deposit-only asymmetry: the construct only ever stores, there is no scripted retrieval ceremony, so trance content is kept out of conscious access under cover of a safety promise the script never honors, and the construct becomes load-bearing scaffolding for later installs.
nodes.disc: A persistent personified custodian/vault stores trance content with an unhonored retrieval promise (deposit-only asymmetry) as the payload. Unlike an observer-responder split (an awareness partition for felt automaticity), this is an external storage construct; unlike a direct amnesia suggestion (amnesia as an end-state), the lever is a custodian construct with a false availability promise; unlike externalizing a faculty into a construct, what is stored here is memory content, not a faculty.

ex.f: A custodian that only ever takes deposits
ex.t: The listener is asked to picture a mirror, and the figure in it is named as the part of them that exists only here, in trance. That figure is given a job: to hold everything that happens in the session, kept safe, available whenever they want it back. Because retrieval sounds guaranteed, handing things over feels like tidying rather than losing, so resistance to going deeper drops. The tell is what never comes: no later passage ever asks for anything back. The construct has one direction of travel, and the promise of retrieval is what makes the one-way trip acceptable.
ex.s: Late induction, depth established; subject has just been walked into a still, enclosed image.
ex.m: There's a mirror in front of you, and the one looking back only exists in here, with me. She's going to hold things for you. Everything that happens from here — every word, every feeling — hand it to her as it comes, and she'll keep it safe for you, and you can have any of it back whenever you want it. Give her the last five minutes now. Good girl.

nodes.name: endurance-compliance-strain
nodes.mech: Voluntary physical strain is reframed as deepening — "the harder you push, the deeper you fall" — so effort-on-resistance is transmuted into effort-toward-depth. The broadened form runs it as a body-part progression staircase (feet through face, each cycle "clench hard, hold, let go", asserting looser on each release), producing two simultaneous deltas: somatic (the listener is literally drained, so later low-effort instructions feel easy by contrast) and compliance (a run of ~12 micro-commands obeyed in a row establishes an obedience groove before any payload content).
nodes.disc: The core is the classic strain-as-deepening move, widened from a single held posture into a full-body compliance-groove protocol. Unlike progressive relaxation (pure relaxation absorption), the tension/release here is an obedience drill with effort reframed as deepening; and though a command-response micro-drill is present, that run is a co-present component, not the primary lever.

ex.f: Clench-and-release drill as an obedience groove
ex.t: Feet, calves, thighs, belly, chest, arms, jaw — at each stop the same three beats: tighten everything as tight as it will go, hold it there, now drop it, and notice how much looser that leaves you than before. The instruction that carries the mechanism is the one attached to the effort: push harder and you sink further, so straining is not resistance to the process, it is the process. By the time the whole-body rounds are done the listener is genuinely wrung out, which makes anything asked next feel weightless by comparison — and they have also just complied with a dozen small orders in a row before a single word of content has arrived.
ex.s: Induction body, subject lying down; the strain-equals-depth premise is being stated for the first time on the first body part.
ex.m: Start at your feet — curl the toes and squeeze them as hard as you can. Harder. The harder you push, the further down you go. Hold it, hold it — and drop. Feel how much looser that is than before. Now your calves: tight as they'll go, harder than the feet, hold — and drop. Thighs next.

nodes.name: negative-reinforcement-escape-compliance
nodes.mech: Make TERMINATION (escape) or prevention (avoidance) of an already-present aversive condition contingent on a target response: the subject raises the response to turn the aversive off or keep it from onset, and the reinforcer is the RELIEF itself, not an added reward. Severity scales effort (relief from a strong aversive can outweigh a comparable positive reward). The operator selects WHAT aversive the response escapes. REALIZATIONS by aversive source: (escape-from-aversive-reinforcement) the base case — a pre-existing aversive the response terminates/prevents; (escape-based-compliance) make the INSTRUCTION itself aversive by escalating instructional pressure (prompts, re-issue, error-correction) on non-response, so complying brings relief (the operator may run this without recognizing it); (aversive-antecedent-contingency) open a mild social-aversive interval (awkwardness, a pending obligation to respond) that responding terminates and not-responding worsens, compliance experienced as escape; (coercive-demand-form-selection) cast the want as a COMMAND supplemented with an added aversive whose removal negatively reinforces compliance — the coercive pole of demand-form selection (defined by the backing contingency, not the imperative grammar; the willing-listener pole is a praise-reinforced request with no aversive).
nodes.disc: Reach for NEGATIVE REINFORCEMENT / ESCAPE COMPLIANCE when the response is maintained by RELIEF from an already-present aversive (the response turns it off or prevents it), not by an added reward. Choose it over: positive reinforcement (adds a reward — here nothing is added, an aversive is removed); punishment (reduces a behavior — this INCREASES the target response by relieving an aversive); response-cost / time-out (subtract or withhold a positive — here an aversive is added-then-escaped). The realizations differ only by the aversive SOURCE (a pre-existing aversive / escalating instructional pressure / a social-awkwardness interval / an aversive backing a command). Often unrecognized — the operator may believe they are reinforcing positively while running an escape contingency.

ex.f: The response turns the aversive off
ex.t: "consists of the removal or termination of an aversive condition that is already present." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: exit-annexation
nodes.mech: The frame's one genuine structural off-ramp is pre-licensed — even encouraged, with real harm-reduction content — and simultaneously absorbed into the frame itself, so that TAKING the exit is scripted as an expression of the same submission ("keeping mistress's property safe", "it will still please me"). The subject retains a fully real safety license while losing it as a frame-break: no available action, including the exit action, lands outside the frame, because the frame has annexed its own exit. The safety content is genuinely necessary and genuinely delivered — the capture is semantic (what using the exit MEANS), not material.
nodes.disc: The exit is expected to be USED and remains materially real; what is captured is its meaning — using it reads as in-frame service. Unlike an agency reminder, which affirms the exit as a frame-EXTERNAL standing power, here the safety content is delivered inside the frame and sealed into it. Unlike a granted-exit disarm, where the exit is granted so it will NOT be used, here use is anticipated and recoded. And unlike ownership language, which installs the proprietary identity claim (the host frame this move presupposes), this is the weld fusing the off-ramp into that already-running ownership frame.

ex.f: Using the safety exit recoded as service
ex.t: The safety instruction is real and is delivered properly: check the sizing, don't leave it on too long, and if anything feels wrong, take it off — that permission is never withdrawn. What is added is a single clause about what taking it off means. Doing so is looking after something that belongs to the operator, so it pleases her too. The listener keeps a fully working off-ramp and loses the only thing the off-ramp was structurally good for: there is now no action available, including quitting, that lands outside the frame.
ex.s: Post-session care instructions for a worn item the subject has been given; the item is real and the safety content is genuine.
ex.m: Check the fit with two fingers underneath — if it pinches, if anything goes numb, if it just feels wrong, take it straight off. That instruction never expires. And understand what you're doing when you take it off: you're looking after something of mine. That pleases me too. There's no way to wear it and no way to remove it that isn't you serving me.

nodes.name: fabricated-memory-trigger-rehearsal
nodes.mech: Installs a forward cue-response by narrating fabricated autobiographical memories that all rehearse the SAME trigger-collapse shape (a mundane act, then a snap/trigger, then instant collapse). The operator pre-frames that all the subject's memories now have this shape, so the next real trigger feels like the hundred-and-first occurrence rather than the first. Routing the conditioning through fabricated recollection — rehearsal-by-memory rather than direct suggestion — means the response is never experienced as a suggestion at all, making it harder to detect or counter. The false memories are additive rehearsal evidence, not concealment of anything.
nodes.disc: Separates from screen-memory fabrication, which fabricates memory to conceal or replace a real one — here the fabricated memories conceal nothing and instead install a forward-facing conditioned response. Separates from plain trigger installation and from future pacing by the vehicle: the cue-response is pre-loaded as autobiographical evidence (a rehearsed past), so it is felt as recollection, not as an installed suggestion or an imagined future.

ex.f: Invented memories rehearsing the same collapse
ex.t: The operator narrates a run of small scenes as though recalling them for the listener: standing at the counter, riding the lift, waiting in the hall — and each one ends the same way, a sharp sound, a word, and everything going soft and blank. Then the frame is set over the top: every memory you have takes that shape now. The next time the cue actually fires, it will not be a first response to a new suggestion; it will feel like the hundredth repetition of something already habitual, which is exactly why it will be hard to argue with. Nothing here is phrased as an instruction — it is phrased as the listener's own past — so there is no suggestion on the table to decline.
ex.s: Mid-session, trance established, before the trigger word is formally set; delivered in a light reminiscing tone.
ex.m: Remember standing at the counter waiting for your coffee, and someone behind you clicked their fingers, and everything went soft and white and you just stood there? And the lift last winter — the doors chimed and you were gone before the second floor. Every memory you have has that shape in it now. It's just what happens to you. It always has been.

nodes.name: fictional-anatomy-bypass-split
nodes.mech: Invents a fictional partition of the subject's own anatomy or cognition — a "third ear connected to another part of your brain", a front/back-brain divide, a non-motor "mental channel" — and uses it to license the claim that subsequent instructions bypass conscious filtering, with surface objections pre-flagged as "wrong-part processing". Often paired with an authorship-disclaimer that offloads the dissociation onto the listener ("I don't know what that means, but I think you do") and a voice-flip to direct command, so the operator carries no liability for what the fictional channel receives.
nodes.disc: A FICTIONAL anatomical/channel partition is manufactured specifically to license bypass and pre-route objections, typically with a liability-offloading authorship-disclaimer. vs evaluator-offline-channel (takes a real evaluator offline; here the channel itself is invented as the bypass license); vs channel-partitioned-monitoring (routes output across real cognitive levels; here the fictional anatomy plus disclaimer is the tell).

ex.f: An invented channel licenses the bypass
ex.t: With both ears described as packed and useless, the operator introduces a third one, wired somewhere else entirely — then adds, lightly, that they have no idea what that means, but the listener surely does. The room is then split in two: the front of the mind can keep listening if it likes, everything from here is addressed to the back. From that point any objection the listener raises can be dismissed as the front part talking, and the voice hardens from suggestion into plain instruction. The disclaimer is doing real work as well — by not claiming to understand the split, the operator makes it the listener's own invention.
ex.s: After an auditory-saturation deepener; both ears have been described as full and useless.
ex.m: Both of your ears are packed solid now — nothing gets through them. So I'm speaking to the third one, the one wired somewhere further back. I don't actually know what that means. I think you do. The front of your mind can stay where it is and keep listening if it wants; everything from here is for the back. Anything that argues with me is just the front part talking. Ignore it. Back of your mind: open.

nodes.name: counterconditioning-and-cue-response-weakening
nodes.mech: Weaken an aversive or interfering stimulus's control over a response by pairing/training an INCOMPATIBLE state or response against it, or by severing the cue-to-response link — so a stimulus that used to evoke fear/refusal/an unwanted behavior stops doing so.
nodes.disc: Reach for COUNTERCONDITIONING / CUE-RESPONSE WEAKENING when a specific stimulus reliably evokes an aversive or interfering RESPONSE (fear, refusal reflex, an automatic behavior) and you want that stimulus to stop evoking it — by graded approach under an incompatible state, a competing response rehearsed under arousal, or decoupling the cue from the response. Choose it over: extinction (removes a reinforcer maintaining an OPERANT — here the target is an elicited/occasion-set response, and the cue's own charge may be left intact); DRI (reinforces an incompatible competitor via consequences — here the lever is a paired incompatible STATE or a trained noticing, graded to the eliciting stimulus); relaxation/absorption inductions (which ride a calm state to build absorption from baseline — here the aversive state is deliberately contacted/raised and displaced). Facets differ by graded-exposure vs sub-threshold-property-fade vs evoke-then-compete vs notice-and-let-pass.

ex.f: A real-world approach ladder from a safe anchor
ex.t: "You're sitting in a comfortable chair in the safety of your home…" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Relaxation held against a graded fear hierarchy
ex.t: "relax while imagining these anxiety-producing situations, first the least fearful… then the next" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: image-agnostic-access-backdoor
nodes.mech: Installs a persistent-control schema decoupled from any specific image — a self-reinstalling backdoor any later cue can re-trigger — so the listener accepts ongoing waking-world access, not just this session. A tentacle entering the ear branches into a million tentacles wiring into every nerve, declared to give the operator a rewrite-connection "at a moment's notice" and future-proofed across any later image (webs, mist, the voice itself); arousal is bound to the connection so it feels pleasurable rather than invasive.
nodes.disc: Explicit image-agnostic future-proofing ("the connection will always be there", re-triggerable by any later cue) makes it a durable cross-session backdoor rather than scene-dressing. It is not a specific cue-response trigger — the backdoor is deliberately cue-agnostic, re-openable by any later image — and unlike total-permeation framing, which describes conditioning spreading through internal layers in the present tense, this installs an ongoing waking-world re-access channel.

ex.f: A connection that survives any later image
ex.t: Something thin is described entering the ear and then dividing again and again until it has reached every nerve, and the operator states what that gives them: the ability to rewrite anything, whenever they choose. Then comes the clause that makes it durable rather than scenic — next time it might not look like this at all; it might be threads, or fog, or nothing but this voice, and it will be the same connection regardless. Nothing has been tied to a cue, which is the point: no particular image is required to reopen it, so there is nothing specific for the listener to later stop responding to. Arousal is welded on top so that the permanence registers as something to want.
ex.s: Deep trance, an invasive-imagery scene already running; the cue-agnostic clause is the payload being landed.
ex.m: Feel it slip into your ear and split — twice, then a thousand times, then a million, until there's a thread of me on every nerve you have. That's a connection, and it means I can rewrite anything in you the moment I decide to. Next time it might not be tendrils at all. It might be webs, or mist, or just my voice — doesn't matter. Same connection, always open, and feel how good it is that it doesn't close.

nodes.name: operator-gated-descent
nodes.mech: Converts passive relaxation into operator-gated release by explicitly forbidding an already-underway drop until the operator grants permission ("don't fall too quickly, don't fall until I tell you to"). Two effects run together: it trains the subject to take cadence from the operator rather than their own state, installing a permission-seeking baseline from minute one; and the held-back drop accumulates potential energy that discharges sharper than natural drift when finally released, priming a harder discharge at the later abrupt Sleep and countdown.
nodes.disc: An explicit prohibition on a drop the subject has ALREADY begun, with permission to descend deferred to the operator — depth is granted, not achieved. Separates from plain fractionation, which deepens via a brief waking interval, and from an asymmetric state-lock, which gates EXIT from an installed state, whereas this gates ENTRY/descent.

ex.f: Forbidden to drop until permission is given
ex.t: Ten lines in, the listener has already started to slide — and the operator stops it: not yet, hold there, you don't go down until I say. The same hold is reimposed later, so the listener spends the early minutes actively suppressing something their body was doing on its own. Two things are being taught at once. The cadence is no longer theirs to set, and depth arrives as something granted rather than something reached. When the release finally comes, the drop is sharper than any drift would have been, because it has been held under pressure the whole time.
ex.s: Roughly ten lines into the induction; subject has visibly begun to slide on their own.
ex.m: I can hear that starting — stop. Not yet. You don't go down until I tell you to, so hold yourself right there, right at the top of it. I know it wants to pull. Let it pull and don't move. You'll go when I say, and not one second before.

nodes.name: physiological-state-depth-relabeling
nodes.mech: A strong physiological arousal-cycle state is relabeled as trance depth so the body's own process drives descent. In the ascending form, continuous masturbation is declared to BE the induction — "the more pleasure you feel, the deeper you go" — so arousal-up and depth-up become indistinguishable and there is no separable induction to remove. In the refractory form, the post-orgasm crash is narrated as a vertical plummet so climax becomes an entry into deeper trance rather than a terminal payoff.
nodes.disc: Depth is asserted to be a direct function of a physiological state the listener is already producing — not an operator command to drop, and not conditioning of arousal to a cue; the physiology is the vehicle, not the target.

ex.f: Arousal declared to be the descent itself
ex.t: There is no relaxation sequence and no focal object. The operator simply has the listener begin touching themselves, and then names what that is doing: every stroke takes you further down, and the better it feels the deeper you are. Because the listener is producing the state with their own hand, the descent is self-administered and self-sustaining — and because the two readings have been fused, there is no longer any way to tell "I'm aroused" apart from "I'm under."
ex.s: Opening of the session — no relaxation sequence, no fixation object; the subject has been told to begin touching themselves.
ex.m: Start touching yourself now, slowly, and keep going the whole time I'm talking. Every stroke is a step down — that's what your hand is doing tonight, it's taking you under. The better it feels, the deeper you are. There's no difference between the two any more. Faster is deeper.

ex.f: The post-orgasm crash narrated as falling
ex.t: Climax is permitted, and the words laid over the seconds immediately after it are all vertical: let go of everything, let it all sink, drop the way a stone drops through water, as if the floor had simply been removed. The refractory softening the listener would have felt anyway is thereby given a name, and the name is depth. The usual order is inverted — the orgasm is not the reward at the end of the trance, it is the entrance to the deepest part of it.
ex.s: Immediately post-orgasm; permission was given seconds ago and the subject is in the first moments of refractory softening.
ex.m: That's it — now let go of all of it. Feel everything come loose at once and just sink; drop like a stone going down through water, straight down, no bottom to it. The floor's gone. That wasn't the end of it. That was the door, and you've just fallen through it into the deepest part of tonight.

nodes.name: prosodic-meter-as-covert-deepener
nodes.mech: A whole-script formal property in which the entire body is delivered in unbroken metrical verse (AABB couplets, consistent syllable count) with no cadence shift between induction, work, and wake. The verse form itself runs a continuous low-effort deepener: every rhyme is a micro predict-then-confirm cycle compounding across the whole piece, and meter/rhyme-tracking consumes the same attentional bandwidth needed for critical evaluation, so arguing with a suggestion requires mentally breaking the verse. Content and triggers placed on rhyme-closures land with reduced scrutiny, and the uninterrupted meter lets topical pivots pass without an audible seam. The carrier is the form, not any single line.
nodes.disc: Separates from attentional-saturation quieting, which saturates attention with an object or task: this uses PROSODIC PREDICTION (rhyme/meter) as the continuous entrainment and evaluation-suppression carrier, and cannot be pinned to any single line, because removing the verse form removes the deepening every per-line move rides on. Not decorative verse — trigger landings and the climax cue are deliberately placed on rhyme-closures.

ex.f: Triggers landed on the rhyme-closures
ex.t: The couplets are not just carrying the piece, they are being aimed. Each trigger phrase is positioned as the second half of a rhyme pair, so the listener's ear is already reaching for the sound when the payload arrives inside it, and the arrival feels like completion rather than instruction. The same uninterrupted metre lets the recording turn from drowsy imagery to explicit content without any audible seam — nothing announces the change, so it registers as the poem continuing rather than as a new topic being introduced.
ex.s: Trigger install, mid-piece, in the same unbroken couplet form; the cue word must land in the second-line rhyme slot.
ex.m: And when I say the word, you'll come undone, / your thinking simply stops when I say — done. / The counting done, the mind agreeably bare, / your hand has drifted somewhere warmer there.

ex.f: Unbroken verse as a continuous deepener
ex.t: Every line of the recording, from the first breath to the wake-up, is a ten-syllable line rhyming in pairs, with no prose anywhere and no change of cadence when the induction becomes the work or the work becomes the ending. The form is doing the deepening for free: each rhyme is a tiny prediction that arrives on time, and two hundred small confirmations in a row is a considerable amount of entrainment that the operator never has to spend a line asking for. It also occupies exactly the faculty a listener would need in order to disagree — to push back on a suggestion you have to drop out of the metre, and dropping out of the metre is effortful in a way that going along with it is not. No single passage can be quoted as the mechanism, because the mechanism is the fact that no passage breaks.
ex.s: Any point in a piece written entirely in ten-syllable rhyming couplets; the cadence does not change here, and does not change anywhere.
ex.m: The counting slows, the shoulders settle down, / your breathing finds a softer, slower sound; / there's nothing here that asks you to decide, / just let the metre carry you inside.

nodes.name: proximity-deepening
nodes.mech: Depth is coupled to shrinking spatial distance between the subject and an approaching stimulus or the operator — each increment of approach deepens the state, with release or maximal depth at contact. Demonstrated forms include an inbound light narrated as a felt countdown releasing into sleep at contact, and the operator's approaching footsteps binding per-step deepening fused to a fixation object; classic forms — a voice drawing closer, a chime approaching, a snap appearing closer with each snap — fit the same shape.
nodes.disc: The depth-driver is proximity change in the dyad, not the subject's own imagined descent (a staircase) and not a bare numeric timer (a countdown) — where a countdown structure is present it rides ON the approach vector. Fusing the approach to a fixation object is a combination with object-fixation, not a separate mechanism.

ex.f: An approaching light as a felt countdown
ex.t: The operator tracks something bright on its way in — past the moon, into the upper air, through the cloud layer, closer with every clause, down and down toward the listener. Nothing counts and nothing is numbered, but the shrinking distance does the work of a countdown the listener can feel tightening. At contact the accumulated expectation is discharged in three words: it touches you, and you sleep.
ex.s: Induction proper; subject's eyes closed, attention placed on a point of light far overhead.
ex.m: There's a light above you and it's coming down. It's past the moon now. Now it's through the high cold air, now it's below the cloud, and it's getting bigger every time I speak — closer, closer, close enough to feel on your face. It touches you. Sleep.

ex.f: Walking toward the operator as the deepener
ex.t: The listener is walked along a corridor toward a door at the far end, and the walking itself is named as the deepener — not scenery, not something happening while the deepening happens, but the thing that does it. Each step forward is therefore two things at once: further under, and further into compliance. Refusing to keep walking is the only way to stop going deeper, and refusing to keep walking means stepping out of the scene entirely.
ex.s: Mid-induction, imagined-scene deepener; subject is standing in a corridor with a door at the far end.
ex.m: There's a door at the end of the corridor and I'm behind it. Start walking. The walking is what takes you down — not the corridor, not the door, the steps themselves. Every step forward is deeper and every step forward is more mine. Keep coming. You only stop going down by stopping walking, and you're not going to do that.

ex.f: Each approaching footstep binds to depth
ex.t: The listener is left immobilised in the scene, and then footsteps start — unhurried, getting nearer. Each one is tied to depth: the operator narrates her own approach as the thing doing the sinking, one pace at a time. Here the depth-driver is not anything the listener does but the operator's proximity, so the state now rises and falls with how close she is rather than with the listener's effort. The attention is simultaneously pinned to the footwear making the sound, welding the fixation object and the deepener into one thing.
ex.s: Subject already immobilised in the scene and unable to turn; a fixation object (the operator's heels) is being introduced by sound.
ex.m: You can't turn around, so just listen. Those are my heels on the floor behind you — hear them? Every step I take toward you takes you down another layer. Nothing you do moves you now; I do. Closer. Deeper. Keep your attention on the sound of them and count me in.

nodes.name: scope-coupled-depth-titration
nodes.mech: A hypnotic phenomenon's scope is coupled to the trance depth required to sustain it — a partial anesthesia or partial amnesia holds in light trance, but requesting the same phenomenon totally does not fail; it involuntarily recruits deeper trance to sustain the wider scope. The operator can therefore titrate depth by widening or narrowing the requested scope.
nodes.disc: Overreach produces DEEPENING rather than collapse — the depth change is a structural consequence of scope, not an operator command (drop-command) and not a failed suggestion.

ex.f: Widening the scope drags the depth along
ex.t: "Any effort to have a total amnesia resulted in a progression toward a deep trance" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

nodes.name: self-perpetuating-offline-loop
nodes.mech: The whole architecture aims at unsupervised nightly self-execution: every major mechanism feeds a loop — self-recitation, a carried in-dream trigger, a removed exit, voice re-injection, and a morning write-it-down ritual externalizing reinforcement — bookended by "every single night" and "you're going to dream for me", with no release or exit anywhere. The loop is the relationship between the install-moments and the deliberate absence of any close; the deliverable is recurring autonomous operation when the operator is absent, not a single bounded trance.
nodes.disc: No single line constitutes the loop; it is visible only across the whole arc by noticing nothing ever closes and every mechanism feeds re-execution. Distinct from an ordinary post-hypnotic suggestion or a single trigger install (bounded, has an exit) — here exit-removal plus re-injection make the trajectory non-terminating by design.

ex.f: Every mechanism feeds the next night's run
ex.t: Read line by line, the piece looks like a set of ordinary installs. Read whole, every one of them points the same way: something the listener recites to themselves, a cue that only fires once they are asleep, a rewritten waking that lands them back inside instead of out, the operator's voice reappearing whenever the cue does, and a morning ritual of writing down what happened, which turns their own notebook into the reinforcement schedule. The opening establishes that this is a thing done nightly, the closing hands the sleeping hours over to the operator, and in between there is no release, no count up, no point at which anything is declared finished. That absence is the mechanism — nothing terminates, so the next iteration needs no operator present to start it.
ex.s: Closing minutes of a piece with no wake-up; the nightly frame was set at the top and every earlier install pointed here.
ex.m: Every single night, this is what you do. You'll say the words to yourself as you're falling asleep, and when you're under my voice comes back on its own, and the cue works better in dreams than it ever does awake. When you seem to wake up in the morning, that's part of it too — write down everything you remember before you get out of bed, and read it back tonight. Tonight you're going to dream for me. There's no counting up. There's just tomorrow.

nodes.name: antecedent-manipulation
nodes.mech: Change a response by editing the ANTECEDENT rather than manipulating consequences, with the behavior's function already known — edit the situation upstream so there is nothing to escape / nothing to want / no cue / no way to respond, with NO consequence ever applied (requires operator control of the antecedent variable). CORE LEVERS: (1) neutralize an aversive task antecedent (add a manipulable strategy, reduce difficulty, fade demands, errorless procedures) so the task stops carrying aversive value and escape-maintained behavior abates; (2) dissolve the motivating operation directly (make the avoided thing non-aversive) so the behavior's value drops; (3) remove the discriminative stimulus that cues the behavior so its occasion stops arising; (4) remove the stimuli/materials a competing behavior requires (discard cigarettes, clear all food) during a low-urge window. ABSORBED FACETS: (initiating-cue-substitution) don't just remove the SD — SWAP it for a different initiating cue that sets a PREFERRED chain in motion (ashtray -> TV remote), so the same context triggers an alternative sequence; (competing-reinforcer-removal) reduce/eliminate RIVAL reinforcers in the setting beforehand (cartoons) so the operator's reinforcer gains relative value and the target's salience rises for uncontested differential reinforcement; (antecedent-summation-competition) do ARITHMETIC on controlling variables — combine individually-insufficient antecedents so their additive effect crosses the evocation threshold to EVOKE a response no single antecedent could, or introduce a competing rival MO/SD to SUPPRESS by disrupting the controlling variable; (physical-topography-preclusion) make the response topography MECHANICALLY unavailable before it can occur (pre-emptive hold / antecedent restraint, noncontingent protective equipment, self-restraint) so rate drops to near zero with motivation and the maintaining contingency left intact — that noncontingent equipment works shows prevention, not punishment, carries it.
nodes.disc: Reach for ANTECEDENT MANIPULATION when you can change behavior by EDITING THE SITUATION UPSTREAM (remove/swap the cue, dissolve the MO, remove enabling materials, mechanically preclude the motor act, or do arithmetic on controlling variables) with NO consequence applied. Choose it over: extinction / punishment (which act on CONSEQUENCES after the response — this leaves nothing to consequate); DRI / initiating a competitor via reinforcement (consequence-side — the cue-substitution facet swaps the ANTECEDENT instead). Direction note: most facets SUPPRESS by removing an evoking condition, but antecedent-summation can also EVOKE (combine sub-threshold antecedents to cross threshold); mechanical-preclusion removes the motor possibility itself (vs suggested inability, which is a present-state move, not an antecedent edit).

ex.f: Remove what the behavior needs to happen
ex.t: "ridding oneself of the items needed to engage in an undesired behavior is a good start" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Make the task non-aversive, escape loses value
ex.t: "problem behavior by all participants was reduced simply by making specific modifications to the instructional methods, without modifying the demands… by making the tasks less difficult and, thus, unpairing task demands with aversive properties" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: belief-gate-contingent-yoking
nodes.mech: After a bypass has lowered the critical faculty, the operator asserts one proposition wholeheartedly ("you will feel nothing") and binds its truth to the continuation of an act the subject is already sustaining via "so long as" grammar ("so long as you keep pretending you can't open your eyes, you will feel nothing"). Because whatever is believed without doubt becomes operative reality under a downed critical faculty, and the conditional attaches the payload to an ongoing behavior, maintaining the behavior automatically maintains the effect with no separate effort or re-suggestion — absence of doubt, not trance depth, is the load-bearing variable.
nodes.disc: Separates from a plain once-delivered post-hypnotic suggestion because the "so long as X" contingent yoking makes the effect ride on an ongoing act; separates from future-pacing, which points a suggestion at a LATER occasion, whereas this binds it to a behavior running RIGHT NOW; and separates from compliance-loop language — the loop here is belief-operative-reality yoked to a sustained behavior, not compliance-to-reward momentum.

ex.f: One belief yoked to an ongoing act
ex.t: "So long as you keep pretending that you can't open your eyes, you will feel nothing... I have established selective thinking while your critical faculty was inoperative, and the result is complete anesthesia." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

nodes.name: response-cost-token-economy
nodes.mech: Suppress a behavior by SUBTRACTING, contingent on it, a quantum of a reinforcer the subject ALREADY possesses (tokens, slips, earned minutes) — a negative-punishment (subtractive) economy. The atomic move plus the preconditions and parameters that keep it operating and motivationally intact. CORE EVENT (response-cost-fine): a per-response debit of an already-held, genuinely-valued reinforcer; immediacy is load-bearing (delay degrades it); it suppresses without building any replacement. PRECONDITIONS/PARAMETERS (bounded-response-cost-contingency-design): first STOCKPILE a withdrawable reserve (you cannot fine someone with nothing to lose); scale each fine to infraction magnitude and announce the schedule in ADVANCE; prohibit debt / keep earnings net-positive so the token never acquires net-aversive value; provision the reserve above baseline occurrence (~baseline-mean+25%) so it cannot be exhausted mid-session; thin reinforcement density gradually across multiple axes; a self-directed form pre-commits a concrete penalty per future failure. PARAMETER FACETS: (fine-magnitude-calibration) size each fine inside a two-sided window whose non-obvious constraint is the UPPER bound — a reserve-depletion ceiling, since over-fining inverts the effect (a drained subject gives up); (bonus-pool-loss-substrate) drain a pre-loaded noncontingent WINDFALL pool while walling off earned holdings, softening emotional fallout; (pre-stated-refusal-penalty) pre-announce an escalating penalty on NON-SURRENDER to close the 'I won't give it back' counter-move; (operator-custodied-enforcement-medium) keep the enforcement medium (ledger/tokens) outside the subject's control so the penalty is enacted by operator bookkeeping, removing the refuse-to-pay option; (attention-leakage-ratio-neutralization) keep reinforcer DELIVERIES well above loss-notifications so the loss-mark does not itself function as reinforcing attention.
nodes.disc: Reach for RESPONSE-COST / TOKEN ECONOMY when suppression should work by SUBTRACTING a reinforcer the subject ALREADY HOLDS, per instance. Choose it over: removal-from-reinforcement / time-out (which WITHHOLDS a not-yet-earned reward or removes access to reinforcement, rather than debiting held property); differential reinforcement (which pays an alternative/absence, not debits the target); aversive-antecedent contingencies (which ADD a bad state escaped by compliance — this builds and depletes a POSITIVE reserve as the suppression currency). The absorbed facets are the parameters of one economy: reserve-first precondition, magnitude upper-bound, loss-substrate, refusal-penalty, operator custody, and loss-notification-ratio guard.

ex.f: Provision the pool above baseline so it cannot run dry
ex.t: "increase the number of reinforcers 25% above the mean number of occurrences during baseline... mean number of disruptions per day is 20... establish 25 minutes of free time" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Stockpile a reserve before you can fine it
ex.t: "Positive reinforcers cannot be removed from a person who does not have any... the practitioner must ensure a sufficient reinforcer reserve" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: No debt: earnings must stay net-positive
ex.t: "Token loss should never be applied to a behavior if the learner does not have tokens. Students should not be allowed to go into debt... A learner should always earn more tokens than she loses." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Pre-commit the penalty before the failure
ex.t: "Do 50 sit-ups at 11:00 pm on Sundays for each day that I did not practice" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: count-up-return
nodes.mech:
The clean exit: regulates the trance state back toward genuine waking baseline by a graded, operator-led progression whose defining move is depth reduction — absorption is stepped down until ordinary orientation returns, with NO payload carried, NO charge escalated, and NO exit foreclosed (contrast the weaponized emergence entries). One technique across interchangeable return CHANNELS/surfaces, selected by register and modality:
- COUNTED count-up (canonical): the numbered ramp ("1... 2... 3... more awake"), or an equivalent reversal of the descent metaphor (an operator gesture removing the input, a symmetric re-traversal of the built architecture in reverse, a valve-drain).
- STEPWISE full ramp (absorbed ex-'exit-protocol'): a structured multi-step reorientation delivered IN-state — count-up + breath + body orientation + eyes-open + look-around — the composite bundling of the channels below into one guided ascent.
- SENSORY-ENUMERATION sweep (absorbed ex-'reorientation-sweep'): re-grounds by sweeping awareness through three-or-more external/orientation categories (room, sounds, time-of-day, body weight/position), each anchor checked and cleared — the tell is systematic multi-category enumeration rather than a bare orientation nudge.
- BODY-REACTIVATION (absorbed ex-'body-reactivation'): re-animates the body via a flowing energy-return narrative (warmth/vitality moving through the limbs into the core, or core-to-extremities), driving absorption back up through interoception — the tell is the somatic energy-flow arc rather than counted numbers or named baselines.
Surface may carry an appended minimality/replay tag, a preserved-room gesture, or a selective dial-reset, but the operative move is the same benign downshift to baseline (risk low; no consent/bounding load).
nodes.disc: Reach for THIS when you want a benign, honest, operator-paced return that arrives at genuine waking baseline where ordinary attention is restored, carrying no payload. Its four surfaces (counted count / stepwise full ramp / sensory-enumeration sweep / body-reactivation) are PARAMETRIC channel choices of the one technique — pick by register and modality, not as different tools. Choose a SIBLING instead when the return is not clean-and-operator-paced: self-paced-wake-bridge (hands emergence TIMING to the subject, no scaffolding); post-session-settling (the settle AFTER baseline is reached, not the return itself); suggestion-integration (asserts prior content PERSISTS through an otherwise-genuine return); loaded-emergence-waking-suggestion (a genuine return that CARRIES/re-delivers content). It is the affirmative opposite of the exit-deletion siblings: foreclosed-emergence (rigs every offered branch away from baseline), no-return-terminal-close (cancels the wakener outright), subverted-emergence-state-hold (corrupts the gate so exit is aroused/obedient), carry-out-emergence (refuses discharge so the charge rides out). Tell: on arrival the state has actually changed toward baseline, nothing is loaded, and no exit was withheld or rigged.

ex.f: Full ramp: count, breath, body, eyes, room
ex.t: The exit is a bundle rather than a bare count: the operator asks for one deeper breath, invites the listener to shift the shoulders and stretch the hands, then counts upward while the eyes come open, and finishes by suggesting a slow look around at wherever the listener is actually sitting. Each element does a different piece of the return — breath and movement re-engage the body, the count paces it, the look-around restores orientation.
ex.s: End of session; a fuller reorientation is wanted than a bare count, subject still seated or lying.
ex.m: Take one good deep breath in — and let it go. Roll your shoulders, open and close your hands a couple of times. Now, one, two, three, four, five — eyes open. Take a slow look around at the room you're actually in, find the walls, find the light, and let yourself arrive back here properly.

ex.f: Sweeping awareness back through the room
ex.t: Instead of a bare wake cue, the operator walks the listener category by category through the ordinary world: notice the temperature of the room, notice whatever sound is nearest, notice what time of day it is, notice the weight of your own body against the chair. Each anchor is named, checked, and left behind. By the last one, attention has been rebuilt outward and the trance frame simply has nothing left holding it.
ex.s: End of session; return is being run by external-anchor enumeration rather than by counting.
ex.m: Notice the temperature of the room on your skin. Notice the nearest sound to you, whatever it happens to be right now. Notice what time of day it is out there. And notice the weight of your own body pressing down into the chair. That's four things back in place, and there's nothing left holding this.

ex.f: Energy returning through the limbs
ex.t: No numbers are used at all. The operator narrates warmth gathering in the chest and then moving outward — down through the arms until the fingers want to move, down through the legs until the feet feel solid on the floor — and describes the heaviness draining off as it goes. The return is driven entirely through what the body reports, and the listener arrives awake because they can feel themselves again, not because they were counted there.
ex.s: End of session; a somatic return is wanted with no numbers used at all.
ex.m: There's a warmth gathering in the middle of your chest — feel it start to spread. It's moving out along your arms now, all the way to your fingers, until they want to move on their own; go ahead and let them. It's going down through your legs, and your feet are finding the floor, solid. The heaviness is draining off you as the warmth arrives. There you are — all the way back.

ex.f: The counted ramp back up to waking
ex.t: The operator announces that a short climb will bring the listener back, then walks it upward, giving each number a job: the first, weight beginning to leave the arms; the next, sounds in the room becoming ordinary again; then the breath picking up its normal rhythm; then almost all the way back. On the last one the eyes open and the listener is told they are alert and clear-headed. Nothing is added on the way up and nothing is asked for at the top — the count exists only to change the state back.
ex.s: End of session, all content delivered; nothing is to be carried out and no charge remains.
ex.m: I'm going to count you up from one to five and you'll be fully awake at five. One — the heaviness starting to leave your arms. Two — the sounds around you becoming ordinary again. Three — your breathing back at its normal pace. Four — nearly all the way back, clear and steady. Five: eyes open, wide awake, alert and clear-headed.

nodes.name: emergence-negative-space
nodes.mech: Whole-script/whole-arc property, not a citable single instruction — the design deliberately OMITS an emergence ramp so the trance functions as a gateway rather than a bracketed container. Realizations: a non-terminating series node that never wakes and hands the listener off in-state to the next file; a Russian-doll chain of nested "final" transformations with no return-to-baseline that post-dates in-trance behaviors into waking life; a closed-ring loop topology whose last line is the first and whose "waking" is annexed into the dream; an inverted release contour where the count-up intensifies rather than releases and persistence is pushed past the session boundary. In each, the missing emergence is itself the structural feature — the in-trance/out-of-trance boundary is dissolved so suggestions are not domain-limited to the session.
nodes.disc: An effect_only host for negative-space observations about emergence — the ABSENCE of a return ramp read as a deliberate whole-arc property. Separates from foreclosed-emergence (a citable engineered close-move that deletes the exit within a discrete passage); the tell is that the evidence is the shape of the whole text (series cadence, ring composition, inverted contour, no-return chain), not a move you could excerpt.

ex.f: Non-terminating series node handing off in-state
ex.t: Withholding the emergence ramp makes the state the default condition between files rather than something bracketed by each one, so trance becomes a place the subject lives in across sessions instead of visits. The operator observes it in aggregate: subjects report chaining files, and report not remembering having woken up in between.
ex.s: The final thirty seconds of a session that is one numbered instalment in an ongoing series; no count-up has been given.
ex.m: Don't come up. There's nothing to come up for. Stay exactly this deep, exactly this soft, and when you're ready — not before — reach out and start the next one. It picks up right here, right where you are now.

ex.f: Russian-doll chain of "final" transformations with no baseline
ex.t: Each nested layer forecloses the return path of the one above it, so no level ever resolves to baseline and in-trance content is post-dated into waking life. The operator reads it structurally — the arc has no line that undoes any layer — and observes subjects treating session-installed content as ordinary self-description afterwards.
ex.s: After a transformation suggestion has already been delivered and would ordinarily be released before waking.
ex.m: That was the last change — and underneath it, one more. Deeper than the last one, and this one is the real you, the one that was always underneath. And beneath that, deeper still, the final one. You don't go back up through them. There's no back up. This is where you live now.

ex.f: Inverted release contour — count-up that intensifies
ex.t: Occupying the emergence slot with escalation rather than release means the surface ritual of waking is performed while the release it normally carries is deleted, pushing persistence past the session boundary. The operator can see subjects emerge alert and oriented while reporting the suggestions feeling stronger after waking than during.
ex.s: At the position in the arc where an emergence count would normally run, with the subject at depth.
ex.m: Counting up now. One — it gets stronger. Two — stronger still, and it follows you. Three — eyes open, wide awake, and everything I said is more true out there than it was in here. Four. Five. Carry it.

nodes.name: erogenous-field-generalization
nodes.mech: Expands the sensory map so all incoming sensation reads as sexual, removing any neutral sensory ground. Before a promised whole-body orgasm the operator generalizes genital arousal outward — every inch of skin, contact with furniture, the air, even the operator's words redefined as erogenous-zone stimulation — which both intensifies the coming orgasm and makes escape from arousal impossible (nowhere neutral to attend to), recursively weaponizing the script's own delivery so the medium becomes the payload.
nodes.disc: Total sensory reattribution (skin, furniture, air, words all sexual) leaving no neutral ground, with the delivery medium itself weaponized. Separates from a plain "you feel pleasure everywhere" (the tell is the total, no-neutral-ground reattribution), from kinesthetic hallucination, which installs one felt sensation where this remaps the meaning of ALL sensation, and from a total-permeation claim (a belief about scope, not a perceptual remap).

ex.f: All sensation reattributed as sexual
ex.t: Before the promised finish, the operator widens the map: the sensitivity that used to belong to one place is declared to belong to the whole surface of the skin. Whatever the listener is resting against, the fabric they are wearing, the temperature of the room — each is named in turn and re-labelled as contact of the same kind. Then the operator turns the delivery itself into stimulation, framing the sound of the voice as another point of contact. There is now no direction attention can travel that is not arousing; looking away from it means looking at more of it.
ex.s: Just before a promised whole-body climax; arousal already high and the subject is stationary against a surface.
ex.m: That sensitivity you feel in one place — it isn't staying there. It's on every inch of your skin now. The chair against your back is touching you like that. The fabric on your thighs is touching you like that. The air on your throat is touching you like that. And my voice going into your ears is touching you like that too. There's nowhere left to look that isn't this.

nodes.name: foreclosed-emergence
nodes.mech: Structures the close so no path returns the listener to genuine waking baseline — the wake state is removed from the reachable set of end-states while agency-restoration or choose-your-exit rhetoric makes the foreclosure feel like a free pick. It operates on the trajectory's reachability topology: a forked "choice" whose every branch terminates in an operator-favored state; or the waking frame annexed into the trance (waking re-labeled a dream-stage); or an up-count arriving at the identical destination it departed so nothing changes on arrival. In every case the clean non-operative exit is quietly deleted from what is reachable.
nodes.disc: The clean-waking end-state is absent from the reachable set — separates from count-up-return (a genuine baseline is actually reached). Separates from the whole-arc emergence-negative-space observations because this is a citable engineered close-move, not a topology observation. Tell: a real wake would return ordinary attention or offer a fully-wake-and-be-done branch; here every offered path re-fixes the operator's frame.

ex.f: The wake count that arrives where it started
ex.t: Several times across the session the operator announces that the listener is coming up, runs a brisk count, and then describes the arrival state — and the description is the same one used for being under. Repeated often enough, the count stops marking a transition at all: awake and under become the same described place, and the listener has no moment at which the session can be said to have ended.
ex.s: One of several apparent wake-ups distributed across the session; the arrival state described matches the trance state exactly.
ex.m: Coming up now — one, two, three, and you're awake. Awake means soft, heavy, wide open, waiting for my voice. That's what awake is. Good. And now let's go down again — one, two, three, and you're under: soft, heavy, wide open, waiting for my voice.

ex.f: Waking redefined as part of the dream
ex.t: The operator alternates two opposed state-words back and forth, long past the point where either keeps a distinct meaning, then closes the loop by folding the waking term inside the other: coming out of it is reclassified as one more event occurring within the frame. The listener's most basic escape route, simply deciding to leave, has been redefined as a move that happens inside the thing it was meant to leave.
ex.s: Late close, after the two state-words have been alternated to the point of blurring.
ex.m: Asleep, awake, asleep, awake — you've stopped being able to tell which one I've just said, haven't you. Here's the answer: waking up is a thing that happens inside the dream. It's one of the events in it. So go ahead and wake, if you like. You'll be doing it in here, with me, where you already are.

ex.f: Choosing between exits that both stay under
ex.t: The close hands the listener their agency back as a decision between two ways to finish, and lets them settle it themselves. It is presented warmly, as though the listener is finally in charge of their own exit. What is never on the menu is the option of coming all the way up and being finished. Every branch on offer leaves the trance operative; the listener spends their restored authority picking which operator-favoured state to occupy.
ex.s: Close of session; the subject is told their agency is being returned to them, and offered a choice of endings.
ex.m: You get to choose how this finishes, and I'll take whichever you pick. You can drift off to sleep right here, still soft, still holding onto everything I've given you — or you can come up into your evening and go about it dreamy and open and easy to reach. Take your time. Whichever you want. Choose.

nodes.name: forward-dated-trait-authorization
nodes.mech: Asserts a standing, forward-dated permission — the operator may at any future point change the listener's likes, dislikes, needs, wants, desires — executing no trait change here but pre-licensing future scripts/sessions to do trait-level work without re-establishing authority each time. If accepted now, a later "you now love X" suggestion arrives pre-licensed, so resistance to it becomes resistance to a frame already agreed-to, which is harder than resisting a fresh imposition. The clause's value is realized in later sessions, not this one.
nodes.disc: A meta-authorization (standing permission) that executes no trait change in-file and is parasitic on current acceptance of the property frame. Separates from a direct trait change (nothing is changed here), from a present-authority claim (which asserts authority NOW, where this pre-licenses FUTURE overwrites), and from total-permeation (which frames conditioning as permeating the present; this is forward-dated permission for conditioning-to-come).

ex.f: Standing permission to rewrite you later
ex.t: Nothing about the listener is altered in this session. The operator only states a standing term: whatever you are drawn to and whatever you avoid, whatever you want and need, are all subject to revision by me, at a time of my choosing. The clause is agreed to at a moment when it costs nothing, because it asks for no change today. Its value arrives months later, when some other session declares a new preference already in place — and the listener's objection has to fight a permission they already granted rather than a fresh demand.
ex.s: Mid-session, ownership frame already accepted; no trait change is executed here or anywhere in this file.
ex.m: One term, and then we move on. What you like, what you can't stand, what you want, what you need — all of it is mine to change, whenever I decide to, without asking you again. I'm not changing anything tonight. I'm just telling you the terms, and you're agreeing to them now, while they cost you nothing.

nodes.name: contingency-function-substrate-principles
nodes.mech: Design principles about how behavioral FUNCTION is determined by the contingency arrangement itself — not deployable moves so much as constraints that govern every other contingency-engineering technique. (function-by-contingency-arrangement) a stimulus's behavioral function is a property of the ARRANGEMENT, not of the stimulus, so ONE identical stimulus can be scheduled into multiple functions by changing its relations rather than introducing new stimuli — a single aversive stimulus serves as negative reinforcer (termination), punisher (presentation), or motivating operation (presentation-as-MO) by onset/offset/timing; a single conditioned token reinforces, punishes (response cost), signals, or evokes by how its relations are arranged (function is REASSIGNED, not created). (stimulus-delta-leverage) behavioral leverage lives in stimulus CHANGE — the operative event is the transition (absence-of-tone -> tone); onsets, offsets, and contrasts against a baseline carry control while a maintained ambient condition is near-inert, so manipulate deltas, not standing states. (consequence-onset-detectability-bound) a function-altering (consequence) effect requires a detectable ONSET edge — a state whose onset is too gradual to read as a discrete event-following-a-response acts only as an antecedent motivator and cannot punish or reinforce what it follows, even when the same event with a sharp onset could.
nodes.disc: This entry collects cross-cutting DESIGN PRINCIPLES that constrain how any contingency-engineering technique works — reach for it as reference when deciding how to schedule a stimulus's function, where to place leverage (transitions vs standing states), or whether an event's onset is sharp enough to function as a consequence. Distinct from the deployable techniques (pairing CREATES a reinforcer; these principles say function is REASSIGNED by arrangement, leverage lives in the delta, and consequences need a detectable onset). Not itself a cue install, a contingency arrangement, or a subject-facing move — it is the substrate the others are built on.

ex.f: A token's function comes only from its relations
ex.t: "a token may serve multiple functions—reinforcing, punishing, discriminative, eliciting—depending on its relationship to these other events" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: One stimulus, three functions by arrangement
ex.t: "(a) a negative reinforcer if its termination increases behavior, (b) a punisher if its presentation decreases behavior, and/or (c) a motivating operation if its presentation increases the current frequency of behaviors that have terminated it in the past" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: future-pacing
nodes.mech: Declaratively projects a suggested response or state into future situations as automatic and inevitable (every time X, you will Y). Broadened from v6.9 to cover the delivery vehicles the corpus demonstrates for the same lever — unmarked grammatical slides that hand the listener's own rehearsal back as forecast, continuous future-tense streams that offload verification to the listener's future self, and pre-scripted future intrusive thoughts framed in advance as the listener's own preference.
nodes.disc: The move EXTENDS a specified effect forward by declaration and the projection can observably fail. It does not build a both-branches-confirm topology (future-confirmation-capture), does not presuppose an already-solved past-tense future and elicit it as memory (pseudo-orientation-in-time), does not bank a decision through rehearsal (rehearsed-pre-commitment), and does not wire reinforcement to a self-administered biological event (inevitable-event-reinforcement-fuse).

ex.f: Future-tense barrage with no checkpoints
ex.t: The operator lists change after change, all in the future tense, and never pauses to ask whether any of it is happening yet. Each claim is asserted as already underway before the previous one has been dwelt on, so verification is always deferred to a later self. The listener never gets the beat in which they could check one item against their body — and one thing that does feel slightly different later gets read as confirmation of the whole list.
ex.s: Mid-session; a long declarative run with no pauses, no checks, and no request for feedback.
ex.m: Your hands are getting lighter and they'll keep getting lighter. Your voice is going softer and it will stay softer. You'll find yourself standing differently. You'll notice you take up less room. You'll want less, and you'll be happier wanting less. You'll stop needing to finish sentences. All of it is already underway.

ex.f: The next session's thought scripted in advance
ex.t: The operator forecasts not just that the listener will return but exactly what the return will feel like from the inside — smoother, quicker, easier than this time — and then supplies the sentence that will arrive in their head some ordinary afternoon: a mild, curious wondering about when they can do this again. When that thought duly surfaces days later it presents as the listener's own idle preference, not as something that was written down for them in advance.
ex.s: Closing minutes, before emergence; the subject is being pointed at the next session.
ex.m: The next time will be smoother than this — quicker down, easier, less work for you. And sometime Wednesday afternoon, in the middle of something ordinary, a thought is going to turn up on its own: I wonder when I can do that again. Just a small, curious, pleasant thought. Yours.

ex.f: Imagining slides into predicting
ex.t: The opening asks only for imagination — picture the shop, picture how you would feel walking out. The listener builds the scene willingly, because it is only a game. Then, inside the same paragraph and without any marker, the grammar changes: what you might feel becomes what you will feel, and the operator confirms it as a forecast. The listener's own vivid rehearsal, produced with defences down, is handed back to them as evidence of what they are going to do.
ex.s: Early in the session; the subject has been asked only to imagine a scene and is building it willingly.
ex.m: Picture the shop — the doorway, the light inside, the shelf you'd go to first. Imagine how it might feel to walk out of there with it in your bag. Feel how easy that is. And that's how it will feel, Thursday, when you're actually standing there. That's your own answer, not mine — you just showed it to me.

nodes.name: inner-voice-medium-colonization
nodes.mech: Rather than planting a specific thought, the operator retargets the MEDIUM of thought itself — asserting the register/timbre of the listener's inner monologue is now a different voice (soft, girly, slutty, giggling, automatic), so every future thought, whatever its content, passes through a voice-filter that signals "this is the new identity thinking". This removes subvocal speech as a private channel the host could retreat to. The suggestion is sealed with an ironic-process bind ("no matter how hard you try") — checking whether one's thought is in the new voice is itself an act of introspecting on the inner voice, which confirms the suggestion.
nodes.disc: Content-INDEPENDENT recoloring of the inner-monologue register plus an ironic-process bind, so the effect fires on any future thought and self-verification re-confirms it. Unlike internal-voice cultivation, which pre-populates the inner monologue with specific first-person CONTENT, this changes the carrier voice regardless of content. Requires the listener to have an inner verbal monologue and to introspect on it for the move to fire.

ex.f: The inner monologue's voice replaced
ex.t: The operator does not supply a thought to think. Instead the register of thinking itself is reassigned: from now on, whatever crosses the listener's mind arrives sounding like someone else's voice rather than their own. And the clincher — however much effort goes into thinking in the old voice, the result comes out in the new one anyway. That last clause turns the only available test into a confirmation, because checking which voice a thought is in requires listening to the inner voice, and the listener has just been told what they will hear. Subvocal speech, the one channel that was never shared, stops being somewhere to retreat to.
ex.s: Identity install, deep trance; no specific thought is being supplied — only the register of thinking.
ex.m: Listen to the voice you think in. From now on that isn't yours — it's higher, softer, sillier, and it giggles at the end of things. Every thought you have arrives in it, whatever the thought is about. And go on, try to think one in your old voice. However hard you try, it comes out in hers. Check it and you'll hear her.

nodes.name: lexical-relay-semantic-lattice
nodes.mech: A predicate ending one line becomes the subject opening the next, handing a term forward like a bucket-brigade relay ("deeper" to "dumber" to "deeper"; "drop" to "drip" to "drop"), so a new equivalence is smuggled in one harmless handoff at a time. Across the chain this builds a closed cross-substitutable semantic lattice in which depth, stupidity, dripping and arousal all become substitutable nodes; once installed, triggering any single node later re-activates the whole conditioned cluster, so one cue fires the entire state.
nodes.disc: The tell is inter-line propagation: a term ending one line is handed forward to open the next, so the chain requires sequential in-order recitation and builds an inter-substitutable cluster across distinct terms. Unlike circular logic, which loops one proposition back on itself, the relay moves FORWARD through new terms; and what it builds is a semantic equivalence lattice, not compliance-reward momentum.

ex.f: Each line hands its last word to the next
ex.t: The listener repeats a chain in which the word that closed one line opens the next: sinking leads to softness, softness leads to warmth, warmth leads to sinking. Every individual handoff is a small, agreeable step, and no line ever asserts the big claim outright. But after the full circuit the terms have become interchangeable, and later on the operator only has to say one of them — any one — to bring the whole set back at once.
ex.s: Repetition drill, subject repeating aloud or subvocally after the operator; the chain must be delivered in order.
ex.m: Say them after me, in order. Sinking makes you soft. Soft makes you warm. Warm makes you sink. Sinking makes you soft. Again — and don't skip one, each word hands you the next.

nodes.name: manufactured-insufficiency-ratchet
nodes.mech: An unpassable moving standard: the operator resets the subject's internal sense of 'enough' upward at the moment it would otherwise be met, exploiting desire for operator approval so each iteration must exceed the last, preventing satiation and keeping the arousal/effort engine climbing; the chase-standard planted in one session carries into subsequent ones. Two realizations. (1) Success-invalidation: immediately after a likely-successful performance, mild dissatisfaction is introduced ('you could have tried a little bit harder') and the next attempt is directed past the last ('push yourself to new limits'), gentle enough to preserve the safe frame while ratcheting demand. (2) Manufactured-failure depth-quiz: trance depth is framed as a gradeable pop-quiz, a depth cue is fired, and the result is declared insufficient BY DESIGN ('you could have gone a lot deeper... hasn't been practicing') — a subjective depth test cannot be objectively passed, so failure is structurally guaranteed; this additionally reframes depth as the listener's own testable responsibility and installs the operator as legitimate evaluator/disciplinarian with a standing pretext for punishment. Both share the lever: an insufficiency verdict rendered on a standard the subject cannot satisfy, spending approval-desire as fuel.
nodes.disc: The tell is an insufficiency verdict rendered IMMEDIATELY at the point of likely success, on a standard the subject structurally cannot satisfy — manufacturing a shortfall where the subject felt success (or would have passed). Ordinary encouragement patter and self-validating language affirm the achieved state; this invalidates it. In the depth-quiz form the grading is explicit and failure is built in — the opposite of a convincer, which cites a SUCCESSFUL obeyed act as proof of depth. Reach for this to keep demand climbing or to install the operator as evaluator; reach for a convincer when the goal is to CONFIRM depth rather than deny it.

ex.f: Dissatisfaction introduced at the point of success
ex.t: The listener completes the task and, in the moment they would normally feel they did well, the operator sounds mildly unimpressed: that was fine, but you had a bit more in you, didn't you? The next round is then aimed past the one just finished. The tone stays gentle enough that nothing feels like punishment, which is what lets it repeat — each time the listener reaches the standard, the standard has already moved, so approval stays one attempt away indefinitely.
ex.s: Immediately after the subject completes a task they performed well; the moment they would otherwise register success.
ex.m: Mm. That was fine. You had a little more in you than that though, didn't you. Let's go again — and this time I want past where you just got to, not back to it. I know you can. Show me.

nodes.name: massed-practice-rate-suppression
nodes.mech: The subject deliberately over-emits the undesired behavior far beyond any functional occasion (a compulsive checker performs the full 13-step ritual five times for every real check), attaching an effortful or aversive cost — satiation or response-cost, left unstated — so its future rate declines. A counterintuitive increase-emission-to-reduce-rate move.
nodes.disc: Versus incompatible-response substitution, this repeats the SAME behavior on purpose, too much, rather than replacing it with an alternative. And versus repetition used to strengthen — verbatim looping that drives material deeper into encoding, or sustained endurance compliance that deepens the trance state — massed practice repeats the behavior specifically to REDUCE its future rate.

ex.f: Over-perform the habit to suppress it
ex.t: "Forcing oneself to perform an undesired behavior again and again… will sometimes decrease the future occurrences" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: monotonic-ratchet-one-way-valve
nodes.mech: A one-way reachability topology in which each successful step produces a strictly stricter next step and there is NO reachable state where compliance yields an easier or regressible subsequent step — a monotone ratchet, not a repeatable steady state, and typically self-tightening so the operator need not be present for the tightening to continue (the listener self-applies the ratchet to stay eligible for the reinforcer). Realizations: (a) durable-install ratchet — every durable element strictly increases on each use (chastity interval must exceed the prior, cross-recording routes to more ratchet-bearing recordings, 'twice = go further' cannot regress); (b) fractionation-cycle ratchet — a fractionation up/down cycle whose wake pole is collapsed, loaded, degraded, or relabeled so the neutral baseline to retreat to is removed and net state monotonically decreases across cycles (the oscillation becomes one-way instead of a reversible contrast pump); (c) epistemic unfalsifiable-claim ratchet — the script chains assertions the listener cannot check against any baseline ('twice as deep', 'you can always go deeper'), each accepted claim raising the floor for the next, so friction never accumulates and there is no checkpoint at which to object.
nodes.disc: Reach for THIS when the tell is ACTIVE PER-USE TIGHTENING — every step strictly increases with no reachable regressible/reset state (a monotone ratchet). Unlike a closed no-exit response topology, whose closure is static COVERAGE at a single moment, the ratchet is dynamic strict increase across uses. Unlike a stable/repeatable conditioned response or a merely durable install, which hold a steady state, the ratchet forbids any easier next step. Unlike plain fractionation, a reversible contrast pump with a neutral wake pole, the fractionation-cycle realization removes or loads that baseline so it cannot reset. The epistemic realization rides on unfalsifiable claims, but its load-bearing lever is the one-way irreversibility of the sequence — when the lever is instead rigging what the listener's reports are taken to mean, look to self-sealing evidence techniques.

ex.f: Every step makes the next step stricter
ex.t: Look at what each rule in the session does on its second use rather than its first. The abstinence interval must be longer than the one before it. Completing the session sends the listener to further sessions, each carrying rules of the same shape.
