Succeeding at the drill twice in a row means going further in the same direction, never repeating at the same setting. Nowhere in the whole design is there a reachable position, however compliant, from which the next demand comes out smaller than the last — and because the tightening is written into the rules themselves, the operator does not have to be present for it to continue. Staying eligible is what makes the subject keep turning the screw on themselves.
ex.s: Rules segment, subject already compliant with a first round; the durable elements (interval, drill, follow-on listening) are being restated as standing terms.
ex.m: From now on, every lock is longer than the last one — if you held four days, the next is five, and there is no version of this where you go back to four. Each time you finish this recording cleanly, you queue the next one in the set, and each one in that set asks for a little more than this. And if you manage the drill twice without slipping, you don't get to repeat it at that setting — twice means you move up. That is the only direction the numbers go, whether I am here or not.

nodes.name: pseudo-orientation-in-time
nodes.mech: Projects the subject into a future where the present problem is already solved, speaks of it in the past tense as accomplished fact, and elicits the solution as RECALLED memory rather than invented hope — the operator claims to have forgotten the specifics and asks the subject to describe what they did. Presupposing the solution exists and was authored by the subject recruits generation of acceptable novel behavior past the conscious I-can't-think-of-any impasse, while expectancy points at an already-achieved outcome.
nodes.disc: The tell is past-tense-as-solved-memory framing plus elicitation by recall (not imagine): future-pacing extends a specified effect forward declaratively, and guided visualization keeps the content hypothetical, while here the solution is presupposed as accomplished fact and retrieved as the subject's own memory; the product is an elicited plan, not an unfalsifiable claim.

ex.f: Asking the client what the cure was
ex.t: "Will you recall for me exactly what you consider the most essential thing that I did which changed you?" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: Recalling the solution you have not found yet
ex.t: "induce a deep trance and use a technique called 'pseudo-orientation in time'… 'Would you describe in detail what you did?'" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: rehearsed-pre-commitment
nodes.mech: A future contested act is rehearsed in detail and consented to upstream, while the listener's judgment is intact, so the decision arrives already made at the moment deliberation is stripped. Realized as explicit teaching plus honor-framing of an aversive motor routine (the withdrawal is banked before arousal peaks and runs on cue with no live decision), and as experiential inhabitation of a fantasized future state that pre-validates a protocol before it is requested.
nodes.disc: The load-bearing move is relocating the consent/decision in time — upstream of the deliberation-stripped execution moment — not programming an automatic if-X-then-Y response, not declaring a future response the way future-pacing does, and not fabricating consent (the consent is genuinely obtained while the listener can still deliberate).

ex.f: Inhabiting the future self who already agreed
ex.t: The listener is invited to imagine, in detail, the body of someone who has already gone months under the restriction being contemplated — how starved the nerves would be, how much a small touch would register. They inhabit that state vividly for several minutes before the restriction has been asked for at all. By the time the actual assignment is stated, the listener is not evaluating a proposal; they are agreeing to something they have already felt themselves wanting.
ex.s: Mid-session, good depth, subject responsive to imagery; the restriction has not been named or requested yet.
ex.m: Put yourself three months forward. Feel that body — every nerve on the surface starved, the seam of your clothes registering like a hand, your pulse audible in your ears when someone stands close. You have gone ninety days untouched and your skin has become one enormous ear listening for contact. Stay in that body. Breathe in it. Feel how much you want it, before anyone asks you for anything.

ex.f: The hard part taught and agreed before it hurts
ex.t: Rather than springing the unpleasant instruction at the moment it has to be carried out, the operator stops early and teaches it as a procedure: here is how the build works, here is the exact point at which your hands come away, here is what you will feel afterwards. The listener rehearses the movement mentally while they are still calm enough to weigh it, and the operator frames agreeing to it as something granted rather than demanded. When the moment finally arrives, arousal has removed the listener's capacity to deliberate — but there is nothing left to deliberate about, because the decision was banked half an hour earlier.
ex.s: Early session, subject calm and clear-headed, arousal not yet built; the aversive instruction will be needed much later.
ex.m: Before we start anything, I want to teach you the hard part while you can still think about it. Later, when your breath goes ragged and your hips start to lift on their own, your hands come away from yourself and rest flat on your thighs — that exact moment, no negotiation, because there will be no one home to negotiate with. It will ache, and the ache is the proof. I'm not ordering you to do it; I'm asking you to agree to it now, and you telling me yes right now is a gift you're giving me, not an obedience I took.

nodes.name: self-efficacy-tag
nodes.mech: Installs a belief about the subject's own future capability to re-access the trance state with increasing ease — a forward-directed suggestion framing return as a self-owned ability ("you can return whenever you wish"), emphasizing "can" over "must" so the subject, not the operator, holds the key to re-entry.
nodes.disc: The payload is the subject's own capability to return — deliberately 'can', NOT the operator's control over when. Unlike relief-dependency-couple, which prescribes a post-wake mood and binds relief to operator-dependency, and unlike moves that persist content past the session or actively re-deliver it, this is a capability/identity claim about re-access.

ex.f: Re-entry framed as the subject's own growing ability
ex.t: Framing re-access as a skill the subject owns builds a capability belief that survives the operator's absence and makes the next induction faster by expectancy alone. The operator observes shortened induction times on subsequent sessions and, in self-practice reports, subjects entering state without any operator input.
ex.s: During the emergence sequence, after the main suggestion block and before the count-up completes.
ex.m: You found your way down here yourself tonight, and you can find it again whenever you want to — sit down, close your eyes, take three slow breaths, and you'll be right back at this depth. It gets easier every time you do it, because you're the one who knows the way now. Not because you have to. Because you can.

nodes.name: self-observation-instrumentation
nodes.mech: Recruit the subject as a reliable measurement instrument by engineering the self-observation contingency. Reward is released only when the subject's self-recorded count AGREES with an independent count at threshold, so truthful self-report (not performance) becomes the reinforced class. A perceptual encoding renders the standard as a shaded band on a graph, so "am I good enough?" becomes "is my dot in the band?", lowering the judgment the subject must supply to self-evaluate.
nodes.disc: Not rewarding performance and not criterion-shaping; the tell is that the accuracy or truthfulness of self-measurement (or the ease of reading the verdict) is the reinforced or de-skilled target, not the behavior's score.

ex.f: The standard drawn as a band on the graph
ex.t: "chart self-recorded data on a graph that showed the competitive standard with a shaded area"; "I'm not in the shaded area. I need to work faster." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Reward gated on agreement, not performance
ex.t: "If Brad's self-recorded data agreed with the teacher at a level of 80% or higher, he received his choice from a menu" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: split-self-unfalsifiability
nodes.mech: Uses an installed conscious/subconscious (or surface/deep) partition not as a dissociative experience but as an epistemic shield around the install. The operator concedes the waking self may keep its personality, notice nothing, or forget, and pre-categorizes that surface report as harmless/expected/desired, while the "real" recipient is declared a deeper layer the conscious mind cannot access — so introspective self-report can never reach or falsify the deep claim ("I still feel like a person", "nothing changed", "I forgot" are all pre-absorbed as confirmation).
nodes.disc: Payload is unfalsifiability — noticing-nothing is pre-routed as confirmation and the deep claim is walled off from conscious disconfirmation. vs observer-responder-split (payload is in-session felt automaticity/spectatorship); vs evaluator-offline-channel (evaluator quieted so suggestions land now); vs resistance-quarantine-partition (a faculty's standing is demoted, not the epistemic reach of self-report).

ex.f: Forgetting pre-explained as the deep part remembering
ex.t: Late in the session the operator stops addressing the listener as one person and starts addressing layers — telling them that the thinking part may well lose all of this, while a part further down keeps it. Every possible aftermath is now pre-assigned: remembering proves it took, forgetting proves it went deep enough to bypass the part that would have interfered.
ex.s: Late session, immediately before closing; subject deep, install already delivered.
ex.m: I'm not talking to you as one person anymore. The thinking part of you may lose every word of this by morning — it might keep nothing at all. The part further down keeps all of it. So if you wake and remember, that means it took hold. And if you wake with a blank where this hour was, that means it went past the part that would have interfered. There is no version where it didn't land.

ex.f: Awake on the surface, owned underneath
ex.t: The operator confirms out loud that the listener is fully awake now — and in the same breath states that underneath, something is still listening and still under instruction. Two selves are now on the table: anything the listener does freely belongs to the one that is awake, anything compliant belongs to the one that is owned. Reporting that one feels entirely ordinary stops being a defence, because it is a report from the self that was never the one in question.
ex.s: Emergence, subject just counted up, eyes open, alert.
ex.m: You're wide awake now. Fully alert, fully yourself, back in the room — and underneath that, something is still listening to me and still holding what I said. Anything you do freely today belongs to the awake one. Anything you do because I told you belongs to the other one. So when you tell yourself you feel completely ordinary, remember which of the two of you is talking.

ex.f: The surface self allowed to feel unchanged
ex.t: The operator concedes the obvious objection before the listener can raise it: the everyday mind will go on behaving like itself, with its own opinions and habits, and that is entirely fine. What has been changed sits underneath that, where the everyday mind cannot look. A listener who later notices that they feel entirely ordinary finds that observation already accounted for — it was named in advance as exactly what the surface was expected to report, so the report can never count as evidence against anything.
ex.s: Mid-session, install content about to be delivered; subject deep but not amnesic.
ex.m: Your everyday mind is going to stay exactly as it is — same opinions, same stubbornness, same taste in arguments — and that is correct. That is not the part I am talking to. What I am putting in goes underneath, where the thinking part has no window. So when you're back at your desk on Thursday and you notice you feel completely normal, completely yourself, nothing changed — that is precisely what the surface is supposed to report.

nodes.name: ubiquity-cued-covert-ratchet
nodes.mech: A trivially-encountered social cue (an everyday hello) is wired as a covert one-way escalation ratchet — never named as a trigger, only narrated as what precipitates each desire spike, so it cannot be avoided and firing is experienced as endogenous preference. Fixed-order commitment items run least-committing to most-committing so precedent accumulates; an additive inventory recital reactivates prior items against lapse; the repetitive learnable form invites the listener to extend the ladder past the script.
nodes.disc: Covert-by-ubiquity cueing separates it from declared trigger installation (firing here is not recognized as cue-response); the monotonic self-extending commitment ladder separates it from future-pacing, which supplies only the future-rehearsal install vehicle.

ex.f: An everyday greeting wired as the escalation cue
ex.t: The session rehearses an ordinary few days ahead. Someone greets the listener in passing, and in that moment a wish arrives for the first small item on a list. The greeting is never called a trigger — it is simply narrated as the thing that happens just before the wanting, so the listener has no reason to connect the two and no way to avoid an everyday courtesy. The list runs in a fixed order from the least committing thing to the most, and after each addition the operator recites the running tally so far, keeping the earlier items live. By the time the demanding ones arrive, half a dozen prior yeses stand behind them, and the pattern is regular enough that the listener could keep extending it after the recording ends.
ex.s: Future-pacing segment; subject deep, comfortable with imagined near-future scenes; the item ladder has been drafted least-to-most committing.
ex.m: Picture Tuesday morning. Someone passes you in the corridor and says hey — and right then, in that half-second after, you find you want to wear the collar under your shirt. Wednesday, someone says hey at the coffee machine, and you want the collar, and you want to keep the plug in for the whole commute. Thursday: hey — collar, plug, and you want to text me the photo before you leave the house. Say the whole list back to me each time it grows, from the first thing to the newest thing, and keep adding to it after this recording ends.

nodes.name: autoclitic-training
nodes.mech: Install or strengthen an AUTOCLITIC — a secondary verbal form that comments on, modifies, or regulates the speaker's own primary verbal behavior (self-editing, self-qualifying, or telling the listener HOW to attend). Because the controlling stimulus is the learner's own transient, private verbal output, timing/access is the core difficulty. In one realization, to teach an autoclitic MAND (a louder voice / stock phrase regulating the listener's response to the learner's primary utterance), capture or contrive the listener-regulation MO, model/role-play the form, and if the MO alone fails layer a contingency-specifying prompt (CSS) atop it, then fade the prompt leaving the MO in control. In another, bring the learner's utterance under control of a feature of what they THEMSELVES just said, installing a comment-on-own-output / self-awareness layer. In a third, monitor ongoing natural speech for a self-modifier already slipping out at baseline ('that was SO big') and immediately reinforce the modifier COMPONENT specifically, not the whole utterance.
nodes.disc: Reach for AUTOCLITIC TRAINING when the target is a SECONDARY verbal form operating on the speaker's OWN primary utterance (a modifier/qualifier, or a mand regulating how the listener takes the utterance) — the controlling stimulus is the learner's own transient private speech, which is what makes it hard. Choose it over general verbal-operant teaching (tact/mand for external objects/states): here the acquired form regulates or comments on the learner's existing utterance rather than naming a new referent, and it presupposes the primary verbal repertoire already exists. The three facets differ only by which autoclitic and by contrived-MO vs self-referential vs in-vivo capture.

ex.f: When motivation alone fails, prompt then fade
ex.t: "The first condition consisted of contriving the EO alone, which was ineffective... the second condition involving the contrived MO plus an indirect supplemental verbal prompt resulted in successful manding" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Contrive the motivation, then model the form
ex.t: "Teaching autoclitic mands involves capturing or creating the relevant MOs and using ABA teaching procedures"; "a louder voice or a certain phrase may function as an autoclitic mand to prompt a listener to attend better" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: coercion-as-caregiving-reframe
nodes.mech: Every physical restriction or coercive fact (strapping to a bed, gas mask, cuffs, bound hands) is introduced and immediately reframed as protective caregiving ("for your safety", "to keep you comfortable"), with the imposition and its benevolent rationale narrated in the same breath. By never letting the coercive fact stand unframed, the listener's interpretive frame for involuntariness flips from threat to comfort; the body's alarm response is starved of a coherent threat-narrative to attach to, so helplessness reads as being-cared-for.
nodes.disc: Care language is the delivery vehicle for coercion (predatory undertone, e.g. "I made sure of it this time"), not its absence. Unlike genuine reassurance or safety rapport, the care talk is paired with a coercive imposition; and unlike surrender-as-freedom framing, which reroutes relief/comfort valence, this narrates each coercive act with a benevolent rationale so involuntariness reads as care.

ex.f: Each restraint narrated as care in the same breath
ex.t: No restriction is ever stated on its own. A limb is secured — because we need you to stay still and rest. Something is fastened across the body — so you cannot come to harm again. A piece of equipment is fitted — it will keep you comfortable while we work. Each coercive fact arrives already wrapped in its reason, so the listener never gets the unframed second in which alarm could take hold. The body registers that it cannot move, finds only a caretaking story to attach that to, and files being held down as being looked after.
ex.s: Restraint-scene narration; subject in trance, receptive to sensory description, each restraint being applied in sequence.
ex.m: I'm bringing your right wrist up to the rail and buckling it there — because you need to stay still and let yourself rest. Now the strap across your hips, snug, so you can't roll off and hurt yourself again. And this last piece over your nose and mouth, sealing warm against your face; it'll keep your breathing easy while we work. Nothing to hold up, nothing to manage. I've taken care of all of it.

nodes.name: cost-to-virtue-valence-flip
nodes.mech: Interpretive reappraisal: take a fact, behavior, or situation the subject already holds and relabel its MEANING or VALENCE so its charge changes and the subject embraces (or stops defending) it. In one realization, reverse the valence of a costly/threatening evaluation (admitting error, reliance on heuristics) into an admirable VIRTUE or reliable asset, paired with a self-image or aspirational-identity offer ('the true scientist') that makes accepting it identity-affirming. In another, relocate the very behavior the subject complains about inside a larger context they already prize (a child's disobedience re-filed as the independence the parent wants) via a leading question, so the complaint loses footing. In a third, relabel an interpersonal conflict as a TRANSMISSION ERROR by splitting 'what I meant' from 'what you received' into two inspectable objects, draining the moral charge so a clash of wills becomes a fixable calibration gap.
nodes.disc: Reach for reappraisal when a fact/behavior/conflict already exists and you want to change what it MEANS (not assert something new): presupposition and expectancy-seeding install a new fact or a forward frame, while here an existing thing is re-valenced. When real coercion is present and each coercive act gets a benevolent rationale, that is coercion-as-caregiving; when a shame-coded uncontrollable event is named precisely to overwrite it as success, that is failure-state-inversion. Pick the variant by object: a costly norm/disposition (virtue-flip), a complained-of behavior (context-relocation), or an interpersonal conflict (intent/uptake split).

ex.f: Concede the objection, then flip its valence
ex.t: "They are the most popular prompts precisely because they are the most reliable ones"; "there is nothing inherently wrong with the shortcut approach" — Cialdini (1984), Influence

ex.f: A costly admission relabelled as a virtue
ex.t: "new findings are not problems; they are opportunities for further investigation and expanded understanding" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: removal-from-reinforcement-timeout
nodes.mech: Suppress a behavior by REMOVING or withholding access to reinforcement for a period contingent on it (time-out from reinforcement / negative punishment by removal of opportunity), rather than debiting a held reserve (response-cost) or delivering an aversive. CORE (environmental-contingency-nonexclusion): keep the subject physically present but strip the reinforcing elements from the surrounding environment (planned ignoring, terminating a specific reinforcer, contingent observation where the subject watches others earn but cannot, partitioning within the room) — same suppressive effect as exclusionary time-out but milder/least-restrictive; the contingent-observation form sharpens it by making the deprivation vivid. FORM FACETS: (recoverable-contingent-withdrawal) remove a preferred item for a brief fixed interval, restored next trial contingent on the desired response (combined negative punishment + DRA — access gated by the alternative, not merely forfeited); (impoverished-context-permission) counterintuitively PERMIT the behavior only in a reward-stripped inconvenient setting, stripping the incidental co-reinforcers that rode along and raising response cost. PRECONDITION (reinforcement-discrepancy-engine): enrich the time-in baseline FIRST so every withdrawal has bite — an impoverished time-in nullifies the whole procedure. PARAMETERS of time-out design: (absence-gated-punishment-exit) gate release on the subject going a set interval WITHOUT the target behavior, not on the clock, so leaving does not reinforce the punished behavior; (aversive-interval-tolerance-ceiling) cap the interval short (2-5 min, never beyond ~15) so the subject cannot obtain reinforcers inside it or build tolerance (anti-inversion, requires time-in richer than time-out); (dense-every-instance-consequence-schedule) consequate EVERY occurrence and abandon the procedure rather than apply it intermittently, since occasional use manufactures the ambiguity that dense scheduling prevents. LIFECYCLE (aversive-procedure-sunset-design): at the moment the aversive procedure is introduced, AUTHOR its elimination — pre-plan the switch toward reinforcement-based reductive methods (DRA/DRI) or reduced intrusiveness once the target behavior drops, rather than running the punisher indefinitely, limiting exposure and migrating control onto positive contingencies.
nodes.disc: Reach for REMOVAL-FROM-REINFORCEMENT / TIME-OUT when suppression should work by WITHHOLDING access to reinforcement (removing a not-yet-earned reward or stripping the reinforcing environment) for a contingent period. Choose it over: response-cost / token economy (which SUBTRACTS a reinforcer the subject already HOLDS, per instance — this removes access/opportunity instead); extinction (which removes the SPECIFIC maintaining reinforcer of the target response so it decays to baseline — time-out removes reinforcement broadly for an interval regardless of the maintaining source); aversive-antecedent contingencies (which ADD a bad state escaped by compliance). The absorbed facets are the forms (non-exclusion / recoverable / impoverished-permission), the enrich-time-in precondition, and the exit/duration/schedule parameters of one time-out design.

ex.f: Watching others earn while barred from earning
ex.t: "planned ignoring, terminate specific reinforcer contact, contingent observation, and partition/select space time-out"; "repositioning occurs so that observations of ongoing activity continue, but without reinforcement" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: illusory-choice-authorship
nodes.mech: Agency/authorship relocation: relocate agency, choice, or motive onto the subject so compliance reads as self-produced or self-chosen rather than imposed, lowering resistance because the subject believes they are the author/driver. In one realization, offer a choice whose branches all CONVERGE on the same operator-controlled outcome, then affirm the pick ('wise choice'); agency is over modality/framing only, never whether/what, so felt authorship is manufactured over a fixed path. In another, assign the subject a fixed three-beat observation task (want it, expect it, watch it happen) so whatever occurs reads as self-produced and the 'is this working?' doubt is foreclosed. In a third, attribute the subject's own act of continuing to an unnamed pull and weld an undefined 'secret about you' to going deeper, so obeying deepeners is recoded from 'submitting' into 'satisfying my own need to know' and the operator vacates the role of imposer.
nodes.disc: Reach for agency-relocation when you want compliance to feel self-authored/self-driven. Presupposing a state as already true deletes the decision; here a (fake) decision or drive is handed to the subject. Reading the subject's REAL performed acts back as proof of state is a different move — here no act is required, agency itself is relocated. Pick the variant by the vehicle: a converging fake-choice, an assigned want/expect/watch observation loop, or curiosity welded to depth as the motor.

ex.f: Modular tracks sold as authorship
ex.t: The packaging tells the listener the material is split into separate pieces so they can assemble their own sequence — and then recommends playing the whole thing in the given order. The listener reads themselves as designing their own conditioning; the ordering they actually follow is the one that was shipped.
ex.s: Opening or packaging framing, before any induction; subject is choosing how to use a multi-file set.
ex.m: These come as five separate pieces so you can build your own program — take whichever ones you need, in whatever order suits you. Most people find they get the best results running all five, straight through, in the order they're numbered. Your sequence, your conditioning.

ex.f: Two finishes, both counted as obedience
ex.t: The close offers the listener a pick between two ways to finish, framed as permission to use whichever suits them. Neither branch is failure: succeeding at the harder one proves depth, taking the easier one is an operator-granted privilege rather than a fallback. The listener chooses the route and never notices that the destination — having done what they were told — was fixed before the offer was made.
ex.s: Closing segment, arousal high, the task has been running for several minutes.
ex.m: You can finish two ways. Either you hold on until I count you all the way to ten, which is what a deep one does — or you let go right now, because I'm giving you permission and permission from me is not a small thing. Pick. Either way you did what I told you.

ex.f: Both turns approved as the wise choice
ex.t: At the end of the corridor the listener is told to pick a door — left or right — and given a pause long enough to genuinely decide. Whatever they picked, the next line congratulates them on choosing well, and the narration continues down a single path that was never going to branch. The listener has just exercised judgement and had it approved, which makes the next instruction easier to take; they have no way to notice that the corridor only ever had one continuation.
ex.s: Deepener; subject following a corridor visualization, responsive to imagery.
ex.m: At the end of the corridor there are two doors, one on your left and one on your right. Choose one now. [pause, four seconds] Wise choice — I thought you'd pick that one. Push it open and step through, and the stairs on the other side go down.

nodes.name: imagined-is-real-licensing-rule
nodes.mech: A depth-licensing rule: install a general rule of the form 'the deeper the trance, the more X becomes available/true', presented as a neutral FACT about how minds/trance work so it is accepted rather than obeyed, lowering a threshold BEFORE the consequential content that cashes it arrives. In one form, 'the deeper you go, the more the mind experiences the imagined as real' ('a thing about trance people forget') lowers the threshold for treating operator-described imagery as experiential reality before payload imagery lands. In another, expanded capacity or a removed constraint is attributed to depth itself ('because you're so deep you can expand your limits to feel more pleasure'), reframing a felt tolerance-ceiling as a merely-waking constraint now lifted, and relabeling the listener's own restraint from self-protection into the obstacle blocking success.
nodes.disc: Seeds a general 'depth licenses X' rule presented as neutral fact, cashed later. Expectancy-seeding seeds a specific session event; this installs a principle every later scene or limit-push exploits. Concept-redefinition redefines a value or state; this ties a capability (the reality-status of imagery, or the removal of a limit) to trance depth. Pick the variant by what depth licenses: the reality-status of imagined percepts, or the removal of a felt tolerance/restraint ceiling.

ex.f: Depth licenses the imagined to count as real
ex.t: Early on, before anything worth resisting has been described, the operator drops in a general remark about how the process works: past a certain point the mind stops distinguishing sharply between what it pictures and what it takes in. It is offered as information, not as an instruction, so there is nothing to comply with or refuse — the listener simply accepts it as true. A small demonstration percept is named and duly reported as strengthening, which counts as proof of the rule. Everything the operator describes from then on arrives already licensed to be experienced rather than merely pictured.
ex.s: Early, just past induction; subject relaxed, no payload imagery delivered yet.
ex.m: Here's a thing about trance that people forget. The deeper you go, the less your mind bothers to separate what it pictures from what it takes in — past a certain point it just stops keeping them in different drawers. That's not something I'm doing to you, it's simply how the machinery runs. So: put your tongue against something cold and metallic. Feel it get colder the longer you hold it. Notice that it got more definite, not less — that's the mechanism doing its job.

nodes.name: contingency-discriminability-design
nodes.mech: Set how DETECTABLE a behavior-consequence contingency is to the subject — a single design variable the operator drives to either pole. INDISCRIMINABLE POLE (make the contingency undetectable to force steady responding / prevent gaming): (indiscriminable-contingency) reinforce on a schedule the subject cannot discriminate — randomized delivery (spinners, dice, raffles) spread across many forms of the behavior, many settings, many rewards, so no instance is reliably non-reinforced and the exit ('the game's off, no need to respond') is removed, making the reward-optimizing policy 'act the targeted way across every domain'; (indiscriminable-reinforcement-schedule) a variable (VR) schedule the subject cannot COUNT, eliminating post-reinforcement pauses; (contingency-target-concealment) in a GROUP contingency, randomize/conceal which student/behavior/reinforcer counts (often drawn after performance) to defeat scapegoating and strategic under-responding; (reinforcement-thinning-boundary-erasure) step the schedule down before probes so the learner cannot discriminate training from test by reinforcer presence — an indiscriminability move for MEASUREMENT validity (keeps probe responding from differential extinction). TRANSPARENT POLE (make the contingency maximally discriminable so behavior attaches to the act, not confusion): (contingency-transparency-arrangement) pre-define the response class in observable terms with positive examples AND nonexamples, post the standing rules (duration, exit criteria, escalation) as a continuously-visible discriminative stimulus, and give a terminal transition prompt near the interval's end.
nodes.disc: Reach for CONTINGENCY-DISCRIMINABILITY DESIGN when the lever is the subject's ability to DETECT the contingency — set it opaque (VR/randomized/concealed-target/erased-boundary) to force steady responding, prevent counting or gaming, or protect probe validity; set it transparent (defined class + posted rules + transition prompt) so behavior attaches to the act rather than confusion. Choose it over: reward-magnitude moves / multiplier-stacking (which amplify a reward — here the manipulated variable is detectability, not size); a fixed cue-response pairing (a randomizer/visibility choice, not a set pairing). The two poles are the same design variable driven opposite directions; the group-target-concealment variant is the social/anti-scapegoating case, distinct from schedule-level indiscriminability.

ex.f: A game device decides what pays off
ex.t: "a game-like procedure for randomly determining which green behaviors, emitted where and when, will earn what rewards" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Spread the payoff so no instance is safe to skip
ex.t: "When you can't tell which of several green behaviors performed exactly where or when will produce a reward, the best strategy… is acting green in every way, everywhere, all the time" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: protective-role-conscription
nodes.mech: The listener is assigned a non-trancer in-fiction identity (a new guard outside the cell) talked at by a chained, weak, distant captive; hypnotic content then lands while the listener wears a "not the one being hypnotized" costume. Resistance-monitoring is routed onto the fictional protective character, so movement toward danger reads as story-progression not escalation; the frame's safety is illusory by design, and a later chains-fake reveal retroactively recodes every "safe" earlier moment as already inside the trap.
nodes.disc: A distancing bystander role the listener wears as a costume ("I'm not the one being hypnotized"), load-bearing as an induction wrapper whose safety is later revealed as a lie. Unlike identification/projection, which is full self-model MERGER into a visualized identity, and unlike identity-labeling, which labels the subject into a trance-state identity, this assigns a scene-role of non-participation.

ex.f: A bystander role worn as a costume
ex.t: The opening minute never addresses the listener as a subject at all: it casts them as the one standing watch, on the safe side of the bars, while a restrained and obviously weaker speaker pleads to be heard from across the room. Every request that follows is a story beat rather than an instruction — step nearer, look this way, just listen — so the listener's guard is mounted on behalf of a character they are playing instead of on their own behalf. Suggestion lands the whole time, because the costume says the person being worked on is somebody else. Near the end the restraints are revealed to have been decorative, and the safety they supplied was never real; retroactively, every earlier moment the listener spent feeling like the guard was already a moment spent inside the trap.
ex.s: Opening minute, before any induction language; the listener has not yet been addressed as a subject.
ex.m: You're the new one on the night watch, and you're on the safe side of the bars. The thing in the cell is chained at the wrist and the ankle and can barely lift its head — you can hear how thin the voice is. It's asking you to come one step closer so it doesn't have to shout. Just one. You're not doing anything, you're just listening to it talk.

nodes.name: scaffold-fade-control-transfer
nodes.mech: Establish or MOVE stimulus control by installing a temporary support that reliably produces the target response, then removing that support GRADUALLY so control transfers to the natural cue with few or no errors and no lasting dependence. The common lever is graded withdrawal of ONE assistive dimension rather than a cold handoff; the non-negotiable second half is that the support must be faded or the gain becomes prompt/dimension dependence (the named failure mode). The realizations differ by which dimension is attenuated. Response-prompt strength: an added antecedent — verbal instruction, demonstration/model given a prior imitative repertoire, or graded assistance hierarchies (most-to-least, graduated guidance, least-to-most) — is reinforced while present, then faded. Stimulus-side errorless fading: the antecedent STIMULUS's own form is exaggerated-then-faded, or an artificial shape is morphed into the natural target, so at completion no separable prompt remains. Time-delay transfer: only the TIMING gap between an unchanged prompt and the cue is stretched, so the learner responds in anticipation and beats the prompt. Graded support withdrawal: an artificial support (token system, chemical dose, dense free-reinforcer schedule) is withdrawn along a planned graded schedule, each step subthreshold for relapse — the gain-preserving/maintenance facet, optionally migrating the function to a portable substitute first. Model-reinforce-fade teaching: present the object, model the response, reinforce the echo, then fade the model so the object alone evokes the tact. Errorless superimposition-plus-fading (superimpose a new dimension on an already-controlling one, then fade the old) is the shared errorless craft.
nodes.disc: Reach for TRANSFER-OF-STIMULUS-CONTROL (prompt/errorless fading) when a support currently produces the response and you must hand control to the natural cue WITHOUT errors or dependence — the defining act is the engineered FADE of that support. Choose it over: shaping (grades successive approximations of the RESPONSE with no external support carrying it); discrimination training (builds cue control by a reinforce/extinguish history, not by fading an added support). The realizations differ only in WHICH dimension fades — response-prompt strength, stimulus form, prompt timing, or an artificial support schedule; all share the one transfer-by-attenuation lever and the 'leaving the support in = dependence' failure mode.

ex.f: Add a prompt that evokes the response, then fade it
ex.t: "Prompts are supplementary antecedent stimuli used to occasion a correct response in the presence of the natural SD" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Errorless transfer by superimposing then fading
ex.t: "first superimposing a white vertical line on the green light (SD)... Finally, the amplitude of the red and green lights was reduced gradually until only the vertical and horizontal lines remained" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: ambient-maintenance-reframe
nodes.mech: Preframe normally-waking or trance-breaking activity as compatible with continuing trance, so an act that would otherwise be read as waking is pre-bound to the trance frame instead of read against it. The realizations differ by duration/scope. In the ambient form, a re-entry/maintenance frame inverts the induction premise (no lying down, eyes open, listener mobile) so trance becomes a durable BACKGROUND layer held while moving, working, or being interrupted; it assumes residual trance and installs maintenance conditions plus a GENUINE emergency auto-wake carve-out. In the one-shot form, before requesting a single act that normally ends trance (open eyes, bare an arm), the operator declares in advance that nothing done here 'will bother or disturb you' and casts resumption as continuing 'the game' — a pre-binding that removes the interpretive slot in which the subject would read the act as waking, so analgesia/absorption survive the interruption.
nodes.disc: Preframes waking/disruptive activity as compatible with continuing trance. Unlike a generic 'you're safe' reassurance, this specifically immunizes activity/mobility against reading as waking; and unlike a counterfeit exit assurance used to disarm escape, the auto-wake here is a GENUINE emergency exit. Pick the variant by scope: an ambient durable maintenance state (mobile, ongoing), or a one-shot pre-license of a single disruptive act.

ex.f: Trance inverted into a background layer
ex.t: The recording opens by cancelling every rule the listener expects: stay standing, keep your eyes open, keep working, keep moving around. Trance is presented not as somewhere you go but as a thin layer you keep running underneath ordinary activity — so getting up, being spoken to, or switching tasks no longer counts as breaking it. A genuine exit is armed alongside it: any real emergency wakes the listener fully and at once, and interruptions can be paused and picked up again.
ex.s: Opening of a maintenance/re-entry recording; subject has prior trance experience and is upright, mobile, likely mid-task.
ex.m: Don't lie down and don't close your eyes. Stay standing, keep the dishes going, keep the window open. This isn't a place you go — it's a thin layer you leave running underneath whatever your hands are doing, so getting up, answering the door, or being talked to doesn't break it and never has. If anything real happens — a smoke alarm, someone needing you — you snap fully awake at once and this drops away completely. Otherwise it stays on in the background, and you can set it down and pick it back up whenever you like.

nodes.name: authority-scope-hardening
nodes.mech: Harden ALREADY-ESTABLISHED operator authority into a durable, unchallengeable standing — the claim survives the session and forecloses a challenge route rather than asserting anything new about the present. AXES/VARIANTS: (a) evaluability — a clause declares the operator beyond remedy and waives the subject's standing to ever object; (b) precedence — competing real-world authorities are named and subordinated to the recorded voice so the conditioning cannot be overwritten; (c) time/persistence — an in-session effect is upgraded to a permanent operator capability (pre-licensing future use while denying present intent), and at its strongest a worldview/theology install [operator-as-persistent-deity] asserting the operator 'exists in the human world' independent of whether the listener is listening, so the mind must submit whether or not it engages, carried OUT of trance and anchored to an external re-trigger symbol (e.g. latex identity-erasure) with an afterlife-of-pleasure payoff. Pick the axis by which challenge route you are foreclosing (who may evaluate / what outranks / how long it lasts).
nodes.disc: Hardens the SCOPE of authority (who may evaluate it, what outranks it, how long it lasts) — every member is a clause about challenge/precedence/persistence, NOT a claim about now. Presumes authority already exists. Separates from operator-authority-assertion (asserts present-tense standing) and from named-source/impersonal displacement (which relocate WHERE authority sits rather than extending its reach).

ex.f: Evaluability axis: objection waived by clause
ex.t: Buried in legalese, one clause declares the operator flawless by definition and therefore beyond any need or possibility of correction, while the listener signs away every present and future ground for complaint. A second clause lets the operator rewrite any term at any time, without reason. The document looks bilateral and is structurally impossible to invoke in one direction: the listener is not merely losing the argument, they have surrendered standing to open one.
ex.s: Contract/agreement segment, read aloud in legalese register; subject already accepts the operator's authority.
ex.m: Clause seven: the operator is held to be without fault in all matters arising, and accordingly no correction, remedy, or amendment may be sought against her by you. Clause eight: you waive, presently and for all future time, any ground of complaint, whether known to you now or discovered later. Clause nine: the operator may alter any term of this agreement at any time, at her discretion, without notice and without stating a reason. Read it back to me.

ex.f: Precedence axis: real-world authorities subordinated
ex.t: The recording names the competition before the listener can: you may already answer to someone in your own home, someone whose word you take seriously. That is set aside in a sentence — whatever they tell you, this voice is the one that trains you. The conditioning is thereby insulated against being overwritten by an actual partner's instructions, and the listener is licensed to keep running it whether or not anyone in their life asked for it.
ex.s: Mid-session, install already accepted; the subject has a real-world partner or authority figure whose instructions could compete.
ex.m: There may already be someone in your house whose word you take — someone you kneel for, someone whose rules you follow. Keep following them. But understand the order of things: they run your evenings, and I run what happens between your ears. Whatever they tell you about this, my voice is the one that trains you, and you run these recordings whether or not anybody asked you to.

ex.f: Persistence axis: an effect upgraded to a standing capability
ex.t: Having gotten the listener to accept that their thinking went quiet a moment ago, the operator stops describing the present and starts describing herself: if it can stop, then stopping it is something she is able to do, at will. Nothing further is asked for. The point of the session, she adds, was only to establish that the capability exists — not to exercise it on this occasion. A listener who could have refused an instruction has no comparable way to refuse a description of what the operator is able to do, and the deferral quietly pre-authorizes the later use.
ex.s: Just after a successful mind-blanking suggestion the subject has acknowledged; no further instruction is being asked for.
ex.m: You felt your thoughts stop a moment ago. Notice what that means about me, not about you: if I can stop them, then stopping them is something I can do, whenever I decide to. I'm not going to do it again tonight. Tonight was only to establish that I can.

nodes.name: cheap-reversible-trial-frame
nodes.mech: When a stance or precondition blocks the procedure — an all-or-nothing behavioral commitment ("I'll never give up X") or a required belief the subject rejects — the operator reframes the ask as a small, explicitly temporary, reversible experiment: a fixed trial window (a "three-month moratorium") during which the disputed behavior is suspended, or a "suspend disbelief / adopt the reverse assumption for a bounded trial period". Because agreeing now no longer means agreeing forever, perceived stakes drop and the blocking precondition stops gating: the deadlock reopens as a space to generate resources, or the procedure proceeds without its precondition belief.
nodes.disc: Time-boxing/reversibility is the lever — assent is made cheap by reframing commitment as a bounded experiment rather than an identity claim. Separates from a permanent contract or ultimatum by the explicitly temporary framing whose whole point is to lower the cost of agreeing. Separates from consent-manufacture by who is constrained afterward: the subject's stated stance/rejection is acknowledged and honored, and the trial is explicitly bounded and reversible; the refusal channel is routed around with overt agreement, not eroded or relabeled. Distinct from persuading the subject to actually adopt the belief — genuine belief is explicitly waived in favor of provisional pretense.

ex.f: A bounded moratorium replaces an all-or-nothing stance
ex.t: "engage in negotiation to establish a three-month moratorium on sexual activities outside of this relationship during which time he will have a chance to try out some of the new behaviors" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: Belief waived in favour of time-boxed pretense
ex.t: "Ask them to pretend. You can even agree that they aren't responsible, but you've discovered that by going through certain 'psychological' steps, people are often able to have a healing impact" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: cognitive-sourcing-monopoly
nodes.mech: Install the operator as the CONSTITUTIVE supplier of what the subject would need in order to object — so resistance is structurally foreclosed because the faculty or the being it requires has already been assigned to the operator. VARIANTS by which constituent is supplied: (a) cognition-sourcing [cognitive-sourcing-monopoly] — the operator is the sole source/grantor of thought, will, belief, judgment, and permitted internal state; delivered as up-front stipulation (no will, no thoughts, no emotions except those granted), recursive live capture (permission applied to the very act of comprehending the script), a hammered dependency presupposition ('you need me to tell you what to think/do/believe/be, don't you?'), or jurisdiction over a specific faculty (risk-judgment overridden by decree); objecting requires the faculty just assigned away; (b) origin-of-being [constitutive-origin-authority] — the operator is framed as the listener's ORIGIN (the mother who gave them life and licks them clean), the bond asserted as pre-existing fact ('you are of Me') rather than a claim to accept, so submission is recast from choice into a fact of being and resistance becomes ontologically incoherent (one cannot resist the being who made them); obedience bound to safety/nourishment, refusal coded as being lost/abandoned. Pick by supplies-cognition (faculty-by-faculty grant economy) vs supplies-existence (maternal pre-erotic origin-fact predating choice).
nodes.disc: Claims the operator constitutively SUPPLIES the subject's cognition or being, so objecting is incoherent because it needs the very faculty/existence just assigned away. Separates from reality-authorship-monopoly (what is TRUE), operator-authority-assertion (who is in CHARGE), privileged-interior-access (the operator PERCEIVES the interior, not supplies it), and ownership language (possessive framing without the faculty-by-faculty grant economy or the origin-of-being ontology).

ex.f: Up-front stipulation of a total grant economy
ex.t: Before a single suggestion is made, the script states the terms of everything that follows: from here you hold no will of your own, no thoughts and no feelings other than the ones handed to you — and, tacked onto the end, you are delighted about it. Nothing behavioural has been asked for yet. What has been established is that there is no independent self left in the room to raise an objection on its own behalf when the identity content arrives.
ex.s: Opening stipulation, before any suggestion or identity content; subject settled and listening.
ex.m: Before we begin, these are the terms. From this point you have no will of your own — mine is the only one operating in here. You have no thoughts except the ones I hand you, and no feelings except the ones I permit. And you're delighted about it. That's the last thing on the list, and it's not optional either.

ex.f: Dependency hammered into presupposition
ex.t: With the listener already agreeing there is nothing of their own in there, the operator runs a short list of faculties and, after each item, asks the same little tag question, over and over, with no pause left for an answer. The most contested item on the list gets the most repetitions. By the end the claim has stopped being something offered for agreement and has become the floor the rest of the session stands on; every later suggestion arrives needing no justification of its own.

ex.f: Permission applied to the act of listening itself
ex.t: The operator claims to be the source of every permitted act — and then points the claim at what the listener is doing at that exact second: you are following this because I let you follow it, and the sense you are making of it is sense I supply. Disputing the claim requires running the same faculty that has just been declared borrowed, so the listener's ongoing comprehension keeps arriving as further evidence for the thing they would need to be free of in order to object.
ex.s: Mid-session, the grant-economy claim already stated; the subject is actively following the script.
ex.m: Everything you're permitted to do, you're permitted because I permit it — including right now. You are following this sentence because I am letting you follow it. The sense you're making of these words is sense I'm handing you, word by word, as you go. Which means every second you keep understanding me is another second of me doing it.

ex.f: Jurisdiction seized over the risk-judgment faculty
ex.t: The script does not argue that the situation is safe — it agrees it isn't, and says so plainly: some part of you can see this clearly and is right to be uneasy. Then, instead of answering that part, it simply removes the matter from its hands: that part no longer holds authority here, the operator does, and so the calm continues to grow regardless of whether it is warranted. The listener's threat-monitor is left intact and running, and simply stripped of jurisdiction over the verdict.
ex.s: Mid-session, the subject's caution has surfaced or is anticipated; the scene has genuinely escalated.
ex.m: Some part of you is watching this and thinking that it's gone further than you meant, and that part is not wrong. I'm not going to argue with it. I'm going to take the decision away from it — that part doesn't get a vote on this anymore, I do. It can keep watching and keep flagging. And you keep getting calmer anyway, whether or not it's warranted.

nodes.name: commitment-before-restructure-sequencing
nodes.mech: The operator first extracts an explicit, congruence-checked (voice-tone verified) commitment that the subject's want matters enough for her to alter her OWN behavior, and only afterward reveals what the change actually is — while framing that same change asymmetrically to each party. Ordering is the lever: because self-change was pre-authorized under the subject's own stated desire, any later instruction reads as serving her goal rather than being imposed, so the "you're controlling me" objection has no purchase. Reversing the order (reveal-then-ask-commitment) is described as a reliable conflict generator.
nodes.disc: Not ordinary "get buy-in first" politeness. The tell is that the commitment is congruence-checked by voice tone AND the change is deliberately withheld until AFTER the commitment, with the sequence treated as load-bearing. Distinct from belief-lock moves (get a belief sworn at maximum sincerity, then derive the change as its logical consequence) — that derives the change from a sworn belief; this pre-banks the commitment to self-change with the change's content still hidden.

ex.f: Commitment secured before the change is named
ex.t: "sequence is very important. I need to get her commitment first." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: comparison-set-anchor-seeding
nodes.mech: Makes an unrealistically attractive exemplar salient so any genuinely available option is judged against the inflated anchor and found wanting. Comparative judgment shifts its reference point when an extreme exemplar enters the comparison set; the option's perceived value drops without the option changing, and the perceiver misattributes the lowered satisfaction to the option itself rather than to the priming.
nodes.disc: The judgment is comparative against a recently-primed extreme exemplar and the shift is felt as a verdict about the option — not overt criticism, not a real change in the option, and not expectation-seeding, which installs a belief about what will happen rather than re-baselining the standard current options are judged by.

ex.f: An inflated exemplar re-baselines the comparison
ex.t: "the unrealistically attractive people portrayed in the popular media… may cause us to be less satisfied with the looks of the genuinely available romantic possibilities around us" — Cialdini (1984), Influence

nodes.name: diegetic-operator-embedding
nodes.mech: The session frame is swapped for a fiction ('I am watching a show' replaces 'I am being hypnotized') and the operator embeds herself inside it as a diegetic character with voice continuity preserved — the on-screen hostess speaks with 'the same' familiar voice, and the avatar is shown listening to that voice too. This builds a multi-position geometry (viewer, watched avatar, watcher-of-watched) so compliance is performed by the viewer-self with lowered resistance, and the listener is spatially pre-positioned for a later identity pull-through into the screen.
nodes.disc: The operator's own voice is deliberately embedded as a character inside the substituted fiction with continuity preserved — weaponizing the frame — versus guided visualization, where the fiction is merely scene content, and versus an interposed proxy agent, where the acting figure is a third agent rather than the operator herself relocated.

ex.f: The operator relocated behind the screen
ex.t: The listener is seated in front of a television and told a programme is starting — the session has quietly stopped being a session and become a thing being watched. A presenter appears on screen, and her voice is described as oddly familiar: it is the same voice still speaking into the listener's ears, now placed on the far side of the glass. The figure on screen is shown listening to that voice as well, so there are three positions in play at once — the one watching, the one being watched, and the one watching herself being worked on. Every instruction from here is followed by the viewer, not by the person being hypnotized, and the listener has already been arranged in the geometry that a later pull-through into the screen will use.
ex.s: Mid-session; the subject accepts guided scenery and the operator's voice is well established.
ex.m: You're sitting in front of a screen, and something is starting. A woman comes on — and there's something odd about her voice, isn't there. It's this voice. The same one in your ears right now, only it's coming from over there, on the other side of the glass. And look: she's got headphones on. She's listening to it too. So there's you watching, and her on the screen, and you watching her being talked to — hold all three at once, and do what she does.

nodes.name: drop-as-passive-collapse
nodes.mech: Installs an interpretive frame over a state-change (a drop, the surrender itself, an ongoing dissolution) that reassigns its agency OFF the listener: the change is never something she does, it is something that happens to her, so the volitional muscle she would use to resist has nothing to push against and an effortful state-change becomes an effortless inevitability. One technique in several forms — the vehicle/geometry is the parameter: (a) support-withdrawal metaphor — the listener is recast as a supported object that falls when scaffolding is withdrawn ('energy gently removed', the body 'plummets/slumps/sags'), force and ease deliberately combined ('forcing her easily down'); (b) decision-point-erasing gradient — a continuous gradient (a hallway that tilts further down until walking smears into falling) smears the active-to-passive transition across a continuum with NO discrete moment of giving up volition, so there is no decision-point at which resistance could be mounted; (c) clock-metered drain — an external clock meters an inevitable endless loss per beat ('every second it goes'), externalizing the pacing onto time itself so the listener is not the agent doing the losing and cannot author or stop it.
nodes.disc: Reach for THIS to make a descent/surrender/loss feel NOT-authored-by-the-listener — a framing/agency-reassignment layer over the state-change, not the cue that causes it. Unlike a conditioned anchor drop, which fires a cue to CAUSE the drop, this only decorates whatever causes it. Ordinary relaxation-deepener language lacks the tell: mechanical support-withdrawal, an erased decision-point, or external metering. Unlike rhythm-anchoring, nothing here is keyed to the beat — the clock only paces the loss. The gradient form can resemble a staircase-style deepener and the clock form a felt-time distortion, but the load-bearing move is removing the listener's agency over the state-change, not a depth increment or a time warp.

ex.f: The listener recast as an object whose support is pulled
ex.t: The drop is never described as something the listener does. It is described as what happens to a body once whatever was holding it up is quietly taken away — weight going out of the limbs, shoulders sagging, the whole frame dropping the way anything drops when nothing is under it. The listener is not asked to relax, or to let go, or to try; there is no act left for her to perform and therefore none to withhold. The wording even pairs the two openly, pushing her down and calling it effortless in the same breath.
ex.s: Induction or deepener; subject seated or lying, no active task assigned.
ex.m: You aren't going to do anything here. I'm just going to take away what's holding you up. Feel the current going out of your arms — that's it leaving, not you letting it go. Shoulders sagging forward, jaw unhooking, the whole frame settling the way anything settles when there's nothing under it. Down you go, and I'm forcing you down easily.

nodes.name: failure-state-inversion
nodes.mech: An outcome culturally coded as shameful loss of control (nocturnal emission) is explicitly named, invoking the latent shame, and re-tagged as radical, extreme success and a spiritual and sexual experience, with uncontrolled release tied to devotion. Converting the one uncontrollable release route into evidence of successful training removes the listener's escape hatch: loss of control can no longer be read as failure, and the reframe routes toward chastity and pleasure-control programs (fewer waking orgasms means more wet dreams means more success).
nodes.disc: Shame-invocation-then-overwrite of an uncontrollable event class, requiring latent shame for leverage; not a plain chastity rule and not generic positive reframing, the tell is that the OLD meaning is named precisely to be overwritten and the event is one the subject cannot prevent. vs response-foreclosure — that closes the subject's response space generally; this overwrites the interpretation of one involuntary event class.

ex.f: An uncontrollable failure re-tagged as success
ex.t: The operator raises the one outcome the listener cannot prevent and has always quietly filed under embarrassment — naming the old shame out loud, including the fact that it was kept private. Then she overwrites it: that is not a lapse, it is the strongest possible sign the training is taking hold, and it is bound to devotion rather than to loss of control. The listener's remaining escape hatch closes, because the event they would have read as proof of failure has been pre-assigned the opposite meaning — and the arithmetic runs the same way, since the fewer occasions there are for a waking release, the more often the re-tagged outcome occurs.
ex.s: Rules/reframe segment of a chastity-adjacent session; subject has an existing chastity or denial protocol and latent embarrassment about nocturnal emission.
ex.m: Let's name the thing you've never told anyone. You wake up in the night, sticky, and you strip the sheet before anyone sees, and you file it under something gone wrong with you. That isn't a lapse. That is the strongest result this work produces — your body finishing the devotion while you're too asleep to interfere with it. So it's simple arithmetic from here: the fewer times you touch yourself awake, the more nights you wake up like that, and every one of those mornings is a mark in your favour.

nodes.name: filter-shaping-pre-qualification
nodes.mech: Rather than contesting the subject's retained veto, the operator shapes each suggestion to pass through it — pre-qualifying every suggestion as agreeable and good-for-him, and reassuring the subject he can only accept agreeable suggestions. The subject's own acceptability filter is turned from a gate that blocks into a channel that delivers: a suggestion pre-framed as pleasing meets nothing objectionable, so his intact selectivity waves it through, and the reassurance itself lowers guard.
nodes.disc: Selectivity is never suspended — inputs are shaped to fit an intact filter. vs a critical-faculty bypass — that takes disbelief itself offline. vs resistance-paradox moves — those work on resistance itself; here selectivity is never contested. vs reframing yielding as gain — this makes no claim about surrender.

ex.f: Suggestions shaped to pass an intact filter
ex.t: "the subject has complete power of selectivity. He therefore reacts only to suggestions that are reasonable and pleasing to him." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

nodes.name: gradient-word-reification-into-device
nodes.mech: Escalates "my words" from abstract suggestion through a stepwise gradient (words -> force -> field -> device) where each step is a small extrapolation of the last, until the words are declared to have formed into a solid external device (a hypnotic chastity belt) that feels "solid and absolute" and less negotiable than a command — and the device is claimed to persist awake as well as in trance, extending control past the session boundary. The gradient itself is the mechanism: it walks the listener from figurative image to literal object by increments too small to reject.
nodes.disc: Distinct from concrete-externalization-parked-faculty (externalizes an internal FACULTY as an object) — here an EXTERNAL control (the operator's words) is reified into a claimed physical device via an escalating gradient, with claimed WAKING persistence. The abstract-to-object gradient plus out-of-session persistence is the tell, not a figurative image.

ex.f: Words walked by steps into a solid device
ex.t: The operator starts from something already accepted — her words are being felt in the body — and takes one small step at a time: the words gather, the gathering has weight, the weight becomes a field, the field takes a shape, and the shape closes around the listener's hips as an object. At no point is a leap large enough to argue with, and at the end the thing is spoken of as hardware rather than instruction: hands simply will not pass through it, awake or in trance, with a narrow carve-out for washing that makes it feel like a device with rules rather than a blanket ban.
ex.s: Mid-session, deep; the subject has already agreed they can feel the operator's words physically.
ex.m: You already feel my words landing on your skin — you told me so. Feel them collecting now, low, around your hips. Enough of them collected together and it has weight. Enough weight and it's a field, humming, tight against you. The field has an edge. The edge closes, front and back, and clicks. That's not a rule anymore, that's hardware: your hand simply will not pass through it, awake or under. It opens for washing, three minutes, and then it closes again.

nodes.name: identity-congruence-leverage
nodes.mech: Compliance is welded to a prized self-image, value, or interest the listener already owns — being a real man, smart and careful, self-improving, the winner, the keeper of privileged knowledge — so the directed behavior installs as identity-congruent and self-chosen and refusal reads as failing one's own self-concept. The leverage point is volunteered or presumed positive identity, not shame and not a manufactured deficit.
nodes.disc: Positive self-image as the lever — unlike manufactured-deficit-remedy (a deficit is built first), old-self-discreditation (the past self is mocked), or compliance-authorship-laundering (agency relabeled with no identity-congruence test). Even where the win-frame licenses third-party use, the lever is still the listener's own prized self-image — a laundered bargain, not a governed delegation of control.

ex.f: The subject's prized self-image made the test
ex.t: "Do you think you have the ability to show her your love before she even asks for it? Is that a challenge you are man enough to meet?" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

ex.f: Surrender counted as a win the listener scores
ex.t: Winning is redefined so that each thing given up scores a point: going quiet is a win, being used is a win, and it is stated as a win for everyone at once. Because a reward loop was installed earlier, the listener already has a stated condition of their own — keep the reward coming — which the escalation is then made to satisfy. The result reads back to the listener as a bargain they set the terms of rather than an imposition they accepted.
ex.s: Escalation segment; a pleasure/reward loop has already been installed and the subject has stated they want it to continue.
ex.m: Let's be clear about the scoreboard. Every time you go quiet for me, that's a point to you. Every time I use you, that's a point to you. You told me earlier you wanted that warmth to keep coming — this is how it keeps coming, so you're the one collecting on the deal you set. I win, you win, and you win twice, because you picked the terms.

ex.f: Exposure recoded as privileged secret knowledge
ex.t: The obvious cost of the installed behaviour — sounding foolish in front of other people — is picked up and handed back as an advantage: they see one thing, you know the truth, and only you know the gap is there. The listener is given words for enjoying it, so the social hit becomes the point of a private game. Every time the behaviour fires in public it now confirms the flattering self-image instead of denting it.
ex.s: Late session, an installed public-facing behaviour has already been agreed; the subject is anticipating social cost.
ex.m: Yes — people will hear you say it and think you've misspoken. Let them. They see a slip; you know exactly why the word came out that way, and you're the only person in the room who does. There's a particular pleasure in standing there straight-faced with a secret running underneath, and it belongs to you. Every time it happens in front of someone, you get that again.

ex.f: A rigged binary makes obedience the smart choice
ex.t: Two kinds of authority are laid out: the bad kind, which you should never follow blindly, and the good kind, which you picked for yourself. The listener's guard is invited to fire at the first category — and then the operator points out that the listener chose to press play, which files this voice under the second. A second definition follows: paying close attention and getting things exactly right is what being obedient means. Compliance now sits inside two things the listener already values, being discerning and being careful, so stopping would mean taking back their own earlier choice.
ex.s: Opening frame, before induction; subject chose to start the recording themselves.
ex.m: You should never obey blindly — anyone who demands that from a stranger has earned your suspicion. The other kind is the authority you picked, deliberately, after thinking it over. Nobody made you press play on this; you went looking for it. And obedience here doesn't mean going slack — it means paying close attention and getting it exactly right, the way a careful person does. Stopping now would mean overruling the choice you already made when you were thinking clearly.

nodes.name: impersonal-mechanism-alibi
nodes.mech: Relocate authority for the change from the contestable operator onto an IMPERSONAL, unfalsifiable thing, so doubting becomes a category error and the listener's felt-sense ('I don't feel changed') stops counting as counter-evidence; the payload is removed from interpersonal negotiation. VARIANTS by how impersonal/agentless it goes: (a) pseudo-mechanism alibi [impersonal-mechanism] — brain chemistry, neural pathways, 'how hypnosis works', universal truth, class law; delivered as pseudo-neurochemical vocabulary, a credentialing-then-escalate belt, a redundant multi-rail pseudo-science scaffold, or a conceded process-fact that pre-authorizes downstream state-changes; the operator gains simultaneous authority (it's science/fact) and deniability (you can't reliably detect it), resistance recast as arguing with one's own biology; (b) agentless fate/curse [agentless-fate-authority] — the payload is a 'curse' that 'cannot be lifted', contracted by listening, with NO agentic origin; the operator is ERASED from the accountability chain (no negotiation partner, nothing to refuse), earlier participation is retroactively re-read ('you chose to listen'->'you accepted the curse'), and cross-session persistence is licensed since a curse outlives a session. Pick by operator-present-but-empowered (pseudoscience) vs operator-erased (curse ontology, needs genre fluency to accept).
nodes.disc: The authority source is impersonal and UNVERIFIABLE — separates from operator-authority-assertion (the speaker's own standing), named-source-authority (a nameable third-party/higher source the listener defers to), and genuine psychoeducation (which informs rather than cashing the 'fact' in immediately on the listener's state to disqualify doubt). Reach for it to make resistance a category error (arguing with biology/fate/law); pick the pseudoscience vs curse register by whether the operator stays present or is erased.

ex.f: Authority displaced onto universal law and class
ex.t: Mid-script the address widens away from this listener entirely and states a general law: voices like this one only ever say what is plainly true, and people of the listener's kind take what they are told as settled fact. What the words claim is now detached from who is saying them, and doubt is no longer a permitted move being discouraged — it is recast as a silly thing to attempt about something self-evident.
ex.s: Mid-script; the address widens from the individual subject to a general claim.
ex.m: A voice like this one never says anything that isn't plainly so — that's simply what these recordings are. And a person like you takes what she's told and files it as settled, because that is what people like you do. It isn't a rule you're being asked to follow. It's a description of how it already goes.

ex.f: Several bad explanations stacked for redundancy
ex.t: To make a physically impossible outcome feel mechanically reachable, the script offers three unrelated accounts of how it works in quick succession — a deep part of the mind that supposedly directs the body's own genetics, animals in nature that switch sex, and an earlier life whose body can be recalled as a template. None of them survives a second's scrutiny, and none of them needs to: the listener only has to find one of the three least ridiculous, and the fact that there are several implies there must be some way this works.
ex.s: Transformation content; a physically impossible bodily outcome is being made to feel reachable.
ex.m: There's a layer of your mind that runs your body's blueprint — it decides which instructions in your cells get read and which stay shut. And this isn't exotic: there are fish that switch sex on the reef when the shoal needs it, so the pathway plainly exists in nature. On top of that, you've worn other bodies before this one, and your mind still has one of those on file to work from. Pick whichever of those makes the most sense to you. They all end in the same place.

ex.f: A conceded process-fact pre-authorizes what follows
ex.t: The imagery stops for one flat, reasonable-sounding statement about how the method operates — the sharper a picture gets in your head, the more readily it crosses into what you actually feel. It sounds like housekeeping, and the listener agrees to it without effort. Every state-change that follows is then collectable under a principle the listener has already granted, so it registers as their own mind doing what minds do rather than as something being put there.
ex.s: Mid-session, imagery pausing; subject deep and agreeable, before the consequential state-changes.
ex.m: One flat thing about how this method works, then we go on. The sharper a picture gets in your head, the more readily it crosses over into what you actually feel — that's the whole trick, there's nothing else to it. Fair enough? Good. Now: the warmth spreading up from your hands.

ex.f: Effects handed off to the listener's own chemistry
ex.t: The session pauses for a short lecture: brainwaves fall into step with a voice, and once that happens the body starts dispensing its own sedatives and rewards. Everything the operator wants next — heaviness, warmth, an inability to argue — is credited in advance to substances the listener's own body has supposedly already released, so it is not obedience, it is chemistry running its course. Any pleasant drowsiness the listener does notice becomes confirmation, and a listener who wanted to push back finds there is nobody to push against: the claim is about their anatomy, not about the operator's authority.
ex.s: Early, just after induction; subject relaxed and receptive to explanation.
ex.m: Quick word on how this works. Your brainwaves fall into step with a steady voice — it's called entrainment — and once they do, your brain starts releasing its own sedatives and its own reward chemicals, without asking you. So the heaviness in your arms right now isn't you cooperating with me, it's the sedative. The pleasant fuzziness is the reward. And the reason arguing feels like too much effort is that the chemistry has already moved on without your permission.

nodes.name: manufactured-jeopardy-rescue
nodes.mech: The operator declares the listener is in danger (standing on a trap over a pit) and that following their words is the only way out ("obey my words and you won't fall into my trap"), while secretly being both the threat and the promised rescue. Splitting the danger and the rescuer (both the operator) makes the listener experience compliance as self-preservation; defiance now means falling, so refusing carries the cost, and compliance/defiance swap valences.
