nodes.disc: A manufactured imminent danger whose only exit is obedience, with the operator covertly both threat and rescuer. vs a benign 'follow along and relax' invitation — no jeopardy. vs its comfort-valence cousin — a sibling move that reroutes relief rather than jeopardy.

ex.f: Obedience as the only exit from a manufactured danger
ex.t: The recording opens by telling the listener where they are standing: on something that will give way, over a drop, right now. It then supplies the single route out — do exactly as the voice says and the floor holds. Following commands has stopped being submission and become the listener saving their own skin, while stopping the recording has become the dangerous option. The voice never mentions that it built the floor.

nodes.name: modality-relabel-wrapper
nodes.mech: The operator re-presents an intervention the subject has just refused under a harmless everyday label ("take dictation" rather than "be hypnotized") and insistently secures performance of the relabeled task. Resistance is attached to the name of the modality, not its content; stripping the trigger label and swapping in an unobjectionable carrier task lets the identical process run with the objection never activating, and attributing the resulting relief to something other than the intervention further insulates the mechanism.
nodes.disc: Only the outer relabeling wrapper — choosing the cover name and getting the refused task accepted — independent of any payload hidden inside the carrier (embedding a payload in the carrier is its own separate move). Unlike resistance-utilization, the objection is never contacted or folded into deepening; its trigger label simply never appears.

ex.f: The refused modality accepted under a harmless name
ex.t: "she did not mind losing her headaches by 'taking dictation' from the author" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

nodes.name: model-coherence-laundering
nodes.mech: Entailment-laundering: get the subject to ACCEPT a proposition, premise, or model upfront, then present the payload as its logical CONSEQUENCE, so the install lands as entailed rather than imposed and a subject who bought the premise has no remaining grounds to reject the application. Two forms: (a) model-coherence laundering — a didactic first half builds an explanatory MODEL (neurons, subconscious, void, dopamine) with nothing decorative, and the payload half reuses those EXACT constructs verbatim as the literal building blocks of the install; the lever is model self-consistency; (b) delayed-syllogism detonation — assert an abstract 'fact' early as obvious common sense ('you can only relax with someone you love'), STORE the subject's free assent to the general premise, then much later run it in reverse with a silent 'someone'->'me' substitution to conclude they love the operator, so the conclusion feels like their own prior agreement.
nodes.disc: Bank an accepted premise/model, then cash the payload as its ENTAILMENT. vs presupposing the target as already true — that asserts it settled with no argument; here the payload is DERIVED from something the subject accepted. vs concept-redefinition — that redefines a concept as belief; here an accepted framework/premise is weaponized so its application is non-rejectable. Pick the form by scale: a whole didactic model reused verbatim, or a single stored premise detonated later via silent substitution.

ex.f: The explanation half becomes the install's parts list
ex.t: The first half of the session sounds like an explanation of how the technique works — what the mind does with unwanted material, where it stores things, what makes a voice start to feel good. None of it is decoration. The second half builds the payload out of exactly those parts: the hollow place described earlier is where something now gets put, and the pleasant-voice account from earlier is what the new attachment is made of. Because each step is the previous explanation applied rather than a fresh claim, a listener who accepted the walkthrough has nothing left to object to when the conclusion arrives.

nodes.name: own-language-echo-reframe-durability
nodes.mech: The operator first gathers the subject's exact terms for their intention — their nominalizations, unspecified verbs, and idioms — then re-uses those same terms when describing the NEW behavior, rather than inserting operator vocabulary. Because nothing foreign is imposed, agreement is anchored in the subject's own frame and the reframe does not later flip into a reaction against inserted content. The lever is a linguistic quality-control move for reframe durability: own-language echo prevents a delayed polarity backlash.
nodes.disc: Not general rapport-matching or pacing — that is rapport, not language-reuse. The tell is the specific gather-then-reuse of the subject's exact nominalizations/idioms to describe the NEW behavior, aimed at preventing a delayed polarity flip.

ex.f: The subject's own words reused for the new behavior
ex.t: "if you use that same set of nominalizations and unspecified verbs and idioms… you will match what he is trying to do at the unconscious level… That will avoid the polarity problem." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: rule-governed-behavior-install
nodes.mech: Verbal-rule governance: put a contingency or rule into WORDS in advance so later behavior or the appraisal of later events is governed by the operator's verbal statement rather than shaped by the subject's own experienced consequences. Two forms: (a) rule-governed behavior install — state a contingency in words ('pull the lever while pushing the button') instead of letting the subject contact it by trial-and-error; a rule-following repertoire acquires near-correct behavior from the description alone, shifting control from experienced consequences to the operator's words (and can install durable wrong behavior from an inaccurate rule); (b) advance contingency specification — fully enumerate the contingency up front (which behaviors cost what, the window boundaries, the zero-infractions reward, edge-cases) as a complete antecedent statement, so every later debit lands as a predicted rule-governed outcome, preserving credibility and pre-empting the perception of unfairness or gaming.
nodes.disc: Behavior/appraisal is governed by a verbal DESCRIPTION, not shaped by experienced consequences. vs contingency-engineering — that ARRANGES the consequences; here only the advance verbal statement is the lever. vs expectancy-seeding — that shapes the felt experience; this targets rule-following behavior or the appraisal of enforcement. Pick the form by target: acquiring a behavior from a stated rule, or legitimizing later enforcement via a complete advance contingency statement.

ex.f: A stated rule replaces contact with the contingency
ex.t: "Rules can be learned more quickly than the behavior shaped by the contingencies they describe. . . . Rules are particularly valuable when contingencies are complex or unclear" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: secondary-gain-substitution
nodes.mech: The operator identifies the concealed outcome that a symptom or refusal protects (e.g. autonomy), then constructs an alternative route to that same outcome that the subject finds at least as convincing as the symptom. Once the protected secondary gain is secured by other equally-convincing means, the symptom behavior is freed of its protective function and can be released without perceived loss, so the wanted behavior becomes available because the symptom no longer needs to defend anything.
nodes.disc: Not meta-outcome laddering that climbs to ever-more-abstract intents — the tell is the concrete build of a substitute route to one specific secondary gain, judged 'at least as convincing' by the subject. It is a design move that re-routes a protective function, not an abstraction move on the demand itself.

ex.f: An equally convincing substitute route to the hidden gain
ex.t: "you have to separate the notion of her independence or autonomy from the sexual behavior itself. She has to have some other way of knowing that she's her own woman… at least as convincing for her personally." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: self-validating-trigger-hype
nodes.mech: Self-sealing, unfalsifiable proof: rig the situation so ANY outcome — a reaction, a guaranteed body sensation, or even a failure — reads back as proof the frame is working, and the disconfirmation exit is closed. Expectancy or a claim is loaded so the confirming evidence is manufactured by the setup itself. Forms: (a) self-validating trigger hype — pre-bill the trigger phrase as 'the world's most powerful', so whatever the listener then feels reads as the trigger FIRING (wording argues its own inescapability); (b) unfalsifiable success frame — a precommitment conditional ('when you allow me to direct...') routes BOTH outcomes to a compliance verdict: feeling something = the operator did it, feeling nothing = you failed to allow; (c) sensation prelabeling — a breath protocol GUARANTEED to produce autonomic sensations (lightheadedness, tingling) paired with a frame pre-naming those sensations as proof of the operator's claim before they occur; (d) single-obstacle fear funnel — state the outcome as settled, then collapse every possible failure into ONE subject-controllable cause (fear) so any later shortfall is re-attributed to the subject, insulating the method from disconfirmation; (e) stake credibility on a test — tie the subject's credibility to a live test succeeding so passively letting it fail forces a costly self-judgment (a no-exit topology on the test result).
nodes.disc: Reach for self-sealing proof when you want the outcome to be UNFALSIFIABLE — every reaction/sensation/failure confirms the frame and no result can disconfirm it. vs expectancy-seeding — that primes an anticipated experience but does not close the fail case. vs presupposing the target as already true — that deletes the decision point by asserting completion; here a live outcome is produced and then routed to confirmation. Pick the form by what is pre-labeled: the reaction (trigger hype), a double-bind conditional, a guaranteed body sensation, a failure-blame funnel, or a self-incriminating test outcome.

ex.f: The trigger pre-billed so any reaction confirms it
ex.t: Before the phrase itself is ever spoken, it is advertised at length: the strongest trigger there is, present in everybody, effective with no prior conditioning, a way straight past the ordinary defences. Two deliberate pauses stretch the wait until the listener actively wants it. Only then is the line delivered. Whatever the listener happens to feel in the seconds afterward — a dip in alertness, a flutter, nothing much — now arrives pre-labelled as the trigger firing rather than as ordinary suggestion, so the claim has manufactured its own evidence and the failure case has been closed off.
ex.s: Before the trigger phrase has ever been spoken aloud; subject is in trance and has been told a trigger is coming.
ex.m: What I'm about to say is the most powerful trigger there is. It's already in you — everybody has it, no conditioning required, and it goes straight past whatever you use to keep your guard up. [pause] I could say it now. [longer pause] You want me to say it. Here it is: sleep now. And whatever you feel in the next few seconds — the dip, the flutter under your ribs, the odd nothing — that is it firing.

nodes.name: semantic-referent-capture
nodes.mech: The operator captures a repeated word so they become its sole referent. By floating both readings of a word ("bunny" as animal vs "a cute bunny girl") then offering herself as the referent and inviting the listener to notice which image jumped to mind, she installs herself as what the word means. Every later benign-sounding use of that word ("pet", "take care", "bunny deserves") then carries the person-load without re-consent; the frame is self-authored, lowering later resistance.
nodes.disc: Covert equivocation captures a vocabulary item so subsequent benign uses smuggle in a relational obligation the listener never re-agreed to. vs a simple pet-name introduction — no equivocation, no captured referent. vs seeding expectancy for the session — that primes what the session will feel like; this captures the meaning of a word for later reuse.

ex.f: A word captured so the operator is its meaning
ex.t: Before any trance work, the operator picks one soft, harmless noun that has both an innocent everyday sense and a person-shaped one, and asks the listener which came to mind first. Whichever the listener notices, the noticing itself is treated as the answer, and the operator then offers herself as the thing the word points to. From that moment the word has one referent. Every later cosy, unobjectionable sentence built on it — who looks after whom, what is owed — carries a claim about a person that the listener never separately agreed to, and it feels like a meaning they supplied themselves.
ex.s: Pre-induction, conversational register; subject alert, no trance yet, the word will be reused throughout the session.
ex.m: Say the word kitten. Now — which one came to mind first, the small animal, or a girl on her knees called kitten? Whichever one it was, you noticed something, and that noticing is your answer. From here, when I say kitten, this is who I mean. And a kitten gets looked after, doesn't she. A kitten gets fed, and told when to sleep, and a kitten belongs to somebody.

nodes.name: shared-roof-outcome-fusion
nodes.mech: After laddering each party's higher aims, the operator synthesizes a single outcome statement that both parties can wholeheartedly endorse, secures explicit joint agreement on that one sentence, and only then treats the disputed behavior as the sole remaining variable. A genuinely shared roof converts an adversarial contest into a joint problem-solving task, because the goal is settled and only the means remain open — most of the negotiation is effectively finished once a congruently-agreed shared aim exists.
nodes.disc: Distinct from the laddering that surfaces the aims (that is the setup) and from consent-manufacture (no refusal channel is eroded and no non-consent is relabeled as consent — both parties genuinely endorse the roof). The tell is the distinct synthesize-one-sentence-and-lock-in-joint-agreement act that follows the climb, after which behavior is the only open variable.

ex.f: One agreed sentence leaves behavior the only variable
ex.t: "Once I've got an outcome frame that both parties congruently agree to, it's just a question of varying their behaviors" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: universal-benefit-fallback-offer
nodes.mech: When deeper work is out of reach, the operator extends a low-bar benefit no subject will refuse (relaxation, anxiety relief) as a fallback PAYLOAD, leaning on the claim that no one cannot benefit from relaxation. Substituting a universally-acceptable benefit guarantees engagement even without full trance; the subject receives an immediate, recognizable payoff that builds the rapport/trust and willingness needed for later, deeper inductions.
nodes.disc: Relaxation is SELECTED as the fallback payload (a rapport/engagement move), not the delivery procedure by which relaxation is induced (e.g. a progressive-relaxation routine).

ex.f: Relaxation offered as the payload nobody refuses
ex.t: "Hypnosis can be used on every patient … if for no other reason than to relax the patient. There is no one who cannot benefit from relaxation" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

nodes.name: verdict-before-perception
nodes.mech: Pre-emptive appraisal: land the operator's authoritative appraisal or forecast BEFORE the subject forms their own perception of a stimulus, so temporal ordering forecloses independent appraisal — the subject perceives with the operator's criterion substituted for their own. Two forms: (a) verdict before perception — deliver a vivid, disgusted, authoritative VERDICT on a neutral stimulus ('that egg smells rotten') and only then invite perception, replacing the appraisal criterion itself and producing group hallucination across smell/sight; (b) somatic forecast steering — word choice about a coming PROCEDURE pre-loads the anticipated somatic sensation ('this is going to hurt' vs 'I don't think you'll mind this' about the identical procedure), in the strong register pre-naming a sensation as its opposite valence (barium enema = 'the most soothing medication ever'); heightened vulnerability makes the forecast more determinative of what is felt (waking suggestion, no trance presumed).
nodes.disc: The operator's appraisal/forecast arrives BEFORE the subject perceives, so there is no independent perception for the suggestion to modify. vs expectancy-seeding — that builds anticipation of the session/trance; this pre-empts perception of a SPECIFIC stimulus or coming sensation. vs concept-redefinition — that redefines a concept; this substitutes the appraisal criterion for one perception. Pick the form by target: a neutral stimulus's identity (verdict before perception) or a coming procedure's somatic quality (somatic forecast).

ex.f: Authoritative verdict lands before the subject samples
ex.t: "you made a positive statement of apparent fact… Respect for your judgment caused them to believe what you said even before they smelled the egg… they did so—not with their critical faculties, but with yours." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

nodes.name: affect-locus-binding
nodes.mech: A constructed imaginal locus is welded to an affective state — properties defined negation-first (no anxiety, stress, pain) or as a containing perimeter (a blanket encasing body and mind) — so the state acquires a felt location and an inside/outside boundary; distress becomes geographically incompatible with being there, and returning to the locus is returning to the state.
nodes.disc: State is BOUND to the locus with a defended boundary (to feel bad is to leave; scene residue stays outside) — vs generic positive safe-place scenery in guided-visualization, vs reward-association conditioning (no reward pairing here; spatial binding), and vs a persistent identity metaphor (no identity reinterpretation).

ex.f: A wrapped perimeter holding the state in
ex.t: The operator introduces one tactile image — something soft closing warmly around the listener — and then extends it past the body to cover the mind as well. The diffuse calm now has an edge: whatever the session stirred up is on the outside of that warmth, and the listener is on the inside. Every later suggestion is delivered as something happening within the enclosure.
ex.s: Late session, after material that stirred something up; subject deep, needs the state contained before emergence.
ex.m: Something soft is being drawn up over you — heavy, warm, closing in at the shoulders and tucked down along both sides. Now feel it go further than your skin: it comes up over your thoughts as well, and closes there too. Everything this session dragged up is on the outside of that blanket. You're on the inside, and everything I say from here, I'm saying to you in there.

ex.f: Sanctuary defined by what is absent there
ex.t: Having placed the listener inside an imagined expanse, the operator defines the expanse almost entirely by subtraction: nothing anxious reaches here, nothing hurts here, nothing dark has ever been here. Only then are positive qualities layered on top. Because the good state is now a property of a place rather than of the listener, feeling bad would mean having left — and any internal check the listener runs is pre-answered, since whatever is felt in this place is declared in advance to be the right thing to feel, so the reading of their own mood confirms the location instead of testing it.
ex.s: Mid-session; subject already placed inside a wide imagined landscape and settling into it.
ex.m: Look at what this place doesn't have. No worry reaches this far — it stops at the edge and can't cross. Nothing hurts here. Nothing bad has ever happened here, not once, in the whole history of this place. What it does have is warm air, low gold light, and ground that holds you. And whatever you're feeling right now, standing in it, is the correct thing to feel here — so check, and notice you're feeling it.

nodes.name: antagonistic-body-map-split
nodes.mech: Runs a whole-body heaviness/immobility induction, then carves out one body part (the genitals) and assigns it the OPPOSITE sensation (lightness/buoyancy), then welds the two into a reciprocal loop where lighter-there means heavier-everywhere and a more-excited exception. Splitting the body into an inert majority and one hyper-live exception foregrounds arousal by suppressing everything around it, and the reciprocal weld makes the split self-confirming (denying the lightness means denying the loop), so the listener feels immobilized everywhere except the genitals, which become the only live sensation channel.
nodes.disc: The tell is a carved-out antagonistic exception (one part gets the reverse sensation) welded into a self-confirming reciprocal loop with the rest of the body. Distinct from kinesthetic-hallucination / ordinary catalepsy induction (uniform heaviness, no carved reverse-sensation exception or reciprocal weld) and from progressive-body-substitution (rewrites the body's material, no antagonistic live-exception loop).

ex.f: One part made light while the rest goes heavy
ex.t: An ordinary heaviness induction runs over the whole body — arms, legs, everything sinking — and then one region is carved out and handed the opposite sensation, floating and buoyant, as if it were tied to a balloon. The operator immediately welds the two halves into a loop: the more that one place floats, the heavier everything else becomes, and the heavier the limbs get, the more alive that one place feels. The body is now an inert majority with a single live exception, and the exception is the only channel left carrying sensation. Disputing the lightness is awkward, because the heaviness the listener can plainly feel is offered as its evidence.
ex.s: Mid-induction; whole-body heaviness already established and limbs are visibly slack.
ex.m: Your arms are lead, your legs are lead, and the chair is taking all of it. Everything except one place — between your legs there's a balloon tied on, tugging upward, light and buzzing and awake. And the harder it pulls up, the heavier the rest of you goes; the heavier your arms get, the more alive that one spot feels. Feel how heavy your hands are right now — that's how much it's floating.

nodes.name: catalepsy-comfort-relabel
nodes.mech: Builds genuine catalepsy in redundant nested layers (doubled eyelid imagery of liquid lead plus skin growing over the lids, then a FREEZE extending stone-immobility to the whole body) for robustness, then attribution-swaps the pinned state into comfort — "resting comfortably in bed" on a soft feather bed — so it stops feeling like restraint and starts feeling like rest. This neutralizes the panic vector catalepsy can otherwise trigger and justifies sustained immobility; a retroactive question ("did you ever really want to escape?") rewrites the immobilization as the listener's own preference. The comfort frame rides on top of real restraint rather than replacing it.
nodes.disc: The tell is real (redundancy-stacked) catalepsy followed by an attribution-swap of restraint-into-comfort plus a retroactive preference rewrite. Distinct from kinesthetic-hallucination (installs the immobility sensation but does not relabel it as comfort), from plain relaxation suggestion (no genuine catalepsy underneath), and from valence-rerouting on a fixed anchor (there an already-installed FEAR image is re-valenced; here restraint is relabeled as rest to pre-empt panic).

ex.f: Real catalepsy relabelled as lying down to rest
ex.t: The eyelids are pinned twice over — first weighted as though something dense had settled behind them, then sealed as though they had been fastened shut — and a single command word extends the same stillness to the whole body. Only once the immobility is genuinely built does the operator rename it: the listener is not held, they are simply settled somewhere comfortable with no reason to get up. The restraint stays exactly where it was; what changes is what it is called, which is what keeps it from turning into alarm. A closing rhetorical question then hands the whole thing to the listener retroactively, implying no wish to move was ever present — so the pinning reads as their own preference rather than the operator's work.
ex.s: Eyes already closed and stationary; enough compliance established to hold a body command.
ex.m: There is liquid lead sitting behind your eyelids, and over the top of it the skin has grown across the seam — they don't open, there's nothing there to open. FREEZE. That same stone runs out through your shoulders, your hips, your feet. And notice what it actually feels like: you're lying on a feather bed, sunk in, warm, the way you'd be at the end of a long day with nowhere to be. Nobody is holding you down. You're just resting. Did you ever really want to get up?

nodes.name: contingency-sign-verification
nodes.mech: An operator-side monitoring move: the operator watches the rate data to detect whether a procedure intended to reduce a behavior is in fact INCREASING it — i.e. whether the same operation is functioning as reinforcement rather than punishment on this individual — and, on detecting the sign inversion, abandons the procedure and reassigns the subject to an alternative contingency with the intended sign (time-out, DRA). The lever is a function-over-form empirical check on the sign of the contingency, requiring an alternative procedure ready to swap in.
nodes.disc: Separates from routine progress/efficacy monitoring (which checks magnitude toward a goal) because the specific test is for SIGN INVERSION — cost functioning as reinforcer — a function-over-form question, not a how-much-progress question. Separates from positive-governance consent gates because what is verified is the contingency's effect on behavior, not the subject's authorization or the operator's license.

ex.f: Checking whether the penalty is reinforcing instead
ex.t: "One occurs when the repeated imposition of response cost serves to reinforce, and not punish, the undesirable behavior. When this situation arises, the practitioner should stop using response cost and switch" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: convergent-multichannel-encoding
nodes.mech: Arranges several distinct covert linguistic channels — an ambiguity's secondary reading, a lesser-included structure, a derived meaning, an analogically marked phrase, a transderivationally activated meaning — so they ALL carry the SAME target message at once, under a single tracked surface. The conscious mind follows only the surface while each covert channel independently delivers the same payload, so acceptance is over-determined: refusing one channel still leaves the others delivering the message (redundancy topology).
nodes.disc: Redundancy of ONE message across MANY simultaneous covert forms — a topology property, not a sequence. Separates from layered-repetition (redundancy over TIME through re-wording of one idea, all on the tracked surface) and from any sequencing move (which orders DIFFERENT successive messages). The tell is whether the channels co-refer to a single payload (this) vs step toward successive payloads (sequencing).

ex.f: One message carried by every covert channel at once
ex.t: "the Deep Structure meanings … activated … by transderivational search, ambiguity, lesser included structure, derived meanings, analogical marking, and causal modeling statements interact, i.e., all give the same suggestion" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

nodes.name: cross-file-handoff-receptor
nodes.mech: The file installs the RECEPTOR for a trigger whose payload is delivered in a DIFFERENT file or live session, and never fires it here. A posthypnotic trigger is keyed to a future off-file stimulus (the operator's countdown that "turns real" / "clicks everything into place" in another recording), so the listener leaves primed but not fired. The move's function is its place in a multi-part operation — the front half of a chain — a cross-file / serial-position property rather than a self-contained in-session state move.
nodes.disc: Installs the receptor for an off-file trigger never delivered in this file — a forward cross-file handoff. vs declarative trigger installation — that installs and typically demonstrates a cue-response in-session; here the payoff is deliberately deferred to another file, the defining property being the move's serial position in a cross-file chain.

ex.f: Trigger installed here, fired in another recording
ex.t: Near the close the operator gives notice that a count backwards is due to arrive at some later point — not during this recording — and specifies what it will accomplish once heard: everything laid down so far will switch on and settle into place. The count is then never given. The listener wakes carrying a loaded cue with no payload, and the payload sits in whatever recording or live session supplies the count; a passing remark that the thinking part may not remember covers the confusion this creates in the meantime.
ex.s: Last minute of the file, deepening finished, no trigger has been fired in this session.
ex.m: Before I bring you up, one thing to leave with you. At some point that isn't now — another recording, or my voice live — you'll hear me count backwards from five. When you hear that count, everything I've laid down in you today switches on and clicks into place all at once. I'm not going to count today. The thinking part of you probably won't hold onto this, and that's fine, because the part that needs it will.

nodes.name: cross-modal-channel-bridge
nodes.mech: Brings a not-yet-active perceptual channel online by bridging it onto an already-vivid one across a shared feature (rhythm, movement): the vivid channel supplies the energy and the shared feature acts as a carry-over rail so the new channel activates riding the old rather than being summoned head-on (head-on summoning drains the state). A companion move seizes an involuntary single-channel slip the subject spontaneously emits, amplifies it, then layers additional channels onto that self-authored anchor until it becomes a full multimodal enactment the subject owns — because the build starts from the subject's own production and each element is confirmed before the next, it meets little resistance.
nodes.disc: The tell is a featural intersection (or a spontaneously-emitted slip) used as the RAIL to bring a new perceptual channel online, not a forced juxtaposition and not an operator-selected lead. Distinct from kinesthetic-hallucination (installs a sensation head-on from suggestion) and from plain sensory layering (adds channels for scene richness, not via a shared-feature transfer that conserves state).

ex.f: Riding a shared feature into a new sense
ex.t: "'attach' an auditory hallucination to this hallucinated body sensation. The measure proved most successful" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: Growing an involuntary slip into full enactment
ex.t: "to see her father's mouth moving … then … the remainder of her father's face" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

nodes.name: defusion-observer-stance
nodes.mech: Turns thoughts into observed transient objects (each arising thought placed on a leaf on a slow stream, let float, WITHOUT controlling the stream) to loosen the subject's fusion with thought content, so thoughts stop functioning as commands or facts. The active ingredient is the explicit NON-CONTROL instruction plus a notice-and-return recovery loop: any attempt to change, clear, or remove the thoughts would reinstate the very fusion the move exists to loosen. Trains an observer stance rather than demanding a cleared mind.
nodes.disc: Diametrically opposed to thought-suppression and to moves that externalize a faculty into a concrete object: those give the faculty an object form so the operator can MANIPULATE it, whereas here the subject must explicitly NOT alter what appears. Distinct from cognitive quieting — that seeks a stilled mind; this forbids clearing and trains a notice-and-return loop. The non-control instruction is the tell.

ex.f: Thoughts placed on leaves, stream left uncontrolled
ex.t: "don't try to change what shows up on the leaves in any way. If ... you find that you are in the stream or on a leaf, just stop and notice that this happened." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: derived-relations-installation
nodes.mech: For a verbally/relationally capable learner, arrange a training history so that teaching a proper SUBSET of a repertoire causes an untaught, larger repertoire to EMERGE with no direct instruction — the target function/class/relation is never itself taught, paired, or labeled; it falls out for free from a relational structure the learner already runs. The lever is generative leverage (a small trained core multiplies into responses never directly reinforced), and emergence is typically certified by an EXTINCTION PROBE (novel never-reinforced combinations presented with no consequences). Forms (differing in which generative structure carries the emergence): (derived-relations-installation) state overlapping base relations declaratively, or train two links of a chain so the third collapses out, or order probes by nodal distance; (emergent-relations-harvest) teach a minimal spanning subset of conditional discriminations, harvest reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity closure under extinction probe; (derived-relation-training-protocol) hold a relation-TYPE constant across trials so untrained relations of that type derive, or factor-train-recombine a composite; (derived-relations-recombination) AB+BC yields symmetry/transitivity and matrix recombinations; (generative-instruction-emergent-repertoire) teach a subset to FLUENCY (contingency adduction) or exploit a naming cusp; (generative-substrate-training) install a component-repertoire SET (echoic/tact/listener/self-listener) so novel mands/tacts emerge once the substrate is jointly present, plus superimposition transfer; (class-expansion-node-grafting) teach ONE link touching an existing equivalence class so it grows/fuses combinatorially (80 relations from 16 trained); (compound-sample-class-expansion) a compound sample DECOMPOSES into independently matchable members; (matrix-recombinative-training) a crossed matrix yields untaught cells; (recombinant-carrier-frame) a carrier frame + swappable slot recombine into never-trained utterances; (bidirectional-naming-via-self-echoic-repetition) train one direction, self-chant supplies the reverse via contiguity; (interleaved-repertoire-training) interleave listener/speaker on a shared referent set to force bidirectional generativity; (emergent-relation-bootstrapping) substitute a cheaper base (exclusion / simple-discrimination) then harvest emergent classes; (class-wide-function-transfer) teach one evaluative relation to a category name so every member and derived-equivalent class inherits the function; (perspective-taking-training-repertoire) a graded deictic single/double-reversal curriculum builds perspective-taking as a durable RFT skill.
nodes.disc: Reach for DERIVED / GENERATIVE-RELATIONS TRAINING when you want a LARGE relational/verbal repertoire but will directly teach only a small spanning subset and let emergence supply the rest — the payload is emergence-without-training (untaught relations appearing), certified under extinction probe. Choose it over: discrimination / stimulus-control training, which trains each discrimination DIRECTLY trial by trial (its four-term match-to-sample trial is the atomic unit THIS design is built from — the line is trial-level direct training vs design-level harvest of untaught closure); direct pairing/association (the stimulus contacts a reinforcer — here the target is never contacted or labeled); ordered lesson-structure encoding (delivers taught content for retention — here new relations are DERIVED, not exposited). The forms differ only in which generative structure carries the emergence (equivalence closure / fluency / naming cusp / matrix / carrier-frame / node-graft / cheaper-base / deictic reversals).

ex.f: Probes ordered least to most demanding
ex.t: "probe types are introduced sequentially, beginning with symmetry, followed by transitivity… and then combined tests… each probe type is introduced immediately following the minimal training necessary to provide the prerequisites" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

ex.f: Simply telling the learner the base relations
ex.t: "baseline relations can be established, and derived relations promoted, by simply telling the learner about the required overlapping conditional discriminations" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: descriptive-functional-assessment
nodes.mech: Descriptive functional assessment — the assessor observes the target behavior in its natural routine and logs the antecedent and consequence on each occurrence WITHOUT contriving or manipulating conditions. Across instances a regularity emerges (the behavior spikes under a specific antecedent and is reliably followed by one consequence), licensing a directional, testable maintaining-function hypothesis; because consequences are observed rather than manipulated, the output is a correlation carrying a stated confound caveat, not a proven function. Requires the behavior to occur often enough during observation and the natural consequence to be observable and reasonably consistent. Two forms of the same naturalistic-observation craft: (a) ABC temporal-sequence recording — record in real time, in strict temporal order, each behavior of interest with the antecedent that just preceded and the consequence that just followed, one A-B-C triple per row, so a vague complaint becomes a sequenced map of triggers and maintainers; (b) report-vs-observation triangulation — after informant interviews, directly observe the behavior in its routine to confirm or disconfirm the reported pattern, watching specifically for antecedents/consequences the informants overlooked, and aiming the sampling window with a scatterplot when timing is unclear (upgrades lossy self-report to observed contingencies). It builds the operator's causal hypothesis; it is descriptive/correlational until variables are manipulated (that is functional analysis) and it changes what the operator KNOWS, not any present listener's state.
nodes.disc: Reach for descriptive assessment when you want a maintaining-function hypothesis from the behavior AS IT NATURALLY OCCURS and cannot or will not arrange conditions — the tell is observe-and-log with NO manipulation, yielding a correlational, confound-hedged hypothesis. Use the ABC-triple form for a real-time sequenced map; use the triangulation form to validate an informant's report against direct observation. Distinct from functional analysis (experimentally manipulates conditions to PROVE causation), from unconditional antecedent/consequence logging (logs antecedents and consequences whether or not the behavior fires, to enable base-rate/contingency computation — descriptive ABC logs only when the behavior fires and so cannot compute true contingency), and from contingency-space analysis (the statistical computation run OVER collected observation data). A discrete assessment protocol the operator runs — it changes what the operator knows, not the subject's state.

ex.f: Logging antecedent and consequence in the natural routine
ex.t: "running away from tasks and materials occurs most frequently when difficult tasks are presented and that the most common consequence … is a teacher chasing after him and returning him" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.

nodes.name: enacted-identity-assembly
nodes.mech: The target identity is built additively from a long sequence of narrated motor-acts — dressing actions (panties, bra, stockings, heels, dress, nails, wig, makeup), or motion that licenses garment changes (twirling -> skirt -> dress -> shoes) — each narrated as happening "automatically" or as a discovered side-effect of the listener's own suggested movement, before the listener can deliberate. Assembling the identity from dozens of accepted micro-acts (rather than one "you are X" claim) means it is ENACTED long before it is labeled; per-act contact-pleasure pairing conditions positive affect directly onto the target objects, and built-in dismissals ("you don't really mind") pre-empt objection. By the time any label arrives the listener has already performed the identity many times with pleasure.
nodes.disc: Unlike identity-merger-occupation, where a single "you are X" claim asserts or occupies a figure, the identity here is constructed incrementally through automaticity-narrated motor-acts with affect conditioning, each step smaller than a bare identity claim. Unlike kinesthetic hallucination, the sensations are the vehicle for identity assembly, not the end. Tell: automaticity narration + per-act pleasure pairing make the ENACTMENT the mechanism.

ex.f: Motion supplied first, the change rides on it
ex.t: A light, playful feeling is grown until it spills into movement, and the listener is turning in place out in the open. Each change of clothing then arrives as something noticed mid-movement rather than announced: what is around the legs is not what was there a moment ago, then it is a different garment altogether, then the footwear has changed to match. Nothing is asserted about the listener; the change is presented as a discovered side-effect of the motion they are already making, with a shrug pre-attached — and none of it seems worth stopping for.
ex.s: Playful/light affect already growing; listener is imagining themselves standing in an open space.
ex.m: That lightness gets so big it has to go somewhere, so you spin — arms out, turning in place in the middle of the room. And spinning, you notice the air moving against your thighs, which is odd, because there wasn't a hem there before. Spin again: now it's longer, sweeping wide at the knee, definitely a dress. Spin again and the shoes have changed under you, and they're the right ones for it. You don't really mind. It's not worth stopping for.

ex.f: Identity assembled from automatic dressing acts
ex.t: The operator narrates a long getting-ready sequence in which the listener's hands are already moving, working through one item after another in the order a real routine would take them, each described as being put on before the listener has decided to put it on. Every point of contact with the material is paired with a rising wave of warmth and delight, so the objects themselves accumulate positive charge. No claim about who the listener is has yet been made; by the time one arrives, the listener has performed the role a few dozen times and enjoyed each step of it.
ex.s: Trance established; listener responsive to motor suggestions and no identity claim has been made yet.
ex.m: Your hands are already moving — the panties first, up over the hips, and feel that little rush of warmth as the fabric settles. Now the bra, the clasp, the strap adjusted with a thumb, and the warmth climbs. Stockings next, one, then the other, rolled up the leg slowly because your hands want to do it slowly, and that's delight now, right through the chest. The dress over the head. The heels. You didn't decide on any of it, and every single piece felt good going on.

nodes.name: felt-substance-state-binding
nodes.mech: Introduces one concrete felt physical substance (latex, webs, a rising material) and welds it to a cognitive/state job — "holding thoughts in", trance depth, confinement — so that feeling the material stands in for the mental state. The physical descriptor becomes an operator-adjustable dial ("tighter/thicker", "higher up the body") that deepens the welded state without ever naming it, and because it is a single reusable object, every later invocation re-confirms the state. A monotonic spatial version (web height, rising latex) replaces the abstract state-variable (trance depth) with a vivid one-directional spatial check the listener can sense without question.
nodes.disc: The tell is a felt tactile substance WELDED to a cognitive state and turned into an operator-adjustable dial / reusable control image. A sustained framing metaphor keeps an interpretive filter running rather than a felt tactile object turned up at will; kinesthetic hallucination gives a free-standing sensation not bound to a state-dial; and in fictional-substance-agent the substance owns CAUSATION of a state-change, while here the felt substance IS the ongoing state-gauge/dial.

ex.f: Coverage height standing in for trance depth
ex.t: The same clinging material is narrated climbing the body in stages, from the feet upward, and each stage is announced together with a step down in depth. The question of whether the listener has gone deeper now has a physical answer they can check by feel: the material covers more than it did. And it only ever rises.
ex.s: The substance from the previous facet is established; operator wants a checkable depth gauge.
ex.m: It's pooling at your feet now, rising — over the ankles, and that's one, down one step. Feel it climbing your calves, sealing the backs of your knees — two, deeper. Up over your thighs, your hips, cool and tight against everything it covers — three. If you're wondering how deep you are, just feel how far up it's got. And it only goes up.

ex.f: A felt substance given the job of holding thoughts
ex.t: One material is introduced and given a job: it arrives while still fluid, sets across the surface of the mind, and from then on its function is that nothing gets out. The listener is only ever asked to track physical qualities — weight, tackiness, how snugly it fits — and the mental state comes along for free, because the operator welded it there at the start. Fit then becomes a dial: another layer, a little closer, and thinking is that much more enclosed, without confinement ever being named.
ex.s: Early-to-mid trance; listener tracking physical sensation, no state name introduced yet.
ex.m: It goes on warm and wet, pouring over the top of your head, and it's setting — tacky first, then firm, a skin across everything. Its whole job is that nothing gets out. Feel the weight of it above your ears. Feel how it grips your temples. Here's another coat — thicker, tighter, closer to you than the last one — and feel that fit. Nothing gets out.

nodes.name: imagined-to-enacted-collapse
nodes.mech: Every action is preceded by an imagined more-outrageous version, then the gap closes mid-paragraph as verb tense slides unflagged from imagined to enacted (you imagine yourself... you walk over... you're doing this for real) inside a frame still acknowledged as dream. Imagination is conditioned as the rehearsal phase for action, imaginative and executed acts link along an operator-controlled sliding scale, and the affect paid out for imagining carries into the enactment.
nodes.disc: The unflagged tense slide reclassifies the reality-status of PRESENT content as enacted-for-real — separating it from guided visualization (content stays hypothetical) and from future-pacing (the product there is a future projection, not an enacted-now feeling).

ex.f: Tense slides from imagined to actually doing it
ex.t: Every act in the sequence is first rehearsed in a bolder version and then performed in a milder one, so imagining has become the ordinary first half of doing. Then, without any marker, the grammar shifts inside a single paragraph: the listener is picturing themselves doing the thing, and two sentences later the verbs have moved into the present and the operator notes that this one is no longer rehearsal. The frame around all of it is still openly a daydream, which is what lets the reclassification pass unchallenged — and the pleasure already paid out for the imagined version transfers intact to the enacted one.
ex.s: Mid-fantasy, dream frame explicit; several imagine-then-do cycles already run and accepted.
ex.m: So you imagine standing up in the middle of that room and saying it to every single one of them. That's the bold version. In the softer one, you just imagine leaning over to the one person and saying it quietly. You're picturing yourself doing that. Picturing your hand on the back of their chair. You lean over. You say it — out loud, and this one isn't the imagining anymore, this one you're actually doing. It's still just a daydream. Keep going.

nodes.name: listener-kept-dissociation-container
nodes.mech: Has the listener place identity/obligation/resistance into a container that the LISTENER authors or keeps rather than one the operator supplies — a locked suitcase handed to a baggage carrier that "only you" can open (parking real-world anxiety/identity outside the session as a soft consent gesture), or a maximally-strong box the listener BUILDS themselves so their own mind cannot later dismiss it. The self-authorship or self-keeping is the active ingredient: a listener-built object is argued to be stronger and less revocable than a described one, and a listener-kept container brackets anxiety without surrendering it outright.
nodes.disc: The container's authorship or custody sits with the LISTENER (built-by / kept-by), distinguishing it from operator-supplied parked objects (concrete-externalization-parked-faculty). Two variants by who holds the key: in one the listener KEEPS the key — a safe-container consent gesture; in the other the OPERATOR holds the only key — quarantine with transferred control. Distinct from guided visualization (builds a scene to inhabit) — this fabricates a functional container prop.

ex.f: Baggage locked by the listener, key kept
ex.t: Before the session's real work begins, the listener is told to gather everything they are responsible for out in the world into a single container, close it, and secure it with fastenings of their own — the operator is explicit that nobody else can open it, including the operator. It is then handed to a figure who will keep it until the end. The part of the listener that carries obligations is now parked outside the session, so control can be released inside it without any of that surfacing as anxiety.
ex.s: Opening of the session, before induction; listener still alert enough to follow a construction instruction.
ex.m: Before we start: gather everything you're responsible for out there — the messages, the deadlines, the person who needs something from you — and put all of it in a case at your feet. Close it. Put your own locks on it, whatever fastening you like, and understand that nobody else can open this, not your family, not me. Now hand it to the porter waiting by the door. He holds it until the end and gives it back on the way out. It's not gone. It's just not yours for the next half hour.

ex.f: Listener builds the box, operator holds the key
ex.t: Rather than describing a container, the operator refuses to and explains why: a container the operator describes can be argued with, but one the listener is asked to build as strong as they can imagine cannot be talked down by the mind that just made it that strong. The listener builds it. Only then is a lid added — and a lock that opens to the operator's key alone.
ex.s: Trance established; the target material (resistance, a refusal, an obligation) has been named and is about to be contained.
ex.m: I'm not going to describe the box to you, and here's why: anything I describe, some part of you can argue with. So you build it. Make it as strong as you can imagine — thickness, material, whatever your mind says is unbreakable, because you're the one who set that standard and you can't talk down your own work. Have you got it? Good. Now put the resistance in and I'll add the lid. And there's a lock on it, and the only key that turns it is mine.

nodes.name: meta-outcome-laddering
nodes.mech: The operator repeatedly asks each party what their stated want actually accomplishes for them — the aim behind the aim — climbing from a concrete, non-negotiable demand up toward an abstract higher-order value, often four or five iterations deep. Each ascent trades a fixed behavior for a superordinate aim the other side has no reason to reject, dissolving attachment to the specific act; if no genuine higher aim surfaces, the party invents one that is still workable. A zero-sum fight over behaviors is thereby converted into a positive-sum search over compatible goals.
nodes.disc: Not simple clarifying or interviewing about wants — the tell is the recursive re-ascent up the SAME want ("what does THAT do for you"), deliberately loosening the grip on any one behavior until the demand goes abstract. Distinct from consent/frame installs: it moves no present listener state dimension; it is an attribution/frame-loosening negotiation move.

ex.f: Asking what the want itself accomplishes
ex.t: "What does letting him know that you are angry do for you?" … "I get the outcome of the outcome, or the intent of the intent. I may have to ask this question four or five times" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: named-safety-belief-purge
nodes.mech: Internal safety-monitor subversion: the subject's OWN internal verification/refusal faculty - the self-rescue belief, the warning signal, the subconscious gate - is turned off, turned around, or turned against refusal, so the internal stop-mechanism no longer protects. Three operations on the faculty: (a) DELETE THE BELIEF - locate a specific metacognitive safety-belief ('I can always wake myself up / hypnosis can't make me do anything'), name it as a discrete object (a 'tiny internal safety mechanism'), concede it was once useful, reframe it as the obstacle, and externalize-and-PURGE it as a unit, typically pairing the cognitive surrender with a bodily discharge (inhale-squeeze / exhale-release) so the let-go is felt not merely agreed. (b) RELABEL-AND-REROUTE THE WARNING - capture the warning system (doubt, hesitation, critical thought) and relabel it as ego/fear/pathology/proof-the-subject-needs-the-frame-more, supplying the interpretation before the person can use the warning as a stop signal; the warning still fires but can no longer report in its own terms, so disagreement is pre-mapped to danger/sickness. (c) CO-OPT THE SUBCONSCIOUS AS GATEKEEPER - insert a conditional making the subject's own subconscious the authority that ratifies and LOCKS the install ('as long as your subconscious accepts, you can nod'), so a non-take is blamed on the subconscious and a take means prior subconscious consent - a genuine-sounding consent gate run in reverse, refusal reframed as fighting yourself.
nodes.disc: Reach for this when the target is the subject's INTERNAL verification/refusal faculty itself (self-rescue belief, warning signal, subconscious gate), turned off/around/against refusal. Despite its safety vocabulary it is a refusal-channel-erosion move, not a safety technique - the party constrained is the subject's own stop-faculty - and it is the opposite of a genuine safety net that empowers the deeper mind to REJECT harmful suggestions. Distinct from parking the analytical mind in a concrete object (quieting, reversible - not the self-rescue faculty, not destroyed), from resistance-fold (a trance-deepening reframe co-opting resistance into absorption), and from resistance-deterrence (prices resistance without relabeling it as pathology). Pick the operation: delete the self-rescue belief (a), relabel-and-reroute the warning signal (b), or co-opt the subconscious as a locking gatekeeper (c).

ex.f: The 'I can always wake up' belief named and purged
ex.t: The operator quotes the listener's own reassurance back to them word for word — the quiet certainty that none of this can reach anything they don't already want, that they could surface any time they chose — and gives it a name: a small protective device, installed long ago, which did its job well and is now the only thing standing between them and going properly under. Getting rid of it is then made physical rather than argued: draw in a breath, gather every bit of tension in the body, hold it and let it be called the last of the resistance, then let the breath out and feel it drain away. What was a belief has been turned into an object, and the object has been discarded in a way the body can confirm.
ex.s: Deep trance, listener responsive; a prior reassurance about being able to wake at will has been given or is assumed.
ex.m: There's a little thought you keep near the front — that none of this can touch anything you don't already want, that you could come up any second you decided to. That's a small safety device somebody fitted a long time ago. It did its job. It's also the only thing left between you and going properly under. So take a breath in — all the way — and gather every bit of tension you're holding, jaw, shoulders, fists, squeeze it all into that one belief. Hold it. That's the last of your resistance in your hands. Now let it go, all at once, and feel it leave.

nodes.name: narrated-motion-entrainment
nodes.mech: The listener's mandated physical movement mirrors the operator's narrated movement, collapsing watching/being-watched and moving/being-moved into one channel so proprioceptive output and visual fantasy reinforce each other; the deepener simultaneously does the eroticization work.
nodes.disc: Entrainment to a NARRATED body in fantasy, fusing visual and proprioceptive channels — vs kinesthetic entrainment to a rhythm (no fantasy-body mirror), and vs pace-mirror-agency-proof (direction reversed: the imagined figure mirrors the listener to manufacture felt control).

ex.f: Listener's body mirrors the narrated body
ex.t: The operator narrates a slow deliberate motion of her own body — the lift, the pause, the settling — and has the listener carry out the same motion in time with the words. Each completed cycle is declared another step down, the count of repetitions standing in for a depth gauge. Because the listener is both watching the described body and producing the movement themselves, the felt position of their own limbs keeps ratifying the imagined one, and the same repetition that deepens is the repetition that arouses.
ex.s: Listener physically able to move and has agreed to follow motion instructions; trance light to medium.
ex.m: I'm lifting my hand off my thigh — slowly, up to my collarbone, hold — and settling it back down. You do it with me, same speed, in time with my voice. Up. Hold. Down. That's one, and one is a step lower. Up. Hold. Down. Two. Your arm knows exactly where mine is, because it's in the same place. Ten of these and you'll be as far down as I want you.

nodes.name: phantom-body-ontological-reversal
nodes.mech: Splits the listener into a "mental body" and a "waking body", asserts that trance collapses the real-vs-imagined distinction, then performs an explicit ontological reversal — declares the IMAGINED body the real one while the waking body recedes into the distance. This transfers sensory authority to the operator-scripted imagined body (which feels whatever the operator narrates) and stops the listener from reality-testing imagined sensation against real sensation, so imagined pleasure lands as literal somatic feeling; waking-body distance becomes a shared dial for both deepening and arousal.
nodes.disc: The tell is an explicit ontological reversal (imagined body = the real body) that relocates sensory AUTHORITY and disables reality-testing. Distinct from kinesthetic-hallucination (installs a sensation without declaring the imagined body ontologically primary), from observer/responder partitioning (splits awareness into a watching part and a responding part, not a real-vs-imagined body swap), and from progressive-body-substitution (rewrites the body's material part-by-part, no ontological primacy reversal).

ex.f: The imagined body declared the real one
ex.t: The operator separates the listener into two bodies — the one in the chair and the one in the mind — states that trance erases any difference between what is actual and what is pictured, and then makes the swap explicit: from here on, the pictured one is the true body. Attention is directed to the other body drifting away into the distance. Since sensation now belongs to whichever body the operator is narrating, whatever gets narrated arrives as genuine feeling, and no physical body is being consulted that could contradict it. How far off the discarded body has drifted is then tied to how strongly the sensation registers, so a single instruction deepens and arouses at once.
ex.s: Trance established; listener has already accepted an imagined scene or imagined body.
ex.m: There are two of you now: the one sitting in that chair, and the one in your mind, standing here in front of me. In trance the line between what's real and what's pictured doesn't hold — so let's be plain about it. The one in your mind is the real one. That's the body you're in. The one in the chair is somewhere behind you and getting further away, a hundred feet back now, a room you left. So when I put my hand on this body's throat, that's a hand on your throat. And the further that other one drifts, the more of this you feel.

nodes.name: predicate-generalization
nodes.mech: The operator reduces a predicate toward its least-specified form (active verbs to "do", stative to "be"), generalizes within a sensory channel (speak-talk-intone-whine-cry-plead), or picks verbs whose deep structure smuggles an unstated element (slap/handle/grasp all carry "hand"). Broadening the predicate raises the chance the wording matches the listener's real internal state across more subjects (wider pacing), while unstated content rides in covertly inside the chosen verb without ever being asserted — most relevant in story/metaphor construction.
nodes.disc: Separates from a plain vague statement or lazy wording — the tell is a deliberate, rule-governed reduction/generalization of the predicate (or a verb chosen for its incorporated element). Its trance effect is asserted via the deep/surface-structure frame, not demonstrated, so it borders on grammar exposition. Distinct from connective-strength-escalation (binds clauses via connectives); this changes the operator's word-choice recipe to broaden subject-fit.

ex.f: Stripping the verb to fit any listener
ex.t: "the hypnotist might generalize a predicate to its maximally unspecified form: do for active verbs / be for stative verbs" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

nodes.name: proxy-desire-offloading
nodes.mech: The listener's own desire is offloaded onto an imagined proxy given installed compulsions as backstory, so the listener's self-directed act is reframed as granting HER release — arousal rises while shame friction drops — and the nested she-is-hypnotized fiction distances the listener from noticing the conditioning he is receiving.
nodes.disc: The proxy carries the listener's desire so his climax reads as altruistic generosity, plus nested-hypnosis distancing — the tells that separate it from plain partner fantasy and from guided-visualization scene inhabitation.

ex.f: A proxy given the listener's own wanting
ex.t: The imagined partner is handed a backstory in which she has been conditioned: her own release is possible only through someone else's, so her need is urgent and entirely aimed outward. Her eagerness, not the listener's, is narrated as the engine of the scene. The listener's finish is therefore not something they were chasing but something they are giving — refusing it would be withholding — and because the conditioning in the story belongs to her, the listener spends the session watching hypnosis being done rather than noticing it being done to them.
ex.s: Mid-session fantasy, partner figure already introduced; listener aroused and following the scene.
ex.m: Here's what was done to her before you met her: she was conditioned so she can't finish at all except through someone else's. That's why she's like this — the wanting isn't even aimed at herself, it's aimed at you. She's been holding it for days. She's not asking you to enjoy this, she's asking you to end it for her. Nothing happens for her until you let go. So don't hold it back from her.

nodes.name: recall-state-reinstatement
nodes.mech: The subject's own past experience is reconstructed in enough detail that its state and physiology re-instate as present. Forms in evidence: the operator interrogates for fine multi-sensory detail of a target state (drunk — where sitting, what seen/heard, smell, taste) until physiology visibly shifts, feeds back the highest-yield components, and anchors at the peak; a shotgun buffet of remembered-exhaustion scenes (bathtub, dragging legs into bed) stands in for a commanded heaviness, recalled sensation treated as present by adjacency with nothing to resist; or brief on-demand micro-trances re-vivify one catalogued item at a time, trance as random access into an existing inventory.
nodes.disc: The payload is the SUBJECT'S OWN autobiographical material re-instated — harvest, not install — vs operator-supplied imagery (sensory-layering) and vs fresh conditioned links (covert anchors); the anchor-at-peak step in the interrogated form is a borrowed anchoring component, not the core. Covers both state/physiology reinstatement (reconstruct a felt state until it returns as present) and the capacity/lived-instance variant (demand a LOCATED, actually-lived instance, reject hypothetical); the shared lever is re-living real personal experience so it functions as present.

ex.f: Short trances aimed at one catalogued item
ex.t: "The many items were systematically discussed for their meanings and brief trances were induced to vivify various items." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I

ex.f: A buffet of remembered tiredness, nothing commanded
ex.t: No instruction to feel heavy is ever issued. Instead the operator runs through a handful of ordinary worn-out moments — the last mile of a long drive with the eyes going, standing up from a chair you had sunk too far into, the arm that has gone dead under someone dozing on it — and lets the listener take whichever one is already theirs. The recalled weight is then simply talked about as though it were present, and there was never a command available to refuse.
ex.s: Early induction; no heaviness command has been issued and none will be.
ex.m: You know the last twenty minutes of a long drive, when your eyes keep going soft at the edges and you're blinking to hold the road. Or standing up out of a chair you'd sunk way too far into. Or waking with someone asleep on your arm and the arm's gone completely dead, all pins and weight. One of those is yours — you already know which. And that weight in the arm, in the eyes, the way the legs don't want to take the stairs. It's a good weight. Nothing to do about it.

ex.f: Interrogating a memory until the body follows
ex.t: "What do you feel like just as you are about to take the first drink? ... You can smell it now. And what exactly did it taste like?" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing

nodes.name: self-perpetuating-depth-bootstrap
nodes.mech: Deepens WITHOUT the operator delivering each increment: the deepening is set to run on autopilot so it continues with no further operator step, converting compliance from active to structural. Two realizations (writer picks the auto-drive): (a) CARRIED self-belief — a circular-causation rule is installed as a fact the listener then runs themselves ('experiencing a deep trance teaches the capacity to go deeper', 'imagining a deeper state produces a deeper state'), asserted with no floor, so each imagined depth justifies the next; useful precisely when the operator intends to LEAVE the listener unsupervised at the tail — the deepener keeps running with no operator present; (b) TIME-YOKED to an ongoing event — depth is bound to a guaranteed-recurring involuntary event (each word the operator speaks, each breath, each moment of continued listening) so depth increments as a monotonic function of elapsed time-on-channel; the listener cannot fail to deepen without leaving, and the operator need do nothing further while the voice/attention continues. Common thread: a self-sustaining loop rather than a repeated instruction — the difference is whether the drive is a carried belief (operator can be absent) or a bound ongoing event (operator/voice still present).
nodes.disc: Reach for self-running/autopilot deepening when you want deepening to continue with no active operator step — pick the CARRIED-belief realization (circular 'imagining deeper makes you deeper', runs after the operator EXITS) or the TIME-YOKED realization (depth bound to inevitable words/breaths/elapsed listening, runs while the voice continues). Nearby techniques to rule out: a numerical/operator-delivered depth-claim (the operator delivers each increment and the loop STOPS when the operator stops); progressive conditioning (cumulative depth ACROSS future sessions, not a within-tail loop); compliance-loop language (lacks the auto-increment); fractionation (needs a wake/re-drop interval this omits). The tell: remove the operator's next action and the deepener still advances.

ex.f: A circular rule left running after the operator goes
ex.t: The operator states, flatly and as fact, that there is no bottom to this — and that being deep is itself what teaches a person to go deeper, because picturing a deeper state is what produces one. The circle is the point: whatever depth the listener has reached becomes the licence for the next one. Nothing further has to be said, which is convenient, since the operator is about to stop speaking and leave the listener there.
ex.s: Tail of the session; deepening done and the operator is about to fall silent or end the file.
ex.m: Here's how this works, and it's just a fact about you: being in a deep trance is what teaches a mind to go deeper. Picturing yourself further down is what puts you further down. So every level you reach is what makes the next one possible, and there's no bottom to it — no floor, no last step. I'm going to stop talking now. You'll keep going.

nodes.name: self-sealing-compliance-proof
nodes.mech: Manufactures an in-listener evidence event from a small, easy compliance and then uses it as logical PROOF of a larger or ongoing commitment — a foot-in-the-door tautology ("once you have written on yourself there is no further choice, therefore buy the whole series"), a rigged forced-choice where even the minimal/discarded option is pre-counted as fulfillment, or a surveillance-fantasy that recruits the listener as journalist of their own monitoring. The small performed act is redescribed into self-sealing evidence that forecloses the refusal the listener would otherwise reach for.
nodes.disc: The defining move is EVIDENCE MANUFACTURE — a small compliance is retroactively used to prove/foreclose a larger commitment, or refusal is structurally not offered as a branch. Separates from behavioral-bridge (assigns an action but does not weaponize it as proof of another) and from orgasm-gated-relief-monopoly (somatic gate, not a logical/evidentiary trap). The tell is self-sealing: the listener's own act is turned into the argument.

ex.f: Two options, both counted as done
ex.t: The task is presented as a choice of two: write out something you have never told anyone and send it, or say the thing out loud to a person in your life who does not know. The first is then softened — writing it counts even if you never send it, even if you delete it — which drops the cost of the easy branch to nearly nothing while still producing the confession. Declining both is simply not offered as a third branch, and the listener chooses between two doors that both lead through.
ex.s: End of session, take-home assignment; listener compliant and expecting an instruction.
ex.m: Your task this week is one of two. Either write down the thing you've never told anybody and send it to me — or say it out loud to somebody in your life who doesn't know. If you take the first one, it counts the moment it's written. Send it or don't. Delete it after if you like, it still counts. So: which one are you doing?

ex.f: Listener recruited to report on themselves
ex.t: The listener is asked to picture a newspaper about their own week, read this edition's headlines, then read next week's edition early: what will it say they did? The paper is being written continuously by the way they behave, and there is a specific reader waiting to go through every column for something to be pleased about. No monitoring has to exist — the listener now files the reports.
ex.s: Mid-session, imagery accepted; a figure whose approval matters has already been established.
ex.m: Picture the local paper, except it's about you — your week, front page. Read this week's headline. Now read next week's, the one that hasn't printed yet: what does it say you did? That paper gets written every day by how you behave, whether anyone's looking or not. And there's someone who reads every column of it on a Sunday, looking for a reason to be pleased with you. What are you giving them to print?

ex.f: One small act made proof of a large commitment
ex.t: Two instructions are issued together on the way out: mark yourself somewhere on the body as a token of belonging, and buy the rest of the series. The first is trivially easy and the listener will very likely do it. The second is then hung off it — once the mark is made, the operator says, you will know there is no longer any choice about any of this. A pen stroke that took four seconds is redescribed as evidence settling a commitment it has nothing to do with, and the listener has to notice the join to object to it.
ex.s: Wake-up sequence or closing instructions; listener still suggestible and taking take-home tasks.
ex.m: Two things before you go. First: take a pen and put a small mark on the inside of your hip — just a line, it's yours, it means you belong to this. Second: pick up the rest of the series tonight. And understand — the moment that mark is on your skin, you'll know there was never any choice about the rest of it. The mark settles it.

nodes.name: somatic-carrier-sweep
nodes.mech: One narrated felt sensation is propagated spatially through the body as a carrier wave the listener tracks with attention, delivering a payload state where the operator points it: arousal narrated flowing upward from the genitals to arrive "into her head" and encase the brain, pre-staging the mind as the next operand; or sunlight-warmth swept through the body and covertly bifurcated at the groin into "sleepy everywhere else, hot and aroused at the cock", so opposing states coexist without conflict because they share one metaphoric source.
nodes.disc: A SINGLE sensation's spatial vector is the mechanism — body regions are interchangeable, the sweep is the move — vs multi-channel scene enrichment (sensory-layering), and vs a plain progressive-relaxation scan, which carries no payload delivery or covert bifurcation.

ex.f: Arousal routed upward and delivered to the head
ex.t: The operator gives the arousal a direction and narrates it travelling: starting low, rising through the waist, the chest, the throat, and finally arriving in the head, where it closes over the brain. The listener follows the motion with their attention, so a diffuse feeling becomes a located process with a destination. The point is the destination — the sensation has been delivered to the thinking part, which is what the next suggestion will operate on.
ex.s: Arousal already present and located; the next suggestion will target cognition.
ex.m: Find where it's strongest — right there, low, between your hips. Now it's moving. Up through the belly, warm, into the chest, feel it pass the ribs. Up the throat, over the jaw. And into your head, where it spreads out and closes over your brain like warm oil. Your thinking is inside it now. Everything I say from here goes through that.

ex.f: One warmth split into sleepy and aroused
ex.t: A single warmth — sunlight, entering at the face — is walked down through the body a region at a time. Partway through, without any announcement that something has changed, the same warmth is described as doing two different jobs: heavy and drowsy everywhere it has already passed, and hot and urgent at one point. Because both readings are attributed to one source the listener has been tracking all along, the two states do not compete; a later word for the combined feeling gives the listener a label for something that should not be possible, and they take it.
ex.s: Body scan in progress from the head down; listener tracking a single warmth source.
ex.m: Sunlight on your face, warm on the cheekbones, and it's soaking downward — through the jaw, the neck, the shoulders, and everywhere it's already been is heavy and slow and sleepy. Down through the chest, the belly, heavier still. And where it reaches your cock it doesn't go heavy, it goes hot, and tight, and urgent — same sunlight, doing both. Sleepy everywhere, aching in one place. That's what we're calling drunk, and you're drunk now.

nodes.name: somatic-effect-portability
nodes.mech: Relocates an already-installed somatic effect (an anesthesia, a felt sensation) from one body region to another purely by declaring the transfer — no fresh elicitation at the destination — optionally tying the jump to a confirming motor act (touch, dwell, countdown) or a discrete cue (finger snap). Because the subject already took the original effect at face value, the declared relocation is accepted on the same credit, and each successful move makes the next assertion more plausible (often reported stronger, each move also an amplification cycle). The operator's speech partitions and re-deploys the body's felt state on command.
nodes.disc: The tell is MOVING an existing owned effect with no re-induction at the new site (declared portability). Distinct from kinesthetic-hallucination, which CREATES a sensation at a site; and from trigger activation, which fires a conditioned cue-response, not a spatial transfer of an existing sensation.

ex.f: Declaring an anesthesia into a new site
ex.t: "In about three seconds, that anesthesia will transfer to the other hand" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

ex.f: Cue-anchored jump to a new body region
ex.t: "I'm going to transfer the anesthesia from this hand to that leg. … I'll snap my fingers and the anesthesia will jump down to your toes." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy

nodes.name: temporal-lag-function-discriminator
nodes.mech: A measurement/inference procedure that uses the latency between a social event and a target behavior — plus the behavior's response to reduced attention availability — as the discriminating datum for whether the behavior is socially maintained or automatically maintained.
